// ── Trit (balanced ternary) tensor tests ─────────────────────────────────────

#[test]
fn trit_quantize_round_trip() {
    // trit_quantize then cast to f32: sum of [1, 0, 1, -1] == 1
    assert_eq!(as_float(&run(r#"
        fn main() -> f32 {
            let x = forge.zeros[f32, [4]]
            x[0] = 0.8   x[1] = -0.3   x[2] = 1.2   x[3] = -0.9
            let t = trit_quantize(x)
            sum(t as f32)
        }
    "#)), 1.0);
}

#[test]
fn trit_neg_inverts_sign() {
    // trit_neg(trit_quantize(x)) == trit_quantize(-x)
    assert_eq!(as_float(&run(r#"
        fn main() -> f32 {
            let x = forge.zeros[f32, [4]]
            x[0] = 0.8   x[1] = -0.3   x[2] = 1.2   x[3] = -0.9
            let t = trit_quantize(x)
            let neg_t = trit_neg(t)
            # trit_quantize(x) = [1, 0, 1, -1]; trit_neg = [-1, 0, -1, 1]; sum = -1
            sum(neg_t as f32)
        }
    "#)), -1.0);
}

#[test]
fn trit_sparsity_fraction() {
    // trit_quantize([0.8, -0.3, 1.2, -0.9]) = [1, 0, 1, -1]; 1 zero out of 4 = 0.25
    let v = as_float(&run(r#"
        fn main() -> f64 {
            let x = forge.zeros[f32, [4]]
            x[0] = 0.8   x[1] = -0.3   x[2] = 1.2   x[3] = -0.9
            let t = trit_quantize(x)
            trit_sparsity(t)
        }
    "#));
    assert!((v - 0.25).abs() < 1e-9, "expected 0.25, got {}", v);
}

#[test]
fn forge_trit_constructor() {
    // forge.trit[4, 3] should produce a zero-filled [4, 3] DType::Trit tensor.
    // sum of zeros is 0.
    assert_eq!(as_float(&run(r#"
        fn main() -> f32 {
            let !w = forge.trit[4, 3]
            sum(w as f32)
        }
    "#)), 0.0);
}

#[test]
fn trit_matmul_ones_by_trit_weight() {
    // x = ones[2,4], w = trit[4,3] with known values.
    // Row sums of w columns: col0=1-1+0+1=1, col1=-1+1+0-1=-1, col2=0+1-1+1=1
    // Both rows of x@w are [1, -1, 1]. sum = 2*(1-1+1) = 2.
    assert_eq!(as_float(&run(r#"
        fn main() -> f32 {
            let x = forge.ones[f32, [2, 4]]
            let !w = forge.trit[4, 3]
            w[0, 0] = 1.0    w[0, 1] = -1.0   w[0, 2] = 0.0
            w[1, 0] = -1.0   w[1, 1] = 1.0    w[1, 2] = 1.0
            w[2, 0] = 0.0    w[2, 1] = 0.0    w[2, 2] = -1.0
            w[3, 0] = 1.0    w[3, 1] = -1.0   w[3, 2] = 1.0
            let y = x @ w
            sum(y)
        }
    "#)), 2.0);
}

#[test]
fn trit_matmul_vs_float_reference() {
    // x @ trit_quantize(W) == x @ (trit_quantize(W) as f32)
    // Both should give the same sum.
    let src = r#"
        fn main() -> f32 {
            let x = forge.ones[f32, [2, 4]]
            let !w = forge.trit[4, 3]
            w[0, 0] = 1.0    w[0, 1] = -1.0   w[0, 2] = 0.0
            w[1, 0] = -1.0   w[1, 1] = 1.0    w[1, 2] = 1.0
            w[2, 0] = 0.0    w[2, 1] = 0.0    w[2, 2] = -1.0
            w[3, 0] = 1.0    w[3, 1] = -1.0   w[3, 2] = 1.0
            let y_trit = x @ w
            let w_f32 = w as f32
            let y_float = x @ w_f32
            sum(y_trit) - sum(y_float)
        }
    "#;
    let diff = as_float(&run(src));
    assert!((diff).abs() < 1e-6, "trit matmul diverges from float reference: diff={}", diff);
}

#[test]
fn trit_quantize_soft_runs() {
    // trit_quantize_soft(ones*0.7, 0.5) — just verify it runs and produces a value
    let v = as_float(&run(r#"
        fn main() -> f32 {
            let x = forge.ones[f32, [3, 3]] .* 0.7
            let w_soft = trit_quantize_soft(x, 0.5)
            sum(w_soft)
        }
    "#));
    // 9 elements, each ~tanh(0.4) + tanh(2.4); should be > 0
    assert!(v > 0.0, "trit_quantize_soft sum should be positive, got {}", v);
}

#[test]
fn trit_pack_returns_masks() {
    // trit_pack([1, 0, -1, 1]) -> (pos=[1,0,0,1], neg=[0,0,1,0])
    // sum(pos) = 2, sum(neg) = 1
    assert_eq!(as_float(&run(r#"
        fn main() -> f32 {
            let x = forge.zeros[f32, [4]]
            x[0] = 0.8   x[1] = -0.3   x[2] = 1.2   x[3] = -0.9
            let t = trit_quantize(x)
            let (pos, neg) = trit_pack(t)
            sum(pos) + sum(neg)
        }
    "#)), 3.0);  // sum(pos)=2 (elems 0,2), sum(neg)=1 (elem 3)
}

#[test]
fn compound_assign_star_slash_bitwise() {
    // #222: `*=`, `/=`, `&=`, `|=`, `^=` silently no-op'd in the interpreter (only
    // `+=`/`-=` were handled), so `acc *= i` left acc unchanged — diverging from
    // the JIT, which applies them. Each must now mutate.
    assert_eq!(as_int(&run("fn main() -> i64 { let !a = 1    a *= 5   a }")), 5);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&run("fn main() -> i64 { let !a = 100  a /= 5   a }")), 20);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&run("fn main() -> i64 { let !a = 6    a &= 3   a }")), 2);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&run("fn main() -> i64 { let !a = 6    a |= 1   a }")), 7);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&run("fn main() -> i64 { let !a = 6    a ^= 3   a }")), 5);
    // Iterative factorial — the jit_scalar_demo repro that was returning 1.
    assert_eq!(as_int(&run(
        "fn main() -> i64 { let !acc = 1  let !i = 1  while i <= 10 { acc *= i  i += 1 }  acc }"
    )), 3628800);
}

// ─── f32 tensor precision (#241) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
// f32-family tensors are rounded through f32 at construction and element
// stores, matching the JIT's true-f32 tensors; f64 tensors keep full width.

#[test]
fn f32_tensor_store_rounds_through_f32() {
    // 0.1 is not f32-representable; the stored element must be the f32
    // rounding (0.10000000149011612), exactly what the JIT sees.
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> f32 {
            let !t = forge.zeros[f32, [1]]
            t[0] = 0.1
            t[0]
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_float(&v), 0.1f32 as f64);
}

#[test]
fn f64_tensor_store_keeps_full_precision() {
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> f64 {
            let !t = forge.zeros[f64, [1]]
            t[0] = 0.1
            t[0]
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_float(&v), 0.1f64);
}

#[test]
fn f32_elementwise_op_rounds_per_op() {
    // Compute-in-f64-then-round equals native f32 for `*` (the 2p+2
    // double-rounding bound), so this must be exactly 0.1f32 * 0.2f32.
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> f32 {
            let !a = forge.zeros[f32, [1]]
            let !b = forge.zeros[f32, [1]]
            a[0] = 0.1
            b[0] = 0.2
            let c = a .* b
            c[0]
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_float(&v), (0.1f32 * 0.2f32) as f64);
}

#[test]
fn f32_scalar_broadcast_demotes_the_scalar() {
    // The JIT splats a scalar into f32 lanes, so `a .* 0.1` multiplies by
    // 0.1f32, not 0.1f64 — the interpreter demotes the scalar the same way.
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> f32 {
            let !a = forge.zeros[f32, [1]]
            a[0] = 0.1
            let s = a .* 0.1
            s[0]
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_float(&v), (0.1f32 * 0.1f32) as f64);
}

#[test]
fn f64_elementwise_op_stays_wide() {
    // Width propagates through ops: an f64 operand keeps the result f64.
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> f64 {
            let !a = forge.zeros[f64, [1]]
            let !b = forge.zeros[f64, [1]]
            a[0] = 0.1
            b[0] = 0.2
            let c = a .* b
            c[0]
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_float(&v), 0.1f64 * 0.2f64);
}

#[test]
fn int_tensor_elementwise_not_corrupted_by_f32_rounding() {
    // An Int operand keeps the result wide: values beyond f32's 2^24 exact
    // range must survive elementwise arithmetic.
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> f64 {
            let !t = forge.zeros[i64, [1]]
            t[0] = 1234567891234567
            let u = t .+ 0
            u[0]
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_float(&v), 1234567891234567.0);
}

#[test]
fn f64_tensor_cast_to_f32_rounds() {
    // Narrowing cast goes through the F32 construction rounding.
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> f32 {
            let !a = forge.zeros[f64, [1]]
            a[0] = 0.1
            let b = a as f32
            b[0]
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_float(&v), 0.1f32 as f64);
}

// --- loud-diagnostics batch: runtime guards (#394/#395/#396) ---------------

#[test]
fn rng_uniform_int_draws_in_range_395() {
    // Implemented (#395): draws land in the half-open [low, high) and the
    // linear (rng, tensor) pair destructures like the float rng ctors.
    let v = run(
        "fn main() -> i64 {\n\
             let rng = Rng.seed(1)\n\
             let (r2, i) = rng.uniform_int[i32,[16]](3, 7)\n\
             let !bad = 0\n\
             for k in 0..16 {\n\
                 if i[k] < 3 { bad = bad + 1 }\n\
                 if i[k] > 6 { bad = bad + 1 }\n\
             }\n\
             bad\n\
         }");
    assert!(matches!(v, Value::Int(0)), "all draws must be in [3, 7), got {:?}", v);
    // An empty range must still be loud.
    let e = run_err("fn main() -> nil { let rng = Rng.seed(1)  let (r2, i) = rng.uniform_int[i32,[3]](5, 5)  nil }");
    assert!(e.contains("uniform_int") && e.contains("greater"), "got: {}", e);
    // The bracket form without the range call must be loud, not a silent nil.
    let e2 = run_err("fn main() -> nil { let rng = Rng.seed(1)  let (r2, i) = rng.uniform_int[i32,[3]]  nil }");
    assert!(e2.contains("uniform_int"), "got: {}", e2);
}

#[test]
fn field_binding_scalar_copies_444() {
    // `let !x = self.field` on a SCALAR field is a value copy (SPEC §3.4),
    // not a live alias — a snapshot must not track later field writes.
    let v = run("model B { !n: i64\n\
                 fn probe(self) -> i64 { let !snap = self.n  self.n = 99  snap } }\n\
                 fn main() -> i64 { let !b = B { n: 7 }  b.probe() }");
    assert!(matches!(v, Value::Int(7)), "snapshot must hold 7, got {:?}", v);
}

#[test]
fn field_binding_tensor_rebind_writes_through_444() {
    // A tensor-field binding is a live alias: whole-binding assignment
    // writes the FIELD (matching element writes), never silently rebinds.
    let v = run("model G { !buf: Tensor[i64, [4]]\n\
                 fn fill!(self, v: i64) -> nil { let !b = self.buf\n\
                     b = forge.ones[i64, [4]] .* v  nil } }\n\
                 fn main() -> bool { let !g = G { buf: forge.zeros[i64, [4]] }\n\
                     g.fill!(7)  g.buf[0] == 7 }");
    assert!(matches!(v, Value::Bool(true)), "rebind must reach the field, got {:?}", v);
}

#[test]
fn field_binding_compound_assign_writes_through_444() {
    // Compound ops through the alias read the field's current value and
    // write the result back to the field.
    let v = run("model C { !t: Tensor[i64, [2]]\n\
                 fn bump!(self) -> nil { let !b = self.t  b += forge.ones[i64, [2]]  nil } }\n\
                 fn main() -> bool { let !c = C { t: forge.zeros[i64, [2]] }\n\
                     c.bump!()  c.bump!()  c.t[1] == 2 }");
    assert!(matches!(v, Value::Bool(true)), "two bumps must reach the field, got {:?}", v);
}

#[test]
fn model_load_errors_394() {
    let e = run_err("model L[D] { w: Tensor[f32,[D]] }\nfn main() -> nil { let l = L[D=4].load(\"/tmp/x\")  nil }");
    assert!(e.contains("#394") && e.contains("serialization"), "got: {}", e);
    // The empty/positional bracket forms parse as Index (not BracketArgs) and
    // used to slip past the guard to a silent opaque — they must also be loud.
    let empty = run_err("model L { w: Tensor[f32,[2]] }\nfn main() -> nil { let l = L[].load(\"/tmp/x\")  nil }");
    assert!(empty.contains("#394") && empty.contains("serialization"),
            "empty-bracket load must error, got: {}", empty);
}

#[test]
fn allreduce_method_form_errors_396() {
    // `allreduce.sum(y)` must not silently desugar to `sum(allreduce, y)` (→ 0.0).
    let e = run_err("fn main() -> nil { let !y = forge.zeros[f32,[3]]  y[0] = 1.0  let r = allreduce.sum(y, axis=0)  nil }");
    assert!(e.contains("#396") && e.contains("collective"), "got: {}", e);
}

// --- tensor .split (SPEC §6.4, #397 built) ---------------------------------

#[test]
fn tensor_split_axis_last() {
    // Split a 2x6 tensor into 3 along axis=-1; check a piece's values.
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> f32 {
            let !t = forge.zeros[f32, [2, 6]]
            for i in 0..6 { t[0, i] = (i as f32)  t[1, i] = ((10 + i) as f32) }
            let (a, b, c) = t.split[3, axis=-1]
            # a=[[0,1],[10,11]] b=[[2,3],[12,13]] c=[[4,5],[14,15]]
            a[1,0] + b[0,1] + c[1,1]   # 10 + 3 + 15 = 28
        }
    "#);
    match v {
        Value::Float(f) => assert!((f - 28.0).abs() < 1e-6, "got {}", f),
        other => panic!("expected float, got {:?}", other),
    }
}

#[test]
fn tensor_split_non_divisible_errors() {
    let e = run_err("fn main() -> nil { let t = forge.zeros[f32,[2,6]]  let (a,b,c,d) = t.split[4, axis=-1]  nil }");
    assert!(e.contains("split") && e.contains("divisible"), "got: {}", e);
}

#[test]
fn tensor_split_bare_index_form() {
    // `t.split[n]` with no `axis=` parses as an Index (not BracketArgs), so it
    // must still dispatch to the split path — otherwise the pieces are opaque
    // and the destructure reads silent nils. axis defaults to -1.
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> f32 {
            let !t = forge.zeros[f32, [8]]
            for i in 0..8 { t[i] = (i as f32) }
            let (a, b) = t.split[2]      # a=[0,1,2,3] b=[4,5,6,7]
            a[3] + b[0]                  # 3 + 4 = 7
        }
    "#);
    match v {
        Value::Float(f) => assert!((f - 7.0).abs() < 1e-6, "got {}", f),
        other => panic!("expected float, got {:?}", other),
    }
}

// --- #393: `x @ pat` bind patterns in match --------------------------------

#[test]
fn match_bind_pattern_393() {
    // `y @ 1` matches when the value is 1 AND binds `y` to it.
    let hit = run("fn f(x: i64) -> i64 { match x { y @ 1 => y + 100, _ => 99 } }\nfn main() -> i64 { f(1) }");
    assert_eq!(as_int(&hit), 101);
    // A non-matching value falls through to the catch-all.
    let miss = run("fn f(x: i64) -> i64 { match x { y @ 1 => y + 100, _ => 99 } }\nfn main() -> i64 { f(7) }");
    assert_eq!(as_int(&miss), 99);
}

// --- #393: `..` rest patterns in tuples (match + let-destructure) ----------

#[test]
fn tuple_rest_pattern_matches_and_binds() {
    // `(a, ..)` binds the head and absorbs the tail — previously it silently
    // failed to match (arity 2 vs 3) and took the `_` arm, returning 0.
    let head = run("fn main() -> i64 { let p = (1, 2, 3)  match p { (a, ..) => a, _ => 0 } }");
    assert_eq!(as_int(&head), 1);

    // Head + tail: the rest absorbs the middle.
    let ht = run("fn main() -> i64 { let p = (10, 20, 30, 40)  match p { (a, .., z) => a + z, _ => 0 } }");
    assert_eq!(as_int(&ht), 50);

    // `let (a, ..) = tuple` destructure binds only the fixed head.
    let destr = run("fn main() -> i64 { let (a, ..) = (7, 8, 9)  a }");
    assert_eq!(as_int(&destr), 7);

    // Standalone `..` is still a catch-all (matches anything).
    let catch = run("fn main() -> i64 { let k = 42  match k { 1 => 10, .. => 999 } }");
    assert_eq!(as_int(&catch), 999);

    // A too-short tuple does NOT match a head+tail rest → falls through. `(1, 2)`
    // has 2 elements but `(a, b, .., z)` needs at least 3.
    let short = run("fn main() -> i64 { match (1, 2) { (a, b, .., z) => a + z, _ => -1 } }");
    assert_eq!(as_int(&short), -1);
}

// --- #399: KV `<-` append capacity enforcement (Spec §3.6 panic) -----------

#[test]
fn kv_append_past_capacity_panics() {
    // Unannotated `let !c = forge.kv[...](capacity = N)` — the common form that
    // previously went untracked and silently overflowed. Appending N+1 frames
    // must now panic (Spec §3.6).
    let over = run_err(
        "fn main() -> i64 {\n\
         \x20   let !c = forge.kv[f32, [1, ~, 4]](capacity = 2)\n\
         \x20   let a = forge.zeros[f32, [1, 1, 4]]\n\
         \x20   c <- a  c <- a  c <- a\n\
         \x20   0\n\
         }");
    assert!(over.contains("capacity") && over.contains("2"),
            "over-capacity append should panic, got: {}", over);
}

#[test]
fn kv_append_uses_declared_stream_axis() {
    // Without a type annotation the append must still concatenate along the `~`
    // axis (axis 1 here), not a shape-differ guess. Two [1,1,4] frames → [1,2,4],
    // so sum over the whole cache is 2 * the single set element.
    let v = run(
        "fn main() -> i64 {\n\
         \x20   let !c = forge.kv[f32, [1, ~, 4]](capacity = 4)\n\
         \x20   let !a = forge.zeros[f32, [1, 1, 4]]\n\
         \x20   a[0, 0, 0] = 5.0\n\
         \x20   c <- a  c <- a\n\
         \x20   sum(c) as i64\n\
         }");
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 10);
}

// --- #443: index expressions must be evaluated before the target is borrowed ---
//
// An indexed element write whose target is a model-field alias (`Value::FieldRef`)
// used to take `borrow_mut()` on the struct's fields and *then* evaluate the index
// expression. Any index that read the same struct re-entered the interpreter, whose
// member-access path borrows that same `RefCell` — a hard panic that aborted the
// whole `dmc test` process mid-suite rather than reporting a failure. The shape
// matrix below is the one from the issue; each case is a separate test so a
// regression shows up as one failing case, not a truncated run.

#[test]
fn field_alias_write_with_self_read_in_index_443() {
    // Shape 1: `let !c = self.cells` then `c[self.table[0]] = 1`. Was: panic.
    let v = run(r#"
model Box {
    !table: Tensor[i64, [4]]
    !cells: Tensor[i64, [8]]
    fn go!(self) -> nil {
        let !c = self.cells
        c[self.table[0]] = 1
        nil
    }
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    let !b = Box { table: vault.zeros[i64, [4]], cells: vault.zeros[i64, [8]] }
    b.table[0] = 3
    b.go!()
    b.cells[3]
}
"#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 1);
}

#[test]
fn field_alias_write_with_self_read_in_value_443() {
    // Shape 3: `self` in value position only. Always worked — `rval` is
    // evaluated before the arm is entered. Guards the pre-eval order.
    let v = run(r#"
model Box {
    !table: Tensor[i64, [4]]
    !cells: Tensor[i64, [8]]
    fn go!(self) -> nil {
        let !c = self.cells
        c[0] = self.table[0] + 7
        nil
    }
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    let !b = Box { table: vault.zeros[i64, [4]], cells: vault.zeros[i64, [8]] }
    b.table[0] = 2
    b.go!()
    b.cells[0]
}
"#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 9);
}

#[test]
fn field_alias_write_with_method_call_in_index_443() {
    // Shape 5: a method call in index position re-enters the interpreter one
    // frame deeper before reading `self`. Was: panic.
    let v = run(r#"
model Box {
    !table: Tensor[i64, [4]]
    !cells: Tensor[i64, [8]]
    fn idx(self) -> i64 { self.table[0] + 1 }
    fn go!(self) -> nil {
        let !c = self.cells
        c[self.idx()] = 1
        nil
    }
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    let !b = Box { table: vault.zeros[i64, [4]], cells: vault.zeros[i64, [8]] }
    b.table[0] = 4
    b.go!()
    b.cells[5]
}
"#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 1);
}

#[test]
fn field_alias_read_with_self_read_in_index_443() {
    // Shape 6: read-only indexing through an alias takes no mutable borrow.
    let v = run(r#"
model Box {
    !table: Tensor[i64, [4]]
    !cells: Tensor[i64, [8]]
    fn go(self) -> i64 {
        let c = self.cells
        c[self.table[0]]
    }
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    let !b = Box { table: vault.zeros[i64, [4]], cells: vault.zeros[i64, [8]] }
    b.table[0] = 3
    b.cells[3] = 11
    b.go()
}
"#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 11);
}

#[test]
fn field_alias_write_indexed_by_same_field_443() {
    // Shape 7: the index reads the *same* field being written. The index is
    // resolved from the pre-write contents, then the store lands.
    let v = run(r#"
model Box {
    !cells: Tensor[i64, [8]]
    fn go!(self) -> nil {
        let !c = self.cells
        c[self.cells[1]] = 1
        nil
    }
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    let !b = Box { cells: vault.zeros[i64, [8]] }
    b.cells[1] = 6
    b.go!()
    b.cells[6]
}
"#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 1);
}

#[test]
fn local_tensor_write_with_self_read_in_index_443() {
    // Shape 8: a plain local target holds no borrow — always worked, kept as
    // the control for the `Value::Tensor` arm now that both share a store path.
    let v = run(r#"
model Box {
    !table: Tensor[i64, [4]]
    fn go(self) -> i64 {
        let !t = forge.zeros[i64, [8]]
        t[self.table[0]] = 5
        t[3]
    }
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    let !b = Box { table: vault.zeros[i64, [4]] }
    b.table[0] = 3
    b.go()
}
"#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 5);
}

#[test]
fn struct_field_write_with_self_read_in_index_443() {
    // The `m.field[i] = v` arm has the same shape as the alias arm: it borrows
    // the struct's fields, so an index that reads `m` must be resolved first.
    let v = run(r#"
model Box {
    !table: Tensor[i64, [4]]
    !cells: Tensor[i64, [8]]
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    let !b = Box { table: vault.zeros[i64, [4]], cells: vault.zeros[i64, [8]] }
    b.table[0] = 2
    b.cells[b.table[0]] = 4
    b.cells[2]
}
"#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 4);
}

#[test]
fn table_driven_register_reset_443() {
    // The form that found the bug: a table-driven loop reading both the index
    // and the value straight off `self` inside the write.
    let v = run(r#"
model Device {
    !reg_offset: Tensor[i64, [3]]
    !reg_reset: Tensor[i64, [3]]
    !regs: Tensor[i64, [2, 8]]
    fn reset_device!(self, dev: i64) -> nil {
        let !regs = self.regs
        for k in 0..3 {
            regs[dev, self.reg_offset[k] / 4] = self.reg_reset[k]
        }
        nil
    }
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    let !d = Device {
        reg_offset: [0, 8, 20],
        reg_reset: [7, 8, 9],
        regs: vault.zeros[i64, [2, 8]],
    }
    d.reset_device!(1)
    d.regs[1, 0] * 100 + d.regs[1, 2] * 10 + d.regs[1, 5] + d.regs[0, 0]
}
"#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 789);
}

#[test]
fn field_alias_slice_write_with_self_read_in_bounds_443() {
    // The hazard is in every index form, not just scalars: a slice bound that
    // reads `self` runs through the same pre-evaluation path.
    let v = run(r#"
model Box {
    !table: Tensor[i64, [4]]
    !cells: Tensor[i64, [8]]
    fn go!(self) -> nil {
        let !c = self.cells
        c[self.table[0]..self.table[1]] = 1
        nil
    }
}
fn main() -> i64 {
    let !b = Box { table: vault.zeros[i64, [4]], cells: vault.zeros[i64, [8]] }
    b.table[0] = 2
    b.table[1] = 5
    b.go!()
    sum(b.cells) as i64
}
"#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 3);

// ── #452: lists are copy-on-write, and still values ──────────────────────────
//
// `Value::List` holds an `Rc<Vec<Value>>` so that `xs = list_push(xs, v)` can
// append in place instead of copying the whole backing vector on every call.
// The sharing that buys the speedup is exactly what would break the language's
// value semantics if a write ever landed on a buffer someone else can see, so
// each mutating builtin gets a test that binds a second name to the list first
// and asserts the second name never moves.

#[test]
fn list_push_does_not_mutate_an_alias_452() {
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> i64 {
            let !xs = list_push(list_push(list(), 1), 2)
            let ys = xs
            xs = list_push(xs, 3)
            xs = list_push(xs, 4)
            list_len(ys) * 100 + list_len(xs)
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 204, "alias saw the pushes");
}

#[test]
fn list_set_does_not_mutate_an_alias_452() {
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> i64 {
            let !xs = list_push(list_push(list(), 1), 2)
            let ys = xs
            xs = list_set(xs, 0, 99)
            list_get(ys, 0) * 100 + list_get(xs, 0)
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 199, "alias saw the element write");
}

#[test]
fn list_pop_does_not_mutate_an_alias_452() {
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> i64 {
            let xs = list_push(list_push(list(), 1), 2)
            let ys = xs
            let (rest, last) = list_pop(xs)
            list_len(ys) * 100 + list_len(rest) * 10 + last
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 212, "alias saw the pop");
}

#[test]
fn list_rev_and_sort_do_not_mutate_an_alias_452() {
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> i64 {
            let xs = list_push(list_push(list_push(list(), 3), 1), 2)
            let ys = xs
            let r = list_rev(xs)
            let s = list_sort(xs)
            list_get(ys, 0) * 100 + list_get(r, 0) * 10 + list_get(s, 0)
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 321, "in-place reverse/sort leaked to the source list");
}

#[test]
fn list_concat_with_itself_keeps_both_sides_452() {
    // Same buffer on both sides of the write: the copy has to happen before the
    // extend, or the source grows while it is being read.
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> i64 {
            let !xs = list_push(list_push(list(), 1), 2)
            let ys = xs
            xs = list_concat(xs, xs)
            list_len(xs) * 100 + list_len(ys) * 10 + list_get(xs, 3)
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 422);
}

#[test]
fn list_alias_survives_a_reassigning_loop_452() {
    // The build-a-list loop that motivated #452, with a live alias taken
    // mid-flight: the in-place append must not be visible through `snapshot`.
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> i64 {
            let !xs = list()
            let !i = 0
            let !snapshot = list()
            while i < 50 {
                xs = list_push(xs, i)
                if i == 9 { snapshot = xs }
                i = i + 1
            }
            list_len(xs) * 1000 + list_len(snapshot)
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 50010);
}

#[test]
fn list_alias_through_a_fn_argument_452() {
    // A list passed to a user fn is a value there too — the callee's pushes
    // must not reach the caller's binding.
    let v = run(r#"
        fn grow(l: list) -> i64 {
            let !inner = l
            inner = list_push(inner, 99)
            list_len(inner)
        }
        fn main() -> i64 {
            let xs = list_push(list_push(list(), 1), 2)
            let n = grow(xs)
            n * 100 + list_len(xs)
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 302, "callee's push reached the caller's list");
}

#[test]
fn list_build_is_not_quadratic_452() {
    // Complexity guard for the #452 fix. Twenty thousand appends is a few
    // milliseconds when `list_push` writes into a uniquely owned buffer and
    // minutes when it deep-copies the backing vector on every call, so the
    // generous bound below still separates linear from quadratic by orders of
    // magnitude — it fails on a regression without being timing-flaky.
    let start = std::time::Instant::now();
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> i64 {
            let !xs = list()
            let !i = 0
            while i < 20000 {
                xs = list_push(xs, i)
                i = i + 1
            }
            list_len(xs)
        }
    "#);
    let elapsed = start.elapsed();
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 20000);
    assert!(elapsed.as_secs() < 20, "20k list_push calls took {:?} — copy-on-write append regressed to a per-call copy", elapsed);
}

#[test]
fn list_reassignment_reading_the_target_twice_452() {
    // The in-place path releases the target binding's handle on the buffer, so
    // it must never fire when something *else* in the statement still has to
    // read that binding. Here the builtin call is only a sub-expression of the
    // right-hand side and `xs` is read again in both branches.
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> i64 {
            let !xs = list_push(list_push(list_push(list(), 1), 2), 3)
            xs = if list_len(xs) > 2 { list_slice(xs, 0, 2) } else { xs }
            list_len(xs) * 10 + list_get(xs, 1)
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 22);
}

#[test]
fn list_reassignment_from_a_short_circuit_reading_the_target_452() {
    // Same hazard through `&&`: the left operand's builtin call must not
    // release `xs` out from under the right operand, nor from under the branch.
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> i64 {
            let !xs = list_push(list_push(list(), 7), 8)
            xs = if list_len(xs) > 1 && list_get(xs, 1) == 8 { list_push(xs, 9) } else { xs }
            list_len(xs) * 10 + list_get(xs, 2)
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 39);
}

#[test]
fn list_reassignment_with_the_target_read_in_a_later_arg_452() {
    // `xs` appears twice in the same call. The release happens only after every
    // argument is evaluated, so the second read still sees the original list.
    let v = run(r#"
        fn main() -> i64 {
            let !xs = list_push(list_push(list(), 5), 6)
            xs = list_push(xs, list_len(xs))
            list_len(xs) * 10 + list_get(xs, 2)
        }
    "#);
    assert_eq!(as_int(&v), 32);
}

//! Phase 4 JIT backend (issue #15) — Cranelift lowering from the typed AST.
//!
//! Direct lowering from the typed AST to Cranelift IR. No intermediate dmc-IR.
//!
//! NOTE ON SCOPE. This started as "slice 1: scalars + control flow" and has
//! grown well past it — it now lowers a large tensor and reverse-mode `@grad`
//! surface. The lowerable set is *not* enumerated here on purpose: it moves, and
//! a hand-maintained list rots (this doc claimed "no tensors, no match, no for"
//! long after all three lowered — the #408 stale-doc finding). For the authoritative,
//! reproducible map run `python3 tools/jit_surface.py`; for the design rationale
//! see `docs/design/DERIVED_SUITE.md §4`. Sketch as of that enumeration:
//!
//!   - scalars: i32/i64/f32/f64/bool/nil — arithmetic, comparison, logical,
//!     bitwise, casts, unary `-`/`!`, if/else + match as expressions, while/for
//!     with break/continue, direct calls (recursion + forward refs), blocks.
//!   - tensors (f32/i32/bf16 construct; `bool` zero-fill does NOT — 32-bit
//!     zero-fill): elementwise dotted ops, broadcast, `@` (2D + batched),
//!     transpose, reductions (sum/mean/max/min/variance, sum_along/mean_along,
//!     argmax/argmin), activations, softmax/rms_norm/layer_norm.
//!   - `@grad` reverse mode for **concrete-shape** fns with a scalar f32 loss.
//!     A *shape-generic* `@grad fn[N]` is NOT lowered (monomorphizing the backward
//!     pass is unimplemented) — it errors with a `dmc run` hint.
//!
//! Anything outside the lowered set (models, most directives, ports, strings in
//! some positions, dynamic/indirect calls, `vault.load_npz`) gets a precise
//! diagnostic pointing at the offending span and a hint to use `dmc run`.
//! Builtins are emitted as runtime symbols (e.g. print_i64/print_f64/…).

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::mem;

use cranelift::codegen::ir::{AbiParam, InstBuilder, Signature, StackSlotData, StackSlotKind, UserFuncName};
use cranelift::codegen::isa::CallConv;
use cranelift::codegen::{settings, settings::Configurable, Context};
use cranelift::frontend::{FunctionBuilder, FunctionBuilderContext, Variable};
use cranelift::prelude::{types as cl, Block, IntCC, FloatCC, Type as ClType, Value};
use cranelift_jit::{JITBuilder, JITModule};
use cranelift_module::{FuncId, Linkage, Module};

use crate::ast::*;
use crate::lexer::Span;

// ─── JIT compile-timing diagnostic (env-gated, DMC_JIT_TIMING) ─────────────────
// Accumulates nanoseconds spent inside cranelift `define_function` (per-fn
// codegen) across the whole compile, so compile_program can report the split
// between dmc-side IR lowering and cranelift codegen. Zero overhead unless
// DMC_JIT_TIMING is set. Established (#325) that compile is ~25 ms on the full
// Qwen3-4B decode — the per-run cost is execution, not compilation.
static JIT_CODEGEN_NS: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0);

// ─── Diagnostics ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct JitError {
    pub msg: String,
    pub line: usize,
    pub col: usize,
}

impl std::fmt::Display for JitError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "jit error at {}:{}: {}", self.line, self.col, self.msg)
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for JitError {}

fn err<T>(span: &Span, msg: impl Into<String>) -> Result<T, JitError> {
    Err(JitError { msg: msg.into(), line: span.line, col: span.col })
}

fn unsupported<T>(span: &Span, what: &str) -> Result<T, JitError> {
    err(span, format!(
        "jit slice 1 does not support {}; use `dmc run` for full semantics",
        what,
    ))
}

// ─── Scalar type bridge ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum ScalarKind {
    I32, I64, F32, F64, Bool, Nil,
    /// A maybe-nil i64 — the result of `map_get`, which is dynamically typed
    /// (`Unknown`) and returns `nil` on a missing key in the interpreter (#300.4).
    /// Packed into an I128: high bit = present flag, low 64 bits = the value.
    /// `nil` is all-zero (present=0). Built in IR from map_contains + map_get;
    /// `print` / `== nil` branch on the present bit, and coercing to a plain i64
    /// traps on nil (matching the interpreter's nil-in-arithmetic error).
    OptI64,
}

/// Bit 64 of the OptI64 I128 packing — set iff the map held the key.
const OPT_PRESENT_BIT: i64 = 64;

impl ScalarKind {
    fn cl(self) -> ClType {
        match self {
            ScalarKind::I32  => cl::I32,
            ScalarKind::I64  => cl::I64,
            ScalarKind::F32  => cl::F32,
            ScalarKind::F64  => cl::F64,
            ScalarKind::Bool => cl::I8,
            ScalarKind::Nil  => cl::I8,
            ScalarKind::OptI64 => cl::I128,
        }
    }

    fn is_int(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, ScalarKind::I32 | ScalarKind::I64)
    }
    fn is_float(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, ScalarKind::F32 | ScalarKind::F64)
    }
    fn is_bool(self) -> bool { matches!(self, ScalarKind::Bool) }
    fn bits(self) -> u8 {
        match self {
            ScalarKind::I32 | ScalarKind::F32 => 32,
            ScalarKind::I64 | ScalarKind::F64 => 64,
            ScalarKind::Bool | ScalarKind::Nil => 8,
            ScalarKind::OptI64 => 128,
        }
    }

    fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            ScalarKind::I32 => "i32",
            ScalarKind::I64 => "i64",
            ScalarKind::F32 => "f32",
            ScalarKind::F64 => "f64",
            ScalarKind::Bool => "bool",
            ScalarKind::Nil => "nil",
            ScalarKind::OptI64 => "i64?",
        }
    }
}

/// Scalar integer types the JIT has no dedicated `ScalarKind` for, but which a
/// `... as T` cast can still target (the result is an i64-backed scalar holding
/// the wrapped/narrowed value, exactly as the interpreter represents them).
fn scalar_int_is_narrow(s: &ScalarType) -> bool {
    matches!(s,
        ScalarType::I8 | ScalarType::I16 | ScalarType::U8 | ScalarType::U16
        | ScalarType::U32 | ScalarType::U64 | ScalarType::Int4 | ScalarType::Int8)
}

/// Diagnostic shared by the three `@cast(int){…}` rejection sites (statement,
/// tail-position, and expression directive blocks). See issue #374.
const INT_CAST_BLOCK_UNSUPPORTED: &str =
    "integer `@cast(...)` block: the JIT cannot truncate a tensor to an integer \
     type (the interpreter truncates toward zero and retags Int), so it would \
     silently compute a different result; only value-preserving float `@cast` \
     (bf16/f16/tf32/f32/f64) is supported here";

/// Name of an *integer* target type in a `@cast(<ty>) { … }` directive.
/// The interpreter truncates such tensor casts toward zero and retags
/// DType::Int (interp.rs `apply_cast_by_name`, #125). Mirrors interp's
/// `is_int_type_name`.
fn is_int_cast_type_name(name: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(name,
        "i8" | "i16" | "i32" | "i64" |
        "u8" | "u16" | "u32" | "u64" |
        "int4" | "int8")
}

/// True when a `@cast(<ty>) { … }` directive block names an integer target.
/// The JIT's `@cast`/`@deterministic` no-op path (the #179 exotic-float
/// convention) is only sound for value-preserving retags (bf16/f16/tf32/f32/
/// f64). Integer targets require the elementwise truncation the interpreter
/// performs, which the JIT can't yet emit — so lowering them as a no-op
/// silently diverges from the interpreter (issue #374). Detect them so the
/// caller can reject loudly (`unsupported`) instead of computing a different
/// numeric answer than `dmc run`.
fn cast_directive_is_int_target(directives: &[Directive]) -> bool {
    directives.iter()
        .filter(|d| d.name == "cast")
        .filter_map(|d| d.args.first())
        .any(|arg| matches!(arg,
            DArg::Positional(Expr::Ident(name, _)) if is_int_cast_type_name(name)))
}

fn scalar_from_ast(ty: &Type) -> Result<ScalarKind, JitError> {
    let span = type_span(ty);
    match ty {
        Type::Scalar(s, _) => match s {
            ScalarType::I32  => Ok(ScalarKind::I32),
            ScalarType::I64  => Ok(ScalarKind::I64),
            ScalarType::F32  => Ok(ScalarKind::F32),
            ScalarType::F64  => Ok(ScalarKind::F64),
            ScalarType::Bool => Ok(ScalarKind::Bool),
            ScalarType::Nil  => Ok(ScalarKind::Nil),
            other => err(&span, format!(
                "scalar type `{:?}` not yet supported by the JIT (slice 1)", other,
            )),
        },
        _ => err(&span, "JIT slice 1 accepts only scalar types in fn signatures"),
    }
}

// ─── Tensor types ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct TensorTy {
    elem: ScalarKind,
    /// Static shape, fully known at compile time (no `~`, no symbolic dims
    /// yet in slice 2 — shape params live in a later slice).
    shape: Vec<i64>,
}

impl TensorTy {
    fn rank(&self) -> usize { self.shape.len() }
    fn nelems(&self) -> i64 {
        self.shape.iter().try_fold(1i64, |acc, &d| acc.checked_mul(d))
            .expect("tensor element count overflows i64 (shape too large)")
    }
    fn nbytes(&self) -> i64 { self.nelems() * (self.elem.bits() as i64 / 8) }
    fn elem_bytes(&self) -> i64 { self.elem.bits() as i64 / 8 }

    fn render(&self) -> String {
        let s: Vec<String> = self.shape.iter().map(|d| d.to_string()).collect();
        format!("Tensor[{}, [{}]]", self.elem.name(), s.join(", "))
    }
}

/// A KV streaming cache: `KV[f32, [.., ~, ..]]`. Lowered to an i64 pointer to a
/// forge region laid out as a 16-byte header followed by the data:
///
/// ```text
///   [ len: i64 @ 0 ][ cap: i64 @ 8 ][ data: f32 * (cap * frame_elems) @ 16 ]
/// ```
///
/// `data` is row-major for the full shape with the streaming axis sized to
/// `cap`; `len` (frames written so far) and `cap` travel with the value at
/// runtime, so a `KV` survives across function calls and mutation through a
/// `!` parameter. Capacity is also recorded at compile time (`cap`) when the
/// value comes from a `forge.kv` constructor in scope, which lets the streaming
/// axis be read back as a static-shape tensor; for a bare `KV` parameter the
/// compile-time capacity is unknown and only the runtime header is consulted.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct KvTy {
    elem: ScalarKind,
    /// All dimensions EXCEPT the streaming axis, in declaration order.
    dims: Vec<i64>,
    /// Position of the streaming `~` axis within the full shape.
    stream_axis: usize,
    /// Compile-time capacity, if known (constructor in scope). `None` for a
    /// `KV` function parameter — its capacity lives only in the runtime header.
    cap: Option<i64>,
}

impl KvTy {
    fn rank(&self) -> usize { self.dims.len() + 1 }
    /// Elements per streaming frame = product of all non-streaming dims.
    fn frame_elems(&self) -> i64 { self.dims.iter().product() }
    /// Product of dims before the streaming axis (the strided "rows").
    fn outer(&self) -> i64 { self.dims[..self.stream_axis].iter().product() }
    /// Product of dims after the streaming axis (contiguous block per frame).
    fn inner(&self) -> i64 { self.dims[self.stream_axis..].iter().product() }
    /// Full non-streaming dim at full-shape position `axis` (axis != stream_axis).
    fn dim_at(&self, axis: usize) -> i64 {
        if axis < self.stream_axis { self.dims[axis] } else { self.dims[axis - 1] }
    }
    /// Static tensor view of the whole buffer — valid only when capacity is
    /// known at compile time. Exact iff the stream is filled (`len == cap`).
    fn as_full_tensor(&self) -> Option<TensorTy> {
        self.cap.map(|c| {
            let mut shape = self.dims.clone();
            shape.insert(self.stream_axis, c);
            TensorTy { elem: self.elem, shape }
        })
    }
    fn render(&self) -> String {
        let mut shape: Vec<String> = self.dims.iter().map(|d| d.to_string()).collect();
        shape.insert(self.stream_axis, "~".to_string());
        format!("KV[{}, [{}]]", self.elem.name(), shape.join(", "))
    }
}

/// Handle to an open counted loop (`loop_begin`/`loop_end`). `iv` is the
/// induction variable (valid inside the body); the rest are the CFG blocks.
struct LoopCtx {
    iv: Value,
    hdr: Block,
    body: Block,
    exit: Block,
}

/// A contiguous f32 tensor whose shape mixes static and runtime extents.
/// Value layout (pointer): `[ext_0: i64]..[ext_{k-1}: i64][ data: f32.. ]`,
/// one i64 slot per dynamic axis (in axis order), then a row-major contiguous
/// data region over the fully-resolved shape. See `TyKind::DynTensor`.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct DynTensorTy {
    elem: ScalarKind,
    /// `Some(n)` = static extent; `None` = dynamic (extent in the header).
    dims: Vec<Option<i64>>,
}

impl DynTensorTy {
    fn rank(&self) -> usize { self.dims.len() }
    /// Number of dynamic axes = i64 header slots preceding the data.
    fn n_dyn(&self) -> usize { self.dims.iter().filter(|d| d.is_none()).count() }
    /// Header slot index (0-based) for dynamic axis `axis`; None if static.
    fn slot_of(&self, axis: usize) -> Option<usize> {
        if self.dims.get(axis).copied().flatten().is_some() { return None; }
        Some(self.dims[..axis].iter().filter(|d| d.is_none()).count())
    }
    fn render(&self) -> String {
        let s: Vec<String> = self.dims.iter()
            .map(|d| d.map(|n| n.to_string()).unwrap_or_else(|| "?".into()))
            .collect();
        format!("Tensor[{}, [{}]] (dyn)", self.elem.name(), s.join(", "))
    }
}

/// A packed ternary weight matrix W: [K, N] trit.
/// Runtime value is an i64 pointer to a flat forge region:
///   [ pos_bits: u64 * n_words * N ][ neg_bits: u64 * n_words * N ]
/// where n_words = ceil(K / 64).  Column `n` pos-words start at byte
/// offset `n * n_words * 8`; neg-words start at `(N + n) * n_words * 8`
/// (i.e. halfway through the buffer).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct TritTensorTy {
    k: i64,   // inner (activation) dimension
    n: i64,   // output (column) dimension
}

impl TritTensorTy {
    fn n_words(&self) -> i64 { (self.k + 63) / 64 }
    fn nbytes(&self) -> i64 { 2 * self.n_words() * self.n * 8 }
    fn render(&self) -> String {
        format!("TritTensor[{}, {}]", self.k, self.n)
    }
}

/// A bf16-storage weight tensor (#324). Runtime value is an i64 pointer to a
/// flat, row-major region of `nelems` **2-byte** bf16 values (the raw on-disk
/// bytes — NOT widened to f32 at load). It exists only as a scoped type so the
/// big Linear/lm-head weights stay at half the footprint and feed a bf16-direct
/// matmul kernel that upconverts in-register (`f32::from_bits((w as u32) << 16)`,
/// bit-identical to the old load-time widen). Any non-matmul use upconverts to a
/// regular f32 `TyKind::Tensor` first (see `bf16_upconvert`).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Bf16TensorTy {
    shape: Vec<i64>,
}

impl Bf16TensorTy {
    fn nelems(&self) -> i64 {
        self.shape.iter().try_fold(1i64, |acc, &d| acc.checked_mul(d))
            .expect("bf16 tensor element count overflows i64 (shape too large)")
    }
    fn nbytes(&self) -> i64 { self.nelems() * 2 }
    fn render(&self) -> String {
        let s: Vec<String> = self.shape.iter().map(|d| d.to_string()).collect();
        format!("Bf16Tensor[{}]", s.join(", "))
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum TyKind {
    Scalar(ScalarKind),
    Tensor(TensorTy),
    /// A KV streaming cache (`forge.kv` / `KV[..]` parameter). i64 header pointer.
    KV(KvTy),
    /// A contiguous f32 tensor with one or more *runtime* axis extents — the
    /// foundation for KV reads of unknown streaming length (issue #176 part 2).
    /// Self-describing: the i64 value points at `[ext: i64; n_dyn][data: f32..]`,
    /// where the dynamic extents are stored in axis order ahead of a row-major
    /// contiguous data region. `DynTensorTy.dims` records which axes are static
    /// (`Some(n)`) vs dynamic (`None`, extent read from the header).
    DynTensor(DynTensorTy),
    /// A model instance (i64 pointer to a forge-allocated flat struct).
    /// The string names the model type so field accesses can resolve offsets.
    /// #267: the `Vec<i64>` carries the concrete type-arg values of a
    /// parameterized model (`Bar[4]` → `[4]`), in declaration order, so a field
    /// whose shape uses those params (`x: Tensor[f32,[N]]`) can be re-resolved
    /// at access time. Empty for bare models / unparameterized instantiations.
    Model(String, Vec<i64>),
    /// i64 pointer to forge-allocated [len: i64, data: u8*]
    Str,
    /// i64 raw pointer to Box<HashMap<String, i64>> (process-lifetime allocation)
    Map,
    /// A fixed-size array of KV streaming caches: `[KV[T, [.., ~, ..]]; N]`.
    /// Represented as a forge-allocated region of `N` i64 KV-header pointers
    /// stored contiguously (8 bytes each). The i64 JIT value is a pointer to
    /// that region. `KvArray` is read-only in the type sense — individual
    /// elements are KV pointers and can be appended to via `<-`.
    KvArray(KvTy, i64),
    /// A first-class function pointer / non-capturing closure.
    /// `fn(param_tys) -> ret_ty`. JIT value is i64 (code pointer).
    /// Created by `Expr::FnLit` or when a named function is used as a value.
    Fn(Vec<TyKind>, Box<TyKind>),
    /// A fixed-size array of model instances: `[ModelName; N]`.
    /// Represented as a forge-allocated region of `N` i64 model-instance pointers
    /// stored contiguously (8 bytes each). The i64 JIT value is a pointer to that
    /// region. Elements are read via index expressions returning `TyKind::Model`.
    /// #267: the trailing `Vec<i64>` carries the element model's concrete
    /// type-arg values (`forge.uninit[Bar[4], [8]]` → `[4]`), propagated to each
    /// `Model` element on read so param-shaped fields resolve.
    ModelArray(String, i64, Vec<i64>),
    /// A packed ternary weight matrix `W: [K, N] trit`.
    /// Runtime i64 points to a forge region:
    ///   [pos_bits: u64 * n_words * N][neg_bits: u64 * n_words * N]
    /// where n_words = ceil(K / 64). Column n pos-words start at byte
    /// offset `n * n_words * 8`; neg-words at `(N + n) * n_words * 8`.
    TritTensor(TritTensorTy),
    /// A bf16-storage weight tensor (#324). Runtime i64 points to a flat
    /// row-major region of 2-byte bf16 values. Feeds a bf16-direct matmul
    /// kernel; upconverts to an f32 `Tensor` for any other use.
    Bf16Tensor(Bf16TensorTy),
    /// #350: a C-like enum value (#336). Backed by the variant's i64 ordinal,
    /// so the JIT value is an `i64` — `Enum` exists only to carry the enum's
    /// name, which lets `match` resolve a bare-variant ident (`Green`) against
    /// the scrutinee's variant set (see `Jit::enums`). Distinct enums never
    /// unify, mirroring the interpreter's tagged `EnumVal`.
    Enum(String),
}

impl TyKind {
    fn render(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            TyKind::Scalar(s) => s.name().to_string(),
            TyKind::Tensor(t) => t.render(),
            TyKind::KV(k) => k.render(),
            TyKind::DynTensor(d) => d.render(),
            TyKind::Model(name, _) => name.clone(),
            TyKind::Str => "str".to_string(),
            TyKind::Map => "Map".to_string(),
            TyKind::KvArray(kv, n) => format!("[{}; {}]", kv.render(), n),
            TyKind::ModelArray(name, n, _) => format!("[{}; {}]", name, n),
            TyKind::TritTensor(tt) => tt.render(),
            TyKind::Bf16Tensor(bt) => bt.render(),
            TyKind::Enum(name) => name.clone(),
            TyKind::Fn(params, ret) => {
                let ps: Vec<String> = params.iter().map(|p| p.render()).collect();
                format!("fn({}) -> {}", ps.join(", "), ret.render())
            }
        }
    }
    fn as_scalar(&self) -> Option<ScalarKind> {
        match self { TyKind::Scalar(s) => Some(*s), _ => None }
    }
    fn as_tensor(&self) -> Option<&TensorTy> {
        match self { TyKind::Tensor(t) => Some(t), _ => None }
    }
    fn as_kv(&self) -> Option<&KvTy> {
        match self { TyKind::KV(k) => Some(k), _ => None }
    }
    fn cl(&self) -> ClType {
        match self {
            TyKind::Scalar(s) => s.cl(),
            TyKind::Tensor(_) => cl::I64,   // tensors are i64 data pointers
            TyKind::KV(_)     => cl::I64,  // KV caches are i64 header pointers
            TyKind::DynTensor(_) => cl::I64, // dyn tensors are i64 header pointers
            TyKind::Model(_, _)  => cl::I64,  // model instances are i64 pointers
            TyKind::Str       => cl::I64,  // strings are i64 forge pointers
            TyKind::Map       => cl::I64,  // maps are i64 raw pointers
            TyKind::KvArray(_, _) => cl::I64, // KV arrays are i64 pointers to pointer arrays
            TyKind::ModelArray(_, _, _) => cl::I64, // model arrays are i64 pointers to pointer arrays
            TyKind::TritTensor(_) => cl::I64, // trit tensors are i64 data pointers
            TyKind::Bf16Tensor(_) => cl::I64, // bf16 tensors are i64 data pointers
            TyKind::Enum(_)   => cl::I64,  // #350: enums are i64 ordinals
            TyKind::Fn(_, _)         => cl::I64, // function pointers are i64 code pointers
        }
    }
    fn is_tensor(&self) -> bool { matches!(self, TyKind::Tensor(_)) }
    fn is_str(&self) -> bool { matches!(self, TyKind::Str) }
    fn is_map(&self) -> bool { matches!(self, TyKind::Map) }
}

/// #350: post-resolve enum-named types. `ty_from_ast` / `lower_ty_for_model`
/// have no view of the enum registry, so an enum-named type (`l: Light`) comes
/// back as `TyKind::Model("Light", [])`. Rewrite any such name that is actually
/// an enum to `TyKind::Enum`, recursing into `fn(...)` parameter and return
/// positions so an enum nested in a function type is caught too. Applied at the
/// type-annotation boundaries (fn signatures, `let`, casts, lambdas, model
/// fields) — never to a value's already-resolved type.
fn enumify(ty: TyKind, enums: &HashMap<String, Vec<String>>) -> TyKind {
    match ty {
        TyKind::Model(name, _) if enums.contains_key(&name) => TyKind::Enum(name),
        TyKind::Fn(params, ret) => TyKind::Fn(
            params.into_iter().map(|p| enumify(p, enums)).collect(),
            Box::new(enumify(*ret, enums)),
        ),
        other => other,
    }
}

/// #350 Part 2b: the tagged-union memory layout of a payload-carrying enum.
/// Slot 0 holds the i64 tag (the variant ordinal); the remaining slots hold
/// payload fields, one slot (8 bytes) per (variant, field) with no sharing
/// (design §4.1). A value is an i64 pointer to a forge region of `n_slots * 8`
/// bytes — the same flat representation as a model instance.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct EnumLayout {
    /// Total 8-byte slots: 1 (tag) + Σ payload field counts.
    n_slots: i64,
    /// Variant name → slot index of its first payload field (tag-only variants
    /// of this enum are absent — they carry no payload, only the tag).
    variant_off: HashMap<String, i64>,
    /// Variant name → its payload field types, in order (scalars in v1).
    variant_tys: HashMap<String, Vec<TyKind>>,
}

/// Lower an AST `Type` to the JIT's TyKind, including tensor support.
/// `env` resolves shape parameters (e.g., `Tensor[f32, [M, K]]`) to their
/// concrete dimensions at the call site. Pass an empty env when no shape
/// parameters are in scope.
fn ty_from_ast(ty: &Type, env: &HashMap<String, i64>) -> Result<TyKind, JitError> {
    match ty {
        Type::Scalar(ScalarType::Str, _) => Ok(TyKind::Str),
        Type::Scalar(_, _) => Ok(TyKind::Scalar(scalar_from_ast(ty)?)),
        Type::Tensor(inner, shape, span) => {
            // Trit element — packed ternary weight; must be exactly 2-D.
            if matches!(inner.as_ref(), Type::Scalar(ScalarType::Trit, _)) {
                let dims: Vec<i64> = shape.elems.iter().map(|d| {
                    resolve_shape_elem(d, env, span)
                }).collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
                if dims.len() != 2 {
                    return err(span, "trit tensors must be 2-D: Tensor[trit, [K, N]]");
                }
                return Ok(TyKind::TritTensor(TritTensorTy { k: dims[0], n: dims[1] }));
            }
            let elem = match inner.as_ref() {
                Type::Scalar(s, _) => match s {
                    ScalarType::F32 => ScalarKind::F32,
                    // bf16/f16/tf32 compute as f32 (#179/#237 no-op convention),
                    // so an annotated `Tensor[bf16, ..]` binding is f32-backed —
                    // matches the constructor path (lower_arena_alloc).
                    ScalarType::Bf16 | ScalarType::F16 | ScalarType::Tf32 => ScalarKind::F32,
                    // #274: integer-element tensors (token ids, index/gather
                    // data). The load/store/offset core is width-generic
                    // (tensor_byte_offset uses elem_bytes; tensor_load_elem loads
                    // at elem.cl()); float-math ops (sum/matmul/…) stay f32-only.
                    ScalarType::I64 | ScalarType::U64 => ScalarKind::I64,
                    ScalarType::I32 | ScalarType::U32 => ScalarKind::I32,
                    other => return err(span, format!(
                        "tensor element type `{:?}` not supported (f32/bf16/i64/i32 only)",
                        other,
                    )),
                },
                _ => return err(span, "tensor element must be a scalar"),
            };
            let mut dims: Vec<i64> = Vec::with_capacity(shape.elems.len());
            for d in &shape.elems {
                let val = resolve_shape_elem(d, env, span)?;
                if val <= 0 {
                    return err(span, format!("tensor dim must be > 0, got {}", val));
                }
                dims.push(val);
            }
            if dims.is_empty() || dims.len() > 4 {
                return err(span, format!(
                    "JIT supports tensor ranks 1..=4, got rank {}", dims.len(),
                ));
            }
            Ok(TyKind::Tensor(TensorTy { elem, shape: dims }))
        }
        Type::KV(inner, shape, span) => {
            let elem = match inner.as_ref() {
                Type::Scalar(ScalarType::F32, _) => ScalarKind::F32,
                _ => return err(span, "KV element type must be f32 (JIT slice surface)"),
            };
            let mut dims: Vec<i64> = Vec::new();
            let mut stream_axis: Option<usize> = None;
            for (i, d) in shape.elems.iter().enumerate() {
                match d {
                    ShapeElem::Streaming(_) => {
                        if stream_axis.is_some() {
                            return err(span, "KV shape may have only one streaming `~` axis");
                        }
                        stream_axis = Some(i);
                    }
                    _ => {
                        let val = resolve_shape_elem(d, env, span)?;
                        if val <= 0 {
                            return err(span, format!("KV dim must be > 0, got {}", val));
                        }
                        dims.push(val);
                    }
                }
            }
            let stream_axis = stream_axis.ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                msg: "KV type must contain a streaming `~` axis".into(),
                line: span.line, col: span.col,
            })?;
            // Capacity is not carried in the parameter type — it lives in the
            // runtime header (see KvTy). `cap: None` marks it compile-time unknown.
            Ok(TyKind::KV(KvTy { elem, dims, stream_axis, cap: None }))
        }
        Type::RawPtr(_, _) => Ok(TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)),
        Type::Named { name, span, .. } if name == "any" => err(span,
            "`any`-typed values are dynamically typed and cannot be JIT-compiled; use `dmc run`"),
        Type::Named { name, .. } if name == "Map" => Ok(TyKind::Map),
        Type::Named { name, args, .. } => Ok(TyKind::Model(name.clone(), type_named_dims(args, env))),
        // `[KV[T, [.., ~, ..]]; N]` — a fixed-size array of KV cache pointers.
        // The element type may be bf16 (quantized weights); map to f32 internally
        // since KV data in the JIT is always f32-typed for compute correctness.
        Type::Array(inner, count_expr, span) => {
            // `[ModelName; N]` -- a fixed-size array of model instance pointers.
            if let Type::Named { name, args, .. } = inner.as_ref() {
                let n = resolve_shape_expr(count_expr, env, span)?;
                if n <= 0 {
                    return err(span, format!("model array size must be > 0, got {}", n));
                }
                return Ok(TyKind::ModelArray(name.clone(), n, type_named_dims(args, env)));
            }
            let kv_ty_raw = ty_from_ast(inner, env).or_else(|_| {
                // Accept bf16 KV by substituting f32 (JIT handles bf16 @cast as no-op).
                if let Type::KV(elem, shape, kspan) = inner.as_ref() {
                    if matches!(elem.as_ref(), Type::Scalar(ScalarType::Bf16, _)
                                             | Type::Scalar(ScalarType::F16, _)) {
                        let f32_elem = Box::new(Type::Scalar(ScalarType::F32, kspan.clone()));
                        return ty_from_ast(&Type::KV(f32_elem, shape.clone(), kspan.clone()), env);
                    }
                }
                err(span, "JIT only supports `[KV[...]; N]` or `[ModelName; N]` fixed-size array types in fn signatures")
            })?;
            let kv = match kv_ty_raw {
                TyKind::KV(k) => k,
                _ => return err(span, "JIT only supports `[KV[...]; N]` or `[ModelName; N]` fixed-size array types in fn signatures"),
            };
            let n = resolve_shape_expr(count_expr, env, span)?;
            if n <= 0 {
                return err(span, format!("KV array size must be > 0, got {}", n));
            }
            Ok(TyKind::KvArray(kv, n))
        }
        // `fn(T1, T2) -> R` — first-class function pointer, represented as i64.
        Type::Fn(param_tys, ret_ty, _) => {
            let params = param_tys.iter()
                .map(|p| ty_from_ast(p, env))
                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
            let ret = ty_from_ast(ret_ty, env)?;
            Ok(TyKind::Fn(params, Box::new(ret)))
        }
        _ => err(&type_span(ty),
            "JIT accepts only scalar and Tensor types in fn signatures"),
    }
}

/// Lower an AST `Type` to `TyKind` for use in model field declarations.
/// All scalars map to their corresponding `ScalarKind`; named types (model
/// references) and other pointer-sized types map to `I64`.
fn lower_ty_for_model(ty: &Type, env: &HashMap<String, i64>, _span: &Span) -> Result<TyKind, JitError> {
    match ty {
        Type::Scalar(s, _) => {
            let sk = match s {
                ScalarType::I32  => ScalarKind::I32,
                ScalarType::I64  => ScalarKind::I64,
                ScalarType::F32  => ScalarKind::F32,
                ScalarType::F64  => ScalarKind::F64,
                ScalarType::Bool => ScalarKind::Bool,
                _ => ScalarKind::I64, // str, nil, etc. → opaque i64 pointer
            };
            Ok(TyKind::Scalar(sk))
        }
        Type::Named { name, span, .. } if name == "any" => err(span,
            "`any`-typed model fields are dynamically typed and cannot be JIT-compiled; use `dmc run`"),
        Type::Named { name, args, .. } => Ok(TyKind::Model(name.clone(), type_named_dims(args, env))),
        Type::Tensor(inner, shape, tspan) => {
            // Map the element type to the nearest representable ScalarKind.
            // The JIT treats @cast(bf16) and @cast(f16) as no-ops (compute in
            // f32); sub-i64 integer types are widened to i32 since that is the
            // smallest integer ScalarKind the JIT supports for tensor indexing.
            let elem = match inner.as_ref() {
                Type::Scalar(s, _) => match s {
                    // Native JIT scalar kinds — exact mapping.
                    ScalarType::F32  => ScalarKind::F32,
                    ScalarType::F64  => ScalarKind::F64,
                    ScalarType::I64  => ScalarKind::I64,
                    ScalarType::U64  => ScalarKind::I64,
                    ScalarType::I32  => ScalarKind::I32,
                    ScalarType::U32  => ScalarKind::I32,
                    // #324: a bf16 model FIELD is a read-only weight stored at
                    // native 2-byte width (Bf16Tensor) — feeds the bf16-direct
                    // matmul kernel, upconverts on any other use. Scoped to
                    // fields here (NOT ty_from_ast) so f32-backed bf16 *activation*
                    // locals (`let !h: Tensor[bf16,..]`) are unaffected.
                    ScalarType::Bf16 => {
                        // Resolve dims; if any is symbolic/dynamic (unbound block
                        // param, wildcard), fall back to an opaque i64 pointer —
                        // the field is re-resolved with concrete params at access
                        // time, exactly like the f32 tensor path below.
                        let mut dims: Vec<i64> = Vec::with_capacity(shape.elems.len());
                        for d in &shape.elems {
                            match resolve_shape_elem(d, env, tspan) {
                                Ok(v) if v > 0 => dims.push(v),
                                _ => return Ok(TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)),
                            }
                        }
                        if dims.is_empty() || dims.len() > 4 {
                            return Ok(TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64));
                        }
                        return Ok(TyKind::Bf16Tensor(Bf16TensorTy { shape: dims }));
                    }
                    // f16/tf32 fields keep the f32-backed convention for now.
                    ScalarType::F16 | ScalarType::Tf32 => ScalarKind::F32,
                    // Bool has its own ScalarKind (cl=I8); keep it so a bool
                    // tensor FIELD matches a `forge.uninit[bool, …]` value
                    // (ty_from_ast lowers bool → ScalarKind::Bool). Widening to
                    // i32 here made `model M { mask: Tensor[bool, …] }` reject
                    // its own constructor. (#273 follow-up.)
                    ScalarType::Bool => ScalarKind::Bool,
                    // Sub-byte / narrow integer types — widen to i32.
                    ScalarType::I8  | ScalarType::I16 |
                    ScalarType::U8  | ScalarType::U16 |
                    ScalarType::Int4 | ScalarType::Int8 |
                    ScalarType::Fp8E4M3 | ScalarType::Fp8E5M2 => ScalarKind::I32,
                    // Trit — packed ternary; must be 2-D.
                    ScalarType::Trit => {
                        let dims: Vec<i64> = shape.elems.iter().map(|d| {
                            resolve_shape_elem(d, env, tspan)
                        }).collect::<Result<_, _>>().unwrap_or_default();
                        if dims.len() != 2 {
                            return Ok(TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64));
                        }
                        return Ok(TyKind::TritTensor(TritTensorTy { k: dims[0], n: dims[1] }));
                    }
                    // Str/Nil in a tensor element position is nonsensical;
                    // fall through to the opaque-i64 path below.
                    _ => {
                        return Ok(TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64));
                    }
                },
                _ => {
                    return Ok(TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64));
                }
            };
            // Resolve each dimension.  If any dimension is dynamic (wildcard,
            // streaming, spread) we cannot represent the shape at compile time;
            // fall back to an opaque i64 pointer so existing @cast-based access
            // paths continue to work.
            let mut dims: Vec<i64> = Vec::with_capacity(shape.elems.len());
            for d in &shape.elems {
                match resolve_shape_elem(d, env, tspan) {
                    Ok(v) if v > 0 => dims.push(v),
                    _ => return Ok(TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)),
                }
            }
            if dims.is_empty() || dims.len() > 4 {
                return Ok(TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64));
            }
            Ok(TyKind::Tensor(TensorTy { elem, shape: dims }))
        }
        // `[ModelName; N]` / `[KV[...]; N]` as a model FIELD type — e.g.
        // `model Qwen3_4B { layers: [QwenBlock; 36] }`. Reuse the fn-signature
        // array lowering (ModelArray / KvArray) so the field is a typed array
        // pointer, not an opaque i64 (which broke both the store and indexed
        // load `qwen.layers[i]`). (#273 follow-up.)
        Type::Array(..) => ty_from_ast(ty, env),
        _ => Ok(TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)),
    }
}

/// Extract a compile-time constant integer from an expression used as an
/// `axis` argument. Handles a bare int literal and a unary negation of one
/// (e.g. `-1`). Returns `None` for anything non-constant.
/// A tensor-literal leaf that is an integer literal (or a negated one), used to
/// decide whether a tensor literal is an i64 or f32 tensor. (#273 follow-up.)
fn is_int_literal_leaf(e: &Expr) -> bool {
    match e {
        Expr::Literal(Literal::Int(..), _) => true,
        Expr::UnOp { op: UnOp::Neg, operand, .. } =>
            matches!(operand.as_ref(), Expr::Literal(Literal::Int(..), _)),
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn const_int_axis(e: &Expr) -> Option<i64> {
    match e {
        Expr::Literal(Literal::Int(n, _), _) => Some(*n),
        Expr::UnOp { op: UnOp::Neg, operand, .. } => {
            const_int_axis(operand).map(|n| -n)
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn resolve_shape_elem(
    d: &ShapeElem,
    env: &HashMap<String, i64>,
    span: &Span,
) -> Result<i64, JitError> {
    match d {
        ShapeElem::Expr(e) => resolve_shape_expr(e, env, span),
        ShapeElem::Wildcard(_) | ShapeElem::Streaming(_) | ShapeElem::Spread(_) => {
            err(span,
                "JIT requires concrete dimensions (`~`, `..`, `_` need slice-4 support)")
        }
    }
}

fn resolve_shape_expr(
    e: &Expr,
    env: &HashMap<String, i64>,
    span: &Span,
) -> Result<i64, JitError> {
    match e {
        Expr::Literal(Literal::Int(n, _), _) => Ok(*n),
        Expr::Ident(name, ispan) => env.get(name).copied().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("unbound shape parameter `{}`", name),
            line: ispan.line, col: ispan.col,
        }),
        Expr::BinOp { op, lhs, rhs, .. } => {
            let l = resolve_shape_expr(lhs, env, span)?;
            let r = resolve_shape_expr(rhs, env, span)?;
            match op {
                BinOp::Add => Ok(l + r),
                BinOp::Sub => Ok(l - r),
                BinOp::Mul => Ok(l * r),
                BinOp::Div if r != 0 => Ok(l / r),
                _ => err(span, format!(
                    "shape expressions support `+ - * /` only, got `{:?}`", op,
                )),
            }
        }
        _ => err(span, "shape elements must be literal ints, idents, or arithmetic"),
    }
}

/// True if a shape-literal element is the streaming axis marker `~`. Inside a
/// constructor's bracket args (`forge.kv[f32, [1, ~, 64]]`) the parser emits
/// `~` as `Expr::Ident("~")`.
fn is_streaming_expr(e: &Expr) -> bool {
    matches!(e, Expr::Ident(name, _) if name == "~")
}

fn type_span(ty: &Type) -> Span {
    match ty {
        Type::Scalar(_, s)
        | Type::Tensor(_, _, s)
        | Type::View(_, _, s)
        | Type::KV(_, _, s)
        | Type::Mesh(_, s)
        | Type::Fn(_, _, s)
        | Type::Tuple(_, s)
        | Type::Array(_, _, s)
        | Type::RawPtr(_, s)
        | Type::Named { span: s, .. } => s.clone(),
    }
}

fn stmt_span(s: &Stmt) -> Span {
    match s {
        Stmt::Let(l) => l.span.clone(),
        Stmt::Expr { span, .. } => span.clone(),
        Stmt::If(i) => i.span.clone(),
        Stmt::Match(m) => m.span.clone(),
        Stmt::For { span, .. } => span.clone(),
        Stmt::While { span, .. } => span.clone(),
        Stmt::Loop { span, .. } => span.clone(),
        Stmt::Stage { span, .. } => span.clone(),
        Stmt::Directive { span, .. } => span.clone(),
        Stmt::DirectiveBlock { span, .. } => span.clone(),
        Stmt::Break(s) | Stmt::Continue(s) => s.clone(),
        Stmt::Return { span, .. } => span.clone(),
    }
}

/// #336: the `EnumDecl` of an item (unwrapping `pub`/directive wrappers), or
/// None. Used to bail the JIT cleanly on enum-declaring programs.
fn item_enum_decl(item: &Item) -> Option<&crate::ast::EnumDecl> {
    match item {
        Item::Enum(e) => Some(e),
        Item::Pub(inner) => item_enum_decl(inner),
        Item::Directive { inner, .. } => item_enum_decl(inner),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn item_span(item: &Item) -> Span {
    match item {
        Item::Fn(f) => f.span.clone(),
        Item::ExternFn(e) => e.span.clone(),
        Item::Model(m) => m.span.clone(),
        Item::TypeAlias(t) => t.span.clone(),
        Item::Enum(e) => e.span.clone(),
        Item::Arena(a) => a.span.clone(),
        Item::Let(l) => l.span.clone(),
        Item::Use(u) => u.span.clone(),
        Item::Directive { span, .. } => span.clone(),
        Item::Pub(inner) => item_span(inner),
    }
}

// ─── Per-function metadata collected in pass 1 ───────────────────────────────

struct FnMeta {
    id: FuncId,
    sig: Signature,
    params: Vec<(String, TyKind, Span)>,
    ret: TyKind,
    body: Block_,  // alias of ast::Block; renamed below
    name: String,
    span: Span,
    /// Shape parameter bindings active when this fn was specialized.
    /// Empty for monomorphic functions; populated when monomorphizing a
    /// template at a call site.
    shape_env: HashMap<String, i64>,
    /// `@grad` compilation mode. `None` for ordinary fns; `Forward` for
    /// the forward-only entry of a `@grad fn`; `FwdBwd` for the
    /// gradient-emitting entry exposed as `f.fwd_bwd(...)`.
    grad_mode: GradMode,
    /// Index of every `!` (mut) tensor parameter, in declaration order.
    /// Empty when `grad_mode == None`. Used by FwdBwd lowering to know
    /// which params to publish gradients for.
    mut_param_idxs: Vec<usize>,
    /// Captured variables for a closure lambda, in order. Each entry is
    /// `(enclosing_name, ty)`. Empty for top-level fns and non-capturing
    /// lambdas. The env array layout is `[cap0: i64, cap1: i64, ...]`
    /// at offsets `0, 8, 16, ...`.
    captures: Vec<(String, TyKind)>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
enum GradMode { None, Forward, FwdBwd, FwdBwdBwd }

// Alias so callers and the AST block don't shadow Cranelift `Block`.
use crate::ast::Block as Block_;

// ─── Compiler / driver ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Canonical list of every builtin the JIT recognizes — the special-form
/// builtins dispatched in `lower_call` plus the registered typed-print
/// symbols. This is the single source of truth for backend parity:
/// `jit::tests::builtin_parity_*` asserts (a) the interpreter recognizes
/// every name here, and (b) the JIT actually dispatches every name here.
///
/// INVARIANT: any builtin added to the `lower_call` match (or registered as
/// a callable print symbol) MUST be added here, and MUST also be implemented
/// in the interpreter (`interp::is_builtin` + `call_builtin`). The parity
/// tests fail otherwise. Do not let the two backends drift.
///
/// Consumed only by the `jit::tests` parity checks, hence `cfg(test)`.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) const JIT_BUILTINS: &[&str] = &[
    // special-form builtins (lower_call match)
    "len", "sum", "mean", "variance", "pull_to_mean", "print_tensor",
    "exp", "sqrt", "log", "sin", "cos", "abs", "floor", "ceil",
    "f32_to_bits", "f32_from_bits",
    "sum_along", "mean_along", "max_along", "min_along", "variance_along", "pull_to_mean_along",
    "softmax", "rms_norm", "layer_norm",
    "attn", "rope", "attn_gqa", "embed",
    // Elementwise activations (scalar or same-shape tensor).
    "relu", "sigmoid", "tanh", "gelu", "silu", "elu", "mish",
    // typed-print symbols (registered, resolved via the normal call path)
    "print_i64", "print_f64", "print_bool", "print_nil",
    // HashMap builtins.
    "map_new", "map_get", "map_set", "map_contains",
    // Terminal / timing builtins (parity with the interpreter).
    "chr", "sleep_ms", "flush",
];

pub struct Jit {
    module: JITModule,
    ctx: Context,
    builder_ctx: FunctionBuilderContext,
    /// Concrete, already-declared functions keyed by their mangled name.
    /// For a monomorphic fn this is just the source name; for a shape-
    /// generic fn it's `name$d0_d1_...` per the instantiated shape args.
    fns: HashMap<String, FnEntry>,
    /// Shape-generic fn templates. Stored as raw FnDecls and instantiated
    /// on demand at call sites that supply concrete tensor arguments.
    templates: HashMap<String, FnDecl>,
    /// Monomorphizations that have been declared during body lowering but
    /// not yet defined. Drained after each fn's body lowering completes.
    /// Each entry's body may itself enqueue further work — the drain loop
    /// runs until fixpoint.
    pending: Vec<PendingMono>,
    finalized: bool,
    /// Pre-registered extern symbol addresses. Populated via
    /// `register_extern_symbol` before `compile_program`. Symbols here are
    /// emitted as local trampolines (call_indirect) rather than relying on
    /// the JIT linker's dlsym-based import resolution.
    extern_sym_addrs: HashMap<String, u64>,
    /// For `@grad fn`, maps the `$fwd_bwd` mangled name to an ordered list of
    /// (mut-param-name, tensor-ty, actual-param-index) entries. Used by
    /// `lower_fwd_bwd_destructure` to synthesize per-parameter local bindings
    /// so `grads.W`, `grads.b` etc. resolve correctly, and to call take_grad_at.
    grad_schemas: HashMap<String, Vec<(String, TyKind, usize)>>,
    /// Model field layouts: model_name → [(field_name, field_ty)].
    /// All fields are 8 bytes wide; byte_offset = field_index * 8.
    /// The `field_ty` here is resolved with the model's params *unbound*, so a
    /// param-shaped field (`x: Tensor[f32,[N]]`) lands as opaque i64; #267
    /// re-resolves such fields per-instantiation (see `model_shape_params` /
    /// `model_field_asts`).
    model_layouts: HashMap<String, Vec<(String, TyKind)>>,
    /// #267: a model's declared shape-param names, in order (`Bar[N]` → `["N"]`).
    /// Zipped with a `TyKind::Model`'s concrete args to resolve param-shaped fields.
    model_shape_params: HashMap<String, Vec<String>>,
    /// #267: a model's field *AST* types, kept so a param-shaped field can be
    /// re-resolved against concrete type args at access time.
    model_field_asts: HashMap<String, Vec<(String, Type)>>,
    /// #268: top-level `let NAME = <literal>` constants (the SPEC §4.5 enum
    /// discriminant idiom). Stored as the initializer expr and re-lowered at each
    /// bare-ident reference. Only compile-time-constant initializers are admitted;
    /// anything else still errors as an unsupported top-level binding.
    global_consts: HashMap<String, Expr>,
    /// Deferred lambda bodies accumulated during function-body lowering.
    /// Drained after each top-level function is compiled (before finalize).
    pending_lambdas: Vec<FnMeta>,
    /// Counter for generating unique lambda names (`__lambda_N`).
    lambda_counter: usize,
    /// #350: top-level C-like enums — name → ordered variant names (mirrors
    /// the interpreter/checker registries). Populated up front in
    /// `compile_program` so fn signatures, `let` annotations, and `match`
    /// scrutinees can resolve an enum-named type and its variant ordinals.
    enums: HashMap<String, Vec<String>>,
    /// #350 Part 2b: payload-carrying enums — name → tagged-union layout. Only
    /// enums with ≥1 payload variant appear here; tag-only enums (#336/Part 1)
    /// stay bare-ordinal i64 values and are absent. A value of a payload enum is
    /// an i64 pointer to a forge-allocated `[tag, slot0, slot1, …]` region laid
    /// out exactly like a model (8 bytes/slot), with one slot per (variant,
    /// field) — no slot sharing (design §4.1).
    enum_payload_layouts: HashMap<String, EnumLayout>,
    /// #326: when true (set by `--gpu`), the `m == 1` bf16 decode GEMV is
    /// lowered to the GPU/Metal builtin `__dmc_matmul_bf16_gpu` instead of the
    /// CPU `__dmc_matmul_bf16`. Only honored when built with `--features gpu`
    /// on macOS; otherwise the symbol is absent and the flag is a no-op.
    gpu: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
struct PendingMono {
    template_name: String,
    shape_env: HashMap<String, i64>,
    mangled_name: String,
    /// Call-site span, used only for diagnostics if instantiation later fails.
    call_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
struct FnEntry {
    id: FuncId,
    sig: Signature,
    params: Vec<(String, TyKind, Span)>,
    ret: TyKind,
    /// Indices (into `params`) of the mutable `!` parameters; non-empty only
    /// on the `$fwd_bwd` entry. Used by destructuring to query `take_grad_at`.
    mut_param_idxs: Vec<usize>,
}

/// Fuse a pipe placeholder stage: replace every `_` in `stage` with `repl`,
/// returning the inlined expression. Returns `None` when `stage` has no
/// placeholder (the application form `x |> f`, lowered as a call). Does not
/// descend into closures (own pipe scope); block-like stages are left intact
/// (lowered through the call path, unchanged). Mirrors the interpreter's
/// `expr_contains_underscore` substitution so `dmc jit` and `dmc run` agree.
fn fuse_underscore(stage: &Expr, repl: &Expr) -> Option<Expr> {
    fn go(e: &Expr, repl: &Expr, hit: &mut bool) -> Expr {
        match e {
            Expr::Underscore(_) => {
                *hit = true;
                repl.clone()
            }
            Expr::Tuple(es, s) => {
                Expr::Tuple(es.iter().map(|x| go(x, repl, hit)).collect(), s.clone())
            }
            Expr::TensorLit(es, s) => {
                Expr::TensorLit(es.iter().map(|x| go(x, repl, hit)).collect(), s.clone())
            }
            Expr::BinOp { op, lhs, rhs, span } => Expr::BinOp {
                op: op.clone(),
                lhs: Box::new(go(lhs, repl, hit)),
                rhs: Box::new(go(rhs, repl, hit)),
                span: span.clone(),
            },
            Expr::UnOp { op, operand, span } => Expr::UnOp {
                op: op.clone(),
                operand: Box::new(go(operand, repl, hit)),
                span: span.clone(),
            },
            Expr::Cast { expr, ty, span } => Expr::Cast {
