                expr: Box::new(go(expr, repl, hit)),
                ty: ty.clone(),
                span: span.clone(),
            },
            Expr::Postfix { expr, op, span } => Expr::Postfix {
                expr: Box::new(go(expr, repl, hit)),
                op: subst_postfix(op, repl, hit),
                span: span.clone(),
            },
            Expr::Range { start, end, inclusive, span } => Expr::Range {
                start: start.as_ref().map(|b| Box::new(go(b, repl, hit))),
                end: end.as_ref().map(|b| Box::new(go(b, repl, hit))),
                inclusive: *inclusive,
                span: span.clone(),
            },
            other => other.clone(),
        }
    }
    fn subst_postfix(op: &PostfixOp, repl: &Expr, hit: &mut bool) -> PostfixOp {
        match op {
            PostfixOp::Index(elems) => PostfixOp::Index(
                elems
                    .iter()
                    .map(|el| match el {
                        IndexElem::Expr(e) => IndexElem::Expr(go(e, repl, hit)),
                        IndexElem::Slice { start, end, step, span } => IndexElem::Slice {
                            start: start.as_ref().map(|b| Box::new(go(b, repl, hit))),
                            end: end.as_ref().map(|b| Box::new(go(b, repl, hit))),
                            step: step.as_ref().map(|b| Box::new(go(b, repl, hit))),
                            span: span.clone(),
                        },
                        IndexElem::FullSlice(s) => IndexElem::FullSlice(s.clone()),
                    })
                    .collect(),
            ),
            PostfixOp::Call(args) => PostfixOp::Call(subst_args(args, repl, hit)),
            PostfixOp::BracketArgs(args) => PostfixOp::BracketArgs(subst_args(args, repl, hit)),
            PostfixOp::Constructor(fields) => PostfixOp::Constructor(
                fields.iter().map(|(n, v)| (n.clone(), go(v, repl, hit))).collect(),
            ),
            PostfixOp::Transpose | PostfixOp::Query | PostfixOp::Field(_) => op.clone(),
        }
    }
    fn subst_args(args: &[CallArg], repl: &Expr, hit: &mut bool) -> Vec<CallArg> {
        args.iter()
            .map(|a| match a {
                CallArg::Positional(e) => CallArg::Positional(go(e, repl, hit)),
                CallArg::Named { name, value, span } => CallArg::Named {
                    name: name.clone(),
                    value: go(value, repl, hit),
                    span: span.clone(),
                },
                CallArg::Spread(s) => CallArg::Spread(s.clone()),
            })
            .collect()
    }
    let mut hit = false;
    let out = go(stage, repl, &mut hit);
    if hit { Some(out) } else { None }
}

impl Jit {
    pub fn new() -> Result<Self, JitError> {
        let mut flag_builder = settings::builder();
        flag_builder.set("use_colocated_libcalls", "false").map_err(setting_err)?;
        flag_builder.set("is_pic", "false").map_err(setting_err)?;
        // Optimize generated code for speed. Cranelift's "speed" level adds
        // register-allocation quality and basic optimization; the compile-
        // time cost is small (single-digit ms for these kernels) and the
        // runtime win on tight loops / recursion is large.
        flag_builder.set("opt_level", "speed").map_err(setting_err)?;
        let isa_builder = cranelift_native::builder().map_err(|e| JitError {
            msg: format!("host ISA unsupported: {}", e),
            line: 0, col: 0,
        })?;
        let isa = isa_builder
            .finish(settings::Flags::new(flag_builder))
            .map_err(|e| JitError { msg: format!("isa finish: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0 })?;

        let mut builder = JITBuilder::with_isa(isa, cranelift_module::default_libcall_names());
        // Builtins exposed to demoniC source by symbol name.
        builder.symbol("print_i64", builtin_print_i64 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("print_f64", builtin_print_f64 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("print_bool", builtin_print_bool as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("print_nil", builtin_print_nil as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_exp_f32", builtin_exp_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_sqrt_f32", builtin_sqrt_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_log_f32", builtin_log_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_sin_f32", builtin_sin_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_cos_f32", builtin_cos_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_exp_f64", builtin_exp_f64 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_sqrt_f64", builtin_sqrt_f64 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_log_f64", builtin_log_f64 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_sin_f64", builtin_sin_f64 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_cos_f64", builtin_cos_f64 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_tanh_f32", builtin_tanh_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_gelu_f32", builtin_gelu_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_sigmoid_f32", builtin_sigmoid_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_silu_f32", builtin_silu_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_elu_f32", builtin_elu_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_mish_f32", builtin_mish_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_silu_deriv_f32", builtin_silu_deriv_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_elu_deriv_f32", builtin_elu_deriv_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_mish_deriv_f32", builtin_mish_deriv_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_powf_f32", builtin_powf_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_powf_f64", builtin_powf_f64 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_fmod_f64", builtin_fmod_f64 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_capture_grad", capture_grad as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_take_grad_at", take_grad_at_idx as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_grad_prologue", grad_call_prologue as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_grad_epilogue", grad_call_epilogue as *const u8);
        // Forge arena allocator + snapshot/restore (internal — invoked by tensor lowering).
        builder.symbol("__dmc_forge_alloc", forge_alloc as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_forge_snapshot", forge_snapshot as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_forge_restore", forge_restore as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_print_tensor_1d_f32", print_tensor_1d_f32 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_print_tensor_2d_f32", print_tensor_2d_f32 as *const u8);
        // String runtime functions.
        builder.symbol("__dmc_str_new_from_raw", dmc_str_new_from_raw as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_str_len",          dmc_str_len          as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_str_get_char",     dmc_str_get_char     as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_str_eq",           dmc_str_eq           as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_str_concat",       dmc_str_concat       as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_str_from_int",     dmc_str_from_int     as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_str_from_f64",     dmc_str_from_f64     as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_str_from_bool",    dmc_str_from_bool    as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_chr",              dmc_chr              as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_sleep_ms",         dmc_sleep_ms         as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_flush",            dmc_flush            as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_match_trap",       dmc_match_trap       as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_nil_trap",         dmc_nil_trap         as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_print_str",        dmc_print_str        as *const u8);
        // HashMap runtime functions.
        builder.symbol("__dmc_map_new",      dmc_map_new      as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_map_get",      dmc_map_get      as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_map_set",      dmc_map_set      as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_map_contains", dmc_map_contains as *const u8);
        // vault.load / vault.load_npz — raw binary and NPZ weight loading.
        builder.symbol("__dmc_vault_load_raw", dmc_vault_load_raw as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_vault_load_npz", dmc_vault_load_npz as *const u8);
        // #323: multi-threaded f32 matmul for the large Linear layers.
        builder.symbol("__dmc_matmul_par", dmc_matmul_par as *const u8);
        // #324: bf16-direct matmul kernel + upconvert-on-use helper.
        builder.symbol("__dmc_matmul_bf16", dmc_matmul_bf16 as *const u8);
        // #326: GPU/Metal bf16 decode GEMV — only present on macOS + `--features gpu`.
        #[cfg(all(target_os = "macos", feature = "gpu"))]
        builder.symbol("__dmc_matmul_bf16_gpu", crate::gpu::dmc_matmul_bf16_gpu as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_bf16_upconvert", dmc_bf16_upconvert as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_f32_to_bf16", dmc_f32_to_bf16 as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_bf16_transpose_2d", dmc_bf16_transpose_2d as *const u8);
        // forge.trit builtins — quantize / manipulate packed trit tensors.
        builder.symbol("__dmc_trit_quantize",  dmc_trit_quantize  as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_trit_neg",       dmc_trit_neg       as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_trit_sparsity",  dmc_trit_sparsity  as *const u8);
        // #259: OOB diagnostic helper — prints a clean error and exits(1).
        builder.symbol("__dmc_oob_trap", dmc_oob_trap as *const u8);
        builder.symbol("__dmc_kv_cap_trap", dmc_kv_cap_trap as *const u8);
        // #265: runtime shift-count range trap — prints a clean error and exits(1).
        builder.symbol("__dmc_shift_trap", dmc_shift_trap as *const u8);
        // #297: INT_MIN / -1 division-overflow trap — prints a clean error and exits(1).
        builder.symbol("__dmc_div_overflow_trap", dmc_div_overflow_trap as *const u8);

        let module = JITModule::new(builder);
        Ok(Jit {
            ctx: module.make_context(),
            module,
            builder_ctx: FunctionBuilderContext::new(),
            fns: HashMap::new(),
            templates: HashMap::new(),
            pending: Vec::new(),
            finalized: false,
            extern_sym_addrs: HashMap::new(),
            grad_schemas: HashMap::new(),
            model_layouts: HashMap::new(),
            model_shape_params: HashMap::new(),
            model_field_asts: HashMap::new(),
            global_consts: HashMap::new(),
            pending_lambdas: Vec::new(),
            lambda_counter: 0,
            enums: HashMap::new(),
            enum_payload_layouts: HashMap::new(),
            gpu: false,
        })
    }

    /// #326: enable GPU lowering for the bf16 decode GEMV (`--gpu`). Present only
    /// on a macOS `--features gpu` build (where `__dmc_matmul_bf16_gpu` is
    /// registered); feature-off builds never call it and keep the CPU kernel.
    #[cfg(all(target_os = "macos", feature = "gpu"))]
    pub fn set_gpu(&mut self, on: bool) {
        self.gpu = on;
    }

    /// Pre-register a symbol address for an `extern fn` declaration.
    ///
    /// Call this before `compile_program` for symbols that are not resolvable
    /// via the system dynamic linker (e.g., functions in Rust crates that are
    /// not exported to the dynamic symbol table). The JIT will emit a thin
    /// `call_indirect` trampoline for each pre-registered symbol instead of
    /// relying on dlsym.
    ///
    /// For symbols that ARE in the dynamic symbol table (system libraries,
    /// shared libraries loaded via dlopen), no pre-registration is needed —
    /// `extern fn` declarations are resolved automatically at finalize time.
    ///
    /// Exercised only by the extern-symbol trampoline tests today, hence
    /// `cfg(test)`; un-gate it if the CLI ever needs to pre-register symbols.
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn register_extern_symbol(&mut self, name: &str, addr: *const u8) {
        self.extern_sym_addrs.insert(name.to_string(), addr as u64);
    }

    /// Compile every fn item in `program`. Other top-level items (let, model,
    /// arena, type alias, use, directive, pub) are walked transparently for
    /// fn extraction; non-fn items are rejected with a diagnostic.
    pub fn compile_program(&mut self, program: &Program) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        let __timing = std::env::var("DMC_JIT_TIMING").is_ok();
        JIT_CODEGEN_NS.store(0, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        let __t_total = std::time::Instant::now();

        // #350: collect C-like enums (name → ordered variants) up front, so fn
        // signatures, `let` annotations, and `match` scrutinees lowered below can
        // resolve an enum-named type to `TyKind::Enum` and look up variant
        // ordinals. An enum value is its variant's i64 ordinal, so the rest of
        // the integer machinery is reused (#336 closed the interpreter/checker
        // half; this is the JIT half).
        for item in &program.items {
            if let Some(e) = item_enum_decl(item) {
                self.enums.insert(
                    e.name.clone(),
                    e.variants.iter().map(|v| v.name.clone()).collect(),
                );
            }
        }
        // #350 Part 2b: build the tagged-union layout for any enum with a
        // payload-carrying variant. A value of such an enum is an i64 pointer to
        // a forge region `[tag, slots…]` (one slot per variant-field, no
        // sharing). v1 supports scalar payload fields; a non-scalar field
        // (tensor/string/model) routes the program cleanly out of the JIT subset.
        let payload_env: HashMap<String, i64> = HashMap::new();
        for item in &program.items {
            if let Some(e) = item_enum_decl(item) {
                if !e.variants.iter().any(|v| !v.fields.is_empty()) { continue; }
                let mut variant_off: HashMap<String, i64> = HashMap::new();
                let mut variant_tys: HashMap<String, Vec<TyKind>> = HashMap::new();
                let mut slot = 1i64; // slot 0 is the tag
                for v in &e.variants {
                    if v.fields.is_empty() { continue; }
                    let mut tys = Vec::with_capacity(v.fields.len());
                    for t in &v.fields {
                        // v1 supports the scalar kinds the JIT slot maps exactly,
                        // guaranteeing interp/JIT parity: i32/i64/f32/f64/bool.
                        // Anything else (str/nil — which `lower_ty_for_model`
                        // would silently collapse to an opaque i64 — narrow/
                        // unsigned/exotic-float scalars, tensors, models) routes
                        // the program cleanly out of the JIT subset.
                        let storable = matches!(t, Type::Scalar(
                            ScalarType::I32 | ScalarType::I64
                            | ScalarType::F32 | ScalarType::F64
                            | ScalarType::Bool, _));
                        if !storable {
                            return unsupported(&v.span, &format!(
                                "a non-scalar payload field in enum variant `{}.{}` \
                                 (#350 Part 2b supports i32/i64/f32/f64/bool payloads)",
                                e.name, v.name));
                        }
                        let k = enumify(lower_ty_for_model(t, &payload_env, &v.span)?, &self.enums);
                        tys.push(k);
                    }
                    variant_off.insert(v.name.clone(), slot);
                    slot += v.fields.len() as i64;
                    variant_tys.insert(v.name.clone(), tys);
                }
                self.enum_payload_layouts.insert(e.name.clone(),
                    EnumLayout { n_slots: slot, variant_off, variant_tys });
            }
        }

        // Pass 0: register extern fn declarations so their names are in
        // `self.fns` before any fn body is lowered (handles forward references).
        self.declare_extern_fns(program)?;

        // Pass 1: declare every monomorphic fn; register shape-generic ones
        // as templates for later on-demand instantiation.
        let mut metas: Vec<FnMeta> = Vec::new();
        for item in &program.items {
            self.collect_fns(item, &mut metas)?;
        }
        self.register_builtins()?;

        // Pass 2: define each declared fn. Bodies may discover template
        // calls and push monomorphizations onto `pending`.
        for meta in &metas {
            self.define_fn(meta)?;
        }

        // Pass 3: drain the monomorphization worklist to fixpoint. Each
        // newly-defined fn may itself enqueue more.
        while let Some(p) = self.pending.pop() {
            let meta = self.declare_monomorph(&p)?;
            self.define_fn(&meta)?;
        }

        // Pass 4: drain deferred lambda bodies (from `Expr::FnLit` encountered
        // during body lowering). Lambda bodies may themselves contain lambdas or
        // trigger monomorphizations, so loop until both queues are empty.
        loop {
            if self.pending_lambdas.is_empty() && self.pending.is_empty() { break; }
            while let Some(meta) = self.pending_lambdas.pop() {
                self.define_fn(&meta)?;
            }
            while let Some(p) = self.pending.pop() {
                let meta = self.declare_monomorph(&p)?;
                self.define_fn(&meta)?;
            }
        }

        let __t_fin = std::time::Instant::now();
        self.module.finalize_definitions()
            .map_err(|e| JitError { msg: format!("finalize: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0 })?;
        let __fin = __t_fin.elapsed();
        self.finalized = true;
        if __timing {
            let total = __t_total.elapsed().as_secs_f64();
            let codegen = JIT_CODEGEN_NS.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) as f64 / 1e9;
            let finalize = __fin.as_secs_f64();
            let lowering = (total - codegen - finalize).max(0.0);
            eprintln!("[#325 jit-timing] total={:.3}s  lowering(dmc IR build)={:.3}s ({:.0}%)  \
                       codegen(define_function)={:.3}s ({:.0}%)  finalize/link={:.3}s ({:.0}%)",
                      total,
                      lowering, 100.0 * lowering / total,
                      codegen, 100.0 * codegen / total,
                      finalize, 100.0 * finalize / total);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Reconstruct an FnMeta for a pending monomorphization. The
    /// signature + entry were already inserted into `self.fns` by
    /// `instantiate_template` at the call site; here we just wire up the
    /// body and shape env so `define_fn` can run.
    fn declare_monomorph(&mut self, p: &PendingMono) -> Result<FnMeta, JitError> {
        let tmpl = self.templates.get(&p.template_name).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("internal: template `{}` missing during monomorphization",
                         p.template_name),
            line: p.call_span.line, col: p.call_span.col,
        })?.clone();
        let entry = self.fns.get(&p.mangled_name).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("internal: entry `{}` missing during monomorphization",
                         p.mangled_name),
            line: p.call_span.line, col: p.call_span.col,
        })?.clone();
        Ok(FnMeta {
            id: entry.id,
            sig: entry.sig,
            params: entry.params,
            ret: entry.ret,
            body: tmpl.body,
            name: p.mangled_name.clone(),
            span: tmpl.span,
            shape_env: p.shape_env.clone(),
            grad_mode: GradMode::None,
            mut_param_idxs: Vec::new(),
            captures: Vec::new(),
        })
    }

    // ─── Pass 0: extern fn declarations ──────────────────────────────────────

    fn declare_extern_fns(&mut self, program: &Program) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        for item in &program.items {
            self.declare_extern_fn_item(item, false)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn declare_extern_fn_item(&mut self, item: &Item, is_public: bool) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        match item {
            Item::ExternFn(e) => self.declare_one_extern_fn(e, is_public),
            Item::Pub(inner) => self.declare_extern_fn_item(inner, true),
            _ => Ok(()),
        }
    }

    /// Register an `extern fn` declaration in `self.fns` so it can be called
    /// from JIT-compiled code.
    ///
    /// If the symbol was pre-registered via `register_extern_symbol`, emits a
    /// local `call_indirect` trampoline (bypasses dlsym). Otherwise declares
    /// with `Linkage::Import` and delegates to the JIT linker (dlsym).
    fn declare_one_extern_fn(&mut self, e: &ExternFnDecl, is_public: bool) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        // SPEC.md §9: `pub` on an `extern fn` is a compile-time error — foreign
        // symbols are always exported, so `pub` is meaningless. `check.rs` is the
        // primary gate (fires in `--check`/`run`); this is the JIT-path fallback,
        // since `dmc jit` skips the checker (main.rs) and does its own per-decl
        // validation.
        if is_public {
            return err(&e.span, format!(
                "`pub` is not allowed on `extern fn` `{}` — an `extern fn` is always \
                 exported; the `pub` keyword on it is a compile-time error (SPEC.md §9)",
                e.name));
        }
        if let Some(abi) = &e.abi {
            if abi != "C" {
                return unsupported(&e.span,
                    &format!("extern \"{}\" ABI not yet supported in JIT (only C ABI)", abi));
            }
        }
        if !e.shape_params.is_empty() {
            return unsupported(&e.span,
                "shape-generic extern fn not supported in JIT");
        }

        let empty_env: HashMap<String, i64> = HashMap::new();
        let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
        let mut params: Vec<(String, TyKind, Span)> = Vec::new();

        for p in &e.params {
            let ast_ty = p.ty.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                msg: format!("extern fn `{}` param `{}` has no type annotation", e.name, p.name),
                line: p.span.line, col: p.span.col,
            })?;
            let ty = ty_from_ast(ast_ty, &empty_env)?;
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(ty.cl()));
            params.push((p.name.clone(), ty, p.span.clone()));
        }

        let ret = match &e.ret_type {
            None => TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil),
            Some(t) => ty_from_ast(t, &empty_env)?,
        };
        if !matches!(ret, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)) {
            sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(ret.cl()));
        }
        sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;

        if let Some(&addr) = self.extern_sym_addrs.get(&e.name) {
            self.emit_extern_trampoline(&e.name, sig, params, ret, addr, &e.span)
        } else {
            let id = self.module
                .declare_function(&e.name, Linkage::Import, &sig)
                .map_err(|e_| JitError {
                    msg: format!("declare extern fn `{}`: {}", e.name, e_),
                    line: e.span.line, col: e.span.col,
                })?;
            self.fns.insert(e.name.clone(), FnEntry { id, sig, params, ret, mut_param_idxs: vec![] });
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    /// Emit a `Linkage::Local` trampoline that calls `addr` via `call_indirect`.
    /// Used for pre-registered symbols that are not in the dynamic symbol table.
    fn emit_extern_trampoline(
        &mut self,
        name: &str,
        sig: Signature,
        params: Vec<(String, TyKind, Span)>,
        ret: TyKind,
        addr: u64,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        let id = self.module
            .declare_function(name, Linkage::Local, &sig)
            .map_err(|e| JitError {
                msg: format!("declare extern trampoline `{}`: {}", name, e),
                line: span.line, col: span.col,
            })?;
        self.fns.insert(name.to_string(), FnEntry {
            id, sig: sig.clone(), params, ret: ret.clone(), mut_param_idxs: vec![],
        });

        self.ctx.func.signature = sig.clone();
        self.ctx.func.name = UserFuncName::user(0, id.as_u32());

        let mut builder = FunctionBuilder::new(&mut self.ctx.func, &mut self.builder_ctx);
        let entry = builder.create_block();
        builder.append_block_params_for_function_params(entry);
        builder.switch_to_block(entry);
        builder.seal_block(entry);

        let n_params = sig.params.len();
        let arg_vals: Vec<Value> = (0..n_params).map(|i| builder.block_params(entry)[i]).collect();

        let sig_ref = builder.import_signature(sig);
        let callee = builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, addr as i64);
        let call = builder.ins().call_indirect(sig_ref, callee, &arg_vals);

        if matches!(ret, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)) {
            builder.ins().return_(&[]);
        } else {
            let result = builder.inst_results(call)[0];
            builder.ins().return_(&[result]);
        }

        builder.finalize(self.module.target_config());
        self.module
            .define_function(id, &mut self.ctx)
            .map_err(|e| JitError {
                msg: format!("define extern trampoline `{}`: {}", name, e),
                line: span.line, col: span.col,
            })?;
        self.module.clear_context(&mut self.ctx);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn collect_fns(&mut self, item: &Item, out: &mut Vec<FnMeta>) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        match item {
            Item::Fn(f) => {
                // Directives on a fn are attached to the FnDecl (not wrapped
                // in Item::Directive). `@grad` routes to the dual-entry path.
                if f.directives.iter().any(|d| d.name == "grad") {
                    return self.declare_grad_fn(f, out);
                }
                if f.directives.iter().any(|d| d.name != "grad") {
                    // Other directives (@deterministic, @cast, ...) are not
                    // yet honored by the JIT; lower the body ignoring them.
                }
                if !f.shape_params.is_empty() {
                    // Shape-generic function: register as a template; defer
                    // declaration + definition until a call site supplies
                    // concrete shape args.
                    if self.templates.contains_key(&f.name) || self.fns.contains_key(&f.name) {
                        return err(&f.span, format!("duplicate function `{}`", f.name));
                    }
                    self.templates.insert(f.name.clone(), f.clone());
                    return Ok(());
                }
                let meta = self.declare_fn(f, &HashMap::new(), &f.name, GradMode::None)?;
                out.push(meta);
                Ok(())
            }
            Item::Directive { directives, inner, .. } => {
                let is_grad = directives.iter().any(|d| d.name == "grad");
                if is_grad {
                    if let Item::Fn(f) = inner.as_ref() {
                        return self.declare_grad_fn(f, out);
                    }
                    return err(&item_span(item), "`@grad` may only annotate a function");
                }
                self.collect_fns(inner, out)
            }
            Item::Pub(inner) => self.collect_fns(inner, out),
            Item::ExternFn(_) => Ok(()), // handled in declare_extern_fns (pass 0)
            Item::Let(l) => {
                // #268: admit a top-level `let NAME = <compile-time literal>` as a
                // module constant (the §4.5 enum-discriminant idiom). Non-const
                // initializers, or non-simple patterns, remain unsupported.
                match (&l.pattern, is_const_literal_expr(&l.value)) {
                    (Pattern::Ident(name, _), true) if !l.mutating && !l.is_mut => {
                        self.global_consts.insert(name.clone(), l.value.clone());
                        Ok(())
                    }
                    _ => unsupported(&l.span,
                        "top-level `let` bindings (only `let NAME = <literal>` constants are supported)"),
                }
            }
            Item::Model(m) => {
                // Register field layouts; skip methods for now. The layout is
                // resolved with params unbound (empty env) — param-shaped fields
                // become opaque i64 here and are re-resolved per-instantiation
                // (#267). We also retain each field's AST type + the model's
                // shape-param names for that re-resolution.
                let mut fields = Vec::new();
                let mut field_asts = Vec::new();
                let empty_env = HashMap::new();
                for member in &m.members {
                    if let ModelMember::Field { name, ty, span, .. } = member {
                        let fty = enumify(lower_ty_for_model(ty, &empty_env, span)?, &self.enums);
                        fields.push((name.clone(), fty));
                        field_asts.push((name.clone(), ty.clone()));
                    }
                    // Methods: skip for now (handled as top-level functions).
                }
                self.model_layouts.insert(m.name.clone(), fields);
                self.model_field_asts.insert(m.name.clone(), field_asts);
                self.model_shape_params.insert(
                    m.name.clone(),
                    m.shape_params.iter().map(|p| p.name.clone()).collect());
                Ok(())
            }
            Item::TypeAlias(t) => unsupported(&t.span, "`type` aliases at top level"),
            Item::Enum(_) => Ok(()), // enums are compile-time metadata (no fns)
            Item::Arena(a) => unsupported(&a.span, "arena blocks as items"),
            Item::Use(u)   => unsupported(&u.span, "`use` imports (single-file only)"),
        }
    }

    /// Declare both entries of a `@grad fn`: the forward-only `f` and the
    /// gradient-emitting `f$fwd_bwd`. Both share the body; they differ only
    /// in whether the backward pass is emitted.
    ///
    /// If `double_grad` is true (stacked `@grad @grad`), also declare a
    /// `f$fwd_bwd_bwd` entry that computes the second derivative via
    /// `tape_backward`.
    fn declare_grad_fn(&mut self, f: &FnDecl, out: &mut Vec<FnMeta>) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        if !f.shape_params.is_empty() {
            return unsupported(&f.span,
                "shape-generic `@grad fn` (monomorphizing the backward) is a later slice");
        }
        // At least one mut param is required (AUTODIFF.md §2).
        let mut_idxs: Vec<usize> = f.params.iter().enumerate()
            .filter(|(_, p)| p.mutating)
            .map(|(i, _)| i)
            .collect();
        if mut_idxs.is_empty() {
            return err(&f.span,
                "`@grad fn` with no `!` (mut) parameter has nothing to differentiate \
                 (AUTODIFF.md §2)");
        }
        if !matches!(&f.ret_type, Some(Type::Scalar(ScalarType::F32, _))) {
            return err(&f.span,
                "JIT slice 6 supports `@grad fn` returning a scalar `f32` loss only");
        }
        // Count how many @grad directives are stacked on this function.
        let grad_count = f.directives.iter().filter(|d| d.name == "grad").count();
        // Forward-only entry: plain function under the source name.
        let fwd = self.declare_fn(f, &HashMap::new(), &f.name, GradMode::Forward)?;
        out.push(fwd);
        // fwd_bwd entry: same signature, mangled name `f$fwd_bwd`.
        let bwd_name = format!("{}$fwd_bwd", f.name);
        let bwd = self.declare_fn(f, &HashMap::new(), &bwd_name, GradMode::FwdBwd)?;
        // Build the schema that drives `let (loss, grads) = f.fwd_bwd(...)`:
        // (mut-param-name, tensor-ty, actual-param-index). Single-param @grad
        // goes here too; the destructuring path decides field-vs-direct binding.
        if !bwd.mut_param_idxs.is_empty() {
            let schema: Vec<(String, TyKind, usize)> = bwd.mut_param_idxs.iter()
                .map(|&i| (bwd.params[i].0.clone(), bwd.params[i].1.clone(), i))
                .collect();
            self.grad_schemas.insert(bwd_name, schema);
        }
        out.push(bwd);
        // fwd_bwd_bwd entry for stacked `@grad @grad`: second derivative.
        if grad_count >= 2 {
            let bwd2_name = format!("{}$fwd_bwd_bwd", f.name);
            let bwd2 = self.declare_fn(f, &HashMap::new(), &bwd2_name, GradMode::FwdBwdBwd)?;
            out.push(bwd2);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Declare a function in the module under `mangled_name`. `shape_env`
    /// resolves shape parameter idents in the signature to concrete dims.
    /// Returns the FnMeta so the caller can later define the body.
    fn declare_fn(
        &mut self,
        f: &FnDecl,
        shape_env: &HashMap<String, i64>,
        mangled_name: &str,
        grad_mode: GradMode,
    ) -> Result<FnMeta, JitError> {
        let mut params = Vec::with_capacity(f.params.len());
        let mut mut_param_idxs = Vec::new();
        let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
        for (idx, p) in f.params.iter().enumerate() {
            if p.is_self {
                return unsupported(&p.span, "`self` parameters");
            }
            if p.mutating {
                // Only meaningful inside a `@grad fn`; outside, a mut tensor
                // param has no gradient target and we don't yet write back.
                if grad_mode == GradMode::None {
                    return unsupported(&p.span,
                        "`!` mutating parameters outside `@grad fn`");
                }
                mut_param_idxs.push(idx);
            }
            let ty_ast = p.ty.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                msg: format!("parameter `{}` needs a type annotation in the JIT", p.name),
                line: p.span.line, col: p.span.col,
            })?;
            let ty = enumify(ty_from_ast(ty_ast, shape_env)?, &self.enums);
            if matches!(ty, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)) {
                return err(&p.span, "`nil` parameters are not meaningful");
            }
            if p.mutating && !ty.is_tensor() {
                return err(&p.span, "`@grad` mut parameters must be tensors in slice 6");
            }
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(ty.cl()));
            params.push((p.name.clone(), ty, p.span.clone()));
        }
        let ret = match &f.ret_type {
            Some(t) => enumify(ty_from_ast(t, shape_env)?, &self.enums),
            None    => TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil),
        };
        if !matches!(ret, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)) {
            sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(ret.cl()));
        }
        // Grad pointers are published via capture_grad (side-channel) and
        // retrieved in-JIT via __dmc_take_grad_at. No extra return values needed.
        sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;

        let id = self.module
            .declare_function(mangled_name, Linkage::Export, &sig)
            .map_err(|e| JitError {
                msg: format!("declare_function `{}`: {}", mangled_name, e),
                line: f.span.line, col: f.span.col,
            })?;

        if self.fns.contains_key(mangled_name) {
            return err(&f.span, format!("duplicate function `{}`", mangled_name));
        }
        self.fns.insert(mangled_name.to_string(), FnEntry {
            id, sig: sig.clone(),
            params: params.clone(),
            ret: ret.clone(),
            mut_param_idxs: mut_param_idxs.clone(),
        });

        Ok(FnMeta {
            id,
            sig,
            params,
            ret,
            body: f.body.clone(),
            name: mangled_name.to_string(),
            span: f.span.clone(),
            shape_env: shape_env.clone(),
            grad_mode,
            mut_param_idxs,
            captures: Vec::new(),
        })
    }

    fn register_builtins(&mut self) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        // Each builtin has a fixed C ABI signature and is bound to a Rust fn
        // pointer above. They appear as ordinary fn calls in source. Tensor
        // builtins (printers, sum, len) are lowered specially in
        // `lower_call` so they don't appear here — only true runtime
        // symbols with scalar-only signatures live in `self.fns`.
        let builtins: [(&str, &[ScalarKind], Option<ScalarKind>); 4] = [
            ("print_i64",  &[ScalarKind::I64],  None),
            ("print_f64",  &[ScalarKind::F64],  None),
            ("print_bool", &[ScalarKind::Bool], None),
            ("print_nil",  &[],                 None),
        ];
        for (name, params, _ret) in builtins {
            let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
            for p in params { sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(p.cl())); }
            sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
            let id = self.module
                .declare_function(name, Linkage::Import, &sig)
                .map_err(|e| JitError {
                    msg: format!("declare builtin `{}`: {}", name, e),
                    line: 0, col: 0,
                })?;
            self.fns.insert(name.to_string(), FnEntry {
                id, sig,
                params: params.iter().enumerate()
                    .map(|(i, k)| (
                        format!("arg{}", i),
                        TyKind::Scalar(*k),
                        Span { line: 0, col: 0, start: 0, end: 0 },
                    ))
                    .collect(),
                ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil), mut_param_idxs: vec![],
            });
        }
        // The Forge allocator symbol — internal, not callable from source.
        let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
        sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
        sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
        let id = self.module
            .declare_function("__dmc_forge_alloc", Linkage::Import, &sig)
            .map_err(|e| JitError {
                msg: format!("declare forge_alloc: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0,
            })?;
        self.fns.insert("__dmc_forge_alloc".to_string(), FnEntry {
            id, sig,
            params: vec![("bytes".to_string(), TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64),
                Span { line: 0, col: 0, start: 0, end: 0 })],
            ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64),
            mut_param_idxs: vec![],
        });
        // forge.snapshot() -> i64  /  forge.restore(mark: i64) -> nil
        {
            let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
            sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
            let id = self.module
                .declare_function("__dmc_forge_snapshot", Linkage::Import, &sig)
                .map_err(|e| JitError {
                    msg: format!("declare forge_snapshot: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0,
                })?;
            self.fns.insert("__dmc_forge_snapshot".to_string(), FnEntry {
                id, sig, params: vec![], ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), mut_param_idxs: vec![],
            });
        }
        {
            let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
            let id = self.module
                .declare_function("__dmc_forge_restore", Linkage::Import, &sig)
                .map_err(|e| JitError {
                    msg: format!("declare forge_restore: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0,
                })?;
            self.fns.insert("__dmc_forge_restore".to_string(), FnEntry {
                id, sig, params: vec![], ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil), mut_param_idxs: vec![],
            });
        }

        // print_tensor_1d_f32(ptr, n)
        let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
        sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
        let id = self.module
            .declare_function("__dmc_print_tensor_1d_f32", Linkage::Import, &sig)
            .map_err(|e| JitError {
                msg: format!("declare print_tensor_1d_f32: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0,
            })?;
        self.fns.insert("__dmc_print_tensor_1d_f32".to_string(), FnEntry {
            id, sig,
            params: vec![],
            ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil), mut_param_idxs: vec![],
        });
        // print_tensor_2d_f32(ptr, rows, cols)
        let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
        sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
        let id = self.module
            .declare_function("__dmc_print_tensor_2d_f32", Linkage::Import, &sig)
            .map_err(|e| JitError {
                msg: format!("declare print_tensor_2d_f32: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0,
            })?;
        self.fns.insert("__dmc_print_tensor_2d_f32".to_string(), FnEntry {
            id, sig,
            params: vec![],
            ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil), mut_param_idxs: vec![],
        });

        // Scalar math: f32->f32 builtins used by tensor kernels and GeLU.
        for sym in &["__dmc_exp_f32", "__dmc_sqrt_f32", "__dmc_log_f32",
                     "__dmc_sin_f32", "__dmc_cos_f32", "__dmc_tanh_f32",
                     "__dmc_gelu_f32", "__dmc_sigmoid_f32", "__dmc_silu_f32",
                     "__dmc_elu_f32", "__dmc_mish_f32",
                     "__dmc_silu_deriv_f32", "__dmc_elu_deriv_f32", "__dmc_mish_deriv_f32"] {
            let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::F32));
            sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::F32));
            sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
            let id = self.module
                .declare_function(sym, Linkage::Import, &sig)
                .map_err(|e| JitError {
                    msg: format!("declare {}: {}", sym, e), line: 0, col: 0,
                })?;
            self.fns.insert(sym.to_string(), FnEntry {
                id, sig,
                params: vec![("x".to_string(), TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32),
                    Span { line: 0, col: 0, start: 0, end: 0 })],
                ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32),
                mut_param_idxs: vec![],
            });
        }
        // #209: f64 scalar-math builtins (`exp`/`sqrt`/`log`/`sin`/`cos`), used
        // only by the scalar dispatch so scalar transcendentals match the
        // interpreter's f64 precision. The f32 variants above remain for kernels.
        for sym in &["__dmc_exp_f64", "__dmc_sqrt_f64", "__dmc_log_f64",
                     "__dmc_sin_f64", "__dmc_cos_f64"] {
            let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::F64));
            sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::F64));
            sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
            let id = self.module
                .declare_function(sym, Linkage::Import, &sig)
                .map_err(|e| JitError {
                    msg: format!("declare {}: {}", sym, e), line: 0, col: 0,
                })?;
            self.fns.insert(sym.to_string(), FnEntry {
                id, sig,
                params: vec![("x".to_string(), TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F64),
                    Span { line: 0, col: 0, start: 0, end: 0 })],
                ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F64),
                mut_param_idxs: vec![],
            });
        }
        // capture_grad(param_idx: i64, ptr: i64, nbytes: i64) -> nil
        // Used by @grad fn's fwd_bwd lowering to publish each mut param's
        // gradient pointer to the host (read via take_grads()). nbytes lets
        // the grad-call epilogue relocate the buffer during compaction.
        let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
        sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
        let id = self.module
            .declare_function("__dmc_capture_grad", Linkage::Import, &sig)
            .map_err(|e| JitError {
                msg: format!("declare capture_grad: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0,
            })?;
        self.fns.insert("__dmc_capture_grad".to_string(), FnEntry {
            id, sig, params: vec![], ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil), mut_param_idxs: vec![],
        });
        // grad_prologue() -> i64  /  grad_epilogue(mark: i64) -> nil
        // AUTODIFF.md §3 automatic activation lifetime: a compiled grad fn
        // snapshots the forge at entry and, at exit, compacts its published
        // gradients down to that watermark, reclaiming every activation.
        {
            let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
            sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
            let id = self.module
                .declare_function("__dmc_grad_prologue", Linkage::Import, &sig)
                .map_err(|e| JitError {
                    msg: format!("declare grad_prologue: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0,
                })?;
            self.fns.insert("__dmc_grad_prologue".to_string(), FnEntry {
                id, sig, params: vec![], ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64),
                mut_param_idxs: vec![],
            });
        }
        {
            let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
            let id = self.module
                .declare_function("__dmc_grad_epilogue", Linkage::Import, &sig)
                .map_err(|e| JitError {
                    msg: format!("declare grad_epilogue: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0,
                })?;
            self.fns.insert("__dmc_grad_epilogue".to_string(), FnEntry {
                id, sig, params: vec![], ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil),
                mut_param_idxs: vec![],
            });
        }
        // take_grad_at(param_idx: i64) -> i64 — read the captured grad ptr for
        // the given mutable parameter index without draining GRAD_SLOTS.
        // Called by fwd_bwd destructuring to retrieve each mut param's gradient.
        {
            let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
            let id = self.module
                .declare_function("__dmc_take_grad_at", Linkage::Import, &sig)
                .map_err(|e| JitError {
                    msg: format!("declare take_grad_at: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0,
                })?;
            self.fns.insert("__dmc_take_grad_at".to_string(), FnEntry {
                id, sig, params: vec![], ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64),
                mut_param_idxs: vec![],
            });
        }
        // powf(base: f32, exp: f32) -> f32 — backs elementwise `.^` on
        // tensors (e.g. `(x .* x) .^ 0.5`). Two f32 params; otherwise the
        // same import shape as the scalar-math symbols above.
        let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::F32));
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::F32));
        sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::F32));
        sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
        let id = self.module
            .declare_function("__dmc_powf_f32", Linkage::Import, &sig)
            .map_err(|e| JitError {
                msg: format!("declare powf: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0,
            })?;
        self.fns.insert("__dmc_powf_f32".to_string(), FnEntry {
            id, sig, params: vec![], ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32), mut_param_idxs: vec![],
        });
        // #261: powf(base: f64, exp: f64) -> f64 — backs the scalar `**` operator.
        // Scalar float arithmetic runs in f64 (#209), so `**` lowers to this f64
        // variant to match the interpreter's `a.powf(b)` precision.
        let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::F64));
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::F64));
        sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::F64));
        sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
        let id = self.module
            .declare_function("__dmc_powf_f64", Linkage::Import, &sig)
            .map_err(|e| JitError {
                msg: format!("declare powf_f64: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0,
            })?;
        self.fns.insert("__dmc_powf_f64".to_string(), FnEntry {
            id, sig, params: vec![], ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F64), mut_param_idxs: vec![],
        });
        // #289: fmod(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 — backs scalar float `%`. The
        // checker types float `%` and the interpreter computes Rust `a % b`
        // (truncated fmod); without this the JIT rejected such programs.
        let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::F64));
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::F64));
        sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::F64));
        sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
        let id = self.module
            .declare_function("__dmc_fmod_f64", Linkage::Import, &sig)
            .map_err(|e| JitError {
                msg: format!("declare fmod_f64: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0,
            })?;
        self.fns.insert("__dmc_fmod_f64".to_string(), FnEntry {
            id, sig, params: vec![], ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F64), mut_param_idxs: vec![],
        });

        // ── String builtins ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
        // __dmc_str_new_from_raw(data_ptr: i64, len: i64) -> i64
        {
            let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
            let id = self.module
                .declare_function("__dmc_str_new_from_raw", Linkage::Import, &sig)
                .map_err(|e| JitError { msg: format!("declare __dmc_str_new_from_raw: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0 })?;
            self.fns.insert("__dmc_str_new_from_raw".to_string(), FnEntry {
                id, sig, params: vec![], ret: TyKind::Str, mut_param_idxs: vec![],
            });
        }
        // __dmc_str_len(s: i64) -> i64
        {
            let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
            let id = self.module
                .declare_function("__dmc_str_len", Linkage::Import, &sig)
                .map_err(|e| JitError { msg: format!("declare __dmc_str_len: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0 })?;
            self.fns.insert("__dmc_str_len".to_string(), FnEntry {
                id, sig, params: vec![], ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), mut_param_idxs: vec![],
            });
        }
        // __dmc_str_get_char(s: i64, i: i64) -> i64
        {
            let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
            let id = self.module
                .declare_function("__dmc_str_get_char", Linkage::Import, &sig)
                .map_err(|e| JitError { msg: format!("declare __dmc_str_get_char: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0 })?;
            self.fns.insert("__dmc_str_get_char".to_string(), FnEntry {
                id, sig, params: vec![], ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), mut_param_idxs: vec![],
            });
        }
        // __dmc_str_eq(s1: i64, s2: i64) -> i64
        {
            let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
            let id = self.module
                .declare_function("__dmc_str_eq", Linkage::Import, &sig)
                .map_err(|e| JitError { msg: format!("declare __dmc_str_eq: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0 })?;
            self.fns.insert("__dmc_str_eq".to_string(), FnEntry {
                id, sig, params: vec![], ret: TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), mut_param_idxs: vec![],
            });
        }
        // __dmc_str_concat(s1: i64, s2: i64) -> i64
        {
            let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
            sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
            let id = self.module
                .declare_function("__dmc_str_concat", Linkage::Import, &sig)

    fn define_fn(&mut self, meta: &FnMeta) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        self.ctx.func.signature = meta.sig.clone();
        self.ctx.func.name = UserFuncName::user(0, meta.id.as_u32());

        let mut builder = FunctionBuilder::new(&mut self.ctx.func, &mut self.builder_ctx);
        let entry = builder.create_block();
        builder.append_block_params_for_function_params(entry);
        builder.switch_to_block(entry);
        builder.seal_block(entry);

        let mut tr = Translator {
            builder,
            module: &mut self.module,
            fns: &mut self.fns,
            templates: &self.templates,
            pending: &mut self.pending,
            grad_schemas: &self.grad_schemas,
            model_layouts: &self.model_layouts,
            model_shape_params: &self.model_shape_params,
            model_field_asts: &self.model_field_asts,
            global_consts: &self.global_consts,
            enums: &self.enums,
            enum_payload_layouts: &self.enum_payload_layouts,
            pending_lambdas: &mut self.pending_lambdas,
            lambda_counter: &mut self.lambda_counter,
            locals: HashMap::new(),
            local_tys: HashMap::new(),
            ret: meta.ret.clone(),
            gpu: self.gpu,
            loop_stack: Vec::new(),
            shape_env: meta.shape_env.clone(),
            block_filled: false,
            ad: if matches!(meta.grad_mode, GradMode::FwdBwd | GradMode::FwdBwdBwd) {
                Some(AdState::new())
            } else { None },
        };

        // ── Trampoline body ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
        // A named-fn trampoline has captures[0].0 starting with
        // "__trampoline_target:". It ignores __env (block_params[0]) and
        // forwards all remaining args to the real function.
        if meta.captures.first().map(|(n, _)| n.starts_with("__trampoline_target:")).unwrap_or(false) {
            let target_name = meta.captures[0].0
                .strip_prefix("__trampoline_target:")
                .unwrap()
                .to_string();
            // block_params: [__env, p0, p1, ...]
            // Skip __env (index 0); pass p0..pN to the real function.
            let real_entry = tr.fns.get(&target_name).cloned().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                msg: format!("trampoline: target fn `{}` not found", target_name),
                line: meta.span.line, col: meta.span.col,
            })?;
            let func_ref = tr.module.declare_func_in_func(real_entry.id, tr.builder.func);
            let n_params = tr.builder.block_params(entry).len();
            let fwd_args: Vec<Value> = (1..n_params)
                .map(|i| tr.builder.block_params(entry)[i])
                .collect();
            let call = tr.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &fwd_args);
            let returns_value = !matches!(meta.ret, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil));
            if returns_value {
                let ret_val = tr.builder.inst_results(call)[0];
                tr.builder.ins().return_(&[ret_val]);
            } else {
                tr.builder.ins().return_(&[]);
            }
            tr.block_filled = true;
            tr.builder.seal_all_blocks();
            let frontend_config = tr.module.target_config();
            tr.builder.finalize(frontend_config);
            let __cg = std::time::Instant::now();
            self.module
                .define_function(meta.id, &mut self.ctx)
                .map_err(|e| JitError {
                    msg: format!("define `{}`: {}", meta.name, e),
                    line: meta.span.line, col: meta.span.col,
                })?;
            JIT_CODEGEN_NS.fetch_add(__cg.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
            self.module.clear_context(&mut self.ctx);
            return Ok(());
        }

        // Bind parameters. In AD (FwdBwd) mode, each tensor param also gets
        // an AD leaf node so gradients can flow back to it.
        // For lambdas, params[0] is "__env" (i64); user params start at index 1.
        // We detect the closure convention by checking for a leading "__env" param.
        let has_env_param = meta.params.first()
            .map(|(n, _, _)| n == "__env")
            .unwrap_or(false);
        let user_params_start = if has_env_param { 1 } else { 0 };
        for (i, (name, ty, _span)) in meta.params.iter().enumerate() {
            let v = tr.builder.declare_var(ty.cl());
            let arg = tr.builder.block_params(entry)[i];
            tr.builder.def_var(v, arg);
            tr.locals.insert(name.clone(), v);
            tr.local_tys.insert(name.clone(), ty.clone());
            if i < user_params_start { continue; } // skip __env for AD
            if let Some(st) = tr.ad.as_mut() {
                if ty.is_tensor() {
                    let ad_i = i - user_params_start;
                    let node = st.push(AdOp::Leaf, vec![], ty.clone(), arg);
                    st.env.insert(name.clone(), node);
                    if meta.mut_param_idxs.contains(&ad_i) {
                        st.mut_params.push((ad_i, node));
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        // ── Restore captured variables from env array ────────────────────────
        // For lambdas with captures, __env holds a pointer to a flat i64 array.
        // Load each capture and bind it as a local before the user body runs.
        if !meta.captures.is_empty() {
            let env_ptr = tr.builder.block_params(entry)[0]; // __env
            let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
            for (k, (cap_name, cap_ty)) in meta.captures.iter().enumerate() {
                let raw = tr.builder.ins().load(
                    cl::I64, flags, env_ptr, (k as i32) * 8,
                );
                // Reinterpret the raw i64 to the capture's declared type.
                let val = match cap_ty {
                    TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32) => {
                        let narrow = tr.builder.ins().ireduce(cl::I32, raw);
                        tr.builder.ins().bitcast(cl::F32, cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new(), narrow)
                    }
                    TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F64) => {
                        tr.builder.ins().bitcast(cl::F64, cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new(), raw)
                    }
                    TyKind::Scalar(sk) if sk.cl() != cl::I64 => {
                        tr.builder.ins().ireduce(sk.cl(), raw)
                    }
                    _ => raw, // i64, pointers, fat ptrs — already i64
                };
                let var = tr.builder.declare_var(cap_ty.cl());
                tr.builder.def_var(var, val);
                tr.locals.insert(cap_name.clone(), var);
                tr.local_tys.insert(cap_name.clone(), cap_ty.clone());
            }
        }

        if matches!(meta.grad_mode, GradMode::FwdBwd | GradMode::FwdBwdBwd) {
            // AD path: lower the body recording the graph, then emit the
            // backward pass and publish gradients before returning the loss.
            //
            // AUTODIFF.md §3 activation lifetime: the call snapshots the forge
            // at entry (prologue, which also clears stale grad slots) and, just
            // before returning, compacts the published gradients down to that
            // watermark (epilogue) — every activation the call allocated is
            // reclaimed in one cursor rewind, and the grads stay valid (never
            // dangling) until the caller rewinds past them.
            let mark_v = tr.call_import0("__dmc_grad_prologue");
            let (loss_v, loss_node) = tr.ad_lower_block(&meta.body, &meta.span)?;
            tr.ad.as_mut().unwrap().loss = Some(loss_node);
            if meta.grad_mode == GradMode::FwdBwdBwd {
                // Double-grad path: tape the backward pass into a new AdState,
                // then run emit_backward on that to get the second derivative.
                let fwd_ad = tr.ad.take().expect("FwdBwdBwd needs AD state");
                let bwd_ad = tr.tape_backward(fwd_ad, &meta.span)?;
                tr.ad = Some(bwd_ad);
                let _grads2 = tr.emit_backward(&meta.span)?;
                if !tr.is_filled() {
                    tr.call_import1("__dmc_grad_epilogue", mark_v);
                    tr.builder.ins().return_(&[loss_v]);
                    tr.block_filled = true;
                }
            } else {
                let _grads = tr.emit_backward(&meta.span)?;
                if !tr.is_filled() {
                    // Return the f32 loss. Grad pointers are published via
                    // capture_grad and retrieved by the caller through take_grad_at.
                    tr.call_import1("__dmc_grad_epilogue", mark_v);
                    tr.builder.ins().return_(&[loss_v]);
                    tr.block_filled = true;
                }
            }
        } else {
            // Ordinary (and forward-only @grad) path.
            //
            // The forward-only entry of a `@grad fn` gets the same automatic
            // activation lifetime: its return value is a scalar (in a
            // register), so everything it allocated can be reclaimed at exit.
            // Gated on a scalar return so an ordinary fn is never wrapped.
            let fwd_only_scope = meta.grad_mode == GradMode::Forward
                && matches!(meta.ret, TyKind::Scalar(k) if k != ScalarKind::Nil);
            let mark_v = if fwd_only_scope {
                Some(tr.call_import0("__dmc_forge_snapshot"))
            } else { None };
            let tail_val = tr.lower_block_value(&meta.body)?;
            if !tr.is_filled() {
                match (&meta.ret, tail_val) {
                    (TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil), _) => { tr.ret_void(); }
                    (want, Some((v, k))) => {
                        let v = tr.coerce_to(v, &k, want, &meta.span)?;
                        if let Some(mark_v) = mark_v {
                            tr.call_import1("__dmc_forge_restore", mark_v);
                        }
                        tr.ret_val(v);
                    }
                    (want, None) => return err(&meta.span, format!(
                        "function `{}` returns `{}` but body has no value",
                        meta.name, want.render(),
                    )),
                }
            }
        }

        tr.builder.seal_all_blocks();
        let frontend_config = tr.module.target_config();
        tr.builder.finalize(frontend_config);

        let __cg = std::time::Instant::now();
        self.module
            .define_function(meta.id, &mut self.ctx)
            .map_err(|e| JitError {
                msg: format!("define `{}`: {}", meta.name, e),
                line: meta.span.line, col: meta.span.col,
            })?;
        JIT_CODEGEN_NS.fetch_add(__cg.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.module.clear_context(&mut self.ctx);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Look up the compiled `main` function and invoke it.
    /// Returns the i64 produced (or 0 if `main` returns nil/non-int).
    /// Run a zero-arg `test_*` under the JIT and return whether it passed. Used
    /// by `dmc test --jit` to run the in-language `test_*` functions under the
    /// JIT as well as the interpreter — turning each into a parity gate. Mirrors
    /// the interpreter's contract: a `bool` test passes iff it returns true, a
    /// `nil` test passes iff it runs to completion. The program must already be
    /// compiled (and finalized).
    pub fn run_test_fn(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<bool, JitError> {
        let meta = self.fns.get(name).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("no `fn {}()` to JIT-execute", name), line: 0, col: 0,
        })?.clone();
        if !meta.params.is_empty() {
            return Err(JitError { msg: format!("`{}` must take no arguments", name), line: 0, col: 0 });
        }
        let ptr = self.module.get_finalized_function(meta.id);
        match meta.ret {
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Bool) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> u8 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                Ok(unsafe { f() } != 0)
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                unsafe { f(); }
                Ok(true) // ran to completion
            }
            _ => Err(JitError { msg: format!("test `{}` must return bool or nil", name), line: 0, col: 0 }),
        }
    }

    pub fn run_main(&mut self) -> Result<i64, JitError> {
        let meta = self.fns.get("main").ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: "no `fn main()` to JIT-execute".into(), line: 0, col: 0,
        })?.clone();
        if !meta.params.is_empty() {
            return Err(JitError {
                msg: "`fn main` must take no arguments in the JIT".into(),
                line: 0, col: 0,
            });
        }
        let ptr = self.module.get_finalized_function(meta.id);
        match &meta.ret {
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                unsafe { f(); }
                Ok(0)
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> i64 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                Ok(unsafe { f() })
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I32) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> i32 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                Ok(unsafe { f() } as i64)
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Bool) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> u8 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                Ok(unsafe { f() } as i64)
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> f32 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                let v = unsafe { f() };
                println!("=> {}", v);
                Ok(0)
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F64) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> f64 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                let v = unsafe { f() };
                println!("=> {}", v);
                Ok(0)
            }
            TyKind::Tensor(_) => Err(JitError {
                msg: "main returning a Tensor is not supported (tensor lifetime crosses the JIT boundary)".into(),
                line: 0, col: 0,
            }),
            TyKind::KV(_) => Err(JitError {
                msg: "main returning a KV cache is not supported (its lifetime crosses the JIT boundary)".into(),
                line: 0, col: 0,
            }),
            TyKind::DynTensor(_) => Err(JitError {
                msg: "main returning a dynamic-shape tensor is not supported (its lifetime crosses the JIT boundary)".into(),
                line: 0, col: 0,
            }),
            TyKind::Model(_, _) => Err(JitError {
                msg: "main returning a model instance is not supported".into(),
                line: 0, col: 0,
            }),
            TyKind::Str => {
                // Returns an i64 forge pointer — return it as i64 so callers
                // can inspect it. (Str-returning main is valid for tests.)
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> i64 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                Ok(unsafe { f() })
            }
            TyKind::Map => {
                // Returns an i64 raw pointer to a HashMap — return it as i64.
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> i64 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                Ok(unsafe { f() })
            }
            TyKind::KvArray(_, _) => Err(JitError {
                msg: "main returning a KV array is not supported (lifetime crosses the JIT boundary)".into(),
                line: 0, col: 0,
            }),
            TyKind::ModelArray(_, _, _) => Err(JitError {
                msg: "main returning a model array is not supported (lifetime crosses the JIT boundary)".into(),
                line: 0, col: 0,
            }),
            TyKind::Fn(_, _) => Err(JitError {
                msg: "main returning a function pointer is not supported by the JIT runner".into(),
                line: 0, col: 0,
            }),
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::OptI64) => Err(JitError {
                msg: "main returning a maybe-nil value is not supported; compare to nil or guard with map_contains first".into(),
                line: 0, col: 0,
            }),
            TyKind::TritTensor(_) => Err(JitError {
                msg: "main returning a trit tensor is not supported (lifetime crosses the JIT boundary)".into(),
                line: 0, col: 0,
            }),
            TyKind::Bf16Tensor(_) => Err(JitError {
                msg: "main returning a bf16 tensor is not supported (lifetime crosses the JIT boundary)".into(),
                line: 0, col: 0,
            }),
            // #350: an enum is its i64 ordinal — return it like any integer.
            TyKind::Enum(_) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> i64 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                Ok(unsafe { f() })
            }
        }
    }

    /// JIT-execute `main` and return its scalar value *structurally* — the
    /// differential-testing counterpart to `run_main` (`dmc selftest`, #408).
    ///
    /// `run_main` prints float returns as a `=> <v>` REPL echo and hands back
    /// `0`, which is lossy: an in-process differ can't compare against the
    /// interpreter's value. This returns the value instead of printing it, for
    /// every scalar `main` the fuzzer can generate (i64 / f32 / bool, plus
    /// f64 / nil for completeness). Non-scalar returns are outside the scalar
    /// fuzz regime and error cleanly.
    pub fn run_main_scalar(&mut self) -> Result<ScalarRet, JitError> {
        let meta = self.fns.get("main").ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: "no `fn main()` to JIT-execute".into(), line: 0, col: 0,
        })?.clone();
        if !meta.params.is_empty() {
            return Err(JitError {
                msg: "`fn main` must take no arguments in the JIT".into(),
                line: 0, col: 0,
            });
        }
        let ptr = self.module.get_finalized_function(meta.id);
        match &meta.ret {
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                unsafe { f(); }
                Ok(ScalarRet::Nil)
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> i64 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                Ok(ScalarRet::I64(unsafe { f() }))
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I32) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> i32 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                Ok(ScalarRet::I64(unsafe { f() } as i64))
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Bool) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> u8 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                Ok(ScalarRet::Bool(unsafe { f() } != 0))
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> f32 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                Ok(ScalarRet::F32(unsafe { f() }))
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F64) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> f64 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                Ok(ScalarRet::F64(unsafe { f() }))
            }
            TyKind::Enum(_) => {
                let f: unsafe extern "C" fn() -> i64 = unsafe { mem::transmute(ptr) };
                Ok(ScalarRet::I64(unsafe { f() }))
            }
            other => Err(JitError {
                msg: format!("selftest: main returns non-scalar type {:?} (outside scalar fuzz regime)", other),
                line: 0, col: 0,
            }),
        }
    }

    /// Pointer to a finalized function by mangled name (test/host helper).
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn func_ptr(&self, name: &str) -> Option<*const u8> {
        self.fns.get(name).map(|e| self.module.get_finalized_function(e.id))
    }
}

/// Structural scalar return value of a JIT-executed `main`, for the in-process
/// interp-vs-JIT differential fuzzer (`dmc selftest`, #408). See `run_main_scalar`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub enum ScalarRet {
    Nil,
    I64(i64),
    Bool(bool),
    F32(f32),
    F64(f64),
}

// Cranelift's JIT module owns mmap'd executable pages. We let them live until
// process exit — leaks are bounded by Jit instance count (one per `dmc jit`
// invocation, one per test). Wrapping in a manual free path requires moving
// out of `self`, which conflicts with `Drop`.

/// One axis of a tensor index expression, classified for slicing.
enum IndexCat {
    /// Single integer index — drops the axis.
    Scalar(Value),
    /// `:` or `..` — keeps the axis at its full extent.
    Full,
    /// `a:b` — keeps the axis at `b - a` (must be literal-int in slice 4).
    Range { start: i64, end: i64 },
}

fn classify_index_static(ie: &IndexElem, span: &Span) -> Result<StaticIndexCat, JitError> {
    match ie {
        // #276: a bounded range in an index (`t[.., 4..5, ..]`) parses as
        // `IndexElem::Expr(Expr::Range)`, not `IndexElem::Slice`. Recognize it as
        // a range with literal bounds (exclusive `a..b`, inclusive `a..=b`).
        IndexElem::Expr(Expr::Range { start, end, inclusive, .. }) => {
            let s = lit_int(start.as_deref()).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                msg: "range slice start must be a literal int in the JIT".into(),
                line: span.line, col: span.col,
            })?;
            let e = lit_int(end.as_deref()).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                msg: "range slice end must be a literal int in the JIT".into(),
                line: span.line, col: span.col,
            })?;
            Ok(StaticIndexCat::Range { start: s, end: if *inclusive { e + 1 } else { e } })
        }
        IndexElem::Expr(_) => Ok(StaticIndexCat::Scalar),
        IndexElem::FullSlice(_) => Ok(StaticIndexCat::Full),
        IndexElem::Slice { start, end, step, .. } => {
            if step.is_some() {
                return err(span, "strided slices (`a:b:c`) need slice-5 support");
            }
            let s = lit_int(start.as_deref()).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                msg: "slice start must be a literal int in slice 4".into(),
                line: span.line, col: span.col,
            })?;
            let e = lit_int(end.as_deref()).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                msg: "slice end must be a literal int in slice 4".into(),
                line: span.line, col: span.col,
            })?;
            Ok(StaticIndexCat::Range { start: s, end: e })
        }
    }
}

enum StaticIndexCat { Scalar, Full, Range { start: i64, end: i64 } }

fn lit_int(e: Option<&Expr>) -> Option<i64> {
    match e? {
        Expr::Literal(Literal::Int(n, _), _) => Some(*n),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Detect `<recv>.split[n, axis=k]` — the tensor-split surface (SPEC §6.4),
/// returning the receiver, the piece-count expr, and the optional `axis=` expr.
/// The `.split[...]` *bracket* form is unambiguously tensor-split (string/list
/// `.split(...)` is a `Call` node, not a bracket), mirroring the checker at
/// check.rs:tensor_split_type and the interpreter's eval_tensor_split dispatch.
fn as_tensor_split_call(e: &Expr) -> Option<(&Expr, &Expr, Option<&Expr>)> {
    let Expr::Postfix { expr, op, .. } = e else { return None; };
    let Expr::Postfix { expr: recv, op: PostfixOp::Field(fname), .. } = expr.as_ref() else {
        return None;
    };
    if fname != "split" { return None; }
    let mut positional: Vec<&Expr> = Vec::new();
    let mut axis: Option<&Expr> = None;
    match op {
        // `t.split[3, axis=-1]` — a named `axis=` arg forces the BracketArgs form.
        PostfixOp::BracketArgs(args) => {
            for a in args {
                match a {
                    CallArg::Positional(x) => positional.push(x),
                    CallArg::Named { name, value, .. } if name == "axis" => axis = Some(value),
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
        }
        // `t.split[3]` (no named arg) may parse as an Index; axis defaults to -1.
        PostfixOp::Index(elems) => {
            for el in elems {
                if let IndexElem::Expr(x) = el { positional.push(x); }
            }
        }
        _ => return None,
    }
    let n = positional.into_iter().next()?;
    Some((recv, n, axis))
}

/// Detect `ident.fwd_bwd(args)` / `ident.fwd_bwd_bwd(args)` — the autodiff
/// source surface. Returns the `@grad fn` name, the method, and the call args.
fn as_fwd_bwd_call(e: &Expr) -> Option<(&str, &str, &[CallArg])> {
    if let Expr::Postfix { expr, op: PostfixOp::Call(args), .. } = e {
        if let Expr::Postfix { expr: inner, op: PostfixOp::Field(m), .. } = expr.as_ref() {
            if m == "fwd_bwd" || m == "fwd_bwd_bwd" {
                if let Expr::Ident(name, _) = inner.as_ref() {
                    return Some((name.as_str(), m.as_str(), args));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

/// #249: true when `e` reads an existing binding (an alias to storage owned
/// elsewhere) rather than producing a fresh, owned temporary. Binding such a
/// value, storing it in a struct field, or passing it by value must deep-copy
/// the tensor so a later write through the source can't leak through — the
/// interpreter clones on every such read. Constructors, elementwise/matmul ops,
/// reductions, transposes, and calls all yield fresh owned tensors and need no
/// copy. A 1-element tuple is transparent parens (`(x)`), so see through it.
/// #263: the base model name of a constructor element-type argument — bare
/// (`Foo`) or parameterized (`Bar[4]`, which parses as an Index/BracketArgs
/// postfix over the model ident). The parameterization doesn't affect a
/// ModelArray's allocation (each slot is a pointer; instances are sized and
/// filled later), so callers key on this base name in `model_layouts`.
/// Recognize a `KV[elem, [.., ~, ..]]` *type expression* used as the element of
/// a forge staging constructor (`forge.uninit[KV[...], [L]]`) and build its KvTy
