/// with capacity unknown — each slot is filled later by `arr[i] = forge.kv(...)`.
/// Returns None if `e` isn't a `KV[...]` expression. (#273 follow-up: per-layer
/// KV-cache staging arrays in the Qwen3 port.)
fn kv_ctor_elem_ty(e: &Expr, env: &HashMap<String, i64>, span: &Span)
    -> Option<Result<KvTy, JitError>>
{
    let targs: Vec<&Expr> = match e {
        Expr::Postfix { expr, op: PostfixOp::Index(idxs), .. }
            if matches!(expr.as_ref(), Expr::Ident(n, _) if n == "KV") =>
            idxs.iter().filter_map(|el| match el { IndexElem::Expr(x) => Some(x), _ => None }).collect(),
        Expr::Postfix { expr, op: PostfixOp::BracketArgs(args), .. }
            if matches!(expr.as_ref(), Expr::Ident(n, _) if n == "KV") =>
            args.iter().filter_map(|a| match a {
                CallArg::Positional(x) => Some(x),
                CallArg::Named { value, .. } => Some(value),
                _ => None }).collect(),
        _ => return None,
    };
    if targs.len() != 2 {
        return Some(err(span, "`KV[...]` element type needs a dtype and a shape: `KV[f32, [.., ~, ..]]`"));
    }
    match targs[0] {
        Expr::Ident(t, _) if matches!(t.as_str(), "f32" | "bf16" | "f16" | "tf32") => {}
        _ => return Some(err(span, "JIT KV element type must be f32 or bf16/f16 (computed as f32)")),
    }
    let elems = match targs[1] {
        Expr::TensorLit(es, _) => es,
        _ => return Some(err(span, "`KV[...]` shape must be a literal like `[B, ~, D]`")),
    };
    let mut dims: Vec<i64> = Vec::new();
    let mut stream_axis: Option<usize> = None;
    for (i, el) in elems.iter().enumerate() {
        if is_streaming_expr(el) {
            if stream_axis.is_some() {
                return Some(err(span, "`KV[...]` shape may have only one streaming `~` axis"));
            }
            stream_axis = Some(i);
        } else {
            match resolve_shape_expr(el, env, span) {
                Ok(v) if v > 0 => dims.push(v),
                Ok(v) => return Some(err(span, format!("`KV[...]` dim must be > 0, got {}", v))),
                Err(e) => return Some(Err(e)),
            }
        }
    }
    let stream_axis = match stream_axis {
        Some(s) => s,
        None => return Some(err(span, "`KV[...]` shape must contain a streaming `~` axis")),
    };
    Some(Ok(KvTy { elem: ScalarKind::F32, dims, stream_axis, cap: None }))
}

fn model_ctor_base_name(e: &Expr) -> Option<&str> {
    match e {
        Expr::Ident(n, _) => Some(n.as_str()),
        Expr::Postfix { expr, op: PostfixOp::Index(_), .. }
        | Expr::Postfix { expr, op: PostfixOp::BracketArgs(_), .. } => match expr.as_ref() {
            Expr::Ident(n, _) => Some(n.as_str()),
            _ => None,
        },
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// #267: resolve expressions to concrete dimension values, best-effort — a
/// non-constant / unbound arg is dropped. Captures a parameterized model's
/// concrete type args at the point of construction.
fn resolve_dim_exprs<'a>(exprs: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Expr>, env: &HashMap<String, i64>) -> Vec<i64> {
    let sp = Span { line: 0, col: 0, start: 0, end: 0 };
    exprs.filter_map(|e| resolve_shape_expr(e, env, &sp).ok()).collect()
}

/// #267: concrete type-arg dims from a `Type::Named`'s args (`Bar[4]` → `[4]`).
fn type_named_dims(args: &[TypeArg], env: &HashMap<String, i64>) -> Vec<i64> {
    let sp = Span { line: 0, col: 0, start: 0, end: 0 };
    args.iter().filter_map(|a| match a {
        TypeArg::Expr(e) => resolve_shape_expr(e, env, &sp).ok(),
        TypeArg::Named { value, .. } => resolve_shape_expr(value, env, &sp).ok(),
        // A bare type-name arg (`Attn[D]`, where D is a shape param) parses as a
        // Type::Named, not an Expr — resolve it via the env so a *nested*
        // parameterized model field (`attn: QwenAttn[H_q, D, ..]`) keeps its args.
        TypeArg::Type(Type::Named { name, args: ta, .. }) if ta.is_empty() =>
            env.get(name).copied(),
        TypeArg::Type(_) => None,
    }).collect()
}

/// #267: concrete type-arg dims from a constructor element expr (`Bar[4]`) —
/// an Index/BracketArgs postfix over the model ident.
fn model_ctor_dims(e: &Expr, env: &HashMap<String, i64>) -> Vec<i64> {
    match e {
        Expr::Postfix { op: PostfixOp::Index(idxs), .. } =>
            resolve_dim_exprs(idxs.iter().filter_map(|el| match el {
                IndexElem::Expr(x) => Some(x), _ => None }), env),
        Expr::Postfix { op: PostfixOp::BracketArgs(args), .. } =>
            resolve_dim_exprs(args.iter().filter_map(|a| match a {
                CallArg::Positional(x) => Some(x),
                CallArg::Named { value, .. } => Some(value),
                _ => None }), env),
        _ => Vec::new(),
    }
}

/// #268: a compile-time-constant scalar literal (admissible as a top-level
/// module constant) — an int/float/bool literal, a negation of one, or a
/// 1-tuple wrapping one (transparent parens).
fn is_const_literal_expr(e: &Expr) -> bool {
    match e {
        Expr::Literal(Literal::Int(_, _), _)
        | Expr::Literal(Literal::Float(_, _), _)
        | Expr::Literal(Literal::Bool(_), _) => true,
        Expr::UnOp { op: UnOp::Neg, operand, .. } => is_const_literal_expr(operand),
        Expr::Tuple(elems, _) if elems.len() == 1 => is_const_literal_expr(&elems[0]),
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn is_aliasing_place_expr(e: &Expr) -> bool {
    match e {
        Expr::Ident(..) => true,
        Expr::Postfix { op: PostfixOp::Field(_), .. } => true,
        // A sub-tensor row view (`grid[0]`) aliases the parent's storage. When
        // the index instead yields a scalar, the copy is a no-op (scalars never
        // alias), so this is safe to apply uniformly to index reads.
        Expr::Postfix { op: PostfixOp::Index(_), .. } => true,
        Expr::Tuple(elems, _) if elems.len() == 1 => is_aliasing_place_expr(&elems[0]),
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn row_major_strides(shape: &[i64]) -> Vec<i64> {
    let r = shape.len();
    let mut s = vec![1_i64; r];
    for i in (0..r.saturating_sub(1)).rev() {
        s[i] = s[i + 1] * shape[i + 1];
    }
    s
}

/// Right-align a shape to `rank` axes by prepending 1s (NumPy convention).
fn pad_left_shape(s: &[i64], rank: usize) -> Vec<i64> {
    let mut v = vec![1_i64; rank];
    let off = rank - s.len();
    for (i, &d) in s.iter().enumerate() { v[off + i] = d; }
    v
}

/// NumPy broadcast of two shapes, right-aligned. Each axis must be equal
/// or one of them 1; the result takes the max per axis.
fn broadcast_out_shape(a: &[i64], b: &[i64], span: &Span) -> Result<Vec<i64>, JitError> {
    let rank = a.len().max(b.len());
    let pa = pad_left_shape(a, rank);
    let pb = pad_left_shape(b, rank);
    let mut out = vec![0_i64; rank];
    for k in 0..rank {
        out[k] = if pa[k] == pb[k] { pa[k] }
            else if pa[k] == 1 { pb[k] }
            else if pb[k] == 1 { pa[k] }
            else {
                return err(span, format!(
                    "cannot broadcast axis {}: {} vs {}", k, pa[k], pb[k]));
            };
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Unify the template parameter's declared AST type against a concrete
/// argument's TyKind, binding shape parameters as a side effect.
fn unify_param_type(
    param_ty: &Type,
    arg_ty: &TyKind,
    bindings: &mut HashMap<String, i64>,
    pspan: &Span,
) -> Result<(), JitError> {
    match (param_ty, arg_ty) {
        (Type::Scalar(s, _), TyKind::Scalar(sk)) => {
            // Loose check: AST scalar type must match the lowered kind.
            // Use scalar_from_ast for the expected kind.
            let expected = scalar_from_ast(param_ty)?;
            // #209: scalar floats are f64 by default; an `f32` scalar annotation
            // is precision-cosmetic (f32 only matters inside tensors), so accept a
            // float arg for a float param regardless of width — the call coerces
            // the value to the param kind. Non-float kinds must match exactly.
            let ok = expected == *sk || (expected.is_float() && sk.is_float());
            if !ok {
                return err(pspan, format!(
                    "scalar arg mismatch: expected `{:?}`, got `{}`", s, sk.name(),
                ));
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        (Type::Tensor(elem_ast, shape_ast, span), TyKind::Tensor(tt)) => {
            // Map the declared element type the same way lower_ty_for_model does
            // (bf16/f16/tf32 compute as f32; bool keeps its kind; sub-narrow ints
            // widen to i32) so non-f32 tensor params like `Tensor[i64, [B,S]]`
            // (input_ids) and `Tensor[bf16, …]` (weights) bind. (#273 follow-up.)
            let expected_elem = match elem_ast.as_ref() {
                Type::Scalar(s, _) => match s {
                    ScalarType::F32 => ScalarKind::F32,
                    ScalarType::F64 => ScalarKind::F64,
                    ScalarType::I64 | ScalarType::U64 => ScalarKind::I64,
                    ScalarType::I32 | ScalarType::U32 => ScalarKind::I32,
                    ScalarType::Bf16 | ScalarType::F16 | ScalarType::Tf32 => ScalarKind::F32,
                    ScalarType::Bool => ScalarKind::Bool,
                    ScalarType::I8 | ScalarType::I16 | ScalarType::U8 | ScalarType::U16
                    | ScalarType::Int4 | ScalarType::Int8
                    | ScalarType::Fp8E4M3 | ScalarType::Fp8E5M2 => ScalarKind::I32,
                    _ => return err(span, "unsupported tensor template element type"),
                },
                _ => return err(span, "tensor template params must have a scalar element type"),
            };
            if tt.elem != expected_elem {
                return err(span, "element type mismatch in template instantiation");
            }
            // Shape: each dim is either a literal (must equal arg dim) or
            // an ident (bind / check consistency).
            if shape_ast.elems.len() != tt.shape.len() {
                return err(span, format!(
                    "rank mismatch: template expects {}, arg has {}",
                    shape_ast.elems.len(), tt.shape.len(),
                ));
            }
            for (i, d) in shape_ast.elems.iter().enumerate() {
                let want = match d {
                    ShapeElem::Expr(e) => e.as_ref(),
                    _ => return err(span,
                        "template shape elements must be literals or idents"),
                };
                let actual = tt.shape[i];
                match want {
                    Expr::Literal(Literal::Int(n, _), _) => {
                        if *n != actual {
                            return err(span, format!(
                                "shape mismatch at dim {}: expected {}, got {}",
                                i, n, actual,
                            ));
                        }
                    }
                    Expr::Ident(name, _) => {
                        if let Some(prev) = bindings.get(name) {
                            if *prev != actual {
                                return err(span, format!(
                                    "shape parameter `{}` would bind to {} but already bound to {}",
                                    name, actual, prev,
                                ));
                            }
                        } else {
                            bindings.insert(name.clone(), actual);
                        }
                    }
                    _ => return err(span, format!(
                        "template shape element `{:?}` is not a literal or ident",
                        want,
                    )),
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        (Type::KV(elem_ast, shape_ast, span), TyKind::KV(kv)) => {
            let expected_elem = match elem_ast.as_ref() {
                Type::Scalar(ScalarType::F32, _) => ScalarKind::F32,
                _ => return err(span, "KV template params must be f32 element"),
            };
            if kv.elem != expected_elem {
                return err(span, "element type mismatch in KV template instantiation");
            }
            if shape_ast.elems.len() != kv.rank() {
                return err(span, format!(
                    "KV rank mismatch: template expects {}, arg has {}",
                    shape_ast.elems.len(), kv.rank(),
                ));
            }
            for (i, d) in shape_ast.elems.iter().enumerate() {
                match d {
                    ShapeElem::Streaming(_) => {
                        if i != kv.stream_axis {
                            return err(span, format!(
                                "KV streaming axis mismatch: template `~` at dim {}, arg at dim {}",
                                i, kv.stream_axis,
                            ));
                        }
                    }
                    ShapeElem::Expr(e) => {
                        let actual = kv.dim_at(i);
                        match e.as_ref() {
                            Expr::Literal(Literal::Int(n, _), _) => {
                                if *n != actual {
                                    return err(span, format!(
                                        "KV shape mismatch at dim {}: expected {}, got {}",
                                        i, n, actual,
                                    ));
                                }
                            }
                            Expr::Ident(name, _) => {
                                if let Some(prev) = bindings.get(name) {
                                    if *prev != actual {
                                        return err(span, format!(
                                            "shape parameter `{}` would bind to {} but already bound to {}",
                                            name, actual, prev,
                                        ));
                                    }
                                } else {
                                    bindings.insert(name.clone(), actual);
                                }
                            }
                            _ => return err(span, "KV template shape element is not a literal or ident"),
                        }
                    }
                    _ => return err(span, "KV template shape elements must be `~`, literals, or idents"),
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        // Model param: `m: Qwen3_4B` (or parameterized `Foo[N]`). Bind any ident
        // type-args positionally from the model's concrete dims. (#273 follow-up.)
        (Type::Named { name, args, .. }, TyKind::Model(mname, mdims)) => {
            if name != mname {
                return err(pspan, format!(
                    "model arg mismatch: expected `{}`, got `{}`", name, mname));
            }
            for (i, a) in args.iter().enumerate() {
                let e = match a {
                    TypeArg::Expr(e) => e,
                    TypeArg::Named { value, .. } => value,
                    TypeArg::Type(_) => continue,
                };
                if let Expr::Ident(pn, _) = e.as_ref() {
                    if let Some(actual) = mdims.get(i).copied() {
                        bindings.entry(pn.clone()).or_insert(actual);
                    }
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        // `[KV[...]; N]` array param (per-layer KV caches): bind shape params
        // from the element KV's shape, mirroring the scalar KV arm. (#273.)
        (Type::Array(inner, _, span), TyKind::KvArray(kv, _)) => {
            let (elem_ast, shape_ast) = match inner.as_ref() {
                Type::KV(elem_ast, shape_ast, _) => (elem_ast, shape_ast),
                _ => return err(span, "KV array template param must wrap a `KV[...]` element"),
            };
            // bf16/f16/tf32 KV caches compute as f32 in the JIT (the bf16 no-op
            // convention, #176/#179), so accept them — the KvTy element is f32.
            let expected_elem = match elem_ast.as_ref() {
                Type::Scalar(ScalarType::F32, _)
                | Type::Scalar(ScalarType::Bf16, _)
                | Type::Scalar(ScalarType::F16, _)
                | Type::Scalar(ScalarType::Tf32, _) => ScalarKind::F32,
                _ => return err(span, "KV array template params must be f32/bf16/f16 element"),
            };
            if kv.elem != expected_elem {
                return err(span, "element type mismatch in KV array template instantiation");
            }
            if shape_ast.elems.len() != kv.rank() {
                return err(span, format!(
                    "KV array rank mismatch: template expects {}, arg has {}",
                    shape_ast.elems.len(), kv.rank()));
            }
            for (i, d) in shape_ast.elems.iter().enumerate() {
                match d {
                    ShapeElem::Streaming(_) => {
                        if i != kv.stream_axis {
                            return err(span, format!(
                                "KV streaming axis mismatch: template `~` at dim {}, arg at dim {}",
                                i, kv.stream_axis));
                        }
                    }
                    ShapeElem::Expr(e) => {
                        let actual = kv.dim_at(i);
                        match e.as_ref() {
                            Expr::Literal(Literal::Int(n, _), _) => {
                                if *n != actual {
                                    return err(span, format!(
                                        "KV array shape mismatch at dim {}: expected {}, got {}",
                                        i, n, actual));
                                }
                            }
                            Expr::Ident(name, _) => {
                                if let Some(prev) = bindings.get(name) {
                                    if *prev != actual {
                                        return err(span, format!(
                                            "shape parameter `{}` would bind to {} but already bound to {}",
                                            name, actual, prev));
                                    }
                                } else {
                                    bindings.insert(name.clone(), actual);
                                }
                            }
                            _ => return err(span, "KV array template shape element is not a literal or ident"),
                        }
                    }
                    _ => return err(span, "KV array template shape elements must be `~`, literals, or idents"),
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        // `[ModelName; N]` array param.
        (Type::Array(inner, _, span), TyKind::ModelArray(mname, _, _)) => {
            match inner.as_ref() {
                Type::Named { name, .. } if name == mname => Ok(()),
                Type::Named { name, .. } => err(span, format!(
                    "model array arg mismatch: expected `{}`, got `{}`", name, mname)),
                _ => err(span, "model array template param must wrap a model name"),
            }
        }
        (Type::Scalar(_, span), TyKind::Tensor(_))
        | (Type::Tensor(_, _, span), TyKind::Scalar(_)) => {
            err(span, "scalar/tensor kind mismatch in template arg")
        }
        _ => err(pspan, "JIT template params support scalar, Tensor, and KV types only"),
    }
}

fn mangle_mono_name(
    name: &str,
    shape_params: &[ShapeParam],
    bindings: &HashMap<String, i64>,
) -> String {
    let mut s = String::from(name);
    s.push('$');
    for (i, sp) in shape_params.iter().enumerate() {
        if i > 0 { s.push('_'); }
        // bindings is guaranteed populated by the caller
        let v = bindings.get(&sp.name).copied().unwrap_or(0);
        s.push_str(&format!("{}{}", sp.name, v));
    }
    s
}

/// Declare a template's specialized signature in the module under
/// `mangled` and return the resulting FnEntry. Body is not lowered here.
fn declare_template_signature(
    module: &mut JITModule,
    tmpl: &FnDecl,
    shape_env: &HashMap<String, i64>,
    mangled: &str,
    enums: &HashMap<String, Vec<String>>,
) -> Result<FnEntry, JitError> {
    let mut sig = module.make_signature();
    let mut params: Vec<(String, TyKind, Span)> = Vec::with_capacity(tmpl.params.len());
    let mut mut_param_idxs = Vec::new();
    for (idx, p) in tmpl.params.iter().enumerate() {
        let ty_ast = p.ty.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("template param `{}` needs a type annotation", p.name),
            line: p.span.line, col: p.span.col,
        })?;
        let ty = enumify(ty_from_ast(ty_ast, shape_env)?, enums);
        if matches!(ty, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)) {
            return err(&p.span, "`nil` parameters are not meaningful");
        }
        // #249: track `!` tensor params so the call site can copy-in/copy-out.
        if p.mutating { mut_param_idxs.push(idx); }
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(ty.cl()));
        params.push((p.name.clone(), ty, p.span.clone()));
    }
    let ret = match &tmpl.ret_type {
        Some(t) => enumify(ty_from_ast(t, shape_env)?, enums),
        None    => TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil),
    };
    if !matches!(ret, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)) {
        sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(ret.cl()));
    }
    sig.call_conv = CallConv::SystemV;
    let id = module
        .declare_function(mangled, Linkage::Export, &sig)
        .map_err(|e| JitError {
            msg: format!("declare_function `{}`: {}", mangled, e),
            line: tmpl.span.line, col: tmpl.span.col,
        })?;
    Ok(FnEntry { id, sig, params, ret, mut_param_idxs })
}

fn setting_err(e: cranelift::codegen::settings::SetError) -> JitError {
    JitError { msg: format!("cranelift setting: {}", e), line: 0, col: 0 }
}

// ─── Translator: per-function lowering ───────────────────────────────────────

struct Translator<'a> {
    builder: FunctionBuilder<'a>,
    module: &'a mut JITModule,
    fns: &'a mut HashMap<String, FnEntry>,
    templates: &'a HashMap<String, FnDecl>,
    pending: &'a mut Vec<PendingMono>,
    /// Multi-param `@grad fn` schemas — maps `$fn$fwd_bwd` → [(param, ty)...].
    /// Shared with `Jit::grad_schemas`; used by `lower_fwd_bwd_destructure`.
    grad_schemas: &'a HashMap<String, Vec<(String, TyKind, usize)>>,
    /// Model field layouts from `Jit::model_layouts`. Used by `lower_struct_lit`
    /// and field-access lowering.
    model_layouts: &'a HashMap<String, Vec<(String, TyKind)>>,
    /// #267: shared with `Jit` — shape-param names + field AST types per model,
    /// for re-resolving param-shaped fields against a parameterized instance's
    /// concrete type args during field-access lowering.
    model_shape_params: &'a HashMap<String, Vec<String>>,
    model_field_asts: &'a HashMap<String, Vec<(String, Type)>>,
    /// #268: top-level module constants — shared with `Jit`. Consulted by
    /// `lower_ident` for a bare-ident reference that isn't a local/shape-param/fn.
    global_consts: &'a HashMap<String, Expr>,
    /// #350: top-level enums — shared with `Jit`. Resolves `Color.Red` values
    /// and bare-variant `match` patterns against the scrutinee's variant set.
    enums: &'a HashMap<String, Vec<String>>,
    /// #350 Part 2b: payload-enum tagged-union layouts — shared with `Jit`.
    /// Present only for enums with a payload variant; drives construction,
    /// tag-loads, and `match`-arm payload binding.
    enum_payload_layouts: &'a HashMap<String, EnumLayout>,
    /// Deferred lambda bodies — shared with `Jit::pending_lambdas`.
    pending_lambdas: &'a mut Vec<FnMeta>,
    /// Counter for generating unique lambda names — shared with `Jit::lambda_counter`.
    lambda_counter: &'a mut usize,
    locals: HashMap<String, Variable>,
    local_tys: HashMap<String, TyKind>,
    ret: TyKind,
    /// #326: copied from `Jit::gpu` — route the m==1 bf16 decode GEMV to Metal.
    gpu: bool,
    loop_stack: Vec<LoopFrame>,
    /// Shape parameter bindings from the enclosing fn's monomorphization.
    /// Empty for non-generic fns. Used to resolve idents in tensor type
    /// annotations on `let` bindings, casts, and tensor-typed locals.
    shape_env: HashMap<String, i64>,
    /// True if the current block has already been terminated (jump / brif /
    /// return / trap). Cranelift doesn't expose `is_filled` publicly, so we
    /// track it ourselves. Reset on every `switch_to_block` via `enter`.
    block_filled: bool,
    /// Reverse-mode AD recording state. `Some` only while lowering the
    /// FwdBwd entry of a `@grad fn`. Forward lowering records a node per
    /// differentiable operation; after the body, the backward pass walks
    /// these in reverse to accumulate gradients.
    ad: Option<AdState>,
}

struct LoopFrame {
    header: Block,
    exit: Block,
}

// ─── Reverse-mode autodiff (@grad) ───────────────────────────────────────

/// A node in the forward computation graph recorded for autodiff. Created
/// in topological (forward) order; the backward pass walks them in reverse.
struct AdNode {
    kind: AdOp,
    inputs: Vec<usize>,
    ty: TyKind,
    /// Forward result: a data pointer for tensors, an f32 Value for scalars.
    fwd: Value,
    /// Auxiliary value for activation backward: the input tensor pointer or scalar.
    aux: Option<Value>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
enum AdOp {
    /// A function parameter or other differentiable leaf.
    Leaf,
    /// A non-differentiable constant (tensor literal, scalar const). The
    /// backward stops here — no gradient flows into it.
    Const,
    Matmul,
    /// Tensor⊙tensor elementwise op (`.+ .- .* ./`).
    Elem(BinOp),
    /// scalar ⊙ tensor (or tensor ⊙ scalar) broadcast. `scalar_is_lhs`
    /// preserves operand order for `.-` / `./`. `scalar` is the scalar's
    /// forward SSA value (used to recompute forward in the second-order tape).
    /// `scalar_node` is the scalar operand's AD node when it is itself a traced
    /// value (e.g. a reduction like `sum(w)`); the backward then reduces the
    /// tensor-shaped contribution to a scalar and flows it there (#260). `None`
    /// for genuine constants and the activation second-derivative nodes built
    /// inside `tape_backward`.
    ScalarTensor { op: BinOp, scalar_is_lhs: bool, scalar: Value, scalar_node: Option<usize> },
    Transpose,
    /// Reduction of a tensor to a scalar.
    Sum,
    Mean,
    /// f32 scalar arithmetic used to compose the loss.
    ScalarBin(BinOp),
    /// Broadcast a scalar to a tensor shape. Used in the tape of the backward
    /// pass (second-order AD) to represent `broadcast_scalar_to_tensor`.
    Broadcast { ty: TensorTy },
    /// Elementwise ReLU on a tensor via the `\>` operator.
    Relu,
    /// Elementwise tensor activations from named calls.
    ActivationRelu,
    ActivationTanh,
    ActivationGelu,
    ActivationSigmoid,
    /// Smooth activations whose first-order VJP is `adj .* act'(x)` via a
    /// runtime derivative extern (#377). aux = input tensor pointer. Second-order
    /// (`@grad @grad`) is not wired for these yet — it falls back to the interp.
    ActivationSilu,
    ActivationElu,
    ActivationMish,
    /// `softmax(x, axis)` over the LAST axis (the attention case). fwd = output
    /// y; the VJP `dx = y .* (g - rowsum(g .* y))` needs only y and the row
    /// length, both recoverable from the node. Only the last axis is supported
    /// (the forward bails otherwise), so no axis payload is carried. First order
    /// only; second order falls back to the interpreter.
    Softmax,
    /// `rms_norm(x, gain, eps)` over the LAST axis. inputs = [x, gain]; the VJP
    /// flows to BOTH (`dx` and `dgain`). fwd = output y; `aux` carries the `eps`
    /// SSA value; `r` is recomputed from x in the backward. First order only;
    /// second order falls back to the interpreter.
    RmsNorm,
    /// `layer_norm(x, gain, bias, eps)` over the LAST axis. inputs = [x, gain,
    /// bias]; the VJP flows to all three (`dx`, `dgain`, `dbias`). fwd = output
    /// y; `aux` carries the `eps` SSA value; mean/std are recomputed from x in
    /// the backward. First order only; second order falls back to the interp.
    LayerNorm,
    /// `rope(x, cos, sin)` over the last two axes `[..., S, D]`. inputs = [x,
    /// cos, sin]; the VJP flows ONLY to `x` — `cos`/`sin` are read-only position
    /// tables. RoPE is a per-pair orthogonal rotation, so `dx = rope(adj, cos,
    /// −sin)` (the inverse rotation). `cos`/`sin` fwd ptrs are read from the
    /// input nodes in the backward. First order only; second order falls back
    /// to the interpreter.
    Rope,
    /// `attn(q, k, v, mask?)` / `attn_gqa(...)` — fused scaled-dot-product
    /// attention `O = softmax(mask((Q Kᵀ)/√D)) V` per (batch, query head).
    /// inputs = [q, k, v]; the VJP flows to all three. The optional bool mask
    /// is lowered outside the tape (masked positions have softmax weight 0,
    /// so no gradient crosses them). `aux` carries the [B,H_q,S,S] buffer of
    /// post-softmax weights P the @grad forward saved; the backward replays
    /// per head: dV += Pᵀ·adj, dP = adj·Vᵀ, dS = P∘(dP − rowsum(dP∘P))/√D,
    /// dQ = dS·K, dK += dSᵀ·Q (GQA accumulates dK/dV across each KV head's
    /// query group). First order only; second order falls back to the
    /// interpreter (#368).
    Attn,
    /// gelu'(x) element-wise. Phase-2 tape node only: stores the first
    /// derivative so that emit_backward can differentiate through it to get
    /// gelu''(x) as the second-order gradient. This is what tape_backward
    /// for ActivationGelu pushes as the accumulated adjoint of x so that the
    /// Phase-2 loss = sum(adj .* gelu'(x)) and emit_backward gives gelu''(x).
    GeluFirstDeriv,
}

/// Reduction mode for `lower_builtin_reduce_along` (#377). `Add` backs both
/// `sum_along` and `mean_along` (the latter divides after); `Max`/`Min` seed
/// the accumulator at ∓∞ and combine with `fmax`/`fmin`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
enum ReduceAlong { Add, Max, Min }

struct AdState {
    nodes: Vec<AdNode>,
    /// node id -> accumulated adjoint (tensor ptr or scalar f32 Value), or
    /// None if no gradient has flowed in yet.
    adjoint: Vec<Option<Value>>,
    /// binding / parameter name -> node id.
    env: HashMap<String, usize>,
    /// (mut-param index, node id) for every `!` parameter.
    mut_params: Vec<(usize, usize)>,
    /// The scalar loss node (set after lowering the body).
    loss: Option<usize>,
}

impl AdState {
    fn new() -> Self {
        AdState { nodes: Vec::new(), adjoint: Vec::new(), env: HashMap::new(),
                  mut_params: Vec::new(), loss: None }
    }
    fn push(&mut self, kind: AdOp, inputs: Vec<usize>, ty: TyKind, fwd: Value) -> usize {
        let id = self.nodes.len();
        self.nodes.push(AdNode { kind, inputs, ty, fwd, aux: None });
        self.adjoint.push(None);
        id
    }
    fn push_aux(&mut self, kind: AdOp, inputs: Vec<usize>, ty: TyKind, fwd: Value, aux: Value) -> usize {
        let id = self.nodes.len();
        self.nodes.push(AdNode { kind, inputs, ty, fwd, aux: Some(aux) });
        self.adjoint.push(None);
        id
    }
}

impl<'a> Translator<'a> {
    fn is_filled(&self) -> bool { self.block_filled }

    fn enter(&mut self, b: Block) {
        self.builder.switch_to_block(b);
        self.block_filled = false;
    }

    fn jump(&mut self, dst: Block, args: &[Value]) {
        let block_args: Vec<_> = args.iter().map(|v| (*v).into()).collect();
        self.builder.ins().jump(dst, &block_args);
        self.block_filled = true;
    }

    fn brif(&mut self, c: Value, t: Block, f: Block) {
        self.builder.ins().brif(c, t, &[], f, &[]);
        self.block_filled = true;
    }

    /// Open a simple counted loop `for iv in 0..bound` (no loop-carried value).
    /// Leaves the builder positioned in the *body*, with `iv` bound. Fill the
    /// body, then call `loop_end` to emit the increment/back-edge and continue
    /// after the loop. Nest freely: an inner `loop_begin`/`loop_end` pair inside
    /// the body is fine (the outer `loop_end`'s exit-enter happens last).
    fn loop_begin(&mut self, bound: Value) -> LoopCtx {
        let hdr  = self.builder.create_block();
        let body = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit = self.builder.create_block();
        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(hdr);
        let iv = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
        let c = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, iv, bound);
        self.brif(c, body, exit);
        self.enter(body);
        LoopCtx { iv, hdr, body, exit }
    }

    /// Close a `loop_begin`: emit `iv += 1`, the back-edge, seal the loop, and
    /// position the builder at the (sealed) exit block.
    fn loop_end(&mut self, lc: LoopCtx) {
        let one = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let nx = self.builder.ins().iadd(lc.iv, one);
        self.jump(lc.hdr, &[nx]);
        self.builder.seal_block(lc.body);
        self.builder.seal_block(lc.hdr);
        self.enter(lc.exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(lc.exit);
    }

    fn ret_void(&mut self) {
        self.builder.ins().return_(&[]);
        self.block_filled = true;
    }

    fn ret_val(&mut self, v: Value) {
        self.builder.ins().return_(&[v]);
        self.block_filled = true;
    }

    fn trap_user(&mut self, code: u8) {
        let tc = cranelift::codegen::ir::TrapCode::user(code).unwrap();
        self.builder.ins().trap(tc);
        self.block_filled = true;
    }

    /// Emit a clean "no arm matched" runtime error (print + exit 1), then a
    /// trap to terminate the block. Replaces a bare SIGILL trap so a
    /// non-exhaustive `match` fails gracefully like the interpreter.
    fn emit_match_trap(&mut self) {
        let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_match_trap")
            .expect("__dmc_match_trap not registered").clone();
        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[]);
        self.trap_user(2);
    }

    /// Decode an OptI64 to a plain i64, trapping cleanly if it is nil (#300.4).
    /// Mirrors the interpreter raising a runtime error when a missing `map_get`
    /// result is used as a value.
    fn opt_unwrap_or_trap(&mut self, opt: Value) -> Value {
        let present = self.opt_present(opt);
        let trap_blk = self.builder.create_block();
        let ok_blk = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.ins().brif(present, ok_blk, &[], trap_blk, &[]);
        self.builder.switch_to_block(trap_blk);
        self.builder.seal_block(trap_blk);
        let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_nil_trap").expect("__dmc_nil_trap not registered").clone();
        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[]);
        self.builder.ins().trap(cranelift::codegen::ir::TrapCode::user(2).unwrap());
        self.builder.switch_to_block(ok_blk);
        self.builder.seal_block(ok_blk);
        self.opt_value(opt)
    }

    /// Lower a block used as an expression. Returns the tail value if the
    /// block has one (and didn't terminate via `return` / `break`).
    ///
    /// When the block has no explicit `tail_expr`, the parser may have
    /// folded the trailing expression into `Stmt::If` (or `Stmt::Match`)
    /// because `if`/`match` are keyword-led. Treat such a final stmt as the
    /// block's value.
    fn lower_block_value(&mut self, b: &Block_) -> Result<Option<(Value, TyKind)>, JitError> {
        let last_is_value = b.tail_expr.is_none()
            && b.stmts.last().map(|s| matches!(s,
                Stmt::If(_) | Stmt::Match(_) | Stmt::DirectiveBlock { .. })).unwrap_or(false);
        let body_len = if last_is_value { b.stmts.len() - 1 } else { b.stmts.len() };
        for stmt in &b.stmts[..body_len] {
            self.lower_stmt(stmt)?;
            if self.is_filled() { return Ok(None); }
        }
        if last_is_value {
            match b.stmts.last() {
                Some(Stmt::If(i)) => return self.lower_if(i),
                Some(Stmt::Match(m)) => return self.lower_match_expr(m).map(Some),
                // A directive block in tail position produces the block's value
                // (e.g. an attention fn whose body ends in `@..@fuse { .. }`).
                Some(Stmt::DirectiveBlock { directives, body, span }) => {
                    if directives.iter().any(|d| d.name == "fuse") {
                        return self.lower_fuse_block(body, span).map(Some);
                    }
                    if cast_directive_is_int_target(directives) {
                        return unsupported(span, INT_CAST_BLOCK_UNSUPPORTED);
                    }
                    if directives.iter().all(|d| matches!(d.name.as_str(), "deterministic" | "cast")) {
                        return self.lower_block_value(body);
                    }
                    return unsupported(span,
                        "directive blocks in tail position (only @fuse, @deterministic, @cast are supported)");
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        if let Some(tail) = &b.tail_expr {
            let val = self.lower_expr(tail)?;
            return Ok(Some(val));
        }
        Ok(None)
    }

    fn lower_stmt(&mut self, stmt: &Stmt) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        match stmt {
            Stmt::Let(l) => self.lower_let(l),
            Stmt::Expr { lhs, assign, span } => self.lower_expr_stmt(lhs, assign.as_ref(), span),
            Stmt::If(i) => {
                // If-as-statement: drop the value.
                let _ = self.lower_if(i)?;
                Ok(())
            }
            Stmt::While { cond, body, span } => self.lower_while(cond, body, span),
            Stmt::Return { value, span } => self.lower_return(value.as_ref(), span),
            Stmt::Break(span) => self.lower_break(span),
            Stmt::Continue(span) => self.lower_continue(span),
            Stmt::Loop { body, span } => self.lower_loop(body, span),
            Stmt::For { pattern, iter, body, span } => self.lower_for(pattern, iter, body, span),
            Stmt::Match(m) => self.lower_match_stmt(m),
            Stmt::Stage { span, .. } => unsupported(span, "`stage` (pipeline parallelism)"),
            Stmt::Directive { span, .. } => unsupported(span, "directives inside a fn body"),
            Stmt::DirectiveBlock { directives, body, span } => {
                // @deterministic and @cast(bf16) are accepted as no-ops: bit-exactness
                // and bf16-compute semantics are not yet enforced by the JIT.
                if directives.iter().any(|d| d.name == "fuse") {
                    // @fuse as a statement: evaluate and discard the value.
                    let _ = self.lower_fuse_block(body, span)?;
                    return Ok(());
                }
                if cast_directive_is_int_target(directives) {
                    return unsupported(span, INT_CAST_BLOCK_UNSUPPORTED);
                }
                if directives.iter().all(|d| matches!(d.name.as_str(), "deterministic" | "cast")) {
                    // All directives are no-op pass-throughs; lower the block normally.
                    let _ = self.lower_block_value(body)?;
                    return Ok(());
                }
                unsupported(span, "directives inside a fn body (only @fuse, @deterministic, @cast are supported)")
            }
        }
    }

    fn lower_let(&mut self, l: &LetStmt) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        // `let (loss, dW) = f.fwd_bwd(W, x)` — the autodiff source surface
        // (and `f.fwd_bwd_bwd(...)` for second-order, on `@grad @grad` fns).
        if let Pattern::Tuple(pats, _) = &l.pattern {
            if let Some((fname, method, args)) = as_fwd_bwd_call(&l.value) {
                return self.lower_fwd_bwd_destructure(pats, fname, method, args, &l.span);
            }
            // `let (a, b, c) = t.split[n, axis=k]` — split a tensor into n equal
            // pieces along `axis`, each bound as a fresh owned slice (SPEC §6.4).
            if let Some((recv, n_expr, axis_expr)) = as_tensor_split_call(&l.value) {
                return self.lower_tensor_split_destructure(pats, recv, n_expr, axis_expr, &l.span);
            }
            return unsupported(&l.span,
                "tuple destructuring is only supported for \
                 `let (loss, g) = f.fwd_bwd(...)` / `f.fwd_bwd_bwd(...)` \
                 and `let (a, b, ..) = t.split[n, axis=k]`");
        }
        let name = match &l.pattern {
            Pattern::Ident(n, _) => n.clone(),
            Pattern::Wildcard(_) => {
                // Evaluate for side effects, discard.
                let _ = self.lower_expr(&l.value)?;
                return Ok(());
            }
            _ => return unsupported(&l.span, "destructuring `let` patterns"),
        };
        let (val, ty) = self.lower_expr(&l.value)?;
        // #249: `let y = x` (or `let y = m.w`) is a value copy — snapshot the
        // tensor so mutating `y` doesn't write through to `x`'s storage.
        let alias = is_aliasing_place_expr(&l.value);
        if let Some(ann) = &l.ty {
            let want = enumify(ty_from_ast(ann, &self.shape_env)?, self.enums);
            let coerced = self.coerce_to(val, &ty, &want, &l.span)?;
            let bound = if alias { self.copy_tensor_value(coerced, &want) } else { coerced };
            self.declare_local(name, want, bound);
        } else {
            let bound = if alias { self.copy_tensor_value(val, &ty) } else { val };
            self.declare_local(name, ty, bound);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Lower `let (loss, dW) = f.fwd_bwd(args)`: call the `f$fwd_bwd` entry
    /// (which returns the f32 loss; gradient pointers travel via the
    /// capture_grad side-channel), then bind both names. `method` is
    /// `"fwd_bwd"` or `"fwd_bwd_bwd"` — the latter calls the `f$fwd_bwd_bwd`
    /// entry (stacked `@grad @grad`), whose published gradients are the
    /// second derivatives ∇p(sum(∇p₀ L)).
    fn lower_fwd_bwd_destructure(
        &mut self,
        pats: &[Pattern],
        fname: &str,
        method: &str,
        args: &[CallArg],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        if pats.len() != 2 {
            return err(span, format!(
                "`f.{}(...)` destructures into exactly `(loss, grads)`", method));
        }
        let loss_name = match &pats[0] {
            Pattern::Ident(n, _) => n.clone(),
            Pattern::Wildcard(_) => "_".to_string(),
            _ => return unsupported(span, "fwd_bwd loss binding must be an identifier"),
        };
        let grad_name = match &pats[1] {
            Pattern::Ident(n, _) => n.clone(),
            Pattern::Wildcard(_) => "_".to_string(),
            _ => return unsupported(span, "fwd_bwd gradient binding must be an identifier"),
        };
        let bwd = format!("{}${}", fname, method);
        let entry = self.fns.get(&bwd).cloned().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: if method == "fwd_bwd_bwd" && self.fns.contains_key(&format!("{}$fwd_bwd", fname)) {
                format!("`{}.fwd_bwd_bwd` (second-order autodiff) requires \
                         stacked `@grad @grad` on fn `{}`", fname, fname)
            } else {
                format!("`{}` is not a `@grad fn` (no {} entry)", fname, method)
            },
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?;
        if args.len() != entry.params.len() {
            return err(span, format!(
                "`{}` expects {} arg(s), got {}", fname, entry.params.len(), args.len(),
            ));
        }
        let mut vals: Vec<Value> = Vec::with_capacity(args.len());
        for (i, a) in args.iter().enumerate() {
            let e = match a {
                CallArg::Positional(e) => e,
                _ => return unsupported(span, "named/spread args to fwd_bwd"),
            };
            let (v, k) = self.lower_expr(e)?;
            let v = self.coerce_to(v, &k, &entry.params[i].1, span)?;
            vals.push(v);
        }
        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &vals);
        // fwd_bwd returns only the f32 loss; grad ptrs were published via
        // capture_grad (side-channel) and are retrieved via take_grad_at below.
        let loss_v = self.builder.inst_results(call)[0];

        // Check multi-param schema; fall back to single-grad path. The schema
        // is registered under the `$fwd_bwd` name; `$fwd_bwd_bwd` shares it
        // (same params, same published-gradient indices).
        let schema     = self.grad_schemas.get(&format!("{}$fwd_bwd", fname)).cloned();
        let grad_entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_take_grad_at").expect("registered").clone();

        if loss_name != "_" {
            self.declare_local(loss_name, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32), loss_v);
        }
        match schema.as_deref() {
            None => {
                return err(span, format!("`{}.{}` has no mutable parameters", fname, method));
            }
            Some([(param_name, grad_ty, param_idx)]) => {
                // Single-param: bind grad_name directly AND bind grad_name$param_name
                // so that `g.W` field access works when the outer fn uses the
                // result in FOMAML-style code (e.g. `let W1 = W .- g.W .* lr`).
                if grad_name != "_" {
                    let grad_ptr = self.call_take_grad_at(&grad_entry, *param_idx);
                    let flat_name = format!("{}${}", grad_name, param_name);
                    self.declare_local(flat_name, grad_ty.clone(), grad_ptr);
                    self.declare_local(grad_name, grad_ty.clone(), grad_ptr);
                }
            }
            Some(schema) => {
                // Multi-param: bind grad_name$param_name for each so `grads.W` resolves.
                if grad_name != "_" {
                    for (param_name, param_ty, param_idx) in schema {
                        let grad_ptr = self.call_take_grad_at(&grad_entry, *param_idx);
                        let local_name = format!("{}${}", grad_name, param_name);
                        self.declare_local(local_name, param_ty.clone(), grad_ptr);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Lower `let (a, b, ..) = t.split[n, axis=k]` (SPEC §6.4): split the tensor
    /// into `n` equal-width contiguous slabs along `axis`, binding each to its
    /// target. Mirrors interp.rs:eval_tensor_split — numpy-style negative axis,
    /// divisibility and axis-range checks. The JIT resolves all shapes statically,
    /// so `n`, `axis`, divisibility and range are compile-time checks; each piece
    /// is materialized as a fresh owned tensor via the existing slice-copy path
    /// (the interpreter `.to_owned()`s each slice too, so binding never aliases).
    fn lower_tensor_split_destructure(
        &mut self,
        pats: &[Pattern],
        recv: &Expr,
        n_expr: &Expr,
        axis_expr: Option<&Expr>,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        // Piece count must be a compile-time positive int — the JIT needs a
        // static tuple arity (matching the checker's n-tuple typing).
        let n = const_int_axis(n_expr).filter(|&k| k > 0).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: "`.split` requires a positive integer piece count, e.g. `t.split[3, axis=-1]`".into(),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })? as usize;
        if pats.len() != n {
            return err(span, format!(
                "`.split[{}, ..]` yields a {}-tuple but {} binding(s) were given",
                n, n, pats.len()));
        }
        let (ptr, recv_ty) = self.lower_expr(recv)?;
        let t = recv_ty.as_tensor().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("`.split` expects a tensor, got `{}`", recv_ty.render()),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?.clone();
        let ndim = t.rank();
        // axis defaults to -1; negative axes resolve from the end (numpy-style).
        let axis_raw = match axis_expr {
            Some(e) => const_int_axis(e).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                msg: "`.split` axis must be a compile-time integer in the JIT".into(),
                line: span.line, col: span.col,
            })?,
            None => -1,
        };
        let axis_norm = if axis_raw < 0 { ndim as i64 + axis_raw } else { axis_raw };
        if axis_norm < 0 || axis_norm as usize >= ndim {
            return err(span, format!(
                "`.split`: axis {} is out of range for a rank-{} tensor", axis_raw, ndim));
        }
        let axis = axis_norm as usize;
        let dim = t.shape[axis];
        if dim % (n as i64) != 0 {
            return err(span, format!(
                "`.split`: axis {} of length {} is not divisible into {} equal pieces",
                axis, dim, n));
        }
        let w = dim / (n as i64);
        // Piece i is the slab `[.., i*w..(i+1)*w, ..]` — a Range on `axis`, Full
        // on every other axis. lower_tensor_slice_read_copy materializes it into
        // a fresh forge-allocated tensor with the reduced shape.
        for (i, pat) in pats.iter().enumerate() {
            let bind = match pat {
                Pattern::Ident(name, _) => Some(name.clone()),
                Pattern::Wildcard(_) => None,
                _ => return unsupported(span, "`.split` bindings must be identifiers"),
            };
            let classified: Vec<IndexCat> = (0..ndim).map(|a| {
                if a == axis {
                    IndexCat::Range { start: i as i64 * w, end: (i as i64 + 1) * w }
                } else {
                    IndexCat::Full
                }
            }).collect();
            let (piece_ptr, piece_ty) =
                self.lower_tensor_slice_read_copy(ptr, &t, &classified, span)?;
            if let Some(name) = bind {
                self.declare_local(name, piece_ty, piece_ptr);
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Emit a call to `__dmc_take_grad_at(param_idx)` and return the i64 grad ptr.
    fn call_take_grad_at(&mut self, entry: &FnEntry, param_idx: usize) -> Value {
        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        let idx_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, param_idx as i64);
        let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[idx_v]);
        self.builder.inst_results(call)[0]
    }

    /// Emit a call to a registered zero-arg import returning one i64.
    fn call_import0(&mut self, name: &str) -> Value {
        let entry = self.fns.get(name)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{} registered", name)).clone();
        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[]);
        self.builder.inst_results(call)[0]
    }

    /// Emit a call to a registered one-i64-arg import with no return value.
    fn call_import1(&mut self, name: &str, arg: Value) {
        let entry = self.fns.get(name)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{} registered", name)).clone();
        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[arg]);
    }

    fn declare_local(&mut self, name: String, ty: TyKind, value: Value) {
        let v = self.builder.declare_var(ty.cl());
        self.builder.def_var(v, value);
        self.locals.insert(name.clone(), v);
        self.local_tys.insert(name, ty);
    }

    fn lower_expr_stmt(
        &mut self,
        lhs: &Expr,
        assign: Option<&(AssignOp, Expr)>,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        let Some((op, rhs)) = assign else {
            // Expression evaluated for side effects.
            let _ = self.lower_expr(lhs)?;
            return Ok(());
        };

        // Indexed LHS: tensor element write `A[i] = x` or KV-array append `caches[i] <- frame`.
        if let Expr::Postfix { expr, op: PostfixOp::Index(idxs), span: pspan } = lhs {
            if matches!(op, AssignOp::Eq | AssignOp::ColonEq) {
                return self.lower_tensor_store(expr, idxs, rhs, pspan);
            }
            // `k_caches[i] <- frame` — stream-append to an element of a KV-array parameter.
            if matches!(op, AssignOp::StreamArrow) {
                return self.lower_kv_array_append(expr, idxs, rhs, pspan);
            }
            return unsupported(pspan, "compound assignment to tensor elements");
        }

        let name = match lhs {
            Expr::Ident(n, _) => n.clone(),
            _ => return unsupported(span, "assignment to non-identifier targets"),
        };
        let var = *self.locals.get(&name).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("assignment to unknown binding `{}`", name),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?;
        let ty = self.local_tys.get(&name).unwrap().clone();
        // `cache <- frame`: stream-append. Handled before coercion — the RHS is a
        // tensor frame, not a value to coerce into the KV binding type.
        if matches!(op, AssignOp::StreamArrow) {
            return self.lower_stream_append(var, &ty, &name, rhs, span);
        }
        let (rhs_val, rhs_ty) = self.lower_expr(rhs)?;
        let rhs_val = self.coerce_to(rhs_val, &rhs_ty, &ty, span)?;
        let new_val = match op {
            AssignOp::Eq | AssignOp::ColonEq => rhs_val,
            AssignOp::PlusEq | AssignOp::MinusEq | AssignOp::StarEq | AssignOp::SlashEq => {
                let sk = ty.as_scalar().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                    msg: "compound assignment requires a scalar binding".into(),
                    line: span.line, col: span.col,
                })?;
                let cur = self.builder.use_var(var);
                let bin = match op {
                    AssignOp::PlusEq  => BinOp::Add,
                    AssignOp::MinusEq => BinOp::Sub,
                    AssignOp::StarEq  => BinOp::Mul,
                    AssignOp::SlashEq => BinOp::Div,
                    _ => unreachable!(),
                };
                self.scalar_binop(&bin, cur, sk, rhs_val, sk, span)?.0
            }
            AssignOp::StreamArrow => unreachable!("stream append `<-` handled before coercion"),
            AssignOp::AmpEq | AssignOp::BarEq | AssignOp::CaretEq => {
                return unsupported(span, "compound bitwise assignment");
            }
        };
        self.builder.def_var(var, new_val);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn lower_return(&mut self, value: Option<&Expr>, span: &Span) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        let ret = self.ret.clone();
        match (&ret, value) {
            (TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil), None)
            | (TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil), Some(Expr::Nil(_))) => {
                self.ret_void();
            }
            (TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil), Some(e)) => {
                let _ = self.lower_expr(e)?;
                self.ret_void();
            }
            (want, Some(e)) => {
                let (v, k) = self.lower_expr(e)?;
                let v = self.coerce_to(v, &k, want, span)?;
                self.ret_val(v);
            }
            (want, None) => return err(span, format!(
                "bare `return` in function returning `{}`", want.render(),
            )),
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn lower_while(&mut self, cond: &Expr, body: &Block_, span: &Span) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        let header = self.builder.create_block();
        let body_block = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit = self.builder.create_block();

        self.jump(header, &[]);
        self.enter(header);
        let (c, ck) = self.lower_expr(cond)?;
        if !ck.as_scalar().map(|s| s.is_bool()).unwrap_or(false) {
            return err(span, format!("while-condition must be `bool`, got `{}`", ck.render()));
        }
        self.brif(c, body_block, exit);

        self.enter(body_block);
        self.loop_stack.push(LoopFrame { header, exit });
        for stmt in &body.stmts {
            self.lower_stmt(stmt)?;
            if self.is_filled() { break; }
        }
        if !self.is_filled() {
            if let Some(tail) = &body.tail_expr {
                let _ = self.lower_expr(tail)?;
            }
        }
        if !self.is_filled() {
            self.jump(header, &[]);
        }
        self.loop_stack.pop();

        self.builder.seal_block(body_block);
        self.builder.seal_block(header);
        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// `loop { body }` — unconditional loop; equivalent to `while true { body }`.
    /// Requires a `break` inside the body to terminate.
    fn lower_loop(&mut self, body: &Block_, span: &Span) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        let header = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit   = self.builder.create_block();

        self.jump(header, &[]);
        self.enter(header);
        self.loop_stack.push(LoopFrame { header, exit });
        for stmt in &body.stmts {
            self.lower_stmt(stmt)?;
            if self.is_filled() { break; }
        }
        if !self.is_filled() {
            if let Some(tail) = &body.tail_expr {
                let _ = self.lower_expr(tail)?;
            }
        }
        if !self.is_filled() {
            self.jump(header, &[]);
        }
        self.loop_stack.pop();

        self.builder.seal_block(header);
        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);

        let _ = span;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// `for <pattern> in <iter> { body }` — only range iteration supported.
    fn lower_for(
        &mut self,
        pattern: &Pattern,
        iter: &Expr,
        body: &Block_,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        // Only range iteration is supported.
        let (lo_expr, hi_expr, inclusive) = match iter {
            Expr::Range { start, end, inclusive, .. } => {
                let lo = start.as_deref().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                    msg: "for-range requires a start bound".into(),
                    line: span.line, col: span.col,
                })?;
                let hi = end.as_deref().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                    msg: "for-range requires an end bound".into(),
                    line: span.line, col: span.col,
                })?;
                (lo, hi, *inclusive)
            }
            _ => return unsupported(span, "for-loop over collections (only range iteration supported)"),
        };

        // Evaluate bounds before entering the loop.
        let (lo_val, lo_ty) = self.lower_expr(lo_expr)?;
        let (hi_val, hi_ty) = self.lower_expr(hi_expr)?;
        // Coerce both to i64.
        let lo_val = self.coerce_to(lo_val, &lo_ty, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;
        let hi_val = self.coerce_to(hi_val, &hi_ty, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;

        // Declare the index variable.
        let idx_var = self.builder.declare_var(cl::I64);
        self.builder.def_var(idx_var, lo_val);

        // Optionally bind the pattern name so the body can read it.
        let bound_name: Option<String> = match pattern {
            Pattern::Ident(name, _) => Some(name.clone()),
            Pattern::Wildcard(_) => None,
            _ => return unsupported(span, "destructuring patterns in `for` loops"),
        };
        if let Some(ref name) = bound_name {
            // Create a Cranelift variable for the body binding; we will
            // re-define it on each iteration in the body block.
            let bind_var = self.builder.declare_var(cl::I64);
            let init_val = self.builder.use_var(idx_var);
            self.builder.def_var(bind_var, init_val);
            self.locals.insert(name.clone(), bind_var);
            self.local_tys.insert(name.clone(), TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64));
        }

        // CFG: current → header(cond) → body → incr(++ , back to header) / exit.
        // The increment lives in its OWN block so `continue` can target it —
        // jumping straight to `header` would skip the increment and spin forever.
        let header = self.builder.create_block();
        let body_block = self.builder.create_block();
        let incr = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit = self.builder.create_block();

        self.jump(header, &[]);

        // Header: check condition.
        self.enter(header);
        let idx_cur = self.builder.use_var(idx_var);
        let cond = if inclusive {
            self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThanOrEqual, idx_cur, hi_val)
        } else {
            self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, idx_cur, hi_val)
        };
        self.brif(cond, body_block, exit);

        // Body block.
        self.enter(body_block);
        // Update the binding variable so body reads are correct.
        if let Some(ref name) = bound_name {
            let cur = self.builder.use_var(idx_var);
            let bind_var = *self.locals.get(name).unwrap();
            self.builder.def_var(bind_var, cur);
        }
        // `continue` jumps to `incr` (advance the iterator), not `header`.
        self.loop_stack.push(LoopFrame { header: incr, exit });
        for stmt in &body.stmts {
            self.lower_stmt(stmt)?;
            if self.is_filled() { break; }
        }
        if !self.is_filled() {
            if let Some(tail) = &body.tail_expr {
                let _ = self.lower_expr(tail)?;
            }
        }
        // End of body falls into the increment block.
        if !self.is_filled() {
            self.jump(incr, &[]);
        }
        self.loop_stack.pop();

        // Increment block: idx += 1, back to header.
        self.enter(incr);
        let cur = self.builder.use_var(idx_var);
        let one = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let next = self.builder.ins().iadd(cur, one);
        self.builder.def_var(idx_var, next);
        self.jump(header, &[]);

        self.builder.seal_block(body_block);
        self.builder.seal_block(incr);
        self.builder.seal_block(header);
        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// #350: if `pat` matches a single variant of `scr_ty`'s enum, return its
    /// i64 ordinal. Covers both the qualified `Light.Red` (`EnumVariant`) and
    /// the bare `Green` (an `Ident` that names a real variant) forms. Returns
    /// `None` for a true catch-all ident, a wildcard, a literal, or any
    /// non-enum scrutinee — those keep their existing lowering. This is what
    /// lets the JIT tell a bare variant apart from a catch-all binding, exactly
    /// as the checker's exhaustiveness pass does.
    fn enum_pattern_ordinal(&self, scr_ty: &TyKind, pat: &Pattern) -> Option<i64> {
        let variants = match scr_ty {
            TyKind::Enum(n) => self.enums.get(n)?,
            _ => return None,
        };
        let name = match pat {
            Pattern::EnumVariant { variant, .. } => variant,
            Pattern::Ident(name, _) => name,
            _ => return None,
        };
        variants.iter().position(|v| v == name).map(|i| i as i64)
    }

    /// #350: lower a `match` scrutinee to an i64 comparison key. An enum is
    /// already its i64 ordinal; a bool widens; any other scalar coerces.
    /// Errors for a non-scalar, non-enum scrutinee (tensors etc.).
    // ── #350 Part 2b: payload-enum (tagged-union) lowering helpers ──────────

    /// Load the i64 tag (variant ordinal) from slot 0 of a payload-enum value.
    fn load_enum_tag(&mut self, ptr: Value) -> Value {
        self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new(), ptr, 0)
    }

    /// Encode a scalar value into its 8-byte slot representation (mirrors the
    /// model-field store: f32→i32→uextend, f64→bitcast i64, narrow int→uextend).
    fn encode_for_slot(&mut self, val: Value, ty: &TyKind) -> Value {
        let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
        match ty {
            TyKind::Scalar(sk) if *sk == ScalarKind::F32 => {
                let as_i32 = self.builder.ins().bitcast(cl::I32, flags, val);
                self.builder.ins().uextend(cl::I64, as_i32)
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(sk) if *sk == ScalarKind::F64 => {
                self.builder.ins().bitcast(cl::I64, flags, val)
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(sk) if sk.cl() != cl::I64 && !sk.is_float() => {
                self.builder.ins().uextend(cl::I64, val)
            }
            _ => val,
        }
    }

    /// Decode a scalar value from its 8-byte slot at `field_ptr` (inverse of
    /// `encode_for_slot`; mirrors the model-field load).
    fn decode_from_slot(&mut self, field_ptr: Value, ty: &TyKind) -> Value {
        let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
        match ty {
            TyKind::Scalar(sk) if *sk == ScalarKind::F32 => {
                let raw = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, field_ptr, 0);
                let as_i32 = self.builder.ins().ireduce(cl::I32, raw);
                self.builder.ins().bitcast(cl::F32, flags, as_i32)
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(sk) if *sk == ScalarKind::F64 => {
                let raw = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, field_ptr, 0);
                self.builder.ins().bitcast(cl::F64, flags, raw)
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(sk) if sk.cl() != cl::I64 && !sk.is_float() => {
                let raw = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, field_ptr, 0);
                self.builder.ins().ireduce(sk.cl(), raw)
            }
            _ => self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, field_ptr, 0),
        }
    }

    /// Construct a payload-enum value `Enum.Variant(args)` (or a tag-only variant
    /// of a payload enum, e.g. `Shape.Empty`, with no args): forge-allocate the
    /// `[tag, slots…]` region, store the ordinal, then store each payload arg.
    /// Returns the i64 pointer typed as the enum.
    fn lower_enum_value(&mut self, enum_name: &str, variant: &str,
                        arg_vals: Vec<(Value, TyKind)>, span: &Span)
        -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError>
    {
        let layout = self.enum_payload_layouts.get(enum_name)
            .expect("lower_enum_value on a non-payload enum").clone();
        let ord = self.enums.get(enum_name)
            .and_then(|vs| vs.iter().position(|v| v == variant))
            .ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                msg: format!("enum `{}` has no variant `{}`", enum_name, variant),
                line: span.line, col: span.col })? as i64;
        let tys = layout.variant_tys.get(variant).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        if arg_vals.len() != tys.len() {
            return err(span, format!(
                "variant `{}.{}` carries {} payload field(s), got {} argument(s)",
                enum_name, variant, tys.len(), arg_vals.len()));
        }
        let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
        let ptr = self.forge_alloc(layout.n_slots * 8);
        let tag = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, ord);
        self.builder.ins().store(flags, tag, ptr, 0);
        if let Some(&off) = layout.variant_off.get(variant) {
            for (i, ((val, vty), fty)) in arg_vals.into_iter().zip(tys.iter()).enumerate() {
                let cval = self.coerce_to(val, &vty, fty, span)?;
                let store_val = self.encode_for_slot(cval, fty);
                let byte_off = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, (off + i as i64) * 8);
                let fptr = self.builder.ins().iadd(ptr, byte_off);
                self.builder.ins().store(flags, store_val, fptr, 0);
            }
        }
        Ok((ptr, TyKind::Enum(enum_name.to_string())))
    }

    /// After a payload-variant `match` arm is selected, bind its sub-patterns to
    /// the value's payload slots (loaded from the scrutinee pointer). A no-op for
    /// tag-only patterns and non-payload scrutinees. v1 binds identifier
    /// sub-patterns; a nested sub-pattern routes the program out of the JIT subset.
    fn bind_enum_payload(&mut self, pat: &Pattern, scr_val: Value, scr_ty: &TyKind, span: &Span)
        -> Result<(), JitError>
    {
        let enum_name = match scr_ty { TyKind::Enum(n) => n, _ => return Ok(()) };
        let layout = match self.enum_payload_layouts.get(enum_name) {
            Some(l) => l.clone(), None => return Ok(()),
        };
        let (variant, bindings) = match pat {
            Pattern::EnumVariant { variant, bindings, .. } if !bindings.is_empty() => (variant, bindings),
            _ => return Ok(()),
        };
        let off = match layout.variant_off.get(variant) { Some(&o) => o, None => return Ok(()) };
        let tys = layout.variant_tys.get(variant).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        for (i, b) in bindings.iter().enumerate() {
            match b {
                Pattern::Ident(name, _) if name == "_" => {}
                Pattern::Ident(name, _) => {
                    let fty = tys.get(i).cloned().unwrap_or(TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64));
                    let byte_off = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, (off + i as i64) * 8);
                    let fptr = self.builder.ins().iadd(scr_val, byte_off);
                    let loaded = self.decode_from_slot(fptr, &fty);
                    let var = self.builder.declare_var(fty.cl());
                    self.builder.def_var(var, loaded);
                    self.locals.insert(name.clone(), var);
                    self.local_tys.insert(name.clone(), fty);
                }
                Pattern::Wildcard(_) => {}
                _ => return unsupported(span,
                    "nested sub-pattern in an enum payload binding (v1 binds identifiers; use `dmc run`)"),
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn match_scrutinee_i64(&mut self, scr_val: Value, scr_ty: &TyKind, span: &Span)
        -> Result<Value, JitError>
    {
        if let TyKind::Enum(name) = scr_ty {
            // #350 Part 2b: a payload enum value is a pointer — the tag (ordinal)
            // lives in slot 0. A tag-only enum value already *is* its ordinal.
            if self.enum_payload_layouts.contains_key(name) {
                return Ok(self.load_enum_tag(scr_val));
            }
            return Ok(scr_val);
        }
        let scr_sk = scr_ty.as_scalar().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: "match scrutinee must be a scalar (i64 / bool) or enum; tensors not supported".into(),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?;
        if scr_sk == ScalarKind::Bool {
            Ok(self.builder.ins().uextend(cl::I64, scr_val))
        } else {
            self.coerce_to(scr_val, scr_ty, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)
        }
    }

    /// `match <scrutinee> { arms... }` as a statement — arm bodies evaluated
    /// for side effects, results discarded.
    fn lower_match_stmt(&mut self, m: &MatchExpr) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        let (scr_val, scr_ty) = self.lower_expr(&m.scrutinee)?;
        // Coerce to i64 for integer comparison; bools widen, enums are already
        // ordinals. (#350: enums join the supported scrutinee kinds.)
        let scr_i64 = self.match_scrutinee_i64(scr_val, &scr_ty, &m.span)?;

        let merge = self.builder.create_block();

        for arm in &m.arms {
            let arm_block = self.builder.create_block();
            let next_check = self.builder.create_block();

            // #350: a qualified or bare enum-variant pattern compares the
            // scrutinee's ordinal against the variant's, exactly like an int
            // literal (it falls through to the shared arm tail below).
            if let Some(ord) = self.enum_pattern_ordinal(&scr_ty, &arm.pattern) {
                let n_val = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, ord);
                let eq = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::Equal, scr_i64, n_val);
                self.brif(eq, arm_block, next_check);
            } else {
            match &arm.pattern {
                Pattern::Literal(Literal::Int(n, _), _) => {
                    let n_val = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, *n);
                    let eq = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::Equal, scr_i64, n_val);
                    self.brif(eq, arm_block, next_check);
                }
                Pattern::Literal(Literal::Bool(b), _) => {
                    let b_val = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, if *b { 1 } else { 0 });
                    let eq = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::Equal, scr_i64, b_val);
                    self.brif(eq, arm_block, next_check);
                }
                Pattern::Ident(name, _) => {
                    // Bind name to scrutinee in this arm, then unconditionally enter arm.
                    // We bind before switching to arm_block so the variable exists.
                    self.jump(arm_block, &[]);
                    self.enter(arm_block);
                    self.builder.seal_block(arm_block);
                    // Bind: re-declare so the arm body can read it.
                    let bind_var = self.builder.declare_var(scr_ty.cl());
                    self.builder.def_var(bind_var, scr_val);
                    self.locals.insert(name.clone(), bind_var);
                    self.local_tys.insert(name.clone(), scr_ty.clone());
                    // Evaluate guard if present.
                    if let Some(guard) = &arm.guard {
                        let (gv, _gk) = self.lower_expr(guard)?;
                        let after_guard = self.builder.create_block();
                        self.brif(gv, after_guard, next_check);
                        self.enter(after_guard);
                        self.builder.seal_block(after_guard);
                    }
                    self.lower_expr_effect(&arm.body)?;
                    if !self.is_filled() { self.jump(merge, &[]); }
                    self.enter(next_check);
                    self.builder.seal_block(next_check);
                    continue;
                }
                Pattern::Wildcard(_) => {
                    self.jump(arm_block, &[]);
                    self.enter(arm_block);
                    self.builder.seal_block(arm_block);
                    if let Some(guard) = &arm.guard {
                        let (gv, _gk) = self.lower_expr(guard)?;
                        let after_guard = self.builder.create_block();
                        self.brif(gv, after_guard, next_check);
                        self.enter(after_guard);
                        self.builder.seal_block(after_guard);
                    }
                    self.lower_expr_effect(&arm.body)?;
                    if !self.is_filled() { self.jump(merge, &[]); }
                    self.enter(next_check);
                    self.builder.seal_block(next_check);
                    continue;
                }
                _ => return unsupported(&m.span, "complex patterns in `match`"),
            }
            }

            // We get here for Literal / enum-variant patterns (brif already emitted).
            self.enter(arm_block);
            self.builder.seal_block(arm_block);
            // #350 Part 2b: bind a payload variant's sub-patterns to the
            // scrutinee's payload slots (no-op for tag-only / non-payload).
            self.bind_enum_payload(&arm.pattern, scr_val, &scr_ty, &m.span)?;
            if let Some(guard) = &arm.guard {
                let (gv, _gk) = self.lower_expr(guard)?;
                let after_guard = self.builder.create_block();
                self.brif(gv, after_guard, next_check);
                self.enter(after_guard);
                self.builder.seal_block(after_guard);
            }
            self.lower_expr_effect(&arm.body)?;
            if !self.is_filled() { self.jump(merge, &[]); }

            self.enter(next_check);
            self.builder.seal_block(next_check);
        }

        // No arm matched at runtime — error cleanly like the interpreter (a
        // non-exhaustive match is not silently a no-op).
        if !self.is_filled() {
            self.emit_match_trap();
        }
        self.enter(merge);
        self.builder.seal_block(merge);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// `match <scrutinee> { arms... }` as an expression — all arm bodies must
    /// produce the same type; the result is the selected arm's value.
    fn lower_match_expr(&mut self, m: &MatchExpr) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        let (scr_val, scr_ty) = self.lower_expr(&m.scrutinee)?;
        // #350: enums join the supported scrutinee kinds (already an i64 ordinal).
        let scr_i64 = self.match_scrutinee_i64(scr_val, &scr_ty, &m.span)?;

        let merge = self.builder.create_block();
        let mut result_ty: Option<TyKind> = None;

        for arm in &m.arms {
            let arm_block = self.builder.create_block();
            let next_check = self.builder.create_block();

            // #350: enum-variant patterns compare ordinals (like an int literal,
            // falling through to the shared arm tail below).
            if let Some(ord) = self.enum_pattern_ordinal(&scr_ty, &arm.pattern) {
                let n_val = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, ord);
                let eq = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::Equal, scr_i64, n_val);
                self.brif(eq, arm_block, next_check);
            } else {
            match &arm.pattern {
                Pattern::Literal(Literal::Int(n, _), _) => {
                    let n_val = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, *n);
                    let eq = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::Equal, scr_i64, n_val);
                    self.brif(eq, arm_block, next_check);
                }
                Pattern::Literal(Literal::Bool(b), _) => {
                    let b_val = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, if *b { 1 } else { 0 });
                    let eq = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::Equal, scr_i64, b_val);
                    self.brif(eq, arm_block, next_check);
                }
                Pattern::Ident(name, _) => {
                    self.jump(arm_block, &[]);
                    self.enter(arm_block);
                    self.builder.seal_block(arm_block);
                    let bind_var = self.builder.declare_var(scr_ty.cl());
                    self.builder.def_var(bind_var, scr_val);
                    self.locals.insert(name.clone(), bind_var);
                    self.local_tys.insert(name.clone(), scr_ty.clone());
                    if let Some(guard) = &arm.guard {
                        let (gv, _gk) = self.lower_expr(guard)?;
                        let after_guard = self.builder.create_block();
                        self.brif(gv, after_guard, next_check);
                        self.enter(after_guard);
                        self.builder.seal_block(after_guard);
                    }
                    let (arm_val, arm_kind) = self.lower_expr(&arm.body)?;
                    if let Some(ref rk) = result_ty {
                        if rk != &arm_kind {
                            return err(&m.span, format!(
                                "match arms disagree on type: `{}` vs `{}`",
                                rk.render(), arm_kind.render(),
                            ));
                        }
                    } else {
