                        self.builder.append_block_param(merge, arm_kind.cl());
                        result_ty = Some(arm_kind);
                    }
                    if !self.is_filled() { self.jump(merge, &[arm_val]); }
                    self.enter(next_check);
                    self.builder.seal_block(next_check);
                    continue;
                }
                Pattern::Wildcard(_) => {
                    self.jump(arm_block, &[]);
                    self.enter(arm_block);
                    self.builder.seal_block(arm_block);
                    if let Some(guard) = &arm.guard {
                        let (gv, _gk) = self.lower_expr(guard)?;
                        let after_guard = self.builder.create_block();
                        self.brif(gv, after_guard, next_check);
                        self.enter(after_guard);
                        self.builder.seal_block(after_guard);
                    }
                    let (arm_val, arm_kind) = self.lower_expr(&arm.body)?;
                    if let Some(ref rk) = result_ty {
                        if rk != &arm_kind {
                            return err(&m.span, format!(
                                "match arms disagree on type: `{}` vs `{}`",
                                rk.render(), arm_kind.render(),
                            ));
                        }
                    } else {
                        self.builder.append_block_param(merge, arm_kind.cl());
                        result_ty = Some(arm_kind);
                    }
                    if !self.is_filled() { self.jump(merge, &[arm_val]); }
                    self.enter(next_check);
                    self.builder.seal_block(next_check);
                    continue;
                }
                _ => return unsupported(&m.span, "complex patterns in `match`"),
            }
            }

            // Literal / enum-variant patterns — arm_block was targeted by brif above.
            self.enter(arm_block);
            self.builder.seal_block(arm_block);
            // #350 Part 2b: bind a payload variant's sub-patterns (no-op otherwise).
            self.bind_enum_payload(&arm.pattern, scr_val, &scr_ty, &m.span)?;
            if let Some(guard) = &arm.guard {
                let (gv, _gk) = self.lower_expr(guard)?;
                let after_guard = self.builder.create_block();
                self.brif(gv, after_guard, next_check);
                self.enter(after_guard);
                self.builder.seal_block(after_guard);
            }
            let (arm_val, arm_kind) = self.lower_expr(&arm.body)?;
            if let Some(ref rk) = result_ty {
                if rk != &arm_kind {
                    return err(&m.span, format!(
                        "match arms disagree on type: `{}` vs `{}`",
                        rk.render(), arm_kind.render(),
                    ));
                }
            } else {
                self.builder.append_block_param(merge, arm_kind.cl());
                result_ty = Some(arm_kind);
            }
            if !self.is_filled() { self.jump(merge, &[arm_val]); }

            self.enter(next_check);
            self.builder.seal_block(next_check);
        }

        // No arm matched at runtime — error cleanly (was a bare SIGILL trap).
        if !self.is_filled() {
            self.emit_match_trap();
        }

        self.enter(merge);
        self.builder.seal_block(merge);

        let rk = result_ty.ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: "match expression has no arms".into(),
            line: m.span.line, col: m.span.col,
        })?;
        let result = self.builder.block_params(merge)[0];
        Ok((result, rk))
    }

    /// Evaluate an expression for its side effects only; discard any value.
    /// Unlike `lower_expr`, block expressions without a tail value are accepted.
    fn lower_expr_effect(&mut self, e: &Expr) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        match e {
            Expr::Block(b) => { let _ = self.lower_block_value(b)?; Ok(()) }
            _ => { let _ = self.lower_expr(e)?; Ok(()) }
        }
    }

    fn lower_break(&mut self, span: &Span) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        let exit = self.loop_stack.last().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: "`break` outside of a loop".into(), line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?.exit;
        self.jump(exit, &[]);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn lower_continue(&mut self, span: &Span) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        let header = self.loop_stack.last().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: "`continue` outside of a loop".into(), line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?.header;
        self.jump(header, &[]);
        Ok(())
    }

    // ─── Expressions ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    fn lower_expr(&mut self, e: &Expr) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        match e {
            Expr::Literal(lit, span) => self.lower_literal(lit, span),
            Expr::Nil(_) => {
                let v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I8, 0);
                Ok((v, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)))
            }
            Expr::Ident(name, span) => self.lower_ident(name, span),
            Expr::BinOp { op, lhs, rhs, span } => self.lower_binop(op, lhs, rhs, span),
            Expr::UnOp { op, operand, span } => self.lower_unop(op, operand, span),
            Expr::If(i) => {
                let v = self.lower_if(i)?;
                v.ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                    msg: "if-expression has no value (both branches terminated)".into(),
                    line: i.span.line, col: i.span.col,
                })
            }
            Expr::Block(b) => {
                let v = self.lower_block_value(b)?;
                v.ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                    msg: "block expression has no tail value".into(),
                    line: b.span.line, col: b.span.col,
                })
            }
            Expr::Postfix { expr, op, span } => self.lower_postfix(expr, op, span),
            Expr::Cast { expr, ty, span } => {
                // #262: a scalar cast to an exotic float (bf16/f16/tf32) is a
                // no-op in the JIT — the same #179 convention as `@cast(bf16){…}`
                // (these compute in f32). Keep the operand's value/kind rather
                // than erroring in ty_from_ast; a later store into a bf16 tensor
                // slot demotes at the store boundary like any f32 write.
                if matches!(ty, Type::Scalar(ScalarType::Bf16 | ScalarType::F16 | ScalarType::Tf32, _)) {
                    return self.lower_expr(expr);
                }
                let (v, k) = self.lower_expr(expr)?;
                // A scalar-typed cast of a whole TENSOR is an elementwise cast in
                // the interpreter; the JIT would otherwise reinterpret the data
                // pointer as a scalar (silent garbage), so reject it cleanly.
                if matches!(k, TyKind::Tensor(_)) {
                    if let Type::Scalar(_, _) = ty {
                        return unsupported(span,
                            "elementwise cast of a whole tensor to a scalar type");
                    }
                }
                // Narrow / unsigned integer scalar targets (#298-adjacent): the
                // JIT has no distinct ScalarKind for i8/i16/u8/u16/u32/u64/int4/
                // int8 — like the interpreter, a scalar narrow-int is just an
                // i64 holding the wrapped/narrowed value. Compute that here so
                // `x as i8` works on the JIT instead of erroring in scalar_from_ast.
                if let Type::Scalar(s, _) = ty {
                    if scalar_int_is_narrow(s) {
                        let r = self.lower_narrow_int_cast(v, &k, s, span)?;
                        return Ok((r, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)));
                    }
                }
                let target = enumify(ty_from_ast(ty, &self.shape_env)?, self.enums);
                let cv = self.coerce_to(v, &k, &target, span)?;
                Ok((cv, target))
            }
            Expr::Tuple(elems, _) if elems.len() == 1 => self.lower_expr(&elems[0]),
            Expr::Tuple(_, span) => unsupported(span, "tuples"),
            Expr::TensorLit(elems, span) => self.lower_tensor_literal(elems, span),
            Expr::Match(m) => self.lower_match_expr(m),
            Expr::FnLit(f) => self.lower_fn_lit(f),
            Expr::ArenaBlock(a) => unsupported(&a.span, "arena blocks as expressions"),
            Expr::DirectiveBlock { directives, body, span } => {
                if directives.iter().any(|d| d.name == "fuse") {
                    return self.lower_fuse_block(body, span);
                }
                if cast_directive_is_int_target(directives) {
                    return unsupported(span, INT_CAST_BLOCK_UNSUPPORTED);
                }
                // @deterministic and @cast(bf16) are accepted as no-ops: bit-exactness
                // and bf16-compute semantics are not yet enforced by the JIT.
                if directives.iter().all(|d| matches!(d.name.as_str(), "deterministic" | "cast")) {
                    return self.lower_block_value(body)?.ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                        msg: "directive block (@deterministic/@cast) must yield a value".into(),
                        line: span.line, col: span.col,
                    });
                }
                unsupported(span, "directive blocks as expressions (only @fuse, @deterministic, @cast are supported)")
            }
            Expr::StructLit { name, type_args, fields, span } => {
                self.lower_struct_lit(name, type_args, fields, span)
            }
            Expr::Range { span, .. } => unsupported(span, "range expressions"),
            Expr::Underscore(s) => err(s, "`_` is only legal in pipe stages, not as a value"),
            Expr::Spread(s) => err(s, "`...` is only legal in call arg lists"),
        }
    }

    fn lower_literal(&mut self, lit: &Literal, span: &Span) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        match lit {
            Literal::Int(n, _) => {
                let v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, *n);
                Ok((v, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)))
            }
            Literal::Float(f, _) => {
                // #209: scalar float literals are f64 (the interpreter is
                // canonical and computes scalar floats in f64). Lowering as f32
                // silently rounded `let x: f64 = 0.1` to f32 precision. f32 still
                // exists inside tensors — a literal stored into an f32 tensor is
                // fdemoted at the store boundary by coerce_to.
                let v = self.builder.ins().f64const(*f);
                Ok((v, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F64)))
            }
            Literal::Bool(b) => {
                let v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I8, if *b { 1 } else { 0 });
                Ok((v, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Bool)))
            }
            Literal::Nil => {
                let v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I8, 0);
                Ok((v, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)))
            }
            Literal::Char(_) => unsupported(span, "character literals"),
            Literal::Str(s) => {
                // Store the bytes in the global leak-list so the pointer stays
                // valid for the lifetime of the process.
                let bytes: Vec<u8> = s.as_bytes().to_vec();
                let len = bytes.len() as i64;
                let raw_ptr = bytes.as_ptr() as i64;
                LEAKED_STRING_DATA.lock().unwrap().push(bytes);
                // Emit: __dmc_str_new_from_raw(raw_ptr, len) -> i64 (forge ptr)
                let ptr_val = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, raw_ptr);
                let len_val = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, len);
                let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_str_new_from_raw")
                    .expect("__dmc_str_new_from_raw not registered").clone();
                let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[ptr_val, len_val]);
                let result = self.builder.inst_results(call)[0];
                Ok((result, TyKind::Str))
            }
        }
    }

    /// Lower a struct literal `ModelName { field: expr, ... }` by
    /// forge-allocating a flat 8-bytes-per-field struct and writing each
    /// field value. Returns an `i64` pointer typed as `TyKind::Model(name)`.
    fn lower_struct_lit(
        &mut self,
        name: &str,
        type_args: &[Expr],
        fields: &[(String, Expr)],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        // Look up model layout.
        let layout = self.model_layouts.get(name).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("unknown model `{}`", name),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?.clone();

        let n_fields = layout.len() as i64;
        let alloc_bytes = n_fields * 8;

        // Allocate struct via forge_alloc.
        let ptr = self.forge_alloc(alloc_bytes);

        // For each field provided in the struct literal, lower and store it.
        for (fname, fexpr) in fields {
            let field_idx = layout.iter().position(|(n, _)| n == fname)
                .ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                    msg: format!("model `{}` has no field `{}`", name, fname),
                    line: span.line, col: span.col,
                })?;
            let (_, field_ty) = &layout[field_idx];
            let field_ty = field_ty.clone();
            let offset = (field_idx as i64) * 8;
            let (val, vty) = self.lower_expr(fexpr)?;
            // Coerce the value to the declared field type if needed.
            let val = self.coerce_to(val, &vty, &field_ty, span)?;
            // #249: a tensor field initialized from an existing binding (`M { w: t }`)
            // is a value copy — snapshot it so a later write through `t` doesn't
            // mutate the stored field.
            let val = if is_aliasing_place_expr(fexpr) {
                self.copy_tensor_value(val, &field_ty)
            } else { val };
            // Extend small scalars to i64 for uniform 8-byte storage.
            let store_val = match &field_ty {
                TyKind::Scalar(sk) if sk.cl() != cl::I64 && !sk.is_float() => {
                    // Zero-extend integer types smaller than 64 bits.
                    self.builder.ins().uextend(cl::I64, val)
                }
                TyKind::Scalar(sk) if *sk == ScalarKind::F32 => {
                    // Bitcast f32 → i32 then zero-extend to i64 for storage.
                    let as_i32 = self.builder.ins().bitcast(cl::I32, cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new(), val);
                    self.builder.ins().uextend(cl::I64, as_i32)
                }
                TyKind::Scalar(sk) if *sk == ScalarKind::F64 => {
                    // Bitcast f64 → i64 for storage.
                    self.builder.ins().bitcast(cl::I64, cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new(), val)
                }
                _ => val,
            };
            let offset_val = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, offset);
            let field_ptr = self.builder.ins().iadd(ptr, offset_val);
            self.builder.ins().store(
                cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new(),
                store_val,
                field_ptr,
                0,
            );
        }

        // #267: capture the concrete type args (`Bar[4]` → [4]) so param-shaped
        // field reads resolve against them.
        let args = resolve_dim_exprs(type_args.iter(), &self.shape_env);
        Ok((ptr, TyKind::Model(name.to_string(), args)))
    }

    /// Lower `fn(params) -> ret { body }` as a deferred module-level function.
    /// Returns a fat closure pointer (forge-allocated 16 bytes: [code_ptr, env_ptr])
    /// and `TyKind::Fn`.
    /// The body is pushed to `pending_lambdas` and compiled after the enclosing
    /// function finishes (Cranelift does not allow nested function builders).
    fn lower_fn_lit(&mut self, lit: &crate::ast::FnLit) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        let name = format!("__lambda_{}", *self.lambda_counter);
        *self.lambda_counter += 1;

        let empty_env: HashMap<String, i64> = HashMap::new();
        let mut params: Vec<(String, TyKind, Span)> = Vec::new();
        for p in &lit.params {
            let ty_ast = p.ty.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                msg: format!("lambda param `{}` needs a type annotation in JIT", p.name),
                line: lit.span.line, col: lit.span.col,
            })?;
            let ty = enumify(ty_from_ast(ty_ast, &empty_env)?, self.enums);
            params.push((p.name.clone(), ty, p.span.clone()));
        }
        let ret = match &lit.ret_type {
            Some(rt) => enumify(ty_from_ast(rt, &empty_env)?, self.enums),
            None => TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil),
        };

        // ── Free-variable analysis (conservative snapshot) ──────────────────
        // Any name currently in scope that is NOT one of the lambda's own
        // declared params is a potential capture.
        let param_names: std::collections::HashSet<&str> =
            params.iter().map(|(n, _, _)| n.as_str()).collect();
        let mut captures: Vec<(String, TyKind)> = self.local_tys
            .iter()
            .filter(|(n, _)| !param_names.contains(n.as_str()))
            .map(|(n, ty)| (n.clone(), ty.clone()))
            .collect();
        // Sort for determinism (HashMap iteration order is random).
        captures.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));

        // ── Build the Cranelift signature (__env first, then user params) ────
        let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
        // __env: i64  — always present; null (0) when there are no captures.
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
        for (_, ty, _) in &params {
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(ty.cl()));
        }
        if !matches!(ret, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)) {
            sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(ret.cl()));
        }
        sig.call_conv = cranelift::codegen::isa::CallConv::SystemV;

        let id = self.module
            .declare_function(&name, cranelift_module::Linkage::Local, &sig)
            .map_err(|e| JitError {
                msg: format!("declare lambda `{}`: {}", name, e),
                line: lit.span.line, col: lit.span.col,
            })?;
        self.fns.insert(name.clone(), FnEntry {
            id,
            sig: sig.clone(),
            params: params.clone(),
            ret: ret.clone(),
            mut_param_idxs: vec![],
        });

        // ── Load captured values from the enclosing scope ────────────────────
        // We emit these reads NOW, inside the enclosing function's builder.
        let mut cap_vals: Vec<Value> = Vec::with_capacity(captures.len());
        for (cap_name, _) in &captures {
            let var = self.locals.get(cap_name.as_str()).copied()
                .expect("capture must be a live local");
            cap_vals.push(self.builder.use_var(var));
        }

        // ── Allocate env array and store captured values ─────────────────────
        let n_caps = captures.len() as i64;
        let env_ptr = if n_caps > 0 {
            let arr = self.forge_alloc(n_caps * 8);
            let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
            for (i, cap_val) in cap_vals.iter().enumerate() {
                self.builder.ins().store(flags, *cap_val, arr, (i as i32) * 8);
            }
            arr
        } else {
            self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0)
        };

        // ── Defer body compilation ────────────────────────────────────────────
        // FnMeta.params must mirror the Cranelift signature exactly: __env first,
        // then the user-declared params. define_fn uses (name, ty) to bind
        // block_params[i] → variable, so they must be in the same order as the sig.
        let mut meta_params = vec![
            ("__env".to_string(), TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), lit.span.clone()),
        ];
        meta_params.extend(params.clone());
        self.pending_lambdas.push(FnMeta {
            id,
            sig,
            params: meta_params,
            ret: ret.clone(),
            body: lit.body.clone(),
            name: name.clone(),
            span: lit.span.clone(),
            shape_env: HashMap::new(),
            grad_mode: GradMode::None,
            mut_param_idxs: vec![],
            captures: captures.clone(),
        });

        // ── Build fat pointer: [code_ptr: i64 @ +0][env_ptr: i64 @ +8] ───────
        let fat = self.forge_alloc(16);
        let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(id, self.builder.func);
        let code_ptr = self.builder.ins().func_addr(cl::I64, func_ref);
        self.builder.ins().store(flags, code_ptr, fat, 0);
        self.builder.ins().store(flags, env_ptr, fat, 8);

        let fn_ty = TyKind::Fn(
            params.into_iter().map(|(_, ty, _)| ty).collect(),
            Box::new(ret),
        );
        Ok((fat, fn_ty))
    }

    /// Emit an indirect call through a fat closure pointer.
    /// `fat_ptr` points to a 16-byte forge allocation `[code_ptr: i64][env_ptr: i64]`.
    /// `param_tys` / `ret_ty` come from the callee's `TyKind::Fn` (user-visible params;
    /// the hidden `__env` first arg is prepended automatically).
    fn lower_indirect_call(
        &mut self,
        fat_ptr: Value,
        param_tys: &[TyKind],
        ret_ty: TyKind,
        args: &[CallArg],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        if args.len() != param_tys.len() {
            return err(span, format!(
                "indirect call expects {} arg(s), got {}",
                param_tys.len(), args.len(),
            ));
        }
        // Load the two words of the fat pointer.
        let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
        let code_ptr = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, fat_ptr, 0);
        let env_ptr  = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, fat_ptr, 8);

        // Signature: (__env: i64, user_params...) -> ret
        let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
        sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64)); // __env
        for ty in param_tys {
            sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(ty.cl()));
        }
        let returns_value = !matches!(ret_ty, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil));
        if returns_value {
            sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(ret_ty.cl()));
        }
        sig.call_conv = cranelift::codegen::isa::CallConv::SystemV;

        // Build arg list: env_ptr first, then user args.
        let mut arg_vals: Vec<Value> = Vec::with_capacity(1 + args.len());
        arg_vals.push(env_ptr);
        for (a, expected) in args.iter().zip(param_tys.iter()) {
            let e = match a {
                CallArg::Positional(e) => e,
                _ => return unsupported(span, "named/spread args in indirect call"),
            };
            let (v, ty) = self.lower_expr(e)?;
            let v = self.coerce_to(v, &ty, expected, span)?;
            arg_vals.push(v);
        }

        let sig_ref = self.builder.import_signature(sig);
        let call = self.builder.ins().call_indirect(sig_ref, code_ptr, &arg_vals);
        if returns_value {
            Ok((self.builder.inst_results(call)[0], ret_ty))
        } else {
            let z = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I8, 0);
            Ok((z, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)))
        }
    }

    fn lower_ident(&mut self, name: &str, span: &Span) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        if let Some(var) = self.locals.get(name) {
            let ty = self.local_tys.get(name).unwrap().clone();
            let v = self.builder.use_var(*var);
            return Ok((v, ty));
        }
        // A shape parameter used as a scalar value (e.g. `D as f32` for the
        // attention scale `1/sqrt(D)`). In a monomorphized function the shape
        // env binds it to a concrete i64; materialize that constant.
        if let Some(&dim) = self.shape_env.get(name) {
            let v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, dim);
            return Ok((v, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)));
        }
        // Named function used as a first-class value: build a fat closure
        // pointer with env_ptr=0 via a thin trampoline __clos_FUNCNAME that
        // accepts (__env: i64, original_params...) and forwards to the named fn.
        // Exclude __dmc_ builtins (ABI mismatch) and template-only entries.
        if let Some(entry) = self.fns.get(name).cloned() {
            if !name.starts_with("__dmc_") {
                let trampoline_name = format!("__clos_{}", name);
                // Declare the trampoline only once.
                if !self.fns.contains_key(&trampoline_name) {
                    // Trampoline sig: (__env: i64, original_params...) -> ret
                    let mut tram_sig = self.module.make_signature();
                    tram_sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64)); // __env (ignored)
                    for (_, ty, _) in &entry.params {
                        tram_sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(ty.cl()));
                    }
                    let returns_value = !matches!(entry.ret, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil));
                    if returns_value {
                        tram_sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(entry.ret.cl()));
                    }
                    tram_sig.call_conv = cranelift::codegen::isa::CallConv::SystemV;
                    let tram_id = self.module
                        .declare_function(&trampoline_name, cranelift_module::Linkage::Local, &tram_sig)
                        .map_err(|e| JitError {
                            msg: format!("declare trampoline `{}`: {}", trampoline_name, e),
                            line: span.line, col: span.col,
                        })?;
                    self.fns.insert(trampoline_name.clone(), FnEntry {
                        id: tram_id,
                        sig: tram_sig.clone(),
                        params: {
                            let mut ps = vec![("__env".to_string(), TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64),
                                span.clone())];
                            ps.extend(entry.params.clone());
                            ps
                        },
                        ret: entry.ret.clone(),
                        mut_param_idxs: vec![],
                    });
                    // Push a sentinel FnMeta that define_fn will recognise as a
                    // trampoline and compile as a forwarding call to the real fn.
                    self.pending_lambdas.push(FnMeta {
                        id: tram_id,
                        sig: tram_sig,
                        params: {
                            let mut ps = vec![("__env".to_string(), TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64),
                                span.clone())];
                            ps.extend(entry.params.clone());
                            ps
                        },
                        ret: entry.ret.clone(),
                        body: crate::ast::Block { stmts: vec![], tail_expr: None, span: span.clone() },
                        name: trampoline_name.clone(),
                        span: span.clone(),
                        shape_env: self.shape_env.clone(),
                        grad_mode: GradMode::None,
                        mut_param_idxs: vec![],
                        // captures[0] sentinel encodes the real function name.
                        captures: vec![
                            (format!("__trampoline_target:{}", name),
                             TyKind::Fn(
                                 entry.params.iter().map(|(_, ty, _)| ty.clone()).collect(),
                                 Box::new(entry.ret.clone()),
                             ))
                        ],
                    });
                }
                // Look up the (possibly just-registered) trampoline.
                let tram_entry = self.fns.get(&trampoline_name).cloned().unwrap();
                let fn_ty = TyKind::Fn(
                    entry.params.iter().map(|(_, ty, _)| ty.clone()).collect(),
                    Box::new(entry.ret.clone()),
                );
                // Build fat pointer: code=trampoline, env=0.
                let fat = self.forge_alloc(16);
                let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
                let tram_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(tram_entry.id, self.builder.func);
                let code_ptr = self.builder.ins().func_addr(cl::I64, tram_ref);
                let env_zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
                self.builder.ins().store(flags, code_ptr, fat, 0);
                self.builder.ins().store(flags, env_zero, fat, 8);
                return Ok((fat, fn_ty));
            }
        }
        // #268: a top-level module constant (`let NAME = <literal>`). Re-lower
        // its (constant) initializer at the use site — for an int/float/bool
        // literal this materializes an iconst/fconst, no globals needed.
        if let Some(init) = self.global_consts.get(name).cloned() {
            return self.lower_expr(&init);
        }
        err(span, format!("unknown binding `{}` (JIT has no globals)", name))
    }

    fn lower_if(&mut self, i: &IfExpr) -> Result<Option<(Value, TyKind)>, JitError> {
        let (c, ck) = self.lower_expr(&i.cond)?;
        let ck_sc = ck.as_scalar();
        if !ck_sc.map(|s| s.is_bool()).unwrap_or(false) {
            return err(&i.span, format!("if-condition must be `bool`, got `{}`", ck.render()));
        }
        let then_block = self.builder.create_block();
        let else_block = self.builder.create_block();
        let join = self.builder.create_block();

        self.brif(c, then_block, else_block);

        // then
        self.enter(then_block);
        let then_val = self.lower_block_value(&i.then_branch)?;
        let then_filled = self.is_filled();
        let mut join_ty: Option<TyKind> = then_val.as_ref().map(|(_, k)| k.clone());
        if !then_filled {
            match &then_val {
                Some((v, _)) => self.jump(join, &[*v]),
                None => self.jump(join, &[]),
            }
        }
        self.builder.seal_block(then_block);

        // else
        self.enter(else_block);
        let else_val = match &i.else_branch {
            Some(ElseBranch::Block(b)) => self.lower_block_value(b)?,
            Some(ElseBranch::If(nested)) => self.lower_if(nested)?,
            None => None,
        };
        let else_filled = self.is_filled();
        if let Some((_, k)) = &else_val {
            if let Some(jk) = &join_ty {
                if jk != k {
                    // A nil-able `map_get` result (i64?) in one branch and a plain
                    // value in the other isn't unified by the JIT yet (#300.4) —
                    // the interpreter handles it dynamically. Point at the fix.
                    let opt_involved = matches!(jk, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::OptI64))
                        || matches!(k, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::OptI64));
                    let hint = if opt_involved {
                        " — a maybe-nil map_get value can't share an `if` with a plain \
                         value in the JIT yet; unwrap it first (e.g. `map_get(..) + 0`), \
                         compare to nil, or use `dmc run`"
                    } else { "" };
                    return err(&i.span, format!(
                        "if/else branches disagree on type: `{}` vs `{}`{}",
                        jk.render(), k.render(), hint,
                    ));
                }
            } else {
                join_ty = Some(k.clone());
            }
        }
        if !else_filled {
            match &else_val {
                Some((v, _)) => self.jump(join, &[*v]),
                None => self.jump(join, &[]),
            }
        }
        self.builder.seal_block(else_block);

        // join
        if let Some(k) = &join_ty {
            self.builder.append_block_param(join, k.cl());
        }
        self.enter(join);
        self.builder.seal_block(join);

        let result = if let Some(k) = join_ty {
            let v = self.builder.block_params(join)[0];
            Some((v, k))
        } else {
            None
        };

        // If both branches terminated (no fall-through), the join block is
        // unreachable. Emit a trap so codegen succeeds.
        if then_filled && else_filled {
            self.trap_user(1);
        }

        Ok(result)
    }

    /// Read a bracketed shape literal (`[H, W]`, `[N]`, or `[[H, 1]]`'s
    /// inner) into concrete dims, resolving shape params via `shape_env`.
    fn const_dims(&self, shape_expr: &Expr, span: &Span) -> Result<Vec<i64>, JitError> {
        match shape_expr {
            Expr::TensorLit(elems, _) => elems.iter()
                .map(|e| resolve_shape_expr(e, &self.shape_env, span))
                .collect(),
            other => Ok(vec![resolve_shape_expr(other, &self.shape_env, span)?]),
        }
    }

    /// `forge.zeros[f32, [shape]]` / `.ones[...]` / `.uninit[...]` — allocate
    /// in the Forge arena. `zeros` fills with 0.0, `ones` with 1.0, `uninit`
    /// skips the fill entirely (contents unspecified). f32-only (slice surface).
    fn lower_arena_alloc(
        &mut self,
        method: &str,
        idxs: &[IndexElem],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        let args: Vec<&Expr> = idxs.iter().filter_map(|e| match e {
            IndexElem::Expr(x) => Some(x),
            _ => None,
        }).collect();
        if args.len() != 2 {
            return err(span, "`zeros`/`ones`/`uninit` take a dtype and a shape: `forge.zeros[f32, [..]]`");
        }
        // #181/#263: model element type -> a ModelArray (an array of `n`
        // model-instance pointers). The element type may be bare (`Foo`, #181)
        // or parameterized (`Bar[4]`, #263); the parameterization doesn't change
        // the array allocation (each slot is a pointer, instances sized/filled
        // later), so we key on the base model name. `uninit` leaves slots
        // unspecified (the staging idiom fills each after); `zeros`/`ones`
        // null-fill them, since forge_alloc isn't guaranteed zeroed.
        if let Some(base) = model_ctor_base_name(args[0]) {
            if self.model_layouts.contains_key(base) {
                let model_name = base.to_string();
                // #267: capture the element model's concrete type args
                // (`Bar[4]` → [4]) so param-shaped fields resolve on read.
                let type_dims = model_ctor_dims(args[0], &self.shape_env);
                let dims = self.const_dims(args[1], span)?;
                if dims.len() != 1 || dims[0] <= 0 {
                    return err(span, format!(
                        "`forge.{}[{}, [N]]` requires a 1D positive size", method, model_name));
                }
                let n = dims[0];
                let out = self.forge_alloc(n * 8);
                if method != "uninit" {
                    self.fill_const(out, n * 2, 0.0);  // n i64 slots = 2n f32 words
                }
                return Ok((out, TyKind::ModelArray(model_name, n, type_dims)));
            }
        }
        // KV element type -> a KvArray of `n` KV-cache pointer slots, the staging
        // idiom for per-layer caches: `forge.uninit[KV[bf16,[B,H,~,D]], [L]]`.
        // Each slot is filled later by `arr[i] = forge.kv[...](capacity = ...)`.
        // (#273 follow-up.)
        if let Some(kv_res) = kv_ctor_elem_ty(args[0], &self.shape_env, span) {
            let kv = kv_res?;
            let dims = self.const_dims(args[1], span)?;
            if dims.len() != 1 || dims[0] <= 0 {
                return err(span, format!(
                    "`forge.{}[KV[...], [N]]` requires a 1D positive size", method));
            }
            let n = dims[0];
            let out = self.forge_alloc(n * 8);  // n i64 pointer slots
            if method != "uninit" {
                self.fill_const(out, n * 2, 0.0);  // n i64 slots = 2n f32 words
            }
            return Ok((out, TyKind::KvArray(kv, n)));
        }
        // #237: map the element type. bf16/f16/tf32 are computed as f32 in the JIT
        // (the `@cast(bf16)` no-op convention, #179), so they allocate as f32.
        let (elem, tname): (ScalarKind, &str) = match args[0] {
            Expr::Ident(t, _) => {
                let k = match t.as_str() {
                    "f32" => ScalarKind::F32,
                    "f64" => ScalarKind::F64,
                    "i32" => ScalarKind::I32,
                    "i64" => ScalarKind::I64,
                    "bool" => ScalarKind::Bool,
                    "bf16" | "f16" | "tf32" => ScalarKind::F32,
                    _ => return err(span, format!("`forge.{}`: unsupported element type `{}`", method, t)),
                };
                (k, t.as_str())
            }
            _ => return err(span, "tensor constructor element type must be a scalar type name"),
        };
        let dims = self.const_dims(args[1], span)?;
        let ty = TensorTy { elem, shape: dims };
        // Guard an oversized shape: nelems()/nbytes() `.expect()`-panic on i64
        // overflow. Surface a located diagnostic instead of a raw Rust
        // backtrace (#368 follow-up).
        if ty.shape.iter().try_fold(1i64, |a, &d| a.checked_mul(d))
            .and_then(|n| n.checked_mul(ty.elem_bytes())).is_none()
        {
            return err(span, format!(
                "`forge.{}`: tensor shape {:?} is too large — its byte size overflows i64",
                method, ty.shape));
        }
        // Reject a shape that can't fit in RAM up front, so it fails with a
        // located diagnostic instead of OOM-killing the process at run time
        // (the forge arena overcommits) (#368 follow-up).
        if let Some(total) = crate::interp::total_system_memory_bytes() {
            let nbytes = ty.nbytes() as u64;
            if nbytes > total {
                const GIB: f64 = 1024.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0;
                return err(span, format!(
                    "`forge.{}`: tensor shape {:?} needs {:.1} GiB but the system has {:.1} GiB of RAM",
                    method, ty.shape, nbytes as f64 / GIB, total as f64 / GIB));
            }
        }
        let out = self.forge_alloc(ty.nbytes());
        // The fill loop writes f32-width (32-bit) words, so it is only correct
        // where the zero/one bit pattern matches at 32 bits. `uninit` never fills,
        // so it works for any element type (this is what the bf16/bool qwen3 paths
        // use); for other element types `zeros`/`ones` point at `uninit`.
        match method {
            "uninit" => {}
            // #274: zero is all-zero bits at any width — fill the whole buffer as
            // 32-bit zero words (nbytes/4). Scoped to the 32/64-bit numeric kinds
            // (f32, incl. bf16-as-f32; i32; i64); `ones` still needs a per-width
            // pattern, and sub-word kinds (bool) keep the explicit-uninit path.
            "zeros" if matches!(elem, ScalarKind::F32 | ScalarKind::I32 | ScalarKind::I64) =>
                self.fill_const(out, ty.nbytes() / 4, 0.0),
            "zeros" => return err(span, format!(
                "`forge.zeros[{}, ..]` not supported (zero-fill is 32-bit); use `forge.uninit` and fill explicitly", tname)),
            "ones" if elem == ScalarKind::F32 => self.fill_const(out, ty.nelems(), 1.0),
            "ones" => return err(span, format!(
                "`forge.ones[{}, ..]` not supported (only f32 `ones`); use `forge.uninit` and fill explicitly", tname)),
            _ => {}
        }
        Ok((out, TyKind::Tensor(ty)))
    }

    /// `forge.trit[K, N]` — allocate a zero-initialised packed trit weight matrix.
    /// Layout: [pos_bits: u64 * n_words * N][neg_bits: u64 * n_words * N]
    /// where n_words = ceil(K / 64). Both halves are zeroed (all zero-trits).
    fn lower_forge_trit(
        &mut self,
        idxs: &[IndexElem],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        let dims: Vec<&Expr> = idxs.iter().filter_map(|e| match e {
            IndexElem::Expr(x) => Some(x),
            _ => None,
        }).collect();
        if dims.len() != 2 {
            return err(span, "`forge.trit` requires exactly 2 dimensions: `forge.trit[K, N]`");
        }
        let k = resolve_shape_expr(dims[0], &self.shape_env, span)?;
        let n = resolve_shape_expr(dims[1], &self.shape_env, span)?;
        if k <= 0 || n <= 0 {
            return err(span, format!("`forge.trit` dimensions must be > 0, got [{}, {}]", k, n));
        }
        let tt = TritTensorTy { k, n };
        let total_bytes = tt.nbytes();
        let ptr = self.forge_alloc(total_bytes);
        // Zero-fill via fill_const treating the buffer as f32 words.
        // total_bytes is always divisible by 8 (u64 aligned), so / 4 is exact.
        let n_f32_words = total_bytes / 4;
        self.fill_const(ptr, n_f32_words, 0.0);
        Ok((ptr, TyKind::TritTensor(tt)))
    }

    /// `forge.kv[f32, [.., ~, ..]](capacity = N)` — allocate a KV streaming
    /// cache. Layout: a 16-byte header (`len = 0`, `cap = N`) followed by a
    /// zero-filled `cap * frame_elems` f32 data region (see `KvTy`).
    fn lower_forge_kv(
        &mut self,
        type_idxs: &[IndexElem],
        args: &[CallArg],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        let targs: Vec<&Expr> = type_idxs.iter().filter_map(|e| match e {
            IndexElem::Expr(x) => Some(x),
            _ => None,
        }).collect();
        if targs.len() != 2 {
            return err(span, "`forge.kv` expects a dtype and a shape: \
                              `forge.kv[f32, [.., ~, ..]](capacity = N)`");
        }
        // #237: bf16/f16 KV caches are computed as f32 in the JIT (the bf16 no-op
        // convention, #176/#179), so accept them and allocate the f32 layout below.
        match targs[0] {
            Expr::Ident(t, _) if matches!(t.as_str(), "f32" | "bf16" | "f16" | "tf32") => {}
            _ => return err(span, "JIT KV constructor element type must be f32 or bf16/f16 (computed as f32)"),
        }
        let elems = match targs[1] {
            Expr::TensorLit(es, _) => es,
            _ => return err(span, "`forge.kv` shape must be a literal like `[B, ~, D]`"),
        };
        let mut dims: Vec<i64> = Vec::new();
        let mut stream_axis: Option<usize> = None;
        for (i, e) in elems.iter().enumerate() {
            if is_streaming_expr(e) {
                if stream_axis.is_some() {
                    return err(span, "`forge.kv` shape may have only one streaming `~` axis");
                }
                stream_axis = Some(i);
            } else {
                let v = resolve_shape_expr(e, &self.shape_env, span)?;
                if v <= 0 {
                    return err(span, format!("`forge.kv` dim must be > 0, got {}", v));
                }
                dims.push(v);
            }
        }
        let stream_axis = stream_axis.ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: "`forge.kv` shape must contain a streaming `~` axis".into(),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?;
        // `capacity = N` — resolved as a shape expression (literal or arithmetic
        // over shape params, e.g. `capacity = S + max_new`).
        let cap_expr = args.iter().find_map(|a| match a {
            CallArg::Named { name, value, .. } if name == "capacity" => Some(value),
            _ => None,
        }).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: "`forge.kv` requires a `capacity = N` argument".into(),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?;
        let cap = resolve_shape_expr(cap_expr, &self.shape_env, span)?;
        if cap <= 0 {
            return err(span, format!("`forge.kv` capacity must be > 0, got {}", cap));
        }

        let kv = KvTy { elem: ScalarKind::F32, dims, stream_axis, cap: Some(cap) };
        let frame = kv.frame_elems();
        let data_elems = cap.checked_mul(frame).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: "`forge.kv` capacity * frame size overflows i64".into(),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?;
        let total_bytes = 16 + data_elems * 4;
        let hdr = self.forge_alloc(total_bytes);
        let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        self.builder.ins().store(flags, zero, hdr, 0);          // len = 0
        let capv = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, cap);
        self.builder.ins().store(flags, capv, hdr, 8);          // cap = N
        // Zero the data region (forge_alloc is not guaranteed zeroed).
        let sixteen = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 16);
        let data = self.builder.ins().iadd(hdr, sixteen);
        self.fill_const(data, data_elems, 0.0);
        Ok((hdr, TyKind::KV(kv)))
    }

    /// `cache <- frame` — append `frame` along the KV streaming axis: copy its
    /// bytes into the next free slot(s) and bump the runtime `len`. Traps if the
    /// append would exceed the declared capacity (Spec §3.6: panic, no realloc).
    ///
    /// This variant looks up the KV header pointer from `var` (a local variable).
    fn lower_stream_append(
        &mut self,
        var: cranelift::frontend::Variable,
        kv_ty: &TyKind,
        name: &str,
        rhs: &Expr,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        let kv = kv_ty.as_kv().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("`<-` stream-append requires a KV stream on the left; \
                          `{}` is `{}`", name, kv_ty.render()),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?.clone();
        let header = self.builder.use_var(var);
        self.lower_stream_append_ptr(header, &kv, rhs, span)
    }

    /// `cache <- frame` — core implementation that takes the KV header pointer
    /// as a `Value` directly (used by both variable-based and array-indexed forms).
    fn lower_stream_append_ptr(
        &mut self,
        header: Value,
        kv: &KvTy,
        rhs: &Expr,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        let (src, src_ty) = self.lower_expr(rhs)?;
        let st = src_ty.as_tensor().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("`<-` requires a tensor on the right, got `{}`", src_ty.render()),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?.clone();
        // Element-type check: allow bf16-sourced frames into f32 KV caches since
        // the JIT maps bf16 @cast to f32 internally. Other mismatches are errors.
        let elem_ok = st.elem == kv.elem
            || (kv.elem == ScalarKind::F32 && st.elem == ScalarKind::F32);
        if !elem_ok {
            return err(span, format!(
                "`<-` element type mismatch: stream is {}, frame is {}",
                kv.elem.name(), st.elem.name()));
        }
        if st.rank() != kv.rank() {
            return err(span, format!(
                "`<-` rank mismatch: stream is rank {}, frame is rank {}",
                kv.rank(), st.rank()));
        }
        // Non-streaming dims must match; the stream-axis extent is the frame count.
        let mut l_frames = 0i64;
        for axis in 0..st.rank() {
            if axis == kv.stream_axis {
                l_frames = st.shape[axis];
            } else if st.shape[axis] != kv.dim_at(axis) {
                return err(span, format!(
                    "`<-` shape mismatch on axis {}: stream has {}, frame has {}",
                    axis, kv.dim_at(axis), st.shape[axis]));
            }
        }
        if l_frames <= 0 {
            return err(span, "`<-` frame must have a positive streaming extent");
        }
        let inner = kv.inner();
        let outer = kv.outer();
        let cnt = l_frames * inner;     // contiguous elems copied per outer row

        let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
        let len = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, header, 0);
        let cap = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, header, 8);
        let lv = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, l_frames);
        let newlen = self.builder.ins().iadd(len, lv);
        // #399: capacity guard — if len + L > cap, call __dmc_kv_cap_trap for a
        // clean "exceeded declared capacity" message + exit(1), matching the
        // interpreter, instead of the old bare `trapnz` (silent SIGILL). The
        // guard runs before the copy below, so no out-of-bounds write occurs.
        let over = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedGreaterThan, newlen, cap);
        let trap_block = self.builder.create_block();
        let ok_block   = self.builder.create_block();
        self.brif(over, trap_block, ok_block);
        self.builder.seal_block(trap_block);
        self.builder.seal_block(ok_block);
        self.enter(trap_block);
        {
            let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_kv_cap_trap")
                .expect("__dmc_kv_cap_trap not registered").clone();
            let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
            self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[len, lv, cap]);
        }
        self.trap_user(10);  // unreachable: the helper calls process::exit
        self.enter(ok_block);

        let sixteen = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 16);
        let data = self.builder.ins().iadd(header, sixteen);
        self.kv_append_copy(src, data, len, cap, outer, cnt, inner);

        self.builder.ins().store(flags, newlen, header, 0);     // commit len += L
        Ok(())
    }

    /// `k_caches[i] <- frame` — stream-append to element `i` of a KV-array parameter.
    ///
    /// `k_caches` is `TyKind::KvArray(kv, n)` — an i64 pointing to a contiguous
    /// block of `n` i64 KV header pointers. Index `i` is a runtime value; we load
    /// the KV pointer from `base_ptr + i * 8`, then delegate to `lower_stream_append_ptr`.
    fn lower_kv_array_append(
        &mut self,
        base: &Expr,
        idxs: &[IndexElem],
        rhs: &Expr,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        let (arr_ptr, arr_ty) = self.lower_expr(base)?;
        let kv = match &arr_ty {
            TyKind::KvArray(kv, _) => kv.clone(),
            other => return err(span, format!(
                "`<-` with indexed LHS requires a `[KV[...]; N]` array, got `{}`",
                other.render(),
            )),
        };
        if idxs.len() != 1 {
            return err(span, "`<-` KV array index must be a single integer index");
        }
        let idx_expr = match &idxs[0] {
            IndexElem::Expr(e) => e,
            _ => return unsupported(span, "non-expression KV array index for `<-`"),
        };
        let (idx_v, idx_ty) = self.lower_expr(idx_expr)?;
        let idx_i64 = self.coerce_to(idx_v, &idx_ty, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;
        // Load the KV header pointer: arr_ptr[idx * 8]
        let eight = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 8);
        let byte_off = self.builder.ins().imul(idx_i64, eight);
        let elem_addr = self.builder.ins().iadd(arr_ptr, byte_off);
        let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
        let kv_ptr = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, elem_addr, 0);
        self.lower_stream_append_ptr(kv_ptr, &kv, rhs, span)
    }

    /// Copy `outer` contiguous blocks of `cnt` f32 from `src` (compact frame
    /// layout) into `data` (cap-strided KV layout) at streaming offset `len`.
    /// `outer`, `cnt`, `inner` are compile-time; `len`, `cap` are runtime.
    fn kv_append_copy(
        &mut self,
        src: Value,
        data: Value,
        len: Value,
        cap: Value,
        outer: i64,
        cnt: i64,
        inner: i64,
    ) {
        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let outer_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, outer);
        let cnt_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, cnt);
        let inner_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, inner);
        let four = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);

        let o_hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let o_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let k_hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let k_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let o_next = self.builder.create_block();
        let done = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(o_hdr, cl::I64);    // o
        self.builder.append_block_param(k_hdr, cl::I64);    // k

        self.jump(o_hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(o_hdr);
        let o = self.builder.block_params(o_hdr)[0];
        let o_cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, o, outer_v);
        self.brif(o_cont, o_body, done);

        self.enter(o_body);
        // dst_base_elems = (o*cap + len) * inner ; src_base_elems = o * cnt
        let ocap = self.builder.ins().imul(o, cap);
        let ocap_len = self.builder.ins().iadd(ocap, len);
        let dst_base = self.builder.ins().imul(ocap_len, inner_v);
        let src_base = self.builder.ins().imul(o, cnt_v);
        self.jump(k_hdr, &[zero]);

        self.enter(k_hdr);
        let k = self.builder.block_params(k_hdr)[0];
        let k_cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, k, cnt_v);
        self.brif(k_cont, k_body, o_next);

        self.enter(k_body);
        let s_elem = self.builder.ins().iadd(src_base, k);
        let s_off = self.builder.ins().imul(s_elem, four);
        let v = self.tensor_load_elem(src, s_off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let d_elem = self.builder.ins().iadd(dst_base, k);
        let d_off = self.builder.ins().imul(d_elem, four);
        self.tensor_store_elem(data, d_off, v);
        let knext = self.builder.ins().iadd(k, one);
        self.jump(k_hdr, &[knext]);

        self.enter(o_next);
        let onext = self.builder.ins().iadd(o, one);
        self.jump(o_hdr, &[onext]);

        self.builder.seal_block(k_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(k_hdr);
        self.builder.seal_block(o_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(o_next);
        self.builder.seal_block(o_hdr);
        self.enter(done);
        self.builder.seal_block(done);
    }

    // ─── Dynamic-shape tensor foundation (issue #176 part 2) ────────────────
    //
    // A `DynTensor` is a self-describing contiguous f32 buffer:
    //   [ ext_0:i64 ]..[ ext_{k-1}:i64 ][ data: f32.. ]
    // with one i64 slot per dynamic axis (axis order) then row-major data over
    // the resolved shape. These helpers are the stable API the Phase-1 kernels
    // (matmul / softmax / transpose over a runtime length) build on.

    /// Runtime-sized forge allocation (`nbytes` is a Value, not a constant).
    fn forge_alloc_v(&mut self, nbytes: Value) -> Value {
        let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_forge_alloc").expect("forge_alloc not registered").clone();
        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[nbytes]);
        self.builder.inst_results(call)[0]
    }

    /// Pointer to the data region of a DynTensor (skips the extent header).
    fn dyn_data_ptr(&mut self, ptr: Value, dt: &DynTensorTy) -> Value {
        let hdr = (dt.n_dyn() as i64) * 8;
        if hdr == 0 { return ptr; }
        let off = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, hdr);
        self.builder.ins().iadd(ptr, off)
    }

    /// Extent of axis `axis` (constant for static dims, header load for dynamic).
    fn dyn_extent(&mut self, ptr: Value, dt: &DynTensorTy, axis: usize) -> Value {
        match dt.dims[axis] {
            Some(n) => self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, n),
            None => {
                let slot = dt.slot_of(axis).expect("dynamic axis has a header slot") as i64;
                let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
                self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, ptr, (slot * 8) as i32)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Total element count = product of all axis extents (runtime).
    fn dyn_total_elems(&mut self, ptr: Value, dt: &DynTensorTy) -> Value {
        let mut acc = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        for axis in 0..dt.rank() {
            let e = self.dyn_extent(ptr, dt, axis);
            acc = self.builder.ins().imul(acc, e);
        }
        acc
    }

    /// Allocate a DynTensor with the given dynamic-axis extents (axis order).
    /// Writes the extent header and returns the base pointer; data is uninit.
    fn dyn_alloc(&mut self, dt: &DynTensorTy, dyn_extents: &[Value]) -> Value {
        debug_assert_eq!(dyn_extents.len(), dt.n_dyn());
        // total elements = product of static dims and dynamic extents.
        let mut total = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let mut di = 0usize;
        for d in &dt.dims {
            let factor = match d {
                Some(n) => self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, *n),
                None => { let v = dyn_extents[di]; di += 1; v }
            };
            total = self.builder.ins().imul(total, factor);
        }
        let four = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);
        let data_bytes = self.builder.ins().imul(total, four);
        let hdr_bytes = (dt.n_dyn() as i64) * 8;
        let hdr_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, hdr_bytes);
        let total_bytes = self.builder.ins().iadd(data_bytes, hdr_v);
        let ptr = self.forge_alloc_v(total_bytes);
        let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
        for (slot, e) in dyn_extents.iter().enumerate() {
            self.builder.ins().store(flags, *e, ptr, (slot * 8) as i32);
        }
        ptr
    }

    /// Row-major byte offset into a DynTensor's data region for `idxs` (one per
    /// axis). Strides are runtime products of trailing extents.
    fn dyn_byte_offset(&mut self, ptr: Value, dt: &DynTensorTy, idxs: &[Value]) -> Value {
        let r = dt.rank();
        let mut offset = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let mut stride = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        for axis in (0..r).rev() {
            let term = self.builder.ins().imul(idxs[axis], stride);
            offset = self.builder.ins().iadd(offset, term);
            let e = self.dyn_extent(ptr, dt, axis);
            stride = self.builder.ins().imul(stride, e);
        }
        let four = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);
        self.builder.ins().imul(offset, four)
    }

    /// Materialize a KV cache's filled prefix `[.., len, ..]` into a fresh
    /// contiguous DynTensor (dynamic on the streaming axis). This is the
    /// KV→tensor conversion the read path uses: after it, all compute sees a
    /// contiguous f32 buffer with one runtime extent, never the cap-strided
    /// KV layout.
    fn kv_materialize(&mut self, kv_ptr: Value, kv: &KvTy) -> (Value, DynTensorTy) {
        let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
        let len = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, kv_ptr, 0);
        let cap = match kv.cap {
            Some(c) => self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, c),
            None => self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, kv_ptr, 8),
        };
        let sixteen = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 16);
        let kv_data = self.builder.ins().iadd(kv_ptr, sixteen);

        let mut dims: Vec<Option<i64>> = kv.dims.iter().map(|&d| Some(d)).collect();
        dims.insert(kv.stream_axis, None);
        let dt = DynTensorTy { elem: kv.elem, dims };

        let out = self.dyn_alloc(&dt, &[len]);
        let out_data = self.dyn_data_ptr(out, &dt);
        self.kv_materialize_copy(kv_data, out_data, kv.outer(), cap, len, kv.inner());
        (out, dt)
    }

    /// Copy `outer` rows of `len*inner` f32 from a cap-strided KV buffer (rows
    /// at `o*cap*inner`) into a contiguous buffer (rows at `o*len*inner`).
    /// `outer`, `inner` are compile-time; `cap`, `len` are runtime.
    fn kv_materialize_copy(
        &mut self,
        src: Value,
        dst: Value,
        outer: i64,
        cap: Value,
        len: Value,
        inner: i64,
    ) {
        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let outer_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, outer);
        let inner_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, inner);
        let four = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);
        let cnt = self.builder.ins().imul(len, inner_v);   // runtime per-row count

        let o_hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let o_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let k_hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let k_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let o_next = self.builder.create_block();
        let done = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(o_hdr, cl::I64);
        self.builder.append_block_param(k_hdr, cl::I64);

        self.jump(o_hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(o_hdr);
        let o = self.builder.block_params(o_hdr)[0];
        let o_cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, o, outer_v);
        self.brif(o_cont, o_body, done);

        self.enter(o_body);
        // src_base = (o*cap)*inner ; dst_base = (o*len)*inner
        let ocap = self.builder.ins().imul(o, cap);
        let src_base = self.builder.ins().imul(ocap, inner_v);
        let olen = self.builder.ins().imul(o, len);
        let dst_base = self.builder.ins().imul(olen, inner_v);
        self.jump(k_hdr, &[zero]);

        self.enter(k_hdr);
        let k = self.builder.block_params(k_hdr)[0];
        let k_cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, k, cnt);
        self.brif(k_cont, k_body, o_next);

        self.enter(k_body);
        let s_elem = self.builder.ins().iadd(src_base, k);
        let s_off = self.builder.ins().imul(s_elem, four);
        let v = self.tensor_load_elem(src, s_off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let d_elem = self.builder.ins().iadd(dst_base, k);
        let d_off = self.builder.ins().imul(d_elem, four);
        self.tensor_store_elem(dst, d_off, v);
        let knext = self.builder.ins().iadd(k, one);
        self.jump(k_hdr, &[knext]);

        self.enter(o_next);
        let onext = self.builder.ins().iadd(o, one);
        self.jump(o_hdr, &[onext]);

        self.builder.seal_block(k_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(k_hdr);
        self.builder.seal_block(o_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(o_next);
        self.builder.seal_block(o_hdr);
        self.enter(done);
        self.builder.seal_block(done);
    }

    /// `forge.snapshot()` — capture the current forge cursor as an i64 mark.
    fn lower_forge_snapshot(
        &mut self,
        args: &[CallArg],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        if !args.is_empty() {
            return err(span, "forge.snapshot() takes no arguments");
        }
        let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_forge_snapshot")
            .expect("forge_snapshot registered").clone();
        let fr = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        let call = self.builder.ins().call(fr, &[]);
        let v = self.builder.inst_results(call)[0];
        Ok((v, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)))
    }

    /// `forge.restore(mark)` — reset forge cursor to a previously-snapshotted mark.
    fn lower_forge_restore(
        &mut self,
        args: &[CallArg],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        if args.len() != 1 {
            return err(span, "forge.restore(mark) takes exactly one argument");
        }
        let mark_e = match &args[0] {
            CallArg::Positional(e) => e.clone(),
            _ => return err(span, "forge.restore: expected positional argument"),
        };
        let (mark_v, mark_ty) = self.lower_expr(&mark_e)?;
        if mark_ty != TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64) {
            return err(span, "forge.restore: argument must be i64 (from forge.snapshot())");
        }
        let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_forge_restore")
            .expect("forge_restore registered").clone();
        let fr = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        self.builder.ins().call(fr, &[mark_v]);
        let nil_val = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        Ok((nil_val, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)))
    }

    /// `vault.load[T, shape](path)` — read a raw binary file into a forge tensor.
    fn lower_vault_load(
        &mut self,
        type_idxs: &[IndexElem],
        args: &[CallArg],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        // Parse type args: [T, shape]
        let type_args: Vec<&Expr> = type_idxs.iter().filter_map(|e| match e {
            IndexElem::Expr(x) => Some(x),
            _ => None,
        }).collect();
        if type_args.len() != 2 {
            return err(span, "`vault.load` requires `vault.load[dtype, shape](path)`");
        }

        // Resolve dtype → elem_bytes
        let elem_bytes: i64 = match type_args[0] {
            Expr::Ident(t, _) => match t.as_str() {
                "f32"  => 4,
                "f64"  => 8,
                "i32"  => 4,
                "i64"  => 8,
                "bf16" => 2,
                "f16"  => 2,
                "bool" => 1,
                other  => return err(span, format!("vault.load: unsupported dtype `{}`", other)),
            },
            _ => return err(span, "vault.load: first type arg must be a dtype identifier"),
        };

        // Resolve shape → TensorTy
        let dims = self.const_dims(type_args[1], span)?;
        let numel: i64 = dims.iter().try_fold(1i64, |a, &d| a.checked_mul(d))
            .ok_or_else(|| JitError { msg: "vault.load: shape overflow".into(), line: span.line, col: span.col })?;

        // Return type — use F32 as elem placeholder for sub-word dtypes
        let ret_elem = match elem_bytes {
            4 => ScalarKind::F32,
            8 => ScalarKind::F64,
            _ => ScalarKind::F32, // bf16, f16, bool stored as raw pointer
        };
        let ret_ty = TyKind::Tensor(TensorTy { elem: ret_elem, shape: dims });

        // Get the path string argument
        if args.is_empty() {
            return err(span, "vault.load requires a path argument");
        }
        let (path_val, _) = match &args[0] {
            CallArg::Positional(e) => self.lower_expr(e)?,
            _ => return err(span, "vault.load: path must be a positional argument"),
        };

        // Emit the call to __dmc_vault_load_raw(path_str, numel, elem_bytes) -> i64
        let numel_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, numel);
        let elem_bytes_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, elem_bytes);
        let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_vault_load_raw")
            .ok_or_else(|| JitError { msg: "__dmc_vault_load_raw not registered".into(), line: span.line, col: span.col })?
            .clone();
        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[path_val, numel_v, elem_bytes_v]);
        let result = self.builder.inst_results(call)[0];
        Ok((result, ret_ty))
    }

    /// `vault.load_npz[T, shape](path, key="name")` — read one array from a NumPy NPZ archive.
    fn lower_vault_load_npz(
        &mut self,
        type_idxs: &[IndexElem],
        args: &[CallArg],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        // Parse type args: [T, shape]
        let type_args: Vec<&Expr> = type_idxs.iter().filter_map(|e| match e {
            IndexElem::Expr(x) => Some(x),
            _ => None,
        }).collect();
        if type_args.len() != 2 {
            return err(span, "`vault.load_npz` requires `vault.load_npz[dtype, shape](path, key=...)`");
        }

        // Resolve dtype → (on-disk elem_bytes, conversion code, JIT-native elem).
        // bf16/f16 are stored f32-backed in the JIT (the `@cast(bf16)` no-op
        // convention), so their 2-byte on-disk data is widened to f32 at load
        // (#292): without this the f32-typed buffer holds half-width data and
        // every downstream f32 op (matmul/transpose) strides it 2× and reads off
        // the end. `ret_elem` is the JIT-native element kind of the returned
        // buffer — it must be derived per-dtype, NOT from `elem_bytes`. The old
        // code keyed `ret_elem` off `elem_bytes` (1 fell through to F32), so a
        // `bool` array (1 on-disk byte, raw-copied to a 1-byte cl::I8 buffer)
        // was typed F32: every downstream f32 op strode the 1-byte buffer 4× and
        // read off the end — the same half-width class as the bf16 segfault
        // fixed in #317. Bool is JIT-native 1-byte (ScalarKind::Bool → cl::I8),
        // identical to numpy's on-disk bool, so it loads at native width (b).
        // #324: `bf16` now loads at native 2-byte width as a Bf16Tensor (no
        // widen, convert=0) so weight fields keep half the footprint and feed
        // the bf16-direct matmul kernel. f16 still widens to f32 (convert=2).
        let bf16_direct = matches!(type_args[0], Expr::Ident(ref t, _) if t == "bf16");
        let (elem_bytes, convert, ret_elem): (i64, i64, ScalarKind) = match type_args[0] {
            Expr::Ident(t, _) => match t.as_str() {
                "f32"  => (4, 0, ScalarKind::F32),
                "f64"  => (8, 0, ScalarKind::F64),
                "i32"  => (4, 0, ScalarKind::F32),
                "i64"  => (8, 0, ScalarKind::F64),
                "bf16" => (2, 0, ScalarKind::F32),   // raw 2-byte copy → Bf16Tensor
                "f16"  => (2, 2, ScalarKind::F32),
                "bool" => (1, 0, ScalarKind::Bool),
                other  => return err(span, format!("vault.load_npz: unsupported dtype `{}`", other)),
            },
            _ => return err(span, "vault.load_npz: first type arg must be a dtype identifier"),
        };

        // Resolve shape → TensorTy
        let dims = self.const_dims(type_args[1], span)?;
        let numel: i64 = dims.iter().try_fold(1i64, |a, &d| a.checked_mul(d))
            .ok_or_else(|| JitError { msg: "vault.load_npz: shape overflow".into(), line: span.line, col: span.col })?;

        let ret_ty = if bf16_direct {
            TyKind::Bf16Tensor(Bf16TensorTy { shape: dims })
        } else {
            TyKind::Tensor(TensorTy { elem: ret_elem, shape: dims })
        };

        // Find path (first positional) and key (named arg key=...)
        let mut path_expr: Option<&Expr> = None;
        let mut key_expr: Option<&Expr> = None;
        for arg in args {
            match arg {
                CallArg::Positional(e) if path_expr.is_none() => path_expr = Some(e),
                CallArg::Named { name, value, .. } if name == "key" => key_expr = Some(value),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        let path_expr = path_expr.ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: "vault.load_npz requires a path argument".into(), line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?;
        let key_expr = key_expr.ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: "vault.load_npz requires `key=` argument".into(), line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?;

        let (path_val, _) = self.lower_expr(path_expr)?;
        let (key_val, _) = self.lower_expr(key_expr)?;

        // Emit the call to __dmc_vault_load_npz(path_str, key_str, numel, elem_bytes, convert) -> i64
        let numel_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, numel);
        let elem_bytes_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, elem_bytes);
        let convert_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, convert);
        let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_vault_load_npz")
            .ok_or_else(|| JitError { msg: "__dmc_vault_load_npz not registered".into(), line: span.line, col: span.col })?
            .clone();
        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[path_val, key_val, numel_v, elem_bytes_v, convert_v]);
        let result = self.builder.inst_results(call)[0];
        Ok((result, ret_ty))
    }

    /// `@fuse { expr }` — lower an elementwise chain as a single-pass kernel.
    ///
    /// Eliminates intermediate Forge allocations: a chain of N same-shape
    /// elementwise ops produces one output tensor and one loop, not N tensors
    /// and N loops. Only pure-elementwise ops over same-shape f32 tensors are
    /// supported; anything else returns a `fuse-infeasible` error.
    ///
    /// When the block contains `let` statements before the tail expression,
    /// we fall back to normal (non-fused) block lowering: all statements are
    /// evaluated in order and the tail expression is the produced value.
    /// The single-kernel fusion guarantee is relaxed in this case, but
    /// correctness is preserved.
    fn lower_fuse_block(
        &mut self,
        body: &Block_,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        // Fast path: no statements — use the single-pass fused kernel.
        if body.stmts.is_empty() {
            let expr = match body.tail_expr.as_ref() {
                Some(e) => e.as_ref(),
                None => return err(span, "fuse-infeasible: @fuse block is empty"),
            };

            // Phase 1: static shape inference — determines output tensor type
            // without emitting any IR. Errors on unsupported ops.
            let out_ty = self.fuse_infer_ty(expr, span)?;
            let n = out_ty.nelems();
            let out_ptr = self.forge_alloc(out_ty.nbytes());

            // Phase 2: emit a single scalar loop over [0, n).
            let zero  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
            let one   = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
            let cap   = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, n);
            let eb    = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);

            let hdr  = self.builder.create_block();
            let body_blk = self.builder.create_block();
            let exit = self.builder.create_block();
            self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);

            self.jump(hdr, &[zero]);
            self.enter(hdr);
            let i = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
            let cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, i, cap);
            self.brif(cont, body_blk, exit);

            self.enter(body_blk);
            let off = self.builder.ins().imul(i, eb);
            let ov = self.fuse_emit_elem(expr, off, span)?;
            self.tensor_store_elem(out_ptr, off, ov);
            let inext = self.builder.ins().iadd(i, one);
            self.jump(hdr, &[inext]);

            self.builder.seal_block(body_blk);
            self.builder.seal_block(hdr);
            self.enter(exit);
            self.builder.seal_block(exit);

            return Ok((out_ptr, TyKind::Tensor(out_ty)));
        }

        // Fallback path: block has `let` statements before the tail expression.
        // Lower all statements normally, then produce the tail value.
        // The single-pass fusion guarantee is waived; intermediate tensors may
        // be materialized. Correctness is not affected.
        for stmt in &body.stmts {
            self.lower_stmt(stmt)?;
            if self.is_filled() {
                return err(span, "fuse-infeasible: @fuse block terminated early (control flow)");
            }
        }
        let expr = match body.tail_expr.as_ref() {
            Some(e) => e.as_ref(),
            None => return err(span, "fuse-infeasible: @fuse block with statements must end with a tail expression"),
        };

        // Lower the tail expression as-is (no fusion optimisation).
        self.lower_expr(expr)
    }

    /// Static pass: infer the TensorTy of a fusable expression without
    /// emitting IR. Returns the output shape, or a `fuse-infeasible` error if
    /// the expression contains an op that cannot be fused.
    fn fuse_infer_ty(&self, expr: &Expr, span: &Span) -> Result<TensorTy, JitError> {
        match expr {
            // Single-element tuple = parenthesised expression; unwrap transparently.
            Expr::Tuple(elems, _) if elems.len() == 1 => {
                return self.fuse_infer_ty(&elems[0], span);
            }
            Expr::BinOp { op, lhs, rhs, span: bspan } => {
                match op {
                    BinOp::DotAdd | BinOp::DotSub | BinOp::DotMul | BinOp::DotDiv
                    | BinOp::DotLt | BinOp::DotGt | BinOp::DotLe | BinOp::DotGe
                    | BinOp::DotPow | BinOp::DotPow2 => {
                        // Scalar operands are valid as broadcast inputs; the tensor
                        // operand (whichever side has one) determines the output shape.
                        let l_tensor = self.fuse_try_infer_tensor_ty(lhs, bspan);
                        let r_tensor = self.fuse_try_infer_tensor_ty(rhs, bspan);
                        match (l_tensor, r_tensor) {
                            (Ok(lt), Ok(rt)) => {
                                if lt.shape != rt.shape {
                                    return err(bspan,
                                        "fuse-infeasible: shape mismatch in @fuse elementwise chain");
                                }
                                Ok(lt)
                            }
                            (Ok(lt), Err(_)) => Ok(lt), // rhs is scalar — use lhs shape
                            (Err(_), Ok(rt)) => Ok(rt), // lhs is scalar — use rhs shape
                            (Err(e), Err(_)) => Err(e), // neither side is a tensor
                        }
                    }
                    _ => err(bspan, format!(
                        "fuse-infeasible: op `{:?}` is not elementwise; \
                         only .+ .- .* ./ .^ .< .> .<= .>= are fusable", op)),
                }
            }
            Expr::UnOp { op: UnOp::ReLU, operand, .. } => {
                self.fuse_infer_ty(operand, span)
            }
            Expr::Ident(name, ispan) => {
                match self.local_tys.get(name) {
                    Some(TyKind::Tensor(t)) => Ok(t.clone()),
                    Some(TyKind::Scalar(_)) => err(ispan,
                        "fuse-infeasible: scalar idents must appear inside an elementwise op, \
                         not as the root expression"),
                    Some(TyKind::Model(_, _)) => err(ispan,
                        "fuse-infeasible: model instances are not supported inside @fuse"),
                    Some(TyKind::KV(_)) => err(ispan,
                        "fuse-infeasible: a KV cache must be read as a tensor (its \
                         streaming-axis read is not yet lowered inside @fuse)"),
                    Some(TyKind::DynTensor(_)) => err(ispan,
                        "fuse-infeasible: dynamic-shape tensors are not yet supported inside @fuse"),
                    Some(TyKind::Str) => err(ispan,
                        "fuse-infeasible: string values are not supported inside @fuse"),
                    Some(TyKind::Map) => err(ispan,
                        "fuse-infeasible: map values are not supported inside @fuse"),
                    Some(TyKind::KvArray(_, _)) => err(ispan,
                        "fuse-infeasible: KV-cache arrays are not supported inside @fuse"),
                    Some(TyKind::ModelArray(_, _, _)) => err(ispan,
