                        "fuse-infeasible: model arrays are not supported inside @fuse"),
                    Some(TyKind::Fn(_, _)) => err(ispan,
                        "fuse-infeasible: function pointer values are not supported inside @fuse"),
                    Some(TyKind::TritTensor(_)) => err(ispan,
                        "fuse-infeasible: trit tensor values are not supported inside @fuse"),
                    Some(TyKind::Bf16Tensor(_)) => err(ispan,
                        "fuse-infeasible: bf16 tensor values are not supported inside @fuse"),
                    Some(TyKind::Enum(_)) => err(ispan,
                        "fuse-infeasible: enum values are not supported inside @fuse"),
                    None => err(ispan, format!("unknown identifier `{}`", name)),
                }
            }
            Expr::Literal(Literal::Float(_, _), _) => {
                err(span, "fuse-infeasible: a bare literal is not a tensor")
            }
            _ => err(span,
                "fuse-infeasible: only elementwise ops (.+ .- .* ./ .^ ReLU) \
                 and tensor idents are supported inside @fuse"),
        }
    }

    /// Like `fuse_infer_ty` but returns `Err` (non-fatal) for scalar leaves
    /// instead of a hard error. Used by the BinOp arm to probe whether each
    /// operand is tensor-typed without short-circuiting on scalar broadcasts.
    fn fuse_try_infer_tensor_ty(&self, expr: &Expr, span: &Span) -> Result<TensorTy, JitError> {
        match expr {
            Expr::Tuple(elems, _) if elems.len() == 1 => {
                self.fuse_try_infer_tensor_ty(&elems[0], span)
            }
            Expr::Ident(name, ispan) => match self.local_tys.get(name) {
                Some(TyKind::Tensor(t)) => Ok(t.clone()),
                _ => err(ispan, "scalar"),
            },
            Expr::Literal(Literal::Float(_, _), _) => err(span, "scalar"),
            _ => self.fuse_infer_ty(expr, span),
        }
    }

    /// Emit per-element IR for a fused expression. `off` is the byte offset
    /// of the current lane inside each tensor. Returns the f32 Value for this
    /// element. Only called from inside the loop body emitted by `lower_fuse_block`.
    fn fuse_emit_elem(&mut self, expr: &Expr, off: Value, span: &Span) -> Result<Value, JitError> {
        match expr {
            // Single-element tuple = parenthesised expression; unwrap transparently.
            Expr::Tuple(elems, _) if elems.len() == 1 => {
                return self.fuse_emit_elem(&elems[0], off, span);
            }
            Expr::BinOp { op, lhs, rhs, span: bspan } => {
                let lv = self.fuse_emit_elem(lhs, off, bspan)?;
                let rv = self.fuse_emit_elem(rhs, off, bspan)?;
                Ok(self.emit_f32_elem(op, lv, rv))
            }
            Expr::UnOp { op: UnOp::ReLU, operand, .. } => {
                let v = self.fuse_emit_elem(operand, off, span)?;
                let fzero = self.builder.ins().f32const(0.0);
                let c = self.builder.ins().fcmp(FloatCC::GreaterThan, v, fzero);
                Ok(self.builder.ins().select(c, v, fzero))
            }
            Expr::Ident(name, ispan) => {
                match self.local_tys.get(name).cloned() {
                    Some(TyKind::Tensor(t)) => {
                        let var = self.locals[name];
                        let ptr = self.builder.use_var(var);
                        Ok(self.tensor_load_elem(ptr, off, t.elem))
                    }
                    Some(TyKind::Scalar(sk)) if sk.is_float() => {
                        // Scalar broadcast: same value for every lane. fuse runs on
                        // f32 lanes, so demote the scalar (now f64 by default, #209).
                        let var = self.locals[name];
                        let v = self.builder.use_var(var);
                        Ok(self.coerce_scalar(v, sk, ScalarKind::F32, ispan)?)
                    }
                    _ => err(ispan, format!("fuse: `{}` is not an f32 tensor or scalar", name)),
                }
            }
            Expr::Literal(Literal::Float(v, _), _) => {
                Ok(self.builder.ins().f32const(*v as f32))
            }
            _ => err(span,
                "fuse-infeasible: unsupported sub-expression in @fuse (only idents, \
                 float literals, and elementwise ops are supported)"),
        }
    }

    /// `t.reshape[[d0, d1, ...]]` — reinterpret a contiguous tensor under a
    /// new shape. No data movement; the element count must be preserved.
    fn lower_reshape(
        &mut self,
        inner: &Expr,
        idxs: &[IndexElem],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        let (ptr, k) = self.lower_expr(inner)?;
        let old = match k {
            TyKind::Tensor(t) => t,
            _ => return err(span, "reshape expects a tensor"),
        };
        let shape_expr = match idxs.iter().find_map(|e| match e {
            IndexElem::Expr(x) => Some(x),
            _ => None,
        }) {
            Some(x) => x,
            None => return err(span, "reshape: expected a shape list in brackets"),
        };
        let dims = self.const_dims(shape_expr, span)?;
        let new = TensorTy { elem: old.elem, shape: dims };
        if new.nelems() != old.nelems() {
            return err(span, format!(
                "reshape: element count must be preserved ({} -> {})",
                old.nelems(), new.nelems(),
            ));
        }
        Ok((ptr, TyKind::Tensor(new)))
    }

    /// Store a constant f32 into every element of a freshly-allocated tensor.
    fn fill_const(&mut self, out: Value, n: i64, val: f32) {
        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let cap = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, n);
        let eb = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);
        let fv = self.builder.ins().f32const(val);
        let hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let body = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(hdr);
        let i = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
        let cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, i, cap);
        self.brif(cont, body, exit);
        self.enter(body);
        let off = self.builder.ins().imul(i, eb);
        self.tensor_store_elem(out, off, fv);
        let inext = self.builder.ins().iadd(i, one);
        self.jump(hdr, &[inext]);
        self.builder.seal_block(body);
        self.builder.seal_block(hdr);
        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);
    }

    fn lower_postfix(
        &mut self,
        expr: &Expr,
        op: &PostfixOp,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        match op {
            PostfixOp::Call(args) => {
                // A `.fwd_bwd(...)` reaching here was not destructured.
                if let Expr::Postfix { op: PostfixOp::Field(m), .. } = expr {
                    if m == "fwd_bwd" {
                        return err(span,
                            "`f.fwd_bwd(...)` must be destructured: \
                             `let (loss, grad) = f.fwd_bwd(...)`");
                    }
                }
                // vault.load[T, shape](path) / vault.load_npz[T, shape](path, key=k)
                // The callee expression is: vault.load[T, shape]
                //   = PostfixOp::Index over PostfixOp::Field("load") over Ident("vault")
                if let Expr::Postfix { expr: inner, op: PostfixOp::Index(type_idxs), .. } = expr {
                    if let Expr::Postfix { expr: base, op: PostfixOp::Field(method), .. } = inner.as_ref() {
                        if let Expr::Ident(arena, _) = base.as_ref() {
                            if arena == "vault" {
                                match method.as_str() {
                                    "load" => return self.lower_vault_load(type_idxs, args, span),
                                    "load_npz" => return self.lower_vault_load_npz(type_idxs, args, span),
                                    _ => {}
                                }
                            }
                            // forge.kv[T, [.., ~, ..]](capacity = N) — KV cache alloc.
                            // `stream.kv[...]` is the same constructor in the Stream arena.
                            if (arena == "forge" || arena == "stream") && method == "kv" {
                                return self.lower_forge_kv(type_idxs, args, span);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
                // forge.snapshot() / forge.restore(mark) — per-frame arena reset.
                if let Expr::Postfix { expr: inner, op: PostfixOp::Field(method), .. } = expr {
                    if let Expr::Ident(base, _) = inner.as_ref() {
                        if base == "forge" {
                            match method.as_str() {
                                "snapshot" => return self.lower_forge_snapshot(args, span),
                                "restore"  => return self.lower_forge_restore(args, span),
                                _ => {}
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
                // #350 Part 2b: `Shape.Circle(args)` — payload-enum construction.
                // Intercept before generic call lowering tries to resolve the
                // enum name as a function.
                if let Expr::Postfix { expr: base, op: PostfixOp::Field(variant), .. } = expr {
                    if let Expr::Ident(en, _) = base.as_ref() {
                        if self.enum_payload_layouts.contains_key(en)
                            && self.enums.get(en).is_some_and(|vs| vs.contains(variant))
                        {
                            let mut arg_vals = Vec::with_capacity(args.len());
                            for a in args {
                                match a {
                                    CallArg::Positional(e) => arg_vals.push(self.lower_expr(e)?),
                                    _ => return unsupported(span,
                                        "named/spread argument in enum-variant construction"),
                                }
                            }
                            return self.lower_enum_value(en, variant, arg_vals, span);
                        }
                    }
                }
                self.lower_call(expr, args, span)
            }
            PostfixOp::Index(idxs) => {
                // `<base>.<method>[...]` parses as Index over a Field. Three
                // such forms are tensor constructors / reshapes, not loads:
                //   forge.zeros[f32, [H, W]]  /  vault.ones[f32, [N]]
                //   forge.uninit[f32, [H, W]]  — allocate without zeroing
                //   t.reshape[[H, 1]]
                if let Expr::Postfix { expr: inner, op: PostfixOp::Field(method), .. } = expr {
                    if method == "zeros" || method == "ones" || method == "uninit" {
                        if let Expr::Ident(base, _) = inner.as_ref() {
                            if base == "forge" || base == "vault" {
                                return self.lower_arena_alloc(method, idxs, span);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    // forge.trit[K, N] — allocate a zero-initialised packed trit matrix.
                    if method == "trit" {
                        if let Expr::Ident(base, _) = inner.as_ref() {
                            if base == "forge" {
                                return self.lower_forge_trit(idxs, span);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    if method == "reshape" {
                        return self.lower_reshape(inner, idxs, span);
                    }
                }
                self.lower_index(expr, idxs, span)
            }
            PostfixOp::Field(field) => {
                // Grad-struct field access: `grads.W` → look up `grads$W` local
                // (synthesized by lower_fwd_bwd_destructure for multi-param @grad).
                if let Expr::Ident(name, _) = expr {
                    let key = format!("{}${}", name, field);
                    if let Some(&var) = self.locals.get(&key) {
                        let ty = self.local_tys[&key].clone();
                        let v = self.builder.use_var(var);
                        return Ok((v, ty));
                    }
                    // #350: `Light.Red` — a qualified enum-variant value. The
                    // enum name is not a binding, so intercept before lowering
                    // the base. For a tag-only enum the value is the variant's
                    // i64 ordinal; for a payload enum (#350 Part 2b) it is a
                    // forge-allocated `[tag, …]` region — `Shape.Empty` reaches
                    // here (a tag-only variant of a payload enum), while
                    // `Shape.Circle(2)` is intercepted as a call.
                    if self.enums.contains_key(name) {
                        if self.enum_payload_layouts.contains_key(name) {
                            return self.lower_enum_value(name, field, Vec::new(), span);
                        }
                        match self.enums.get(name).and_then(|vs| vs.iter().position(|vn| vn == field)) {
                            Some(ord) => {
                                let v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, ord as i64);
                                return Ok((v, TyKind::Enum(name.clone())));
                            }
                            None => return err(span,
                                format!("enum `{}` has no variant `{}`", name, field)),
                        }
                    }
                }
                // Model field access: `p.x` where `p` is a model instance.
                let (base_val, base_ty) = self.lower_expr(expr)?;
                if let TyKind::Model(model_name, type_args) = &base_ty {
                    let model_name = model_name.clone();
                    let type_args = type_args.clone();
                    let layout = self.model_layouts.get(model_name.as_str()).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                        msg: format!("unknown model `{}`", model_name),
                        line: span.line, col: span.col,
                    })?.clone();
                    let (field_idx, mut field_ty) = layout.iter().enumerate()
                        .find(|(_, (n, _))| n == field)
                        .map(|(i, (_, t))| (i, t.clone()))
                        .ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                            msg: format!("model `{}` has no field `{}`", model_name, field),
                            line: span.line, col: span.col,
                        })?;
                    // #267: for a parameterized model with concrete args, the
                    // param-agnostic layout stored a param-shaped field (e.g.
                    // `Tensor[f32,[N]]`) as opaque i64. Re-resolve it from the
                    // field's AST type against env = {param → arg}, so the load
                    // below interprets it as the real tensor/model type.
                    if !type_args.is_empty() {
                        let resolved = match (self.model_shape_params.get(&model_name),
                                              self.model_field_asts.get(&model_name)) {
                            (Some(params), Some(fasts)) => {
                                let env: HashMap<String, i64> = params.iter().cloned()
                                    .zip(type_args.iter().copied()).collect();
                                fasts.iter().find(|(n, _)| n == field)
                                    .and_then(|(_, fast)| lower_ty_for_model(fast, &env, span).ok())
                                    .map(|t| enumify(t, self.enums))
                            }
                            _ => None,
                        };
                        if let Some(rt) = resolved { field_ty = rt; }
                    }
                    let offset = (field_idx as i64) * 8;
                    let offset_val = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, offset);
                    let field_ptr = self.builder.ins().iadd(base_val, offset_val);
                    // Load 8 bytes from storage; interpret as the appropriate type.
                    let loaded = match &field_ty {
                        TyKind::Scalar(sk) if *sk == ScalarKind::F32 => {
                            // Stored as bitcast-to-i32 zero-extended to i64; load i64 then truncate+reinterpret.
                            let raw = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new(), field_ptr, 0);
                            let as_i32 = self.builder.ins().ireduce(cl::I32, raw);
                            self.builder.ins().bitcast(cl::F32, cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new(), as_i32)
                        }
                        TyKind::Scalar(sk) if *sk == ScalarKind::F64 => {
                            // Stored as bitcast-to-i64; load i64 then reinterpret.
                            let raw = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new(), field_ptr, 0);
                            self.builder.ins().bitcast(cl::F64, cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new(), raw)
                        }
                        TyKind::Scalar(sk) if sk.cl() != cl::I64 && !sk.is_float() => {
                            // Integer types narrower than i64: load i64 then truncate.
                            let raw = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new(), field_ptr, 0);
                            self.builder.ins().ireduce(sk.cl(), raw)
                        }
                        _ => {
                            // i64, tensors (i64 pointers), nested model pointers (i64).
                            self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new(), field_ptr, 0)
                        }
                    };
                    return Ok((loaded, field_ty));
                }
                unsupported(span, "field access on non-model type")
            }
            PostfixOp::BracketArgs(_) => unsupported(span, "generic-style bracket args"),
            PostfixOp::Constructor(_) => unsupported(span, "model constructor"),
            PostfixOp::Transpose => self.lower_transpose(expr, span),
            PostfixOp::Query => unsupported(span, "error propagation `?`"),
        }
    }

    fn lower_call(
        &mut self,
        callee: &Expr,
        args: &[CallArg],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        // Indirect call: callee is a local variable with a `TyKind::Fn` type.
        // Handles both typed `fn(...)` locals and i64 pointers via explicit annotation.
        if let Expr::Ident(name, _) = callee {
            if let Some(var) = self.locals.get(name.as_str()).copied() {
                if let Some(TyKind::Fn(param_tys, ret_ty)) = self.local_tys.get(name.as_str()) {
                    let param_tys = param_tys.clone();
                    let ret_ty = *ret_ty.clone();
                    let ptr = self.builder.use_var(var);
                    return self.lower_indirect_call(ptr, &param_tys, ret_ty, args, span);
                }
            }
        }
        // General indirect call: any expression that evaluates to TyKind::Fn.
        // This handles chained calls like `make_adder(5)(10)` where the callee
        // is itself a call expression returning a fat closure pointer.
        let is_simple_ident = matches!(callee, Expr::Ident(_, _));
        if !is_simple_ident {
            // Try to evaluate the callee expression. If it yields TyKind::Fn, route
            // to lower_indirect_call. If it doesn't, fall through to the normal path.
            if let Ok((fat_ptr, TyKind::Fn(param_tys, ret_ty))) = self.lower_expr(callee) {
                return self.lower_indirect_call(fat_ptr, &param_tys, *ret_ty, args, span);
            }
            // Non-Fn callee expression — will fall through to unsupported below.
        }
        let name = match callee {
            Expr::Ident(n, _) => n.clone(),
            // Generic call with explicit shape args: `f[H, W](..)`. The
            // brackets are redundant here — instantiate_template infers the
            // shape params from the argument tensors — so take the name and
            // proceed.
            Expr::Postfix { expr: inner, op: PostfixOp::Index(_) | PostfixOp::BracketArgs(_), .. } => {
                match inner.as_ref() {
                    Expr::Ident(n, _) => n.clone(),
                    _ => return unsupported(span, "indirect / dynamic calls"),
                }
            }
            _ => return unsupported(span, "indirect / dynamic calls"),
        };

        // Tensor-aware special-form builtins. These dispatch on the shape of
        // their argument and emit specialized code rather than calling a
        // runtime symbol.
        // Every arm here MUST appear in `JIT_BUILTINS` and be implemented in
        // the interpreter too — parity is enforced by jit::tests::builtin_parity_*.
        match name.as_str() {
            "len" => return self.lower_builtin_len(args, span),
            "str_concat"   => return self.lower_builtin_str_concat(args, span),
            "str_eq"       => return self.lower_builtin_str_eq(args, span),
            "str_get_char" => return self.lower_builtin_str_get_char(args, span),
            "print_str"    => return self.lower_builtin_print_str(args, span),
            "chr"          => return self.lower_builtin_chr(args, span),
            "sleep_ms"     => return self.lower_builtin_sleep_ms(args, span),
            "flush"        => return self.lower_builtin_flush(args, span),
            // `print(s)` where s is TyKind::Str — dispatch to __dmc_print_str.
            "print" if args.len() == 1 => {
                if let CallArg::Positional(e) = &args[0] {
                    let (v, ty) = self.lower_expr(e)?;
                    if ty.is_str() {
                        let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_print_str")
                            .expect("__dmc_print_str not registered").clone();
                        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                        self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[v]);
                        let z = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I8, 0);
                        return Ok((z, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)));
                    }
                    // OptI64 (maybe-nil map_get result, #300.4): branch at runtime
                    // — print the value if present, else "nil" — matching the
                    // interpreter's dynamic print of a `map_get` miss.
                    if matches!(ty, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::OptI64)) {
                        let present = self.opt_present(v);
                        let value = self.opt_value(v);
                        let val_blk = self.builder.create_block();
                        let nil_blk = self.builder.create_block();
                        let join = self.builder.create_block();
                        self.builder.ins().brif(present, val_blk, &[], nil_blk, &[]);
                        self.builder.switch_to_block(val_blk);
                        self.builder.seal_block(val_blk);
                        let pi = self.fns.get("print_i64").expect("print_i64 not registered").clone();
                        let pir = self.module.declare_func_in_func(pi.id, self.builder.func);
                        self.builder.ins().call(pir, &[value]);
                        self.builder.ins().jump(join, &[]);
                        self.builder.switch_to_block(nil_blk);
                        self.builder.seal_block(nil_blk);
                        let pn = self.fns.get("print_nil").expect("print_nil not registered").clone();
                        let pnr = self.module.declare_func_in_func(pn.id, self.builder.func);
                        self.builder.ins().call(pnr, &[]);
                        self.builder.ins().jump(join, &[]);
                        self.builder.switch_to_block(join);
                        self.builder.seal_block(join);
                        let z = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I8, 0);
                        return Ok((z, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)));
                    }
                    // Not a string; dispatch to the appropriate typed print_* fn.
                    let fn_name = match &ty {
                        TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64) | TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I32) => "print_i64",
                        TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F64) | TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32) => "print_f64",
                        TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Bool) => "print_bool",
                        TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)  => "print_nil",
                        _ => return err(span, format!("print: unsupported type `{}`", ty.render())),
                    };
                    let coerce_ty = match fn_name {
                        "print_i64"  => TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64),
                        "print_f64"  => TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F64),
                        "print_bool" => TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Bool),
                        _            => TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil),
                    };
                    let v2 = self.coerce_to(v, &ty, &coerce_ty, span)?;
                    let entry = self.fns.get(fn_name).expect("print builtin not registered").clone();
                    let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                    if fn_name == "print_nil" {
                        self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[]);
                    } else {
                        self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[v2]);
                    }
                    let z = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I8, 0);
                    return Ok((z, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)));
                }
            }
            "sum" => return self.lower_builtin_sum(args, span),
            "mean" => return self.lower_builtin_mean(args, span),
            // #272: tensor max/min/argmax/argmin reductions.
            "max" | "min" => return self.lower_builtin_minmax(name.as_str(), args, span),
            "argmax" | "argmin" => return self.lower_builtin_argreduce(name.as_str(), args, span),
            "variance" => return self.lower_builtin_variance(args, span),
            "pull_to_mean" => return self.lower_builtin_pull_to_mean(args, span),
            "print_tensor" => return self.lower_builtin_print_tensor(args, span),
            // Scalar math primitives.
            "exp" => return self.lower_builtin_scalar_math("__dmc_exp_f64", args, span),
            "sqrt" => return self.lower_builtin_scalar_math("__dmc_sqrt_f64", args, span),
            "log" => return self.lower_builtin_scalar_math("__dmc_log_f64", args, span),
            "sin" => return self.lower_builtin_scalar_math("__dmc_sin_f64", args, span),
            "cos" => return self.lower_builtin_scalar_math("__dmc_cos_f64", args, span),
            // abs/floor/ceil lower to native Cranelift float instructions.
            "abs"   => return self.lower_builtin_scalar_native_math("abs", args, span),
            "floor" => return self.lower_builtin_scalar_native_math("floor", args, span),
            "ceil"  => return self.lower_builtin_scalar_native_math("ceil", args, span),
            // IEEE-754 bit reinterpret (#189) — no arithmetic conversion.
            "f32_to_bits"   => return self.lower_builtin_f32_to_bits(args, span),
            "f32_from_bits" => return self.lower_builtin_f32_from_bits(args, span),
            // Per-axis reductions and variance trait.
            "sum_along" => return self.lower_builtin_reduce_along(ReduceAlong::Add, args, span, /*divide=*/ false),
            "mean_along" => return self.lower_builtin_reduce_along(ReduceAlong::Add, args, span, /*divide=*/ true),
            "max_along" => return self.lower_builtin_reduce_along(ReduceAlong::Max, args, span, /*divide=*/ false),
            "min_along" => return self.lower_builtin_reduce_along(ReduceAlong::Min, args, span, /*divide=*/ false),
            "variance_along" => return self.lower_builtin_variance_along(args, span),
            "pull_to_mean_along" => return self.lower_builtin_pull_to_mean_along(args, span),
            // Fused ML primitives.
            "softmax" => return self.lower_builtin_softmax(args, span),
            "rms_norm" => return self.lower_builtin_rms_norm(args, span),
            "layer_norm" => return self.lower_builtin_layer_norm(args, span),
            "attn"     => return self.lower_builtin_attn(args, span),
            "rope"     => return self.lower_builtin_rope(args, span),
            "attn_gqa" => return self.lower_builtin_attn_gqa(args, span),
            "embed"    => return self.lower_builtin_embed(args, span),
            // Elementwise activation functions.
            "relu"    => return self.lower_builtin_activation("relu",    args, span),
            "tanh"    => return self.lower_builtin_activation("tanh",    args, span),
            "gelu"    => return self.lower_builtin_activation("gelu",    args, span),
            "sigmoid" => return self.lower_builtin_activation("sigmoid", args, span),
            "silu"    => return self.lower_builtin_activation("silu",    args, span),
            "elu"     => return self.lower_builtin_activation("elu",     args, span),
            "mish"    => return self.lower_builtin_activation("mish",    args, span),

            // First-class function pointer builtins.
            // `fn_ptr("fname")` — returns an i64 function pointer for a named
            // demoniC function. The argument must be a string literal; the
            // function name is resolved at JIT compile time.
            "fn_ptr" if args.len() == 1 => {
                let fname = match &args[0] {
                    CallArg::Positional(Expr::Literal(Literal::Str(s), _)) => s.clone(),
                    _ => return err(span, "fn_ptr: argument must be a string literal"),
                };
                let entry = self.fns.get(&fname).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                    msg: format!("fn_ptr: unknown function `{}`", fname),
                    line: span.line,
                    col: span.col,
                })?.clone();
                let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                let ptr_val = self.builder.ins().func_addr(cl::I64, func_ref);
                return Ok((ptr_val, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)));
            }

            // `call_fn(fp, args...)` — calls a function through an i64 pointer.
            // All arguments are treated as i64; return type is i64.
            // Limitation: callee functions with non-i64 params will be called
            // incorrectly; cast at call site if needed.
            "call_fn" if args.len() >= 1 => {
                // First arg is the function pointer (i64).
                let fp_val = match &args[0] {
                    CallArg::Positional(e) => self.lower_expr(e)?.0,
                    CallArg::Named { span: s, .. } => return unsupported(s, "named call arguments"),
                    CallArg::Spread(s) => return unsupported(s, "spread call arguments"),
                };
                // Remaining args are the call arguments (all i64).
                let mut arg_vals: Vec<Value> = Vec::with_capacity(args.len() - 1);
                for a in &args[1..] {
                    let v = match a {
                        CallArg::Positional(e) => self.lower_expr(e)?.0,
                        CallArg::Named { span: s, .. } => return unsupported(s, "named call arguments"),
                        CallArg::Spread(s) => return unsupported(s, "spread call arguments"),
                    };
                    arg_vals.push(v);
                }
                // Build signature: (i64, ...) -> i64, SystemV calling convention.
                let mut sig = self.module.make_signature();
                sig.call_conv = cranelift::codegen::isa::CallConv::SystemV;
                for _ in &arg_vals {
                    sig.params.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
                }
                sig.returns.push(AbiParam::new(cl::I64));
                let sig_ref = self.builder.import_signature(sig);
                let inst = self.builder.ins().call_indirect(sig_ref, fp_val, &arg_vals);
                let result = self.builder.inst_results(inst)[0];
                return Ok((result, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)));
            }

            // HashMap builtins.
            "map_new"      => return self.lower_builtin_map_new(args, span),
            "map_get"      => return self.lower_builtin_map_get(args, span),
            "map_set"      => return self.lower_builtin_map_set(args, span),
            "map_contains" => return self.lower_builtin_map_contains(args, span),
            // Trit tensor builtins — delegate to C runtime functions.
            "trit_quantize" => return self.lower_builtin_trit_quantize(args, span),
            "trit_neg"      => return self.lower_builtin_trit_neg(args, span),
            "trit_sparsity" => return self.lower_builtin_trit_sparsity(args, span),
            _ => {}
        }

        // Lower args first so we know their shapes — needed for either
        // direct monomorphic resolution OR shape-var unification against a
        // template.
        let mut arg_vals: Vec<(Value, TyKind)> = Vec::with_capacity(args.len());
        for a in args {
            let e = match a {
                CallArg::Positional(e) => e,
                CallArg::Named { span, .. } => return unsupported(span, "named call arguments"),
                CallArg::Spread(s) => return unsupported(s, "spread call arguments"),
            };
            let (v, k) = self.lower_expr(e)?;
            arg_vals.push((v, k));
        }

        // Resolve callee: direct fn entry first, then template instantiation.
        let entry = if let Some(e) = self.fns.get(&name) {
            e.clone()
        } else if let Some(tmpl) = self.templates.get(&name).cloned() {
            self.instantiate_template(&tmpl, &arg_vals, span)?
        } else {
            return err(span, format!("unknown function `{}`", name));
        };

        if arg_vals.len() != entry.params.len() {
            return err(span, format!(
                "`{}` expects {} arg(s), got {}", name, entry.params.len(), arg_vals.len(),
            ));
        }
        // #249: `!` tensor params are copy-in/copy-out. The callee mutates a
        // private copy of the arg; on return the copy is written back into the
        // caller's tensor. This isolates aliased args — `f(t, t)` where only
        // the first param is `!` must not let the mutation leak through the
        // second — while preserving the single-arg "callee mutates the caller's
        // tensor" behavior (the writeback restores it). Matches the
        // interpreter's clone-args + writeback-`!` semantics.
        let mut vals: Vec<Value> = Vec::with_capacity(arg_vals.len());
        let mut writebacks: Vec<(Value, Value, TensorTy)> = Vec::new(); // (orig, copy, ty)
        for (i, (v, k)) in arg_vals.into_iter().enumerate() {
            let want = &entry.params[i].1;
            let v = self.coerce_to(v, &k, want, span)?;
            if entry.mut_param_idxs.contains(&i) {
                if let TyKind::Tensor(t) = want {
                    let copy = self.copy_tensor_value(v, want);
                    writebacks.push((v, copy, t.clone()));
                    vals.push(copy);
                    continue;
                }
            }
            vals.push(v);
        }
        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &vals);
        // Copy each mutated `!` tensor back into the caller's storage.
        for (orig, copy, t) in &writebacks {
            self.emit_memcpy_loop(*orig, *copy, t.nelems(), t.elem_bytes());
        }
        let results = self.builder.inst_results(call);
        if entry.ret == TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil) {
            let z = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I8, 0);
            Ok((z, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Nil)))
        } else {
            Ok((results[0], entry.ret))
        }
    }

    /// Bind a template's shape parameters from concrete arg types, declare
    /// the specialized function in the module (if not already declared),
    /// and enqueue the body for definition later.
    fn instantiate_template(
        &mut self,
        tmpl: &FnDecl,
        arg_vals: &[(Value, TyKind)],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<FnEntry, JitError> {
        if arg_vals.len() != tmpl.params.len() {
            return err(span, format!(
                "`{}` expects {} arg(s), got {}",
                tmpl.name, tmpl.params.len(), arg_vals.len(),
            ));
        }
        // Unify each param's declared type against the actual arg type to
        // bind shape variables.
        let mut bindings: HashMap<String, i64> = HashMap::new();
        for (p, (_v, k)) in tmpl.params.iter().zip(arg_vals.iter()) {
            let p_ty = p.ty.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                msg: format!("template param `{}` needs a type annotation", p.name),
                line: p.span.line, col: p.span.col,
            })?;
            unify_param_type(p_ty, k, &mut bindings, &p.span)?;
        }
        // Every declared shape_param must end up bound.
        for sp in &tmpl.shape_params {
            if !bindings.contains_key(&sp.name) {
                return err(span, format!(
                    "could not infer shape parameter `{}` of `{}` from call args",
                    sp.name, tmpl.name,
                ));
            }
        }
        let mangled = mangle_mono_name(&tmpl.name, &tmpl.shape_params, &bindings);
        if let Some(e) = self.fns.get(&mangled) {
            return Ok(e.clone());
        }
        // Declare the specialized fn in the module now (signature only) so
        // we have a FuncId for the call. Definition is queued for later.
        let sig_decl = declare_template_signature(self.module, tmpl, &bindings, &mangled, self.enums)?;
        self.fns.insert(mangled.clone(), sig_decl.clone());
        self.pending.push(PendingMono {
            template_name: tmpl.name.clone(),
            shape_env: bindings,
            mangled_name: mangled,
            call_span: span.clone(),
        });
        Ok(sig_decl)
    }

    fn lower_binop(
        &mut self,
        op: &BinOp,
        lhs: &Expr,
        rhs: &Expr,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        if matches!(op, BinOp::And | BinOp::Or) {
            return self.lower_short_circuit(op, lhs, rhs, span);
        }
        // `x |> f` and `x >> f` desugar to `f(x)`. The placeholder-fusion form
        // `x |> _ .+ b` instead inlines `x` into the `_` slots and lowers the
        // fused expression directly — no indirect call, and the stages collapse
        // into the surrounding op sequence (the SIMD-fusion the syntax promises).
        if matches!(op, BinOp::Pipe | BinOp::RShift) {
            if let Some(fused) = fuse_underscore(rhs, lhs) {
                return self.lower_expr(&fused);
            }
            // Bare activation as a pipe stage (`x \|> \>`): the parser lowers a
            // standalone `\>`/`\<` to an identifier, but there is no callable of
            // that name to invoke — lower it as the corresponding unary op.
            if let Expr::Ident(name, ispan) = rhs {
                let act = match name.as_str() {
                    "\\>" => Some(UnOp::ReLU),
                    "\\<" => Some(UnOp::GeLU),
                    _ => None,
                };
                if let Some(op) = act {
                    let synth = Expr::UnOp {
                        op,
                        operand: Box::new(lhs.clone()),
                        span: ispan.clone(),
                    };
                    return self.lower_expr(&synth);
                }
            }
            let arg = CallArg::Positional(lhs.clone());
            let synth = Expr::Postfix {
                expr: Box::new(rhs.clone()),
                op: PostfixOp::Call(vec![arg]),
                span: span.clone(),
            };
            return self.lower_expr(&synth);
        }
        // #256: validate constant shift amounts at JIT lowering time so the JIT
        // agrees with the interpreter's range error (#215). The interpreter
        // rejects any shift count outside 0..=63; Cranelift's ishl/sshr would
        // silently mod-64 wrap it. When the RHS is a compile-time literal we can
        // produce a clean JIT compile error before emitting any code.
        if matches!(op, BinOp::BitShl | BinOp::BitShr) {
            if let Some(count) = const_int_axis(rhs) {
                if !(0..64).contains(&count) {
                    let op_str = if *op == BinOp::BitShl { "<<" } else { ">>" };
                    return err(span, format!(
                        "{} shift amount {} out of range (expected 0..=63)", op_str, count
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
        // Native KV-cache attention scores `q @ k_cache'` (issue #176 part 2).
        // This must be intercepted *before* generic operand lowering: the RHS
        // is a postfix-transpose over a KV, and `lower_transpose` can't
        // transpose a KV — we fold the transpose into indexing instead.
        if *op == BinOp::Matmul {
            if let Some(res) = self.try_lower_kv_scores_matmul(lhs, rhs, span)? {
                return Ok(res);
            }
        }
        let (l, lk) = self.lower_expr(lhs)?;
        // Native KV-cache attention output `probs @ v_cache`: a DynTensor LHS
        // (only ever produced by a KV read) matmul'd with a KV/DynTensor RHS.
        if *op == BinOp::Matmul {
            if let TyKind::DynTensor(pdt) = &lk {
                let pdt = pdt.clone();
                let (v_ptr, vdt) = match self.lower_expr(rhs)? {
                    (p, TyKind::KV(kv)) if kv.elem == ScalarKind::F32 => self.kv_materialize(p, &kv),
                    (p, TyKind::DynTensor(dt)) if dt.elem == ScalarKind::F32 => (p, dt),
                    (_, other) => return err(span, format!(
                        "attention `probs @ v_cache`: RHS must be a KV/DynTensor, got `{}`",
                        other.render())),
                };
                return self.lower_kv_output(l, &pdt, v_ptr, &vdt, span);
            }
        }
        let (r, rk) = self.lower_expr(rhs)?;
        // Trit matmul: x @ w where w is a packed trit tensor.
        // Must be intercepted before the generic tensor-tensor match which
        // only accepts TyKind::Tensor on both sides.
        if *op == BinOp::Matmul {
            if let TyKind::TritTensor(wt) = &rk {
                let wt = wt.clone();
                let xt = match &lk {
                    TyKind::Tensor(t) if t.elem == ScalarKind::F32 => t.clone(),
                    _ => return err(span, format!(
                        "trit matmul `@`: LHS must be f32 tensor, got `{}`", lk.render())),
                };
                return self.lower_trit_matmul(l, &xt, r, &wt, span);
            }
        }
        // #324: bf16-direct matmul — `x @ w` where w is a 2-byte bf16 weight.
        // Route to the general batched path with the bf16 kernel (handles all
        // ranks via broadcasting). LHS must be an f32 tensor (the activation).
        if *op == BinOp::Matmul {
            if let TyKind::Bf16Tensor(wt) = &rk {
                let wt = wt.clone();
                let xt = match &lk {
                    TyKind::Tensor(t) if t.elem == ScalarKind::F32 => t.clone(),
                    _ => return err(span, format!(
                        "bf16 matmul `@`: LHS must be f32 tensor, got `{}`", lk.render())),
                };
                return self.lower_matmul_general(l, &xt, r, &wt.shape, true, span);
            }
        }
        match (&lk, &rk) {
            (TyKind::Scalar(ls), TyKind::Scalar(rs)) => {
                let (v, k) = self.scalar_binop(op, l, *ls, r, *rs, span)?;
                Ok((v, TyKind::Scalar(k)))
            }
            (TyKind::Tensor(lt), TyKind::Tensor(rt)) => {
                self.lower_tensor_tensor_binop(op, l, lt, r, rt, span)
            }
            // Scalar-broadcast: `scalar OP tensor` or `tensor OP scalar`
            // for elementwise ops. The scalar is splatted across every
            // tensor element in a single fused loop.
            (TyKind::Scalar(s), TyKind::Tensor(tt)) => {
                self.lower_scalar_tensor_broadcast(op, l, *s, r, tt, span, true)
            }
            (TyKind::Tensor(tt), TyKind::Scalar(s)) => {
                self.lower_scalar_tensor_broadcast(op, r, *s, l, tt, span, false)
            }
            // Scalar-broadcast over a dynamic-shape tensor (e.g. the attention
            // scale `scores .* (1/sqrt(D))`, where `scores` is `[B,H,1,len]`).
            (TyKind::DynTensor(dt), TyKind::Scalar(s)) => {
                let dt = dt.clone();
                self.lower_scalar_dyn_broadcast(op, r, *s, l, &dt, span, false)
            }
            (TyKind::Scalar(s), TyKind::DynTensor(dt)) => {
                let dt = dt.clone();
                self.lower_scalar_dyn_broadcast(op, l, *s, r, &dt, span, true)
            }
            (TyKind::Model(_, _), _) | (_, TyKind::Model(_, _)) => {
                unsupported(span, "binary operators are not supported on model instances")
            }
            // String operators: concatenation (`+`) and equality / inequality.
            (TyKind::Str, TyKind::Str) => {
                match op {
                    BinOp::Add => {
                        // `s1 + s2` — concatenate two forge strings via __dmc_str_concat.
                        let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_str_concat")
                            .expect("__dmc_str_concat not registered").clone();
                        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                        let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[l, r]);
                        Ok((self.builder.inst_results(call)[0], TyKind::Str))
                    }
                    BinOp::Eq | BinOp::NotEq => {
                        let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_str_eq")
                            .expect("__dmc_str_eq not registered").clone();
                        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                        let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[l, r]);
                        let eq_i64 = self.builder.inst_results(call)[0];
                        // eq_i64 is 1 for equal, 0 for not-equal.
                        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
                        let cc = if *op == BinOp::Eq { IntCC::NotEqual } else { IntCC::Equal };
                        let result = self.builder.ins().icmp(cc, eq_i64, zero);
                        Ok((result, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Bool)))
                    }
                    _ => err(span, format!(
                        "operator `{:?}` is not defined on str; only `+`, `==`, `!=` are supported",
                        op,
                    )),
                }
            }
            // `str + x` / `x + str` — stringify the non-string operand and
            // concatenate, matching the interpreter (#368 follow-up). `--check`
            // and the interpreter both accept this; previously only the JIT
            // rejected it, so `"n=" + 5` ran under `dmc run`/`test` but broke
            // under `--jit`. The non-string side goes through the same `as str`
            // conversion as an explicit cast. Only `+` is meaningful for strings.
            (TyKind::Str, _) | (_, TyKind::Str) if *op == BinOp::Add => {
                let ls = self.coerce_to(l, &lk, &TyKind::Str, span)?;
                let rs = self.coerce_to(r, &rk, &TyKind::Str, span)?;
                let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_str_concat")
                    .expect("__dmc_str_concat not registered").clone();
                let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[ls, rs]);
                Ok((self.builder.inst_results(call)[0], TyKind::Str))
            }
            _ => err(span, format!(
                "operator `{:?}` is not defined for types `{}` and `{}`",
                op, lk.render(), rk.render(),
            )),
        }
    }

    /// Lower a `scalar OP tensor` (or `tensor OP scalar`) elementwise op.
    /// `scalar_is_lhs` controls operand order — matters for `-` and `/`.
    fn lower_scalar_tensor_broadcast(
        &mut self,
        op: &BinOp,
        s_val: Value, s_kind: ScalarKind,
        t_val: Value, t_ty: &TensorTy,
        span: &Span,
        scalar_is_lhs: bool,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        // Dotted elementwise ops broadcast a scalar across the tensor; the
        // bare `+ - * /` forms on a tensor are illegal (SPEC §4.4). `.^` and
        // the comparison masks join the arithmetic ops here.
        if !matches!(op,
            BinOp::DotAdd | BinOp::DotSub | BinOp::DotMul | BinOp::DotDiv
            | BinOp::DotPow | BinOp::DotPow2
            | BinOp::DotLt | BinOp::DotGt | BinOp::DotLe | BinOp::DotGe) {
            return err(span, format!(
                "operator `{:?}` is not defined on scalar/tensor mix; \
                 use a dotted broadcast form (`.+ .- .* ./ .^ .< .> .<= .>=`)",
                op,
            ));
        }
        if t_ty.elem != ScalarKind::F32 {
            return err(span, "scalar-tensor broadcast is f32-only in slice 4");
        }
        // Coerce the scalar to f32 so the kernel is uniform.
        let s_val = self.coerce_scalar(s_val, s_kind, ScalarKind::F32, span)?;

        let out_ty = t_ty.clone();
        let out_ptr = self.forge_alloc(out_ty.nbytes());
        let n = out_ty.nelems();

        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let cap = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, n);
        let eb = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);

        let hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let body = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);

        self.jump(hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(hdr);
        let i = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
        let cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, i, cap);
        self.brif(cont, body, exit);

        self.enter(body);
        let off = self.builder.ins().imul(i, eb);
        let tv = self.tensor_load_elem(t_val, off, t_ty.elem);
        let (lhs, rhs) = if scalar_is_lhs { (s_val, tv) } else { (tv, s_val) };
        let ov = self.emit_f32_elem(op, lhs, rhs);
        self.tensor_store_elem(out_ptr, off, ov);
        let inext = self.builder.ins().iadd(i, one);
        self.jump(hdr, &[inext]);
        self.builder.seal_block(body);
        self.builder.seal_block(hdr);

        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);

        Ok((out_ptr, TyKind::Tensor(out_ty)))
    }

    /// `scalar OP dyn_tensor` / `dyn_tensor OP scalar` — scalar broadcast over a
    /// dynamic-shape tensor. Allocates a fresh DynTensor of the same shape and
    /// applies the elementwise op over a runtime element count.
    fn lower_scalar_dyn_broadcast(
        &mut self,
        op: &BinOp,
        s_val: Value, s_kind: ScalarKind,
        t_val: Value, dt: &DynTensorTy,
        span: &Span,
        scalar_is_lhs: bool,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        if !matches!(op,
            BinOp::DotAdd | BinOp::DotSub | BinOp::DotMul | BinOp::DotDiv
            | BinOp::DotPow | BinOp::DotPow2
            | BinOp::DotLt | BinOp::DotGt | BinOp::DotLe | BinOp::DotGe) {
            return err(span, format!(
                "operator `{:?}` is not defined on scalar/dynamic-tensor mix; \
                 use a dotted broadcast form (`.+ .- .* ./ .^ .< .> .<= .>=`)",
                op,
            ));
        }
        if dt.elem != ScalarKind::F32 {
            return err(span, "scalar/dynamic-tensor broadcast is f32-only");
        }
        let s_val = self.coerce_scalar(s_val, s_kind, ScalarKind::F32, span)?;

        // Fresh output of the same dynamic shape (input buffer is not mutated).
        let mut extents = Vec::new();
        for axis in 0..dt.rank() {
            if dt.dims[axis].is_none() {
                extents.push(self.dyn_extent(t_val, dt, axis));
            }
        }
        let out = self.dyn_alloc(dt, &extents);
        let out_data = self.dyn_data_ptr(out, dt);
        let in_data = self.dyn_data_ptr(t_val, dt);
        let n = self.dyn_total_elems(t_val, dt);

        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let eb = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);

        let hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let body = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);

        self.jump(hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(hdr);
        let i = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
        let cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, i, n);
        self.brif(cont, body, exit);

        self.enter(body);
        let off = self.builder.ins().imul(i, eb);
        let tv = self.tensor_load_elem(in_data, off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let (lhs, rhs) = if scalar_is_lhs { (s_val, tv) } else { (tv, s_val) };
        let ov = self.emit_f32_elem(op, lhs, rhs);
        self.tensor_store_elem(out_data, off, ov);
        let inext = self.builder.ins().iadd(i, one);
        self.jump(hdr, &[inext]);
        self.builder.seal_block(body);
        self.builder.seal_block(hdr);

        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);

        Ok((out, TyKind::DynTensor(dt.clone())))
    }

    fn lower_short_circuit(
        &mut self,
        op: &BinOp,
        lhs: &Expr,
        rhs: &Expr,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        let (l, lk) = self.lower_expr(lhs)?;
        if !lk.as_scalar().map(|s| s.is_bool()).unwrap_or(false) {
            return err(span, "logical operators require `bool` operands");
        }
        let cont = self.builder.create_block();
        let rhs_block = self.builder.create_block();
        let join = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(join, cl::I8);
        match op {
            BinOp::And => {
                // l && r: if l then evaluate r, else result = false.
                self.brif(l, rhs_block, cont);
                self.enter(cont);
                let f = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I8, 0);
                self.jump(join, &[f]);
                self.builder.seal_block(cont);
            }
            BinOp::Or => {
                // l || r: if l then result = true, else evaluate r.
                self.brif(l, cont, rhs_block);
                self.enter(cont);
                let t = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I8, 1);
                self.jump(join, &[t]);
                self.builder.seal_block(cont);
            }
            _ => unreachable!(),
        }
        self.enter(rhs_block);
        let (r, rk) = self.lower_expr(rhs)?;
        if !rk.as_scalar().map(|s| s.is_bool()).unwrap_or(false) {
            return err(span, "logical operators require `bool` operands");
        }
        self.jump(join, &[r]);
        self.builder.seal_block(rhs_block);
        self.enter(join);
        self.builder.seal_block(join);
        let v = self.builder.block_params(join)[0];
        Ok((v, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Bool)))
    }

    fn scalar_binop(
        &mut self,
        op: &BinOp,
        l: Value, lk: ScalarKind,
        r: Value, rk: ScalarKind,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, ScalarKind), JitError> {
        // `map_get(...) == nil` / `!= nil` (#300.4): a maybe-nil value compared to
        // nil tests its present bit, not the payload. Must run before the kind
        // check below (OptI64 vs Nil would otherwise read as "operands disagree").
        if matches!(op, BinOp::Eq | BinOp::NotEq) {
            let opt = if lk == ScalarKind::OptI64 && rk == ScalarKind::Nil { Some(l) }
                      else if rk == ScalarKind::OptI64 && lk == ScalarKind::Nil { Some(r) }
                      else { None };
            if let Some(o) = opt {
                let present = self.opt_present(o);
                let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
                // present == 0 ⇔ nil ⇒ `== nil` is true.
                let cc = if matches!(op, BinOp::Eq) { IntCC::Equal } else { IntCC::NotEqual };
                let res = self.builder.ins().icmp(cc, present, zero);
                return Ok((res, ScalarKind::Bool));
            }
        }
        // Any other use of a maybe-nil operand (arithmetic, ordering) decodes it
        // to its i64 payload, trapping on nil — matching the interpreter, which
        // errors when a missing `map_get` result is used as a value (#300.4).
        let (l, lk) = if lk == ScalarKind::OptI64 {
            (self.opt_unwrap_or_trap(l), ScalarKind::I64)
        } else { (l, lk) };
        let (r, rk) = if rk == ScalarKind::OptI64 {
            (self.opt_unwrap_or_trap(r), ScalarKind::I64)
        } else { (r, rk) };
        // #209: all scalar float arithmetic/comparison runs in f64 (the
        // interpreter is canonical). f32 scalars still arise — from an f32 tensor
        // element, an f32-returning math builtin, or an f32-annotated binding — so
        // promote any f32 operand to f64 here. Both the comparison and arithmetic
        // paths below then see matching f64 floats, and the result is f64. (f32
        // only lives inside tensor storage; stores fdemote at the boundary.)
        let (l, lk) = if lk == ScalarKind::F32 {
            (self.builder.ins().fpromote(cl::F64, l), ScalarKind::F64)
        } else { (l, lk) };
        let (r, rk) = if rk == ScalarKind::F32 {
            (self.builder.ins().fpromote(cl::F64, r), ScalarKind::F64)
        } else { (r, rk) };
        // Comparisons accept matching int or matching float and return bool.
        let is_cmp = matches!(
            op,
            BinOp::Eq | BinOp::NotEq | BinOp::Lt | BinOp::Gt | BinOp::LtEq | BinOp::GtEq,
        );
        if is_cmp {
            if lk != rk {
                return err(span, format!(
                    "comparison operands disagree: `{}` vs `{}` (no implicit cast)",
                    lk.name(), rk.name(),
                ));
            }
            let v = match (op, lk) {
                (cmp, k) if k.is_int() => {
                    let cc = int_cc(cmp);
                    self.builder.ins().icmp(cc, l, r)
                }
                (cmp, k) if k.is_float() => {
                    let cc = float_cc(cmp);
                    self.builder.ins().fcmp(cc, l, r)
                }
                (cmp, ScalarKind::Bool) | (cmp, ScalarKind::Nil) => {
                    if !matches!(cmp, BinOp::Eq | BinOp::NotEq) {
                        return err(span, "ordering comparison on bool/nil");
                    }
                    let cc = int_cc(cmp);
                    self.builder.ins().icmp(cc, l, r)
                }
                _ => return err(span, "unsupported comparison"),
            };
            return Ok((v, ScalarKind::Bool));
        }

        // Arithmetic and bitwise require matching numeric type.
        if lk != rk {
            return err(span, format!(
                "operands disagree: `{}` vs `{}` (no implicit cast)", lk.name(), rk.name(),
            ));
        }
        if lk.is_int() {
            let v = match op {
                BinOp::Add => self.builder.ins().iadd(l, r),
                BinOp::Sub => self.builder.ins().isub(l, r),
                BinOp::Mul => self.builder.ins().imul(l, r),
                // #208: integer `/` and `%` by zero are TOTAL in demoniC and
                // yield 0 (the interpreter is canonical). Cranelift's sdiv/srem
                // trap on a zero divisor (SIGILL), so guard it: divide by 1 when
                // the divisor is 0 to dodge the trap, then select 0 as the result.
                BinOp::Div | BinOp::Mod => {
                    // #297: INT_MIN / -1 (and % -1) overflow i64 and raise a
                    // hardware #DE (SIGFPE) on x86 sdiv/srem. The interpreter
                    // returns a clean overflow error, so trap with the same
                    // message before the division can fault.
                    self.div_overflow_check(l, r, matches!(op, BinOp::Div));
                    let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
                    let one = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
                    let is_zero = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::Equal, r, zero);
                    let safe_r = self.builder.ins().select(is_zero, one, r);
                    let q = if matches!(op, BinOp::Div) {
                        self.builder.ins().sdiv(l, safe_r)
                    } else {
                        self.builder.ins().srem(l, safe_r)
                    };
                    self.builder.ins().select(is_zero, zero, q)
                }
                BinOp::BitAnd => self.builder.ins().band(l, r),
                BinOp::BitOr  => self.builder.ins().bor(l, r),
                BinOp::BitXor => self.builder.ins().bxor(l, r),
                // #265: a *runtime* shift count outside 0..=63 would be silently
                // masked mod 64 by ishl/sshr; guard it so the JIT matches the
                // interpreter's range error. Out-of-range *constants* are already
                // rejected at lowering (#256, lower_binop); for an in-range
                // constant the guard is a never-taken branch.
                BinOp::BitShl => {
                    self.shift_range_check(r, true);
                    self.builder.ins().ishl(l, r)
                }
                BinOp::BitShr => {
                    self.shift_range_check(r, false);
                    self.builder.ins().sshr(l, r)
                }
                _ => return err(span, format!("operator `{:?}` not supported on ints in slice 1", op)),
            };
            Ok((v, lk))
        } else if lk.is_float() {
            let v = match op {
                BinOp::Add => self.builder.ins().fadd(l, r),
                BinOp::Sub => self.builder.ins().fsub(l, r),
                BinOp::Mul => self.builder.ins().fmul(l, r),
                BinOp::Div => self.builder.ins().fdiv(l, r),
                // #275: a dotted/elementwise op on two scalars is the scalar op
                // (the checker types `5.0 ./ 2.0` as a scalar f32). Match it.
                BinOp::DotAdd => self.builder.ins().fadd(l, r),
                BinOp::DotSub => self.builder.ins().fsub(l, r),
                BinOp::DotMul => self.builder.ins().fmul(l, r),
                BinOp::DotDiv => self.builder.ins().fdiv(l, r),
                // #261: `**` (and `pow`) on scalar floats -> powf. Scalar floats
                // run in f64 (#209), so route through the f64 helper to match the
                // interpreter's `a.powf(b)`. #275: dotted `.^` on scalars too.
                BinOp::Pow | BinOp::StarStar | BinOp::DotPow | BinOp::DotPow2 => {
                    let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_powf_f64")
                        .expect("__dmc_powf_f64 not registered").clone();
                    let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                    let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[l, r]);
                    self.builder.inst_results(call)[0]
                }
                // #289: scalar float `%` — the interpreter computes Rust
                // `a % b` (truncated fmod), so route through the f64 helper
                // instead of rejecting a program `dmc run` accepts.
                BinOp::Mod => {
                    let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_fmod_f64")
                        .expect("__dmc_fmod_f64 not registered").clone();
                    let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                    let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[l, r]);
                    self.builder.inst_results(call)[0]
                }
                _ => return err(span, format!("operator `{:?}` not supported on floats", op)),
            };
            Ok((v, lk))
        } else {
            err(span, format!(
                "operator `{:?}` not supported on `{}`", op, lk.name(),
            ))
        }
    }

    // ─── Tensor lowering ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    /// Emit a call to the Forge allocator and return the resulting i64 ptr.
    fn forge_alloc(&mut self, nbytes: i64) -> Value {
        let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_forge_alloc").expect("forge_alloc not registered").clone();
        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        let n = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, nbytes);
        let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[n]);
        self.builder.inst_results(call)[0]
    }

    /// #249: deep-copy a tensor value into a fresh forge allocation so the new
    /// binding/field/argument does not alias the source's backing store. This
    /// matches the interpreter's value-copy (clone) semantics — `let y = x`,
    /// `M { w: t }`, and by-value argument passing all snapshot the tensor, so
    /// a later write through the source doesn't leak into the copy (and vice
    /// versa). Scalars and other non-tensor kinds are SSA values, never alias,
    /// and pass through unchanged.
    fn copy_tensor_value(&mut self, val: Value, ty: &TyKind) -> Value {
        match ty {
            TyKind::Tensor(t) => {
                let dst = self.forge_alloc(t.nbytes());
                self.emit_memcpy_loop(dst, val, t.nelems(), t.elem_bytes());
                dst
            }
            TyKind::DynTensor(dt) => self.dyn_copy(val, dt),
            // Trit-packed tensors and non-tensors: leave as-is (trit aliasing is
            // a narrower, separately-tracked gap; scalars never alias).
            _ => val,
        }
    }

    /// Compute a flat element offset (in bytes) for a tensor access using
    /// row-major strides. `idxs` must match the tensor's rank.
    /// flat = sum(idxs[i] * stride[i]); offset = flat * elem_bytes.
    fn tensor_byte_offset(
        &mut self,
        t: &TensorTy,
        idxs: &[Value],
    ) -> Value {
        let r = t.shape.len();
        // strides[i] = product of shape[i+1..]
        let mut strides: Vec<i64> = vec![1; r];
        for i in (0..r.saturating_sub(1)).rev() {
            strides[i] = strides[i + 1] * t.shape[i + 1];
        }
        let mut flat = idxs[0];
        if strides[0] != 1 {
            let s0 = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, strides[0]);
            flat = self.builder.ins().imul(flat, s0);
        }
        for i in 1..r {
            let term = if strides[i] == 1 {
                idxs[i]
            } else {
                let s = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, strides[i]);
                self.builder.ins().imul(idxs[i], s)
            };
            flat = self.builder.ins().iadd(flat, term);
        }
        let elem_bytes = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, t.elem_bytes());
        self.builder.ins().imul(flat, elem_bytes)
    }

    fn tensor_load_elem(&mut self, ptr: Value, byte_off: Value, elem: ScalarKind) -> Value {
        let addr = self.builder.ins().iadd(ptr, byte_off);
        let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
        self.builder.ins().load(elem.cl(), flags, addr, 0)
    }

    fn tensor_store_elem(&mut self, ptr: Value, byte_off: Value, val: Value) {
        let addr = self.builder.ins().iadd(ptr, byte_off);
        let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
        self.builder.ins().store(flags, val, addr, 0);
    }

    /// #206/#259: bounds-check a user scalar index against its axis extent.
    /// If out of range, calls `__dmc_oob_trap(idx, dim)` which prints a clean
    /// "index N out of bounds for axis 0 of size M" message and exits(1),
    /// matching the interpreter's error.  The old bare `trapnz` (code 10)
    /// produced a silent SIGILL with no diagnostic output.
    /// Resolve a (possibly negative, Python-style) scalar index against `dim`
    /// and bounds-check it. Returns the resolved non-negative index, for the
    /// caller to fold into the load/store offset. On out-of-range, calls
    /// `__dmc_oob_trap` (clean message + exit). #270: previously this trapped on
    /// any negative index; the interpreter resolves `-1` to the last element, so
    /// the JIT now matches by adding `dim` to a negative index first.
    fn bounds_check_index(&mut self, idx: Value, dim: i64) -> Value {
        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let dimc = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, dim);
        // #270: resolve a negative index as `dim + idx` (Python-style).
        let is_neg   = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, idx, zero);
        let plus_dim = self.builder.ins().iadd(idx, dimc);
        let resolved = self.builder.ins().select(is_neg, plus_dim, idx);
        // Bounds-check the *resolved* index against [0, dim).
        let lt0  = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, resolved, zero);
        let ged  = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedGreaterThanOrEqual, resolved, dimc);
        let oob  = self.builder.ins().bor(lt0, ged);

        // Branch to an error block on OOB; continue in ok_block otherwise.
        let oob_block = self.builder.create_block();
        let ok_block  = self.builder.create_block();
        // Use self.brif so block_filled is tracked correctly.
        self.brif(oob, oob_block, ok_block);
        // Both blocks have exactly one predecessor (this brif); seal them now.
        self.builder.seal_block(oob_block);
        self.builder.seal_block(ok_block);

        // ── OOB block: call the runtime helper then trap (helper never returns) ──
        self.enter(oob_block);
        {
            let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_oob_trap")
                .expect("__dmc_oob_trap not registered")
                .clone();
            let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
            self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[idx, dimc]);
        }
        // `__dmc_oob_trap` calls process::exit — this trap is unreachable
        // but required to terminate the block in Cranelift's IR.
        self.trap_user(10);

        // ── OK block: normal control flow continues ──
        self.enter(ok_block);
        resolved
    }

    /// Clamp/resolve a *runtime* slice bound to match the interpreter's
    /// `normalize` (interp.rs:503): a negative bound resolves from the end
    /// (`max(0, dim + v)`), a positive bound clamps to `min(dim, v)`. Unlike
    /// `bounds_check_index` this never traps — slices clamp rather than error.
    /// Used by the slice-store path so `t[0..100] = rhs` clamps under
    /// `dmc jit` exactly as it does under `dmc run` (#291.4 store sub-note).
    fn clamp_slice_bound(&mut self, val: Value, dim: i64) -> Value {
        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let dimc = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, dim);
        let is_neg = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, val, zero);
        let plus = self.builder.ins().iadd(val, dimc);
        let plus_neg = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, plus, zero);
        let neg_branch = self.builder.ins().select(plus_neg, zero, plus); // max(0, dim+val)
        let over = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedGreaterThan, val, dimc);
        let pos_branch = self.builder.ins().select(over, dimc, val);      // min(dim, val)
        self.builder.ins().select(is_neg, neg_branch, pos_branch)
    }

    /// #265: range-check a *runtime* shift count against `0..=63`. If out of
    /// range, calls `__dmc_shift_trap(count, op_is_shl)` (prints the same message
    /// the interpreter raises, then exits(1)); otherwise control continues.
    /// Modelled on `bounds_check_index`.
    fn shift_range_check(&mut self, count: Value, op_is_shl: bool) {
        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let max  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 63);
        let lt0  = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, count, zero);
        let gt63 = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedGreaterThan, count, max);
        let oob  = self.builder.ins().bor(lt0, gt63);

        let oob_block = self.builder.create_block();
        let ok_block  = self.builder.create_block();
        self.brif(oob, oob_block, ok_block);
        self.builder.seal_block(oob_block);
        self.builder.seal_block(ok_block);

        // ── OOB block: call the runtime helper then trap (helper never returns) ──
        self.enter(oob_block);
        {
            let flag = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, if op_is_shl { 1 } else { 0 });
            let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_shift_trap")
                .expect("__dmc_shift_trap not registered")
                .clone();
            let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
            self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[count, flag]);
        }
        self.trap_user(10);

        // ── OK block: normal control flow continues ──
        self.enter(ok_block);
    }

    /// #297: trap on the one signed integer division that overflows i64 —
    /// `INT_MIN / -1` (and `% -1`) — which raises a hardware #DE (SIGFPE) on
    /// x86 sdiv/srem. Calls `__dmc_div_overflow_trap(l, r)` (clean message +
    /// exit 1) so the JIT matches the interpreter's overflow error instead of
    /// crashing. Modelled on `shift_range_check`.
    fn div_overflow_check(&mut self, l: Value, r: Value, op_is_div: bool) {
        let imin = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, i64::MIN);
        let neg1 = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, -1);
        let l_is_min  = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::Equal, l, imin);
        let r_is_neg1 = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::Equal, r, neg1);
        let overflow  = self.builder.ins().band(l_is_min, r_is_neg1);

        let trap_block = self.builder.create_block();
        let ok_block   = self.builder.create_block();
        self.brif(overflow, trap_block, ok_block);
        self.builder.seal_block(trap_block);
        self.builder.seal_block(ok_block);

        self.enter(trap_block);
        {
            let flag = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, if op_is_div { 1 } else { 0 });
            let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_div_overflow_trap")
                .expect("__dmc_div_overflow_trap not registered")
                .clone();
            let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
            self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[l, r, flag]);
        }
        self.trap_user(11);

        self.enter(ok_block);
    }

    /// Walk a nested-literal tree, returning the inferred shape and the
    /// flat list of leaf expressions in row-major order. Errors on jagged
    /// nesting, empty inner literals, or mixed depth.
    fn flatten_tensor_literal<'b>(
        elems: &'b [Expr],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Vec<i64>, Vec<&'b Expr>), JitError> {
        if elems.is_empty() {
            return err(span, "empty tensor literals are not allowed (no inferable shape)");
        }
        // Determine inner shape from first element; require uniformity.
        let inner_is_lit = matches!(&elems[0], Expr::TensorLit(_, _));
        if !inner_is_lit {
            // Leaf row: all elements are scalars.
            for (i, e) in elems.iter().enumerate() {
                if matches!(e, Expr::TensorLit(_, _)) {
                    return err(span, format!(
                        "row 0 is flat but element {} is a nested literal", i,
                    ));
                }
            }
            return Ok((vec![elems.len() as i64], elems.iter().collect()));
        }
        // Recurse into first row to get inner shape.
        let first_inner = match &elems[0] {
            Expr::TensorLit(es, _) => es,
            _ => unreachable!(),
        };
        let (inner_shape, _) = Self::flatten_tensor_literal(first_inner, span)?;
        // Walk all rows, accumulating leaves.
        let mut all_leaves: Vec<&Expr> = Vec::new();
        for (i, row) in elems.iter().enumerate() {
            let row_es = match row {
                Expr::TensorLit(es, _) => es,
                _ => return err(span, format!(
                    "row 0 is nested but row {} is flat", i,
                )),
            };
            let (row_shape, row_leaves) = Self::flatten_tensor_literal(row_es, span)?;
            if row_shape != inner_shape {
                return err(span, format!(
                    "row 0 has inner shape {:?} but row {} has {:?}",
                    inner_shape, i, row_shape,
                ));
            }
            all_leaves.extend(row_leaves);
        }
        let mut shape = vec![elems.len() as i64];
        shape.extend(inner_shape);
        Ok((shape, all_leaves))
    }

    fn lower_tensor_literal(
        &mut self,
        elems: &[Expr],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        // Detect `[kv0, kv1, ..., kvN]` — a KV-cache array literal.
        // We check the type of the first element WITHOUT emitting IR (via local_tys)
        // before committing to this path, since we can't roll back Cranelift IR.
        if let Some(kv) = self.peek_kv_lit_elem_type(elems) {
            let kv = kv.clone();
            let n = elems.len() as i64;
            let arr_ptr = self.forge_alloc(n * 8);
            let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
            for (i, e) in elems.iter().enumerate() {
                let (vi, ki) = self.lower_expr(e)?;
                match &ki {
                    TyKind::KV(kvi) if kvi.dims == kv.dims
                                    && kvi.stream_axis == kv.stream_axis => {}
                    _ => return err(span, format!(
                        "KV-array literal element {} has type `{}`, expected `{}`",
                        i, ki.render(), TyKind::KV(kv.clone()).render(),
                    )),
                }
                let off = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, i as i64 * 8);
                let elem_addr = self.builder.ins().iadd(arr_ptr, off);
                self.builder.ins().store(flags, vi, elem_addr, 0);
            }
            return Ok((arr_ptr, TyKind::KvArray(kv, n)));
        }
        // Detect `[m0, m1, ..., mN]` -- a model-instance array literal.
        // Check element type without emitting IR (local_tys only) so we never
        // produce Cranelift IR that cannot be rolled back.
