        if let Some(model_name) = self.peek_model_lit_elem_type(elems) {
            let model_name = model_name.to_string();
            let n = elems.len() as i64;
            let arr_ptr = self.forge_alloc(n * 8);
            let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
            let mut elem_args: Vec<i64> = Vec::new();  // #267: element model's type args
            for (i, e) in elems.iter().enumerate() {
                let (vi, ki) = self.lower_expr(e)?;
                match &ki {
                    TyKind::Model(mn, a) if *mn == model_name => {
                        if i == 0 { elem_args = a.clone(); }
                    }
                    _ => return err(span, format!(
                        "model-array literal element {} has type `{}`, expected `{}`",
                        i, ki.render(), model_name,
                    )),
                }
                let off = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, i as i64 * 8);
                let elem_addr = self.builder.ins().iadd(arr_ptr, off);
                self.builder.ins().store(flags, vi, elem_addr, 0);
            }
            return Ok((arr_ptr, TyKind::ModelArray(model_name, n, elem_args)));
        }
        let (shape, leaves) = Self::flatten_tensor_literal(elems, span)?;
        if shape.len() > 4 {
            return err(span, format!(
                "tensor literal has rank {}; JIT supports 1..=4", shape.len(),
            ));
        }
        // Infer the element kind from the leaves: an all-integer-literal tensor
        // (e.g. token ids `[[785, 6722, 315]]`) is an i64 tensor; anything with a
        // float leaf is f32. This matches the interpreter, which carries integer
        // tensor literals as i64 — without it, `Tensor[i64, …]` params reject a
        // literal arg under JIT. (#273 follow-up.)
        let all_int = !leaves.is_empty() && leaves.iter().all(|e| is_int_literal_leaf(e));
        let elem = if all_int { ScalarKind::I64 } else { ScalarKind::F32 };
        let t = TensorTy { elem, shape };
        let ptr = self.forge_alloc(t.nbytes());
        let target = TyKind::Scalar(elem);
        for (i, e) in leaves.iter().enumerate() {
            let (v, k) = self.lower_expr(e)?;
            let v = self.coerce_to(v, &k, &target, span)?;
            let off = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, i as i64 * t.elem_bytes());
            self.tensor_store_elem(ptr, off, v);
        }
        Ok((ptr, TyKind::Tensor(t)))
    }

    /// `A[i]` for scalar reads, `A[a:b]` / `A[i, :]` / `A[a:b, :, :]` for
    /// contiguous slicing. Slicing produces a view into the same Forge
    /// allocation — the JIT tracks the slice's static shape and starting
    /// offset; the underlying memory is shared.
    ///
    /// Contiguity rule (slice 4): the kept axes must form a suffix of the
    /// tensor's rank. The leading kept axis may be a range; all subsequent
    /// Return the `KvTy` of a KV-array literal's elements if the first element
    /// is a bare identifier whose type in `local_tys` is `TyKind::KV`. This
    /// lets `lower_tensor_literal` choose the KvArray path before emitting any
    /// Cranelift IR (which cannot be rolled back).
    fn peek_kv_lit_elem_type(&self, elems: &[Expr]) -> Option<&KvTy> {
        let first = elems.first()?;
        let name = match first {
            Expr::Ident(n, _) => n,
            _ => return None,
        };
        match self.local_tys.get(name.as_str()) {
            Some(TyKind::KV(kv)) => Some(kv),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Return the model name of a model-array literal's first element if it is a
    /// bare identifier typed `TyKind::Model` in `local_tys`. This lets
    /// `lower_tensor_literal` choose the ModelArray path before emitting any IR.
    fn peek_model_lit_elem_type(&self, elems: &[Expr]) -> Option<&str> {
        let first = elems.first()?;
        let name = match first {
            Expr::Ident(n, _) => n,
            _ => return None,
        };
        match self.local_tys.get(name.as_str()) {
            Some(TyKind::Model(model_name, _)) => Some(model_name.as_str()),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// Dispatch `expr[idxs]` to either string indexing or tensor indexing
    /// depending on the runtime type of `expr`.
    fn lower_index(
        &mut self,
        base: &Expr,
        idxs: &[IndexElem],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        let (base_v, base_ty) = self.lower_expr(base)?;
        // `k_caches[i]` — read the i-th KV header pointer from a KV-array parameter.
        // Returns `(kv_ptr, TyKind::KV(kv))` so downstream compute (matmul, etc.) works.
        if let TyKind::KvArray(kv, _) = &base_ty {
            let kv = kv.clone();
            if idxs.len() != 1 {
                return err(span, "KV array indexing requires exactly one index");
            }
            let idx_expr = match &idxs[0] {
                IndexElem::Expr(e) => e,
                _ => return unsupported(span, "non-expression KV array index"),
            };
            let (idx_v, idx_ty) = self.lower_expr(idx_expr)?;
            let idx_i64 = self.coerce_to(idx_v, &idx_ty, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;
            let eight = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 8);
            let byte_off = self.builder.ins().imul(idx_i64, eight);
            let elem_addr = self.builder.ins().iadd(base_v, byte_off);
            let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
            let kv_ptr = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, elem_addr, 0);
            return Ok((kv_ptr, TyKind::KV(kv)));
        }
        // `model_arr[i]` -- read the i-th model instance pointer from a ModelArray.
        // Returns `(model_ptr, TyKind::Model(name, args))` so field accesses work
        // normally; #267 propagates the array's element type args to the element.
        if let TyKind::ModelArray(model_name, _, type_args) = &base_ty {
            let model_name = model_name.clone();
            let type_args = type_args.clone();
            if idxs.len() != 1 {
                return err(span, "model array indexing requires exactly one index");
            }
            let idx_expr = match &idxs[0] {
                IndexElem::Expr(e) => e,
                _ => return unsupported(span, "non-expression model array index"),
            };
            let (idx_v, idx_ty) = self.lower_expr(idx_expr)?;
            let idx_i64 = self.coerce_to(idx_v, &idx_ty, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;
            let eight = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 8);
            let byte_off = self.builder.ins().imul(idx_i64, eight);
            let elem_addr = self.builder.ins().iadd(base_v, byte_off);
            let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
            let model_ptr = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, elem_addr, 0);
            return Ok((model_ptr, TyKind::Model(model_name, type_args)));
        }
        // Reading a KV cache: expose the cap-strided data buffer as a static
        // tensor of the full shape (exact while the stream is filled to
        // capacity). The header pointer skips its 16-byte [len, cap] prefix.
        if let TyKind::KV(kv) = &base_ty {
            let t = kv.as_full_tensor().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                msg: "indexing a KV parameter of compile-time-unknown capacity \
                      is not yet supported in the JIT (read needs the runtime length)".into(),
                line: span.line, col: span.col,
            })?;
            let sixteen = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 16);
            let data = self.builder.ins().iadd(base_v, sixteen);
            return self.lower_tensor_load_with(data, &t, idxs, span);
        }
        if base_ty.is_str() {
            if idxs.len() != 1 {
                return err(span, "string indexing requires exactly one index");
            }
            let idx_expr = match &idxs[0] {
                IndexElem::Expr(e) => e,
                _ => return unsupported(span, "non-expr string index"),
            };
            let (idx_v, idx_ty) = self.lower_expr(idx_expr)?;
            if idx_ty.as_scalar().map(|s| !s.is_int()).unwrap_or(true) {
                return err(span, "string index must be an integer");
            }
            let idx_i64 = self.coerce_to(idx_v, &idx_ty, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;
            let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_str_get_char")
                .expect("__dmc_str_get_char not registered").clone();
            let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
            let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[base_v, idx_i64]);
            let result = self.builder.inst_results(call)[0];
            return Ok((result, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)));
        }
        // Tensor load — dispatch to the inner helper with already-lowered ptr+type.
        let t = base_ty.as_tensor().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("indexing requires a tensor or str, got `{}`", base_ty.render()),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?.clone();
        self.lower_tensor_load_with(base_v, &t, idxs, span)
    }

    fn lower_tensor_load_with(
        &mut self,
        ptr: Value,
        t: &TensorTy,
        idxs: &[IndexElem],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        let t = t.clone();
        if idxs.len() > t.rank() {
            return err(span, format!(
                "tensor has rank {} but indexed with {} dim(s)",
                t.rank(), idxs.len(),
            ));
        }
        // Pad with implicit FullSlice on trailing axes so `A[i]` on a 2D
        // tensor means `A[i, :]`.
        let mut classified: Vec<IndexCat> = Vec::with_capacity(t.rank());
        for ie in idxs {
            classified.push(self.classify_index(ie, span)?);
        }
        for _ in idxs.len()..t.rank() {
            classified.push(IndexCat::Full);
        }

        // #276: route any *non-contiguous* slice to the element-wise copy path.
        // The view path below only represents a contiguous slab — scalars must
        // precede all kept axes, and at most one range as the first kept axis.
        // Anything else (a scalar after a kept axis, a range not first-kept, two
        // ranges) needs a strided copy, which is correct for every combination.
        let mut first_kept = false;
        let mut contiguous = true;
        for c in &classified {
            match c {
                IndexCat::Scalar(_) => { if first_kept { contiguous = false; } }
                IndexCat::Full => { first_kept = true; }
                IndexCat::Range { .. } => {
                    if first_kept { contiguous = false; }
                    first_kept = true;
                }
            }
        }
        if !contiguous {
            return self.lower_tensor_slice_read_copy(ptr, &t, &classified, span);
        }

        // Walk classified indices, computing:
        //   - base_offset (in elements), accumulating scalar indices × strides
        //   - result_shape: kept axes after the first-kept is a range or full
        //   - contiguity: trailing kept axes must be Full
        let strides = row_major_strides(&t.shape);
        let mut base_off: i64 = 0;
        let mut result_shape: Vec<i64> = Vec::new();
        let mut first_kept_seen = false;
        // Runtime offset accumulator: scalar indices may be runtime values.
        let mut dyn_off: Option<Value> = None;

        for (axis, cat) in classified.iter().enumerate() {
            let dim = t.shape[axis];
            let stride = strides[axis];
            match cat {
                IndexCat::Scalar(_) => {
                    if first_kept_seen {
                        return err(span,
                            "slice 4 only supports contiguous slicing: \
                             scalar indices must come before any kept axis. \
                             Got a scalar index after a slice.");
                    }
                }
                IndexCat::Full => {
                    first_kept_seen = true;
                    result_shape.push(dim);
                }
                IndexCat::Range { start, end } => {
                    if first_kept_seen {
                        return err(span,
                            "slice 4 only supports contiguous slicing: \
                             a range slice may only appear as the FIRST \
                             kept axis. Trailing kept axes must be `:`.");
                    }
                    // Normalize/clamp to match the interpreter (#291.4): negative
                    // bounds resolve from the end, positive bounds clamp to
                    // [0, dim], and an empty (start >= end) range yields a
                    // zero-extent axis rather than an error. Keeps `dmc jit`
                    // slice bounds in step with `dmc run` (interp.rs:503).
                    let norm = |v: i64| if v < 0 { (dim + v).max(0) } else { v.min(dim) };
                    let s = norm(*start);
                    let e = norm(*end);
                    base_off += s * stride;
                    first_kept_seen = true;
                    result_shape.push((e - s).max(0));
                }
            }
        }
        // Apply scalar offsets — they may be either compile-time literal
        // (folded into base_off) or runtime values (composed into dyn_off).
        for (axis, cat) in classified.iter().enumerate() {
            if let IndexCat::Scalar(v) = cat {
                // #206: bounds-check the user index before folding it into the
                // load address (the JIT otherwise read OOB heap memory). #270:
                // use the resolved (negative-adjusted) index for the offset.
                let ri = self.bounds_check_index(*v, t.shape[axis]);
                let stride = strides[axis];
                let stride_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, stride);
                let scaled = self.builder.ins().imul(ri, stride_v);
                dyn_off = Some(match dyn_off {
                    Some(prev) => self.builder.ins().iadd(prev, scaled),
                    None => scaled,
                });
            }
        }

        let elem_bytes = t.elem_bytes();
        let total_off = if let Some(d) = dyn_off {
            let base_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, base_off);
            let sum = self.builder.ins().iadd(base_v, d);
            let eb = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, elem_bytes);
            self.builder.ins().imul(sum, eb)
        } else {
            self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, base_off * elem_bytes)
        };
        let addr = self.builder.ins().iadd(ptr, total_off);

        if result_shape.is_empty() {
            // All dims consumed by scalar indices — scalar load.
            let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
            let v = self.builder.ins().load(t.elem.cl(), flags, addr, 0);
            Ok((v, TyKind::Scalar(t.elem)))
        } else {
            // View into the same buffer with a new static shape.
            let view_ty = TensorTy { elem: t.elem, shape: result_shape };
            Ok((addr, TyKind::Tensor(view_ty)))
        }
    }

    /// #276: read a (possibly non-contiguous) slice into a fresh tensor — one
    /// flat loop over the output, mapping each output element to its source
    /// offset. Handles any mix of scalar (drops the axis), full (keeps the axis),
    /// and bounded range (keeps `b-a` of the axis) indices. Always copies (the
    /// interpreter does too; binding a slice already deep-copies via #249).
    fn lower_tensor_slice_read_copy(
        &mut self,
        ptr: Value,
        t: &TensorTy,
        classified: &[IndexCat],
        _span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        let src_strides = row_major_strides(&t.shape); // in elements
        // Per source axis: start index (runtime i64), extent, and whether kept.
        let mut starts: Vec<Value> = Vec::with_capacity(t.rank());
        let mut extents: Vec<i64> = Vec::with_capacity(t.rank());
        let mut kept: Vec<bool> = Vec::with_capacity(t.rank());
        for (axis, cat) in classified.iter().enumerate() {
            let dim = t.shape[axis];
            match cat {
                IndexCat::Scalar(v) => {
                    let ri = self.bounds_check_index(*v, dim); // resolve negative + bounds
                    starts.push(ri);
                    extents.push(1);
                    kept.push(false);
                }
                IndexCat::Full => {
                    starts.push(self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0));
                    extents.push(dim);
                    kept.push(true);
                }
                IndexCat::Range { start, end } => {
                    // Clamp/normalize to match the interpreter (#291.4); see the
                    // contiguous read path above.
                    let norm = |v: i64| if v < 0 { (dim + v).max(0) } else { v.min(dim) };
                    let s = norm(*start);
                    let e = norm(*end);
                    starts.push(self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, s));
                    extents.push((e - s).max(0));
                    kept.push(true);
                }
            }
        }
        let out_shape: Vec<i64> = (0..t.rank()).filter(|&a| kept[a]).map(|a| extents[a]).collect();
        let out_ty = TensorTy { elem: t.elem, shape: out_shape.clone() };
        let total = out_ty.nelems();
        let out_ptr = self.forge_alloc(out_ty.nbytes());
        // Output strides (elements) + the output-axis position of each kept source
        // axis, so a flat output index decomposes into per-axis coordinates.
        let out_strides = row_major_strides(&out_shape);
        let mut out_pos = vec![0usize; t.rank()];
        let mut j = 0;
        for a in 0..t.rank() {
            if kept[a] { out_pos[a] = j; j += 1; }
        }
        let elem_bytes = t.elem_bytes();

        // for i in 0..total { out[i] = src[ map(i) ] }
        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let cap = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, total);
        let hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let body = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(hdr);
        let i = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
        let cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, i, cap);
        self.brif(cont, body, exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);

        self.enter(body);
        // src_flat = Σ_axis (start_axis + coord_axis) * src_stride_axis
        let mut src_flat = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        for a in 0..t.rank() {
            // coordinate along this source axis (0 for a dropped scalar axis).
            let coord = if kept[a] {
                let os = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, out_strides[out_pos[a]]);
                let div = self.builder.ins().udiv(i, os);
                let ext = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, extents[a]);
                self.builder.ins().urem(div, ext)
            } else {
                zero
            };
            let src_idx = self.builder.ins().iadd(starts[a], coord);
            let st = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, src_strides[a]);
            let term = self.builder.ins().imul(src_idx, st);
            src_flat = self.builder.ins().iadd(src_flat, term);
        }
        let eb = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, elem_bytes);
        let src_byte = self.builder.ins().imul(src_flat, eb);
        let out_byte = self.builder.ins().imul(i, eb);
        let v = self.tensor_load_elem(ptr, src_byte, t.elem);
        self.tensor_store_elem(out_ptr, out_byte, v);
        let inext = self.builder.ins().iadd(i, one);
        self.jump(hdr, &[inext]);
        self.builder.seal_block(body);
        self.builder.seal_block(hdr);

        self.enter(exit);
        Ok((out_ptr, TyKind::Tensor(out_ty)))
    }

    /// Classify a single AST index into the IndexCat used by the slicer.
    /// Scalars are lowered through the IR builder so they may be runtime
    /// values; ranges must be literal-int (slice 4 limit).
    fn classify_index(&mut self, ie: &IndexElem, span: &Span) -> Result<IndexCat, JitError> {
        // #276: resolve a range slice's bounds through the shape env, so a
        // shape-parametric range (`cos_table[0..S, ..]`, S bound at
        // monomorphization) works — not only literal-int bounds.
        if let IndexElem::Expr(Expr::Range { start, end, inclusive, .. }) = ie {
            let s = match start.as_deref() {
                Some(e) => resolve_shape_expr(e, &self.shape_env, span)?,
                None => 0,
            };
            let mut e = match end.as_deref() {
                Some(e) => resolve_shape_expr(e, &self.shape_env, span)?,
                None => return err(span, "range slice needs an explicit end in the JIT"),
            };
            if *inclusive { e += 1; }
            return Ok(IndexCat::Range { start: s, end: e });
        }
        let static_cat = classify_index_static(ie, span)?;
        match (ie, static_cat) {
            (IndexElem::Expr(e), StaticIndexCat::Scalar) => {
                let (v, k) = self.lower_expr(e)?;
                let v = self.coerce_to(v, &k, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;
                Ok(IndexCat::Scalar(v))
            }
            (_, StaticIndexCat::Full) => Ok(IndexCat::Full),
            (_, StaticIndexCat::Range { start, end }) => Ok(IndexCat::Range { start, end }),
            _ => unreachable!(),
        }
    }

    /// `A[i] = x`, `A[i, j] = x`. Tensor is treated as an alias of memory;
    /// no CoW yet (MEMORY.md §4 is deferred to a later slice).
    fn lower_tensor_store(
        &mut self,
        base: &Expr,
        idxs: &[IndexElem],
        rhs: &Expr,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        // If any index is a slice, full-slice, or range expression, dispatch to
        // the slice-store path.  Note: `a[0..4]` parses as
        // `IndexElem::Expr(Expr::Range{..})`, not `IndexElem::Slice`, so we
        // check for that case too.
        let has_slice = idxs.iter().any(|ie| match ie {
            IndexElem::FullSlice(_) | IndexElem::Slice { .. } => true,
            IndexElem::Expr(Expr::Range { .. }) => true,
            IndexElem::Expr(_) => false,
        });
        if has_slice {
            return self.lower_tensor_slice_store(base, idxs, rhs, span);
        }

        let (ptr, ty) = self.lower_expr(base)?;
        // TritTensor element-assign: `w[i, j] = v` where v ∈ {-1.0, 0.0, 1.0}.
        // We update the packed bit-layout: column-major, n_words u64s per column.
        if let TyKind::TritTensor(tt) = &ty {
            let tt = tt.clone();
            if idxs.len() != 2 {
                return err(span, "trit tensor element-assign requires exactly 2 indices [row, col]");
            }
            let row_expr = match &idxs[0] { IndexElem::Expr(e) => e.clone(), _ => return err(span, "trit: row index must be a scalar") };
            let col_expr = match &idxs[1] { IndexElem::Expr(e) => e.clone(), _ => return err(span, "trit: col index must be a scalar") };
            let (rv, rk) = self.lower_expr(rhs)?;
            let (row_v, rrow) = self.lower_expr(&row_expr)?;
            let (col_v, rcol) = self.lower_expr(&col_expr)?;
            let row_i64 = self.coerce_to(row_v, &rrow, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;
            let col_i64 = self.coerce_to(col_v, &rcol, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;
            let val_f32 = self.coerce_to(rv, &rk, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32), span)?;
            // val_i = sign: 1 if val > 0, -1 if val < 0, 0 otherwise (via fcmp)
            let zerof  = self.builder.ins().f32const(0.0_f32);
            let is_pos = self.builder.ins().fcmp(cranelift::codegen::ir::condcodes::FloatCC::GreaterThan, val_f32, zerof);
            let is_neg = self.builder.ins().fcmp(cranelift::codegen::ir::condcodes::FloatCC::LessThan, val_f32, zerof);
            let nw_c   = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, tt.n_words());
            let sixty4 = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 64);
            let eight  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 8);
            let one    = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
            let zero64 = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
            // word index = col * n_words + row / 64
            let row_word    = self.builder.ins().udiv(row_i64, sixty4);
            let bit_in_word = self.builder.ins().urem(row_i64, sixty4);
            let col_nw      = self.builder.ins().imul(col_i64, nw_c);
            let word_idx    = self.builder.ins().iadd(col_nw, row_word);
            let word_byte   = self.builder.ins().imul(word_idx, eight);
            let neg_stride  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, tt.n * tt.n_words() * 8);
            let neg_word_byte = self.builder.ins().iadd(word_byte, neg_stride);
            let bit_mask    = self.builder.ins().ishl(one, bit_in_word);
            let not_mask    = self.builder.ins().bnot(bit_mask);
            let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
            // Read-modify-write pos_mask word
            let pos_word = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, ptr, 0);
            // We can't use a runtime offset in load() — use iadd to get pointer
            let pos_ptr  = self.builder.ins().iadd(ptr, word_byte);
            let pos_old  = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, pos_ptr, 0);
            let pos_cleared = self.builder.ins().band(pos_old, not_mask);
            let pos_contrib = self.builder.ins().select(is_pos, bit_mask, zero64);
            let pos_new  = self.builder.ins().bor(pos_cleared, pos_contrib);
            self.builder.ins().store(flags, pos_new, pos_ptr, 0);
            // Read-modify-write neg_mask word
            let neg_ptr  = self.builder.ins().iadd(ptr, neg_word_byte);
            let neg_old  = self.builder.ins().load(cl::I64, flags, neg_ptr, 0);
            let neg_cleared = self.builder.ins().band(neg_old, not_mask);
            let neg_contrib = self.builder.ins().select(is_neg, bit_mask, zero64);
            let neg_new  = self.builder.ins().bor(neg_cleared, neg_contrib);
            self.builder.ins().store(flags, neg_new, neg_ptr, 0);
            let _ = pos_word; // suppress unused warning
            return Ok(());
        }
        // ModelArray index-assign: `arr[i] = model_val` stores a model pointer.
        if let TyKind::ModelArray(_, _, _) = &ty {
            if idxs.len() != 1 {
                return err(span, "model array index-assign requires exactly one index");
            }
            let idx_expr = match &idxs[0] {
                IndexElem::Expr(e) => e.clone(),
                _ => return unsupported(span, "non-expression model array index in assign"),
            };
            let (idx_v, idx_ty) = self.lower_expr(&idx_expr)?;
            let idx_i64 = self.coerce_to(idx_v, &idx_ty, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;
            let eight = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 8);
            let byte_off = self.builder.ins().imul(idx_i64, eight);
            let elem_addr = self.builder.ins().iadd(ptr, byte_off);
            let (rv, _rk) = self.lower_expr(rhs)?;
            let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
            self.builder.ins().store(flags, rv, elem_addr, 0);
            return Ok(());
        }
        // KvArray index-assign: `caches[i] = forge.kv(...)` stores a KV-cache
        // pointer (the per-layer staging idiom). Same 8-byte pointer slots as
        // ModelArray above. (#273 follow-up.)
        if let TyKind::KvArray(_, _) = &ty {
            if idxs.len() != 1 {
                return err(span, "KV array index-assign requires exactly one index");
            }
            let idx_expr = match &idxs[0] {
                IndexElem::Expr(e) => e.clone(),
                _ => return unsupported(span, "non-expression KV array index in assign"),
            };
            let (idx_v, idx_ty) = self.lower_expr(&idx_expr)?;
            let idx_i64 = self.coerce_to(idx_v, &idx_ty, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;
            let eight = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 8);
            let byte_off = self.builder.ins().imul(idx_i64, eight);
            let elem_addr = self.builder.ins().iadd(ptr, byte_off);
            let (rv, _rk) = self.lower_expr(rhs)?;
            let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
            self.builder.ins().store(flags, rv, elem_addr, 0);
            return Ok(());
        }
        let t = ty.as_tensor().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("index-assign requires a tensor, got `{}`", ty.render()),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?.clone();
        if idxs.len() != t.rank() {
            return err(span, format!(
                "tensor has rank {} but indexed with {} dim(s)", t.rank(), idxs.len(),
            ));
        }
        let mut idx_vals: Vec<Value> = Vec::with_capacity(idxs.len());
        for ie in idxs {
            match ie {
                IndexElem::Expr(e) => {
                    let (v, k) = self.lower_expr(e)?;
                    let v = self.coerce_to(v, &k, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;
                    idx_vals.push(v);
                }
                _ => unreachable!("slice indices filtered above"),
            }
        }
        let (rv, rk) = self.lower_expr(rhs)?;
        let rv = self.coerce_to(rv, &rk, &TyKind::Scalar(t.elem), span)?;
        // #206: bounds-check each user index before computing the store address.
        // #270: use the resolved (negative-adjusted) indices for the offset.
        let resolved_idx: Vec<Value> = idx_vals.iter().enumerate()
            .map(|(axis, &iv)| self.bounds_check_index(iv, t.shape[axis]))
            .collect();
        let byte_off = self.tensor_byte_offset(&t, &resolved_idx);
        self.tensor_store_elem(ptr, byte_off, rv);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Handle `tensor[..slice_indices..] = rhs` where at least one index is a
    /// `FullSlice` or `Slice`. Emits nested while-loops (one per slice dim) that
    /// copy elements from `rhs` into the appropriate range of `base`.
    fn lower_tensor_slice_store(
        &mut self,
        base: &Expr,
        idxs: &[IndexElem],
        rhs: &Expr,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        // Lower destination tensor.
        let (dst_ptr, dst_ty) = self.lower_expr(base)?;
        let dst_t = dst_ty.as_tensor().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("slice-assign requires a tensor, got `{}`", dst_ty.render()),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?.clone();

        if idxs.len() != dst_t.rank() {
            return err(span, format!(
                "tensor rank {} but {} indices", dst_t.rank(), idxs.len()
            ));
        }

        // Lower source tensor.
        let (src_ptr, src_ty) = self.lower_expr(rhs)?;
        let src_t = src_ty.as_tensor().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("slice-assign RHS must be a tensor, got `{}`", src_ty.render()),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?.clone();

        // For each dimension, compute start/end values and whether it's scalar.
        let n = idxs.len();
        let mut dst_starts: Vec<Value> = Vec::with_capacity(n);
        let mut dst_ends: Vec<Value> = Vec::with_capacity(n);
        let mut is_scalar: Vec<bool> = Vec::with_capacity(n);
        let mut scalar_vals: Vec<Option<Value>> = Vec::with_capacity(n);

        for (dim, ie) in idxs.iter().enumerate() {
            let dim_size = dst_t.shape[dim];
            match ie {
                // `a[0..4]` parses as IndexElem::Expr(Expr::Range{..}) — treat
                // it as a range slice.  Inclusive ranges (`0..=3`) are also
                // supported; the end is bumped by one to convert to exclusive.
                IndexElem::Expr(Expr::Range { start: rstart, end: rend, inclusive, .. }) => {
                    let s = if let Some(se) = rstart {
                        let (v, k) = self.lower_expr(se)?;
                        self.coerce_to(v, &k, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?
                    } else {
                        self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0)
                    };
                    let e_val = if let Some(ee) = rend {
                        let (v, k) = self.lower_expr(ee)?;
                        let v = self.coerce_to(v, &k, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;
                        if *inclusive {
                            let one = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
                            self.builder.ins().iadd(v, one)
                        } else {
                            v
                        }
                    } else {
                        self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, dim_size)
                    };
                    // Clamp to interpreter semantics (#291.4): negatives resolve
                    // from the end, positives clamp to dim, and an empty range
                    // (start >= end) is held at zero extent.
                    let s = self.clamp_slice_bound(s, dim_size);
                    let e_val = self.clamp_slice_bound(e_val, dim_size);
                    let s_gt_e = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedGreaterThan, s, e_val);
                    let e_val = self.builder.ins().select(s_gt_e, s, e_val);
                    dst_starts.push(s);
                    dst_ends.push(e_val);
                    is_scalar.push(false);
                    scalar_vals.push(None);
                }
                IndexElem::Expr(e) => {
                    let (v, k) = self.lower_expr(e)?;
                    let v = self.coerce_to(v, &k, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;
                    // dst_ends is unused for scalar dims but we push a placeholder.
                    let placeholder = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
                    dst_starts.push(v);
                    dst_ends.push(placeholder);
                    is_scalar.push(true);
                    scalar_vals.push(Some(v));
                }
                IndexElem::FullSlice(_) => {
                    let start = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
                    let end = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, dim_size);
                    dst_starts.push(start);
                    dst_ends.push(end);
                    is_scalar.push(false);
                    scalar_vals.push(None);
                }
                IndexElem::Slice { start, end, step, .. } => {
                    if step.is_some() {
                        return err(span, "slice-assign: stepped slices are not supported in the JIT");
                    }
                    let s = if let Some(se) = start {
                        let (v, k) = self.lower_expr(se)?;
                        self.coerce_to(v, &k, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?
                    } else {
                        self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0)
                    };
                    let e_val = if let Some(ee) = end {
                        let (v, k) = self.lower_expr(ee)?;
                        self.coerce_to(v, &k, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?
                    } else {
                        self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, dim_size)
                    };
                    // Clamp to interpreter semantics (#291.4); see the Range arm.
                    let s = self.clamp_slice_bound(s, dim_size);
                    let e_val = self.clamp_slice_bound(e_val, dim_size);
                    let s_gt_e = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedGreaterThan, s, e_val);
                    let e_val = self.builder.ins().select(s_gt_e, s, e_val);
                    dst_starts.push(s);
                    dst_ends.push(e_val);
                    is_scalar.push(false);
                    scalar_vals.push(None);
                }
            }
        }

        // Collect which dst dims are slice (non-scalar) dims.
        let slice_dims: Vec<usize> = (0..n).filter(|&i| !is_scalar[i]).collect();

        // Validate: src rank must equal number of slice dims.
        if src_t.rank() != slice_dims.len() {
            return err(span, format!(
                "slice-assign: src has rank {} but there are {} slice dims in the index",
                src_t.rank(), slice_dims.len()
            ));
        }

        // Per-axis extent validation: static where possible, runtime trap otherwise.
        for (j, &sdim) in slice_dims.iter().enumerate() {
            match &idxs[sdim] {
                IndexElem::FullSlice(_)
                | IndexElem::Slice { start: None, end: None, step: None, .. } => {
                    if dst_t.shape[sdim] != src_t.shape[j] {
                        return err(span, format!(
                            "slice-assign: dst dim {} has extent {} but src dim {} has size {}",
                            sdim, dst_t.shape[sdim], j, src_t.shape[j]
                        ));
                    }
                }
                _ => {
                    let ok_block   = self.builder.create_block();
                    let fail_block = self.builder.create_block();
                    let extent   = self.builder.ins().isub(dst_ends[sdim], dst_starts[sdim]);
                    let expected = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, src_t.shape[j]);
                    let cond = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::Equal, extent, expected);
                    self.brif(cond, ok_block, fail_block);
                    self.enter(fail_block);
                    self.builder.seal_block(fail_block);
                    self.trap_user(1);
                    self.enter(ok_block);
                    self.builder.seal_block(ok_block);
                }
            }
        }

        // Allocate one loop Variable per slice dim (declared before entering loops).
        let mut loop_vars: Vec<cranelift::frontend::Variable> = Vec::with_capacity(slice_dims.len());
        for _ in &slice_dims {
            let lv = self.builder.declare_var(cl::I64);
            loop_vars.push(lv);
        }

        // Emit nested loops. We build them iteratively: for each level (outermost
        // first), emit header → body; after all levels, emit the innermost copy
        // body, then close loops in reverse (increment → jump back → seal).

        // Structures to remember the CFG blocks for each loop level so we can
        // wire the back-edges and exits after building the body.
        struct LoopLevel {
            header: cranelift::codegen::ir::Block,
            body:   cranelift::codegen::ir::Block,
            exit:   cranelift::codegen::ir::Block,
            lv:     cranelift::frontend::Variable,
        }

        let mut levels: Vec<LoopLevel> = Vec::with_capacity(slice_dims.len());

        // Open all loops (outer to inner).
        for (j, &sdim) in slice_dims.iter().enumerate() {
            let lv = loop_vars[j];
            let start = dst_starts[sdim];
            let end   = dst_ends[sdim];

            // Initialise loop counter to start.
            self.builder.def_var(lv, start);

            let header = self.builder.create_block();
            let body   = self.builder.create_block();
            let exit   = self.builder.create_block();

            self.jump(header, &[]);

            // Header: check counter < end.
            self.enter(header);
            let cur = self.builder.use_var(lv);
            let cond = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, cur, end);
            self.brif(cond, body, exit);

            self.enter(body);
            self.loop_stack.push(LoopFrame { header, exit });

            levels.push(LoopLevel { header, body, exit, lv });
        }

        // ── Innermost body: copy one element ──────────────────────────────────
        let elem_bytes = dst_t.elem_bytes();

        // Compute dst linear index: sum over all dims of idx[d] * dst_stride[d].
        let mut dst_off = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let mut src_dim_counter = 0usize;
        for d in 0..dst_t.rank() {
            let stride: i64 = dst_t.shape[d+1..].iter().product();
            let idx_v = if is_scalar[d] {
                scalar_vals[d].unwrap()
            } else {
                let lv = loop_vars[src_dim_counter];
                self.builder.use_var(lv)
            };
            if stride == 1 {
                dst_off = self.builder.ins().iadd(dst_off, idx_v);
            } else {
                let sv = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, stride);
                let term = self.builder.ins().imul(idx_v, sv);
                dst_off = self.builder.ins().iadd(dst_off, term);
            }
            if !is_scalar[d] { src_dim_counter += 1; }
        }
        let eb_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, elem_bytes);
        let dst_byte_off = self.builder.ins().imul(dst_off, eb_v);

        // Compute src linear index: sum over slice dims of
        //   (loop_var[j] - dst_start[sdim]) * src_stride[j].
        let mut src_off = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        for (j, &sdim) in slice_dims.iter().enumerate() {
            let src_stride: i64 = src_t.shape[j+1..].iter().product();
            let lv = loop_vars[j];
            let loop_val = self.builder.use_var(lv);
            let relative = self.builder.ins().isub(loop_val, dst_starts[sdim]);
            if src_stride == 1 {
                src_off = self.builder.ins().iadd(src_off, relative);
            } else {
                let ssv = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, src_stride);
                let term = self.builder.ins().imul(relative, ssv);
                src_off = self.builder.ins().iadd(src_off, term);
            }
        }
        let src_byte_off = self.builder.ins().imul(src_off, eb_v);

        // Load from src, store to dst.
        let loaded = self.tensor_load_elem(src_ptr, src_byte_off, src_t.elem);
        self.tensor_store_elem(dst_ptr, dst_byte_off, loaded);

        // ── Close loops (inner to outer) ────────────────────────────────────
        for ll in levels.into_iter().rev() {
            if !self.is_filled() {
                // Increment and jump back to header.
                let cur = self.builder.use_var(ll.lv);
                let one = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
                let next = self.builder.ins().iadd(cur, one);
                self.builder.def_var(ll.lv, next);
                self.jump(ll.header, &[]);
            }
            self.loop_stack.pop();
            self.builder.seal_block(ll.body);
            self.builder.seal_block(ll.header);
            self.enter(ll.exit);
            self.builder.seal_block(ll.exit);
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    /// `A .+ B`, `A .- B`, `A .* B`, `A ./ B`, `A @ B`. Shapes must match
    /// exactly (no broadcasting yet). Result allocates a fresh tensor in
    /// Forge.
    fn lower_tensor_tensor_binop(
        &mut self,
        op: &BinOp,
        l: Value, lt: &TensorTy,
        r: Value, rt: &TensorTy,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        match op {
            BinOp::Matmul => self.lower_matmul(l, lt, r, rt, span),
            BinOp::DotAdd | BinOp::DotSub | BinOp::DotMul | BinOp::DotDiv
            | BinOp::DotPow | BinOp::DotPow2
            | BinOp::DotLt | BinOp::DotGt | BinOp::DotLe | BinOp::DotGe => {
                self.lower_elementwise(op, l, lt, r, rt, span)
            }
            _ => err(span, format!(
                "operator `{:?}` is not defined on tensors; use elementwise \
                 (`.+`, `.-`, `.*`, `./`, `.^`, `.< .> .<= .>=`) or matmul (`@`)",
                op,
            )),
        }
    }

    /// Emit a single f32 elementwise op on two already-loaded lane values.
    /// Shared by the scalar-broadcast and same-shape tensor kernels so `.^`
    /// and the comparison masks behave identically in both. `.^` lowers to
    /// a `powf` libcall per lane; comparisons yield 1.0/0.0 f32 masks
    /// (matching the interpreter's 0/1 tensors used in select arithmetic).
    fn emit_f32_elem(&mut self, op: &BinOp, lhs: Value, rhs: Value) -> Value {
        match op {
            BinOp::DotAdd => self.builder.ins().fadd(lhs, rhs),
            BinOp::DotSub => self.builder.ins().fsub(lhs, rhs),
            BinOp::DotMul => self.builder.ins().fmul(lhs, rhs),
            BinOp::DotDiv => self.builder.ins().fdiv(lhs, rhs),
            BinOp::DotPow | BinOp::DotPow2 => {
                let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_powf_f32")
                    .expect("powf symbol registered").clone();
                let fr = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                let call = self.builder.ins().call(fr, &[lhs, rhs]);
                self.builder.inst_results(call)[0]
            }
            BinOp::DotLt | BinOp::DotGt | BinOp::DotLe | BinOp::DotGe => {
                let cc = match op {
                    BinOp::DotLt => FloatCC::LessThan,
                    BinOp::DotGt => FloatCC::GreaterThan,
                    BinOp::DotLe => FloatCC::LessThanOrEqual,
                    BinOp::DotGe => FloatCC::GreaterThanOrEqual,
                    _ => unreachable!(),
                };
                let c = self.builder.ins().fcmp(cc, lhs, rhs);
                let one = self.builder.ins().f32const(1.0);
                let zero = self.builder.ins().f32const(0.0);
                self.builder.ins().select(c, one, zero)
            }
            _ => unreachable!("emit_f32_elem: unsupported op {:?}", op),
        }
    }

    /// Elementwise op over two tensors of *different* but broadcast-
    /// compatible shapes. Shapes are compile-time known, so a single flat
    /// loop over the output decomposes each index per axis and accumulates
    /// each operand's element offset with stride-0 on its broadcast axes
    /// (dim == 1). General rank; the renderer hits it as `[1,W] op [H,1]`.
    fn lower_elementwise_broadcast(
        &mut self,
        op: &BinOp,
        l: Value, lt: &TensorTy,
        r: Value, rt: &TensorTy,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        let out_shape = broadcast_out_shape(&lt.shape, &rt.shape, span)?;
        let rank = out_shape.len();
        let la = pad_left_shape(&lt.shape, rank);
        let lb = pad_left_shape(&rt.shape, rank);
        let sa = row_major_strides(&la);
        let sb = row_major_strides(&lb);
        let out_ty = TensorTy { elem: ScalarKind::F32, shape: out_shape.clone() };
        let out_ptr = self.forge_alloc(out_ty.nbytes());
        let n = out_ty.nelems();

        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let cap = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, n);
        let eb = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);

        let hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let body = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);

        self.jump(hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(hdr);
        let o = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
        let cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, o, cap);
        self.brif(cont, body, exit);

        self.enter(body);
        // Decompose the flat output index `o` into per-axis indices, last
        // axis first, accumulating source offsets. Divisors are constants.
        let mut rem = o;
        let mut a_off = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let mut b_off = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        for axis in (0..rank).rev() {
            let dimc = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, out_shape[axis]);
            let idx = self.builder.ins().urem(rem, dimc);
            rem = self.builder.ins().udiv(rem, dimc);
            if la[axis] > 1 {
                let s = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, sa[axis]);
                let term = self.builder.ins().imul(idx, s);
                a_off = self.builder.ins().iadd(a_off, term);
            }
            if lb[axis] > 1 {
                let s = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, sb[axis]);
                let term = self.builder.ins().imul(idx, s);
                b_off = self.builder.ins().iadd(b_off, term);
            }
        }
        let a_byte = self.builder.ins().imul(a_off, eb);
        let b_byte = self.builder.ins().imul(b_off, eb);
        let o_byte = self.builder.ins().imul(o, eb);
        let av = self.tensor_load_elem(l, a_byte, ScalarKind::F32);
        let bv = self.tensor_load_elem(r, b_byte, ScalarKind::F32);
        let ov = self.emit_f32_elem(op, av, bv);
        self.tensor_store_elem(out_ptr, o_byte, ov);
        let onext = self.builder.ins().iadd(o, one);
        self.jump(hdr, &[onext]);

        self.builder.seal_block(body);
        self.builder.seal_block(hdr);
        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);

        Ok((out_ptr, TyKind::Tensor(out_ty)))
    }

    fn lower_elementwise(
        &mut self,
        op: &BinOp,
        l: Value, lt: &TensorTy,
        r: Value, rt: &TensorTy,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(Value, TyKind), JitError> {
        if lt.elem != ScalarKind::F32 || rt.elem != ScalarKind::F32 {
            return err(span, "elementwise op only supports f32 in slice 2");
        }
        // NumPy-style axis broadcasting when shapes differ but are
        // compatible (e.g. ray grid `[1, W] .op [H, 1]` -> `[H, W]`).
        if lt.shape != rt.shape {
            return self.lower_elementwise_broadcast(op, l, lt, r, rt, span);
        }
        let out_ty = lt.clone();
        let out_ptr = self.forge_alloc(out_ty.nbytes());
        let n = out_ty.nelems();

        // SIMD fast path: when the element count is a multiple of 4, process
        // four f32 lanes per iteration with F32X4 vector ops. Shapes are
        // compile-time known, so this branch is chosen statically. Only the
        // arithmetic ops have a vector form here; `.^` (libcall) and the
        // comparison masks take the scalar loop below.
        let simd_ok = matches!(op,
            BinOp::DotAdd | BinOp::DotSub | BinOp::DotMul | BinOp::DotDiv);
        if simd_ok && n % 4 == 0 && n >= 4 {
            self.simd_elementwise(op, l, r, out_ptr, n);
            return Ok((out_ptr, TyKind::Tensor(out_ty)));
        }

        // for i in 0..n: out[i] = l[i] OP r[i]  (scalar fallback)
        let header = self.builder.create_block();
        let body = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(header, cl::I64);

        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        self.jump(header, &[zero]);

        self.enter(header);
        let i = self.builder.block_params(header)[0];
        let cap = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, n);
        let cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, i, cap);
        self.brif(cont, body, exit);

        self.enter(body);
        let elem_bytes = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, out_ty.elem_bytes());
        let off = self.builder.ins().imul(i, elem_bytes);
        let lv = self.tensor_load_elem(l, off, lt.elem);
        let rv = self.tensor_load_elem(r, off, rt.elem);
        let ov = self.emit_f32_elem(op, lv, rv);
        self.tensor_store_elem(out_ptr, off, ov);
        let one = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let inext = self.builder.ins().iadd(i, one);
        self.jump(header, &[inext]);

        self.builder.seal_block(body);
        self.builder.seal_block(header);
        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);

        Ok((out_ptr, TyKind::Tensor(out_ty)))
    }

    /// Vectorized elementwise kernel: 4 f32 lanes per iteration via F32X4.
    /// `n` must be a multiple of 4. Unaligned vector load/store (the Forge
    /// base is 64-byte aligned but element offsets need not be), which the
    /// host backend lowers to `movups`/equivalent.
    fn simd_elementwise(&mut self, op: &BinOp, l: Value, r: Value, out: Value, n: i64) {
        let flags = cranelift::codegen::ir::MemFlagsData::new();
        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let step = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 16); // 4 lanes * 4 bytes
        let byte_count = n.checked_mul(4).expect("simd_elementwise: byte count overflows i64");
        let cap = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, byte_count);
        let hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let body = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(hdr);
        let off = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
        let cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, off, cap);
        self.brif(cont, body, exit);
        self.enter(body);
        let la = self.builder.ins().iadd(l, off);
        let ra = self.builder.ins().iadd(r, off);
        let oa = self.builder.ins().iadd(out, off);
        let lv = self.builder.ins().load(cl::F32X4, flags, la, 0);
        let rv = self.builder.ins().load(cl::F32X4, flags, ra, 0);
        let ov = match op {
            BinOp::DotAdd => self.builder.ins().fadd(lv, rv),
            BinOp::DotSub => self.builder.ins().fsub(lv, rv),
            BinOp::DotMul => self.builder.ins().fmul(lv, rv),
            BinOp::DotDiv => self.builder.ins().fdiv(lv, rv),
            _ => unreachable!(),
        };
        self.builder.ins().store(flags, ov, oa, 0);
        let noff = self.builder.ins().iadd(off, step);
        self.jump(hdr, &[noff]);
        self.builder.seal_block(body);
        self.builder.seal_block(hdr);
        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);
    }

    /// 2D transpose via copy. Slice 4 keeps the row-major contiguous
    /// invariant for every Tensor value, so transpose materializes a fresh
    /// allocation rather than emitting a strided view. The matmul kernel
    /// then sees a normal contiguous tensor on both sides.
    ///
    /// 1D transpose is a no-op (a 1D vector has no notion of row vs col);
    /// we still allocate a fresh copy so callers can rely on transpose
    /// returning fresh memory.
    // ─── @grad: forward recording + reverse-mode backward ──────────────────

    /// FOMAML: Lower `let (loss, g) = inner.fwd_bwd(args)` inside a @grad fn.
    ///
    /// The inner `fwd_bwd` call is emitted as a black-box call; its result
    /// gradient pointers (read via `take_grad_at_idx` immediately after the
    /// call, while GRAD_SLOTS still holds the inner values) become
    /// stop-gradient `Const` nodes in the outer AD graph.
    ///
    /// This implements First-Order MAML: we do NOT differentiate through the
    /// inner gradient computation. The outer backward only flows through
    /// operations applied TO the inner gradient tensors (e.g. W .- g.W .* lr).
    ///
    /// GRAD_SLOTS ordering safety: GRAD_SLOTS is a HashMap. The inner fwd_bwd
    /// writes GRAD_SLOTS[param_idx] = inner_ptr. We call take_grad_at_idx
    /// immediately after (reading inner_ptr, no drain). Later, the outer
    /// emit_backward writes GRAD_SLOTS[param_idx] = outer_ptr (overwriting).
    /// The test harness calls take_grads() after the outer fwd_bwd returns,
    /// which drains {param_idx: outer_ptr} — the outer gradient only.
    fn ad_lower_fwd_bwd_destructure(
        &mut self,
        pats: &[Pattern],
        fname: &str,
        args: &[CallArg],
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        if pats.len() != 2 {
            return err(span, "`f.fwd_bwd(...)` destructures into exactly `(loss, grads)`");
        }
        let loss_name = match &pats[0] {
            Pattern::Ident(n, _) => n.clone(),
            Pattern::Wildcard(_) => "_".to_string(),
            _ => return unsupported(span, "fwd_bwd loss binding must be an identifier"),
        };
        let grad_name = match &pats[1] {
            Pattern::Ident(n, _) => n.clone(),
            Pattern::Wildcard(_) => "_".to_string(),
            _ => return unsupported(span, "fwd_bwd gradient binding must be an identifier"),
        };
        let bwd = format!("{}$fwd_bwd", fname);
        let entry = self.fns.get(&bwd).cloned().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("`{}` is not a `@grad fn` (no fwd_bwd entry)", fname),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?;
        let schema = self.grad_schemas.get(&bwd).cloned().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("`{}.fwd_bwd` has no gradient schema (no `!` mut params?)", fname),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?;
        if args.len() != entry.params.len() {
            return err(span, format!(
                "`{}` expects {} arg(s), got {}", fname, entry.params.len(), args.len(),
            ));
        }

        // Lower each argument in the non-AD path (inner call is a black box).
        let mut vals: Vec<Value> = Vec::with_capacity(args.len());
        for (i, a) in args.iter().enumerate() {
            let e = match a {
                CallArg::Positional(e) => e,
                _ => return unsupported(span, "named/spread args to fwd_bwd"),
            };
            let (v, k) = self.lower_expr(e)?;
            let v = self.coerce_to(v, &k, &entry.params[i].1, span)?;
            vals.push(v);
        }

        // Emit the inner fwd_bwd call. It returns only the f32 loss;
        // grad ptrs are captured into GRAD_SLOTS via capture_grad.
        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &vals);
        let loss_v = self.builder.inst_results(call)[0];

        // Bind loss as a Const (stop-gradient) AD node.
        if loss_name != "_" {
            let loss_node = self.ad.as_mut().unwrap().push(
                AdOp::Const, vec![], TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32), loss_v);
            self.ad.as_mut().unwrap().env.insert(loss_name.clone(), loss_node);
            self.declare_local(loss_name, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32), loss_v);
        }

        // Read each inner gradient immediately (before outer backward overwrites
        // GRAD_SLOTS), bind as stop-gradient Const AD nodes and as locals so
        // `g.W` field access can resolve them in the outer @grad fn body.
        if grad_name != "_" {
            let grad_entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_take_grad_at").expect("registered").clone();
            for (param_name, param_ty, param_idx) in &schema {
                let grad_ptr = self.call_take_grad_at(&grad_entry, *param_idx);
                let flat_name = format!("{}${}", grad_name, param_name);
                let grad_node = self.ad.as_mut().unwrap().push(
                    AdOp::Const, vec![], param_ty.clone(), grad_ptr);
                self.ad.as_mut().unwrap().env.insert(flat_name.clone(), grad_node);
                self.declare_local(flat_name, param_ty.clone(), grad_ptr);
            }
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    /// Lower a `@grad fn` body in recording mode. Handles `let` bindings
    /// followed by a single scalar-f32 loss expression. Returns the loss
    /// Value and its AD node id.
    fn ad_lower_block(&mut self, b: &Block_, span: &Span) -> Result<(Value, usize), JitError> {
        // Identify the loss expression: either the explicit tail_expr, or
        // the final stmt if it's a bare expression.
        let n_stmts = b.stmts.len();
        let final_from_stmt = b.tail_expr.is_none()
            && matches!(b.stmts.last(), Some(Stmt::Expr { assign: None, .. }));
        let body_len = if final_from_stmt { n_stmts - 1 } else { n_stmts };

        for stmt in &b.stmts[..body_len] {
            self.ad_lower_stmt(stmt, span)?;
        }

        let loss_expr: &Expr = if let Some(t) = &b.tail_expr {
            t
        } else if final_from_stmt {
            match b.stmts.last().unwrap() {
                Stmt::Expr { lhs, .. } => lhs,
                _ => unreachable!(),
            }
        } else {
            return err(span, "`@grad fn` body must end in a scalar loss expression");
        };

        let (v, ty, node) = self.ad_lower_expr(loss_expr, span)?;
        if !matches!(ty, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32)) {
            return err(span, format!(
                "`@grad fn` loss must be a scalar `f32`, got `{}`", ty.render(),
            ));
        }
        Ok((v, node))
    }

    /// Lower one non-final statement of a `@grad fn` body onto the AD graph
    /// (#368). Handles straight-line `let` / side-effect exprs, plus the control
    /// flow the JIT can resolve at compile time: accumulator reassignment and
    /// `for k in <const>..<const>` loops, which are UNROLLED. Reverse-mode needs
    /// a static tape, so a loop's trip count must be a compile-time constant (a
    /// literal or a shape parameter); runtime-data-dependent control flow
    /// (runtime `if`, `while`, runtime loop bounds) stays unsupported and makes
    /// the whole `@grad fn` fall back to the interpreter reference path.
    fn ad_lower_stmt(&mut self, stmt: &Stmt, span: &Span) -> Result<(), JitError> {
        match stmt {
            Stmt::Let(l) => {
                // `let (loss, g) = inner.fwd_bwd(...)` inside a @grad fn:
                // FOMAML — the inner gradient is a stop-gradient leaf.
                if let Pattern::Tuple(pats, _) = &l.pattern {
                    if let Some((fname, "fwd_bwd", args)) = as_fwd_bwd_call(&l.value) {
                        self.ad_lower_fwd_bwd_destructure(pats, fname, args, &l.span)?;
                        return Ok(());
                    }
                    return unsupported(&l.span,
                        "tuple destructuring inside `@grad fn` is only \
                         supported for `let (loss, g) = f.fwd_bwd(...)`");
                }
                let name = match &l.pattern {
                    Pattern::Ident(n, _) => n.clone(),
                    _ => return unsupported(&l.span, "destructuring `let` inside `@grad fn`"),
                };
                let (_v, _ty, node) = self.ad_lower_expr(&l.value, &l.span)?;
                self.ad.as_mut().unwrap().env.insert(name, node);
                Ok(())
            }
            // Accumulator reassignment (`acc = e`, `acc += -= *= /= e`): re-lower
            // and rebind env[name] so the gradient threads through the updated
            // node — the JIT analogue of the interpreter's var_node threading.
            Stmt::Expr { lhs: Expr::Ident(name, _), assign: Some((op, rhs)), span: sp } => {
                let node = match op {
                    AssignOp::Eq => self.ad_lower_expr(rhs, sp)?.2,
                    AssignOp::PlusEq | AssignOp::MinusEq | AssignOp::StarEq | AssignOp::SlashEq => {
                        let acc_node = *self.ad.as_ref().unwrap().env.get(name).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                            msg: format!("@grad: `{}` reassigned before it was bound", name),
                            line: sp.line, col: sp.col,
                        })?;
                        let is_tensor = matches!(self.ad.as_ref().unwrap().nodes[acc_node].ty, TyKind::Tensor(_));
                        let binop = match op {
                            AssignOp::PlusEq  => if is_tensor { BinOp::DotAdd } else { BinOp::Add },
                            AssignOp::MinusEq => if is_tensor { BinOp::DotSub } else { BinOp::Sub },
                            AssignOp::StarEq  => if is_tensor { BinOp::DotMul } else { BinOp::Mul },
                            AssignOp::SlashEq => if is_tensor { BinOp::DotDiv } else { BinOp::Div },
                            _ => unreachable!(),
                        };
                        let lhs_expr = Expr::Ident(name.clone(), sp.clone());
                        self.ad_lower_binop(&binop, &lhs_expr, rhs, sp)?.2
                    }
                    _ => return unsupported(sp,
                        "compound assignment in `@grad fn` supports only `=` `+=` `-=` `*=` `/=` \
                         (bitwise / stream ops have no VJP)"),
                };
                self.ad.as_mut().unwrap().env.insert(name.clone(), node);
                Ok(())
            }
            Stmt::Expr { lhs, assign: None, .. } => {
                // A bare expr stmt for side effects — lower but ignore.
                let _ = self.ad_lower_expr(lhs, span)?;
                Ok(())
            }
            // Compile-time `for k in LO..HI` → unroll onto the static tape.
            Stmt::For { pattern, iter, body, span: sp } => {
                let (lo_e, hi_e, inclusive) = match iter {
                    Expr::Range { start: Some(s), end: Some(e), inclusive, .. } =>
                        (s.as_ref(), e.as_ref(), *inclusive),
                    _ => return unsupported(sp,
                        "`@grad fn` for-loop needs a bounded range `for k in lo..hi`"),
                };
                let lo = self.ad_const_int(lo_e).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                    msg: "`@grad fn` for-loop bound must be a compile-time constant (a literal or \
                          shape parameter) — reverse-mode unrolls the loop".into(),
                    line: sp.line, col: sp.col })?;
                let hi = self.ad_const_int(hi_e).ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                    msg: "`@grad fn` for-loop bound must be a compile-time constant (a literal or \
                          shape parameter) — reverse-mode unrolls the loop".into(),
                    line: sp.line, col: sp.col })?;
                let hi = if inclusive { hi + 1 } else { hi };
                let idx_name = match pattern {
                    Pattern::Ident(n, _) => Some(n.clone()),
                    Pattern::Wildcard(_) => None,
                    _ => return unsupported(sp, "destructuring pattern in `@grad fn` for-loop"),
                };
                // Declare the index local once; redefine it per unrolled
                // iteration so the body reads the concrete value via lower_ident
                // (a non-differentiable Const node — loop indices aren't traced).
                let idx_var = idx_name.as_ref().map(|n| {
                    let var = self.builder.declare_var(cl::I64);
                    self.locals.insert(n.clone(), var);
                    self.local_tys.insert(n.clone(), TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64));
                    var
                });
                for k in lo..hi {
                    if let Some(var) = idx_var {
                        let kv = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, k);
                        self.builder.def_var(var, kv);
                    }
                    for s in &body.stmts {
                        self.ad_lower_stmt(s, sp)?;
                    }
                    if let Some(t) = &body.tail_expr {
                        let _ = self.ad_lower_expr(t, sp)?;
                    }
                }
                Ok(())
            }
            other => {
                let s = stmt_span(other);
                unsupported(&s,
                    "unsupported statement inside `@grad fn` (slice 6): supported are `let`, \
                     accumulator reassignment, and compile-time `for` loops; runtime `if` / \
                     `while` fall back to the interpreter")
            }
        }
    }

    /// Resolve an expression to a compile-time `i64` for `@grad` loop unrolling:
    /// integer literals (via `const_int_axis`) or shape parameters bound in the
    /// monomorphized `shape_env`. `None` if it isn't statically known.
    fn ad_const_int(&self, e: &Expr) -> Option<i64> {
        if let Some(n) = const_int_axis(e) { return Some(n); }
        if let Expr::Ident(name, _) = e { return self.shape_env.get(name).copied(); }
        None
    }

    /// Forward-lower an expression while recording an AD node. Returns
    /// `(fwd_value, ty, node_id)`. Only the differentiable subset is
    /// accepted; everything else errors with an AUTODIFF diagnostic.
    fn ad_lower_expr(&mut self, e: &Expr, span: &Span)
        -> Result<(Value, TyKind, usize), JitError>
    {
        match e {
            Expr::Ident(name, ispan) => {
                if let Some(&node) = self.ad.as_ref().unwrap().env.get(name) {
                    let n = &self.ad.as_ref().unwrap().nodes[node];
                    return Ok((n.fwd, n.ty.clone(), node));
                }
                // A non-AD local (e.g., a scalar bound outside the graph).
                let (v, ty) = self.lower_ident(name, ispan)?;
                let node = self.ad.as_mut().unwrap().push(AdOp::Const, vec![], ty.clone(), v);
                Ok((v, ty, node))
            }
            Expr::Literal(_, _) | Expr::TensorLit(_, _) | Expr::Nil(_) => {
                let (v, ty) = self.lower_expr(e)?;
                let node = self.ad.as_mut().unwrap().push(AdOp::Const, vec![], ty.clone(), v);
                Ok((v, ty, node))
            }
            Expr::Cast { expr, ty, span: cspan } => {
                // f32 -> f32 cast is identity for AD; other casts are
                // treated as constants (gradient stops).
                let target = ty_from_ast(ty, &self.shape_env)?;
                let (v, sty, node) = self.ad_lower_expr(expr, cspan)?;
                if target == sty {
                    Ok((v, sty, node))
                } else {
                    let (cv, _) = self.lower_expr(e)?;
                    let cnode = self.ad.as_mut().unwrap()
                        .push(AdOp::Const, vec![], target.clone(), cv);
                    Ok((cv, target, cnode))
                }
            }
            Expr::UnOp { op: UnOp::ReLU, operand: relu_op, span: uspan } => {
                let (v, ty, inode) = self.ad_lower_expr(relu_op, uspan)?;
                let t = ty.as_tensor().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                    msg: "`\\>` in @grad requires a tensor operand".into(),
                    line: uspan.line, col: uspan.col,
                })?.clone();
                let (out, _out_ty) = self.lower_tensor_relu(v, &t, uspan)?;
                let node = self.ad.as_mut().unwrap().push_aux(
                    AdOp::Relu, vec![inode], TyKind::Tensor(t.clone()), out, v);
                Ok((out, TyKind::Tensor(t), node))
            }
            Expr::Postfix { expr, op, span: pspan } => {
                match op {
                    PostfixOp::Transpose => {
                        let (v, ty, inode) = self.ad_lower_expr(expr, pspan)?;
                        let t = ty.as_tensor().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                            msg: "transpose in @grad requires a tensor".into(),
                            line: pspan.line, col: pspan.col,
                        })?.clone();
                        let (out, out_ty) = self.raw_transpose(v, &t, pspan)?;
                        let node = self.ad.as_mut().unwrap().push(
                            AdOp::Transpose, vec![inode], TyKind::Tensor(out_ty.clone()), out);
                        Ok((out, TyKind::Tensor(out_ty), node))
                    }
                    PostfixOp::Call(args) => self.ad_lower_call(expr, args, pspan),
                    PostfixOp::Field(field) => {
                        // FOMAML field access: `g.W` resolves to the local
                        // `"g$W"` bound by `ad_lower_fwd_bwd_destructure`.
                        // It is a stop-gradient Const node — differentiating
                        // through inner gradients would be full MAML, not FOMAML.
                        let base_name = match expr.as_ref() {
                            Expr::Ident(n, _) => n.clone(),
                            _ => return unsupported(pspan,
                                "field access on non-identifier base in @grad fn"),
                        };
                        let flat = format!("{}${}", base_name, field);
                        // Check if already registered as an AD Const node.
                        if let Some(&node) = self.ad.as_ref().unwrap().env.get(&flat) {
                            let n = &self.ad.as_ref().unwrap().nodes[node];
                            return Ok((n.fwd, n.ty.clone(), node));
                        }
                        // Fall back: look up as a plain local and wrap as Const.
                        let (v, ty) = self.lower_ident(&flat, pspan)?;
                        let node = self.ad.as_mut().unwrap()
                            .push(AdOp::Const, vec![], ty.clone(), v);
                        Ok((v, ty, node))
                    }
                    _ => unsupported(pspan,
                        "this postfix op is not differentiable in slice 6"),
                }
            }
            Expr::BinOp { op, lhs, rhs, span: bspan } => self.ad_lower_binop(op, lhs, rhs, bspan),
            Expr::Tuple(elems, _) if elems.len() == 1 => self.ad_lower_expr(&elems[0], span),
            _ => unsupported(span,
                "expression form not differentiable in slice 6 \
                 (supported: matmul, .+ .- .* ./, transpose, sum, mean, scalar f32 math)"),
        }
    }

    fn ad_lower_call(&mut self, callee: &Expr, args: &[CallArg], span: &Span)
        -> Result<(Value, TyKind, usize), JitError>
    {
        let name = match callee {
            Expr::Ident(n, _) => n.clone(),
            _ => return unsupported(span, "indirect calls in @grad"),
        };
        // Fused tensor ops with their own arity handled before the 1-arg gate.
        if name == "softmax" {
            return self.ad_lower_softmax(args, span);
        }
        if name == "rms_norm" {
            return self.ad_lower_rms_norm(args, span);
        }
        if name == "layer_norm" {
            return self.ad_lower_layer_norm(args, span);
        }
        if name == "rope" {
            return self.ad_lower_rope(args, span);
        }
        if name == "attn" || name == "attn_gqa" {
            return self.ad_lower_attn(&name, args, span);
        }
        if args.len() != 1 {
            return err(span, format!("`{}` takes exactly 1 argument", name));
        }
        let e = match &args[0] {
            CallArg::Positional(e) => e,
            _ => return unsupported(span, "non-positional arg in @grad reduction"),
        };

        // Tensor elementwise activations.
        match name.as_str() {
            "relu" | "tanh" | "gelu" | "sigmoid" | "silu" | "elu" | "mish" => {
                let (inp_v, ty, inode) = self.ad_lower_expr(e, span)?;
                let t = ty.as_tensor().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
                    msg: format!("`{}` in @grad requires a tensor argument", name),
                    line: span.line, col: span.col,
                })?.clone();
                let (out_ptr, out_ty_k) = match name.as_str() {
                    "relu"    => self.lower_tensor_relu(inp_v, &t, span)?,
                    "tanh"    => self.lower_tensor_activation(inp_v, &t, "__dmc_tanh_f32", span)?,
                    "gelu"    => self.lower_tensor_gelu(inp_v, &t, span)?,
                    "sigmoid" => self.lower_tensor_activation(inp_v, &t, "__dmc_sigmoid_f32", span)?,
                    "silu"    => self.lower_tensor_activation(inp_v, &t, "__dmc_silu_f32", span)?,
                    "elu"     => self.lower_tensor_activation(inp_v, &t, "__dmc_elu_f32", span)?,
                    "mish"    => self.lower_tensor_activation(inp_v, &t, "__dmc_mish_f32", span)?,
                    _ => unreachable!(),
                };
                let out_t = out_ty_k.as_tensor().unwrap().clone();
                let ad_op = match name.as_str() {
                    "relu"    => AdOp::ActivationRelu,
                    "tanh"    => AdOp::ActivationTanh,
                    "gelu"    => AdOp::ActivationGelu,
                    "sigmoid" => AdOp::ActivationSigmoid,
                    "silu"    => AdOp::ActivationSilu,
                    "elu"     => AdOp::ActivationElu,
                    "mish"    => AdOp::ActivationMish,
                    _ => unreachable!(),
                };
                let node = self.ad.as_mut().unwrap().push_aux(
                    ad_op, vec![inode], TyKind::Tensor(out_t.clone()), out_ptr, inp_v);
                return Ok((out_ptr, TyKind::Tensor(out_t), node));
            }
            _ => {}
        }

        let kind = match name.as_str() {
            "sum" => AdOp::Sum,
            "mean" => AdOp::Mean,
            _ => return unsupported(span, format!(
                "`{}` is not differentiable in slice 6 (supported: `sum`, `mean`, `relu`, `tanh`, `gelu`, `sigmoid`)",
                name,
            ).as_str()),
        };
        let (_v, ty, inode) = self.ad_lower_expr(e, span)?;
        let t = ty.as_tensor().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: format!("`{}` requires a tensor argument", name),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?.clone();
        // Forward value: reuse the existing fused-sum / mean machinery.
        let ptr = self.ad.as_ref().unwrap().nodes[inode].fwd;
        let total = self.fused_sum(ptr, t.nelems());
        let fwd = if matches!(kind, AdOp::Mean) {
            let n = self.builder.ins().f32const(t.nelems() as f32);
            self.builder.ins().fdiv(total, n)
        } else {
            total
        };
        let node = self.ad.as_mut().unwrap().push(
            kind, vec![inode], TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32), fwd);
        Ok((fwd, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32), node))
    }

    /// Forward-lower `softmax(x[, axis])` in a @grad body over the LAST axis
    /// (#368). Records an `AdOp::Softmax` node whose fwd is the output `y`; the
    /// VJP `dx = y .* (g - rowsum(g .* y))` is emitted in the backward. Rank ≥ 2
    /// static tensors only (the attention case); other forms bail to interp.
    fn ad_lower_softmax(&mut self, args: &[CallArg], span: &Span)
        -> Result<(Value, TyKind, usize), JitError>
    {
        if args.is_empty() || args.len() > 2 {
            return err(span, "`softmax` takes (x) or (x, axis)");
        }
        let xe = match &args[0] {
            CallArg::Positional(e) => e,
            _ => return unsupported(span, "non-positional arg to softmax in @grad"),
        };
        let (inp_v, ty, inode) = self.ad_lower_expr(xe, span)?;
        let t = ty.as_tensor().ok_or_else(|| JitError {
            msg: "softmax in @grad requires a tensor".into(),
            line: span.line, col: span.col,
        })?.clone();
        if t.elem != ScalarKind::F32 {
            return unsupported(span, "@grad softmax is f32-only");
        }
        if t.rank() < 2 {
            return unsupported(span,
                "@grad softmax requires a rank ≥ 2 static tensor (1D softmax VJP not JIT-lowered); use `dmc run`");
        }
        let last = (t.rank() - 1) as i64;
        if let Some(CallArg::Positional(ae)) = args.get(1) {
            if let Some(a) = const_int_axis(ae) {
                let norm = if a < 0 { a + t.rank() as i64 } else { a };
                if norm != last {
                    return unsupported(span,
                        "@grad softmax reduces over the last axis only; a non-last axis needs `dmc run`");
                }
            }
        }
        // Forward: per-row softmax over the last axis on a private copy.
        let l = t.shape[t.rank() - 1];
