                    return err(span, format!("`{}` on tensors is f32-only", name));
                }
                match name {
                    "relu"    => self.lower_tensor_relu(v, &tt, span),
                    "tanh"    => self.lower_tensor_activation(v, &tt, "__dmc_tanh_f32", span),
                    "gelu"    => self.lower_tensor_gelu(v, &tt, span),
                    "sigmoid" => self.lower_tensor_activation(v, &tt, "__dmc_sigmoid_f32", span),
                    "silu"    => self.lower_tensor_activation(v, &tt, "__dmc_silu_f32", span),
                    "elu"     => self.lower_tensor_activation(v, &tt, "__dmc_elu_f32", span),
                    "mish"    => self.lower_tensor_activation(v, &tt, "__dmc_mish_f32", span),
                    _ => unreachable!(),
                }
            }
            TyKind::Scalar(sk) => {
                let v = self.coerce_scalar(v, sk, ScalarKind::F32, span)?;
                match name {
                    "relu" => {
                        let z = self.builder.ins().f32const(0.0);
                        let c = self.builder.ins().fcmp(FloatCC::GreaterThan, v, z);
                        let r = self.builder.ins().select(c, v, z);
                        Ok((r, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32)))
                    }
                    "tanh"    => Ok((self.call_f32_math("__dmc_tanh_f32", v),    TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32))),
                    "gelu"    => Ok((self.emit_gelu_f32(v),                       TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32))),
                    "sigmoid" => Ok((self.call_f32_math("__dmc_sigmoid_f32", v), TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32))),
                    "silu"    => Ok((self.call_f32_math("__dmc_silu_f32", v),    TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32))),
                    "elu"     => Ok((self.call_f32_math("__dmc_elu_f32", v),     TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32))),
                    "mish"    => Ok((self.call_f32_math("__dmc_mish_f32", v),    TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32))),
                    _ => unreachable!(),
                }
            }
            _ => err(span, format!("`{}` requires an f32 scalar or f32 tensor", name)),
        }
    }

    /// Elementwise ReLU indicator mask: out[i] = (inp[i] > 0) ? adj[i] : 0.
    fn tensor_relu_mask(&mut self, adj: Value, inp: Value, t: &TensorTy) -> Value {
        let out    = self.forge_alloc(t.nbytes());
        let n      = t.nelems();
        let zero_i = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one_i  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let cap    = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, n);
        let eb     = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);
        let fzero  = self.builder.ins().f32const(0.0_f32);
        let hdr    = self.builder.create_block();
        let body   = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit   = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(hdr, &[zero_i]);
        self.enter(hdr);
        let i    = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
        let cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, i, cap);
        self.brif(cont, body, exit);
        self.enter(body);
        let off  = self.builder.ins().imul(i, eb);
        let xv   = self.tensor_load_elem(inp, off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let gv   = self.tensor_load_elem(adj, off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let pos  = self.builder.ins().fcmp(FloatCC::GreaterThan, xv, fzero);
        let ov   = self.builder.ins().select(pos, gv, fzero);
        self.tensor_store_elem(out, off, ov);
        let inext = self.builder.ins().iadd(i, one_i);
        self.jump(hdr, &[inext]);
        self.builder.seal_block(body);
        self.builder.seal_block(hdr);
        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);
        out
    }

    /// Elementwise activation VJP via a runtime derivative fn:
    ///   out[i] = adj[i] * deriv(inp[i])
    /// Used for silu/elu/mish, whose first derivatives are the `__dmc_<act>_
    /// deriv_f32` externs (#377). `deriv_sym` must be a registered f32→f32
    /// symbol; the derivative is taken over the stored input `inp` (the node's
    /// `aux`), matching interp's activation_deriv_f64.
    fn tensor_activation_deriv_backward(
        &mut self, adj: Value, inp: Value, t: &TensorTy, deriv_sym: &str,
    ) -> Value {
        let out    = self.forge_alloc(t.nbytes());
        let n      = t.nelems();
        let zero_i = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one_i  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let cap    = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, n);
        let eb     = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);
        let hdr    = self.builder.create_block();
        let body   = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit   = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(hdr, &[zero_i]);
        self.enter(hdr);
        let i    = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
        let cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, i, cap);
        self.brif(cont, body, exit);
        self.enter(body);
        let off  = self.builder.ins().imul(i, eb);
        let xv   = self.tensor_load_elem(inp, off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let dv   = self.call_f32_math(deriv_sym, xv);
        let gv   = self.tensor_load_elem(adj, off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let ov   = self.builder.ins().fmul(gv, dv);
        self.tensor_store_elem(out, off, ov);
        let inext = self.builder.ins().iadd(i, one_i);
        self.jump(hdr, &[inext]);
        self.builder.seal_block(body);
        self.builder.seal_block(hdr);
        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);
        out
    }

    /// softmax VJP over the last axis (#368): for each row,
    ///   s = Σ_c g[c]·y[c] ;  dx[c] = y[c]·(g[c] − s)
    /// `y` is the forward output; the last dim of `t` is the row length.
    fn tensor_softmax_backward(&mut self, adj: Value, y: Value, t: &TensorTy) -> Value {
        let l    = t.shape[t.rank() - 1];
        let rows = t.nelems() / l;
        let out  = self.forge_alloc(t.nbytes());
        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let eb   = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);
        let rows_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, rows);
        let l_v    = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, l);
        let fzero  = self.builder.ins().f32const(0.0_f32);

        // Outer loop over rows.
        let r_hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let r_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let r_exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(r_hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(r_hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(r_hdr);
        let r = self.builder.block_params(r_hdr)[0];
        let cont_r = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, r, rows_v);
        self.brif(cont_r, r_body, r_exit);

        self.enter(r_body);
        let base_e = self.builder.ins().imul(r, l_v);
        let base_b = self.builder.ins().imul(base_e, eb);
        let y_base = self.builder.ins().iadd(y, base_b);
        let g_base = self.builder.ins().iadd(adj, base_b);
        let o_base = self.builder.ins().iadd(out, base_b);

        // Pass 1: s = Σ_c g[c]·y[c]  (accumulator carried on the header block).
        let s_hdr  = self.builder.create_block();
        let s_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let s_exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(s_hdr, cl::I64);
        self.builder.append_block_param(s_hdr, cl::F32);
        self.builder.append_block_param(s_exit, cl::F32);
        self.jump(s_hdr, &[zero, fzero]);
        self.enter(s_hdr);
        let c1  = self.builder.block_params(s_hdr)[0];
        let acc = self.builder.block_params(s_hdr)[1];
        let cont_s = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, c1, l_v);
        self.builder.ins().brif(cont_s, s_body, &[], s_exit, &[acc.into()]);
        self.block_filled = true;
        self.enter(s_body);
        let off1 = self.builder.ins().imul(c1, eb);
        let gv   = self.tensor_load_elem(g_base, off1, ScalarKind::F32);
        let yv   = self.tensor_load_elem(y_base, off1, ScalarKind::F32);
        let gy   = self.builder.ins().fmul(gv, yv);
        let acc2 = self.builder.ins().fadd(acc, gy);
        let c1n  = self.builder.ins().iadd(c1, one);
        self.jump(s_hdr, &[c1n, acc2]);
        self.builder.seal_block(s_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(s_hdr);
        self.enter(s_exit);
        let s = self.builder.block_params(s_exit)[0];
        self.builder.seal_block(s_exit);

        // Pass 2: dx[c] = y[c]·(g[c] − s).
        let d_hdr  = self.builder.create_block();
        let d_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let d_exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(d_hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(d_hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(d_hdr);
        let c2 = self.builder.block_params(d_hdr)[0];
        let cont_d = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, c2, l_v);
        self.brif(cont_d, d_body, d_exit);
        self.enter(d_body);
        let off2 = self.builder.ins().imul(c2, eb);
        let gv2  = self.tensor_load_elem(g_base, off2, ScalarKind::F32);
        let yv2  = self.tensor_load_elem(y_base, off2, ScalarKind::F32);
        let gms  = self.builder.ins().fsub(gv2, s);
        let dxv  = self.builder.ins().fmul(yv2, gms);
        self.tensor_store_elem(o_base, off2, dxv);
        let c2n  = self.builder.ins().iadd(c2, one);
        self.jump(d_hdr, &[c2n]);
        self.builder.seal_block(d_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(d_hdr);
        self.enter(d_exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(d_exit);

        // Next row.
        let rn = self.builder.ins().iadd(r, one);
        self.jump(r_hdr, &[rn]);
        self.builder.seal_block(r_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(r_hdr);
        self.enter(r_exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(r_exit);
        out
    }

    /// rms_norm VJP over the last axis (#368). `g` is the incoming adjoint, `x`
    /// the input, `gain` the rank-1 gain `[D]`, `t` the x shape, `eps` the SSA
    /// epsilon. Returns `(dx, dgain)`. Per row (r recomputed = √(mean(x²)+eps),
    /// matching the forward's `__dmc_sqrt_f32`, and S = Σ gᵢ·gainᵢ·xᵢ):
    ///   dx_k    = g_k·gain_k/r − x_k·S/(D·r³)
    ///   dgain_k = Σ_rows g_k·x_k/r
    fn tensor_rms_norm_backward(
        &mut self, g: Value, x: Value, gain: Value, t: &TensorTy, eps: Value,
    ) -> (Value, Value) {
        let d    = t.shape[t.rank() - 1];
        let rows = t.nelems() / d;
        let dx    = self.forge_alloc(t.nbytes());
        let dgain_ty = TensorTy { elem: ScalarKind::F32, shape: vec![d] };
        let dgain = self.forge_alloc(dgain_ty.nbytes());
        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let eb   = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);
        let d_v  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, d);
        let rows_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, rows);
        let d_f  = self.builder.ins().f32const(d as f32);
        let fzero = self.builder.ins().f32const(0.0_f32);

        // Zero-fill dgain (accumulated across rows).
        let z_hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let z_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let z_exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(z_hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(z_hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(z_hdr);
        let zk = self.builder.block_params(z_hdr)[0];
        let zc = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, zk, d_v);
        self.brif(zc, z_body, z_exit);
        self.enter(z_body);
        let zoff = self.builder.ins().imul(zk, eb);
        self.tensor_store_elem(dgain, zoff, fzero);
        let zkn = self.builder.ins().iadd(zk, one);
        self.jump(z_hdr, &[zkn]);
        self.builder.seal_block(z_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(z_hdr);
        self.enter(z_exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(z_exit);

        // Outer loop over rows.
        let r_hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let r_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let r_exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(r_hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(r_hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(r_hdr);
        let r = self.builder.block_params(r_hdr)[0];
        let cont_r = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, r, rows_v);
        self.brif(cont_r, r_body, r_exit);

        self.enter(r_body);
        let base_e = self.builder.ins().imul(r, d_v);

        // Pass A: sumsq = Σ x², S = Σ g·gain·x  (two accumulators on the header).
        let a_hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let a_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let a_exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(a_hdr, cl::I64);
        self.builder.append_block_param(a_hdr, cl::F32);   // sumsq
        self.builder.append_block_param(a_hdr, cl::F32);   // S
        self.builder.append_block_param(a_exit, cl::F32);
        self.builder.append_block_param(a_exit, cl::F32);
        self.jump(a_hdr, &[zero, fzero, fzero]);
        self.enter(a_hdr);
        let ak = self.builder.block_params(a_hdr)[0];
        let sumsq = self.builder.block_params(a_hdr)[1];
        let sacc  = self.builder.block_params(a_hdr)[2];
        let cont_a = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, ak, d_v);
        self.builder.ins().brif(cont_a, a_body, &[], a_exit, &[sumsq.into(), sacc.into()]);
        self.block_filled = true;
        self.enter(a_body);
        let elem_a = self.builder.ins().iadd(base_e, ak);
        let xoff_a = self.builder.ins().imul(elem_a, eb);
        let goff_a = self.builder.ins().imul(ak, eb);
        let xv_a = self.tensor_load_elem(x, xoff_a, ScalarKind::F32);
        let gv_a = self.tensor_load_elem(g, xoff_a, ScalarKind::F32);
        let gk_a = self.tensor_load_elem(gain, goff_a, ScalarKind::F32);
        let sq   = self.builder.ins().fmul(xv_a, xv_a);
        let sumsq2 = self.builder.ins().fadd(sumsq, sq);
        let ggx  = self.builder.ins().fmul(gv_a, gk_a);
        let ggx2 = self.builder.ins().fmul(ggx, xv_a);
        let sacc2 = self.builder.ins().fadd(sacc, ggx2);
        let akn = self.builder.ins().iadd(ak, one);
        self.jump(a_hdr, &[akn, sumsq2, sacc2]);
        self.builder.seal_block(a_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(a_hdr);
        self.enter(a_exit);
        let sumsq_f = self.builder.block_params(a_exit)[0];
        let s_f     = self.builder.block_params(a_exit)[1];
        self.builder.seal_block(a_exit);

        // r = sqrt(sumsq/D + eps) — same as the forward.
        let ms = self.builder.ins().fdiv(sumsq_f, d_f);
        let ms_eps = self.builder.ins().fadd(ms, eps);
        let rr = self.call_f32_math("__dmc_sqrt_f32", ms_eps);
        let rr3 = { let r2 = self.builder.ins().fmul(rr, rr); self.builder.ins().fmul(r2, rr) };
        let d_rr3 = self.builder.ins().fmul(d_f, rr3);

        // Pass B: dx and dgain.
        let b_hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let b_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let b_exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(b_hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(b_hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(b_hdr);
        let bk = self.builder.block_params(b_hdr)[0];
        let cont_b = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, bk, d_v);
        self.brif(cont_b, b_body, b_exit);
        self.enter(b_body);
        let elem_b = self.builder.ins().iadd(base_e, bk);
        let xoff_b = self.builder.ins().imul(elem_b, eb);
        let goff_b = self.builder.ins().imul(bk, eb);
        let xv_b = self.tensor_load_elem(x, xoff_b, ScalarKind::F32);
        let gv_b = self.tensor_load_elem(g, xoff_b, ScalarKind::F32);
        let gk_b = self.tensor_load_elem(gain, goff_b, ScalarKind::F32);
        // dx = g·gain/r − x·S/(D·r³)
        let t1 = { let ggk = self.builder.ins().fmul(gv_b, gk_b); self.builder.ins().fdiv(ggk, rr) };
        let t2 = { let xs = self.builder.ins().fmul(xv_b, s_f); self.builder.ins().fdiv(xs, d_rr3) };
        let dxk = self.builder.ins().fsub(t1, t2);
        self.tensor_store_elem(dx, xoff_b, dxk);
        // dgain[k] += g·x/r
        let gx = self.builder.ins().fmul(gv_b, xv_b);
        let contrib = self.builder.ins().fdiv(gx, rr);
        let old = self.tensor_load_elem(dgain, goff_b, ScalarKind::F32);
        let newg = self.builder.ins().fadd(old, contrib);
        self.tensor_store_elem(dgain, goff_b, newg);
        let bkn = self.builder.ins().iadd(bk, one);
        self.jump(b_hdr, &[bkn]);
        self.builder.seal_block(b_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(b_hdr);
        self.enter(b_exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(b_exit);

        // Next row.
        let rn = self.builder.ins().iadd(r, one);
        self.jump(r_hdr, &[rn]);
        self.builder.seal_block(r_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(r_hdr);
        self.enter(r_exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(r_exit);
        (dx, dgain)
    }

    /// Reverse-mode VJP for `layer_norm(x, gain, bias, eps)` over the last axis
    /// (#368). `g` is the incoming adjoint ∂L/∂y. Per row, with x̂=(x−μ)/std and
    /// dx̂=g·gain:
    ///     dx_k     = (dx̂_k − mean(dx̂) − x̂_k·mean(dx̂·x̂)) / std
    ///     dgain_k += g_k·x̂_k      dbias_k += g_k
    /// mean/std are recomputed from x (matching the forward). Returns
    /// (dx, dgain, dbias); dgain/dbias are rank-1 `[D]` accumulated across rows.
    fn tensor_layer_norm_backward(
        &mut self, g: Value, x: Value, gain: Value, t: &TensorTy, eps: Value,
    ) -> (Value, Value, Value) {
        let d    = t.shape[t.rank() - 1];
        let rows = t.nelems() / d;
        let dx    = self.forge_alloc(t.nbytes());
        let vec_ty = TensorTy { elem: ScalarKind::F32, shape: vec![d] };
        let dgain = self.forge_alloc(vec_ty.nbytes());
        let dbias = self.forge_alloc(vec_ty.nbytes());
        let zero = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let eb   = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);
        let d_v  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, d);
        let rows_v = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, rows);
        let d_f  = self.builder.ins().f32const(d as f32);
        let fzero = self.builder.ins().f32const(0.0_f32);

        // Zero-fill dgain and dbias (accumulated across rows).
        let z_hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let z_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let z_exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(z_hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(z_hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(z_hdr);
        let zk = self.builder.block_params(z_hdr)[0];
        let zc = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, zk, d_v);
        self.brif(zc, z_body, z_exit);
        self.enter(z_body);
        let zoff = self.builder.ins().imul(zk, eb);
        self.tensor_store_elem(dgain, zoff, fzero);
        self.tensor_store_elem(dbias, zoff, fzero);
        let zkn = self.builder.ins().iadd(zk, one);
        self.jump(z_hdr, &[zkn]);
        self.builder.seal_block(z_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(z_hdr);
        self.enter(z_exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(z_exit);

        // Outer loop over rows.
        let r_hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let r_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let r_exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(r_hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(r_hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(r_hdr);
        let r = self.builder.block_params(r_hdr)[0];
        let cont_r = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, r, rows_v);
        self.brif(cont_r, r_body, r_exit);

        self.enter(r_body);
        let base_e = self.builder.ins().imul(r, d_v);

        // Pass A: mean and inv_std via the shared centered two-pass (matches the
        // forward, so recomputed std is bit-identical).
        let (mean, inv_std) = self.layer_norm_row_stats(x, base_e, d, eps);

        // Pass B: a = Σ dx̂,  bsum = Σ dx̂·x̂  (dx̂ = g·gain, x̂ = (x−μ)·inv_std).
        let b_hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let b_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let b_exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(b_hdr, cl::I64);
        self.builder.append_block_param(b_hdr, cl::F32);   // a
        self.builder.append_block_param(b_hdr, cl::F32);   // bsum
        self.builder.append_block_param(b_exit, cl::F32);
        self.builder.append_block_param(b_exit, cl::F32);
        self.jump(b_hdr, &[zero, fzero, fzero]);
        self.enter(b_hdr);
        let bk = self.builder.block_params(b_hdr)[0];
        let aacc = self.builder.block_params(b_hdr)[1];
        let bacc = self.builder.block_params(b_hdr)[2];
        let cont_b = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, bk, d_v);
        self.builder.ins().brif(cont_b, b_body, &[], b_exit, &[aacc.into(), bacc.into()]);
        self.block_filled = true;
        self.enter(b_body);
        let elem_b = self.builder.ins().iadd(base_e, bk);
        let xoff_b = self.builder.ins().imul(elem_b, eb);
        let goff_b = self.builder.ins().imul(bk, eb);
        let xv_b = self.tensor_load_elem(x, xoff_b, ScalarKind::F32);
        let gv_b = self.tensor_load_elem(g, xoff_b, ScalarKind::F32);
        let gk_b = self.tensor_load_elem(gain, goff_b, ScalarKind::F32);
        let cen_b = self.builder.ins().fsub(xv_b, mean);
        let xhat_b = self.builder.ins().fmul(cen_b, inv_std);
        let dxhat_b = self.builder.ins().fmul(gv_b, gk_b);
        let a_n = self.builder.ins().fadd(aacc, dxhat_b);
        let dxx = self.builder.ins().fmul(dxhat_b, xhat_b);
        let b_n = self.builder.ins().fadd(bacc, dxx);
        let bkn = self.builder.ins().iadd(bk, one);
        self.jump(b_hdr, &[bkn, a_n, b_n]);
        self.builder.seal_block(b_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(b_hdr);
        self.enter(b_exit);
        let a_sum = self.builder.block_params(b_exit)[0];
        let bsum  = self.builder.block_params(b_exit)[1];
        self.builder.seal_block(b_exit);
        let a_mean = self.builder.ins().fdiv(a_sum, d_f);
        let b_mean = self.builder.ins().fdiv(bsum, d_f);

        // Pass C: dx, dgain, dbias.
        let c_hdr = self.builder.create_block();
        let c_body = self.builder.create_block();
        let c_exit = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(c_hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(c_hdr, &[zero]);
        self.enter(c_hdr);
        let ck = self.builder.block_params(c_hdr)[0];
        let cont_c = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, ck, d_v);
        self.brif(cont_c, c_body, c_exit);
        self.enter(c_body);
        let elem_c = self.builder.ins().iadd(base_e, ck);
        let xoff_c = self.builder.ins().imul(elem_c, eb);
        let goff_c = self.builder.ins().imul(ck, eb);
        let xv_c = self.tensor_load_elem(x, xoff_c, ScalarKind::F32);
        let gv_c = self.tensor_load_elem(g, xoff_c, ScalarKind::F32);
        let gk_c = self.tensor_load_elem(gain, goff_c, ScalarKind::F32);
        let cen_c = self.builder.ins().fsub(xv_c, mean);
        let xhat_c = self.builder.ins().fmul(cen_c, inv_std);
        let dxhat_c = self.builder.ins().fmul(gv_c, gk_c);
        // dx = (dx̂ − mean(dx̂) − x̂·mean(dx̂·x̂)) · inv_std
        let t1 = self.builder.ins().fsub(dxhat_c, a_mean);
        let xb = self.builder.ins().fmul(xhat_c, b_mean);
        let t2 = self.builder.ins().fsub(t1, xb);
        let dxk = self.builder.ins().fmul(t2, inv_std);
        self.tensor_store_elem(dx, xoff_c, dxk);
        // dgain[k] += g·x̂ ;  dbias[k] += g
        let gx = self.builder.ins().fmul(gv_c, xhat_c);
        let old_g = self.tensor_load_elem(dgain, goff_c, ScalarKind::F32);
        let new_g = self.builder.ins().fadd(old_g, gx);
        self.tensor_store_elem(dgain, goff_c, new_g);
        let old_b = self.tensor_load_elem(dbias, goff_c, ScalarKind::F32);
        let new_b = self.builder.ins().fadd(old_b, gv_c);
        self.tensor_store_elem(dbias, goff_c, new_b);
        let ckn = self.builder.ins().iadd(ck, one);
        self.jump(c_hdr, &[ckn]);
        self.builder.seal_block(c_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(c_hdr);
        self.enter(c_exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(c_exit);

        // Next row.
        let rn = self.builder.ins().iadd(r, one);
        self.jump(r_hdr, &[rn]);
        self.builder.seal_block(r_body);
        self.builder.seal_block(r_hdr);
        self.enter(r_exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(r_exit);
        (dx, dgain, dbias)
    }

    /// Elementwise tanh backward: out[i] = adj[i] * (1 - fwd[i]^2).
    fn tensor_tanh_backward(&mut self, adj: Value, fwd_out: Value, t: &TensorTy) -> Value {
        let out    = self.forge_alloc(t.nbytes());
        let n      = t.nelems();
        let zero_i = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one_i  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let cap    = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, n);
        let eb     = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);
        let fone   = self.builder.ins().f32const(1.0_f32);
        let hdr    = self.builder.create_block();
        let body   = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit   = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(hdr, &[zero_i]);
        self.enter(hdr);
        let i    = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
        let cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, i, cap);
        self.brif(cont, body, exit);
        self.enter(body);
        let off  = self.builder.ins().imul(i, eb);
        let tv   = self.tensor_load_elem(fwd_out, off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let gv   = self.tensor_load_elem(adj, off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let t2   = self.builder.ins().fmul(tv, tv);
        let dt   = self.builder.ins().fsub(fone, t2);
        let ov   = self.builder.ins().fmul(gv, dt);
        self.tensor_store_elem(out, off, ov);
        let inext = self.builder.ins().iadd(i, one_i);
        self.jump(hdr, &[inext]);
        self.builder.seal_block(body);
        self.builder.seal_block(hdr);
        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);
        out
    }

    /// Elementwise sigmoid backward: out[i] = adj[i] * fwd[i] * (1 - fwd[i]).
    fn tensor_sigmoid_backward(&mut self, adj: Value, fwd_out: Value, t: &TensorTy) -> Value {
        let out    = self.forge_alloc(t.nbytes());
        let n      = t.nelems();
        let zero_i = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one_i  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let cap    = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, n);
        let eb     = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);
        let fone   = self.builder.ins().f32const(1.0_f32);
        let hdr    = self.builder.create_block();
        let body   = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit   = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(hdr, &[zero_i]);
        self.enter(hdr);
        let i    = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
        let cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, i, cap);
        self.brif(cont, body, exit);
        self.enter(body);
        let off  = self.builder.ins().imul(i, eb);
        let sv   = self.tensor_load_elem(fwd_out, off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let gv   = self.tensor_load_elem(adj, off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let om   = self.builder.ins().fsub(fone, sv);
        let ds   = self.builder.ins().fmul(sv, om);
        let ov   = self.builder.ins().fmul(gv, ds);
        self.tensor_store_elem(out, off, ov);
        let inext = self.builder.ins().iadd(i, one_i);
        self.jump(hdr, &[inext]);
        self.builder.seal_block(body);
        self.builder.seal_block(hdr);
        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);
        out
    }

    /// Elementwise GELU backward using input x (stored in aux).
    /// dgelu/dx = 0.5*(1+t) + 0.5*x*(1-t^2)*c*(1+3*k*x^2),
    /// where t = tanh(c*(x + k*x^3)), c = sqrt(2/pi), k = 0.044715.
    fn tensor_gelu_backward(&mut self, adj: Value, inp: Value, t_shape: &TensorTy) -> Value {
        let out    = self.forge_alloc(t_shape.nbytes());
        let n      = t_shape.nelems();
        let zero_i = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one_i  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let cap    = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, n);
        let eb     = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);
        let c_f32  = (2.0f64 / std::f64::consts::PI).sqrt() as f32;
        let c_val  = self.builder.ins().f32const(c_f32);
        let k_val  = self.builder.ins().f32const(0.044715_f32);
        let f1     = self.builder.ins().f32const(1.0_f32);
        let fhalf  = self.builder.ins().f32const(0.5_f32);
        let f3     = self.builder.ins().f32const(3.0_f32);
        let hdr    = self.builder.create_block();
        let body   = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit   = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(hdr, &[zero_i]);
        self.enter(hdr);
        let i    = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
        let cont = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, i, cap);
        self.brif(cont, body, exit);
        self.enter(body);
        let off    = self.builder.ins().imul(i, eb);
        let x      = self.tensor_load_elem(inp, off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let g      = self.tensor_load_elem(adj, off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let x2     = self.builder.ins().fmul(x, x);
        let x3     = self.builder.ins().fmul(x2, x);
        let kx3    = self.builder.ins().fmul(k_val, x3);
        let xpkx3  = self.builder.ins().fadd(x, kx3);
        let inner  = self.builder.ins().fmul(c_val, xpkx3);
        let t      = self.call_f32_math("__dmc_tanh_f32", inner);
        let t2     = self.builder.ins().fmul(t, t);
        let dt     = self.builder.ins().fsub(f1, t2);
        let one_pt = self.builder.ins().fadd(f1, t);
        let lhs    = self.builder.ins().fmul(fhalf, one_pt);
        let kx2    = self.builder.ins().fmul(k_val, x2);
        let tkx2   = self.builder.ins().fmul(f3, kx2);
        let inner2 = self.builder.ins().fadd(f1, tkx2);
        let rhs    = self.builder.ins().fmul(fhalf, x);
        let rhs2   = self.builder.ins().fmul(rhs, dt);
        let rhs3   = self.builder.ins().fmul(rhs2, c_val);
        let rhs4   = self.builder.ins().fmul(rhs3, inner2);
        let dg     = self.builder.ins().fadd(lhs, rhs4);
        let ov     = self.builder.ins().fmul(g, dg);
        self.tensor_store_elem(out, off, ov);
        let inext  = self.builder.ins().iadd(i, one_i);
        self.jump(hdr, &[inext]);
        self.builder.seal_block(body);
        self.builder.seal_block(hdr);
        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);
        out
    }

    /// gelu''(x) = c*(1-t²) * [(1+3*k*x²)*(1 - t*x*c*(1+3*k*x²)) + 3*k*x²]
    /// where t = tanh(c*(x+k*x³)), c=sqrt(2/π), k=0.044715.
    /// gelu'(x) = 0.5*(1+t) + 0.5*x*(1-t²)*c*(1+3*k*x²)
    /// where t = tanh(c*(x+k*x³)), c=sqrt(2/π), k=0.044715.
    /// Used as the Phase-2 tape forward value for `GeluFirstDeriv` nodes so
    /// that emit_backward can differentiate through it to get gelu''(x).
    fn tensor_gelu_first_deriv(&mut self, inp: Value, t_shape: &TensorTy) -> Value {
        let out    = self.forge_alloc(t_shape.nbytes());
        let n      = t_shape.nelems();
        let zero_i = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one_i  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let cap    = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, n);
        let eb     = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);
        let c_f32  = (2.0f64 / std::f64::consts::PI).sqrt() as f32;
        let c_val  = self.builder.ins().f32const(c_f32);
        let k_val  = self.builder.ins().f32const(0.044715_f32);
        let f1     = self.builder.ins().f32const(1.0_f32);
        let f3k    = self.builder.ins().f32const(3.0_f32 * 0.044715_f32);
        let half   = self.builder.ins().f32const(0.5_f32);
        let hdr    = self.builder.create_block();
        let body   = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit   = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(hdr, &[zero_i]);
        self.enter(hdr);
        let i      = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
        let cont   = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, i, cap);
        self.brif(cont, body, exit);
        self.enter(body);
        let off    = self.builder.ins().imul(i, eb);
        let x      = self.tensor_load_elem(inp, off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let x2     = self.builder.ins().fmul(x, x);                   // x²
        let x3     = self.builder.ins().fmul(x2, x);                  // x³
        let kx3    = self.builder.ins().fmul(k_val, x3);              // k*x³
        let xpkx3  = self.builder.ins().fadd(x, kx3);                 // x + k*x³
        let u      = self.builder.ins().fmul(c_val, xpkx3);           // c*(x+k*x³)
        let t      = self.call_f32_math("__dmc_tanh_f32", u);         // tanh(u)
        let t2     = self.builder.ins().fmul(t, t);                   // t²
        let sech2  = self.builder.ins().fsub(f1, t2);                 // 1-t²
        let f3kx2  = self.builder.ins().fmul(f3k, x2);                // 3k*x²
        let one_3kx2 = self.builder.ins().fadd(f1, f3kx2);            // 1+3k*x²
        // term1 = 0.5*(1+t)
        let one_pt = self.builder.ins().fadd(f1, t);                  // 1+t
        let term1  = self.builder.ins().fmul(half, one_pt);           // 0.5*(1+t)
        // term2 = 0.5*x*sech²*c*(1+3k*x²)
        let half_x = self.builder.ins().fmul(half, x);                // 0.5*x
        let sc     = self.builder.ins().fmul(sech2, c_val);           // sech²*c
        let sc3k   = self.builder.ins().fmul(sc, one_3kx2);           // sech²*c*(1+3k*x²)
        let term2  = self.builder.ins().fmul(half_x, sc3k);           // 0.5*x*sech²*c*(1+3k*x²)
        let gelu_d = self.builder.ins().fadd(term1, term2);           // gelu'(x)
        self.tensor_store_elem(out, off, gelu_d);
        let inext  = self.builder.ins().iadd(i, one_i);
        self.jump(hdr, &[inext]);
        self.builder.seal_block(body);
        self.builder.seal_block(hdr);
        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);
        out
    }

    fn tensor_gelu_second_deriv(&mut self, inp: Value, t_shape: &TensorTy) -> Value {
        let out    = self.forge_alloc(t_shape.nbytes());
        let n      = t_shape.nelems();
        let zero_i = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
        let one_i  = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1);
        let cap    = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, n);
        let eb     = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 4);
        let c_f32  = (2.0f64 / std::f64::consts::PI).sqrt() as f32;
        let c_val  = self.builder.ins().f32const(c_f32);
        let k_val  = self.builder.ins().f32const(0.044715_f32);
        let f1     = self.builder.ins().f32const(1.0_f32);
        let f3k    = self.builder.ins().f32const(3.0_f32 * 0.044715_f32);
        let hdr    = self.builder.create_block();
        let body   = self.builder.create_block();
        let exit   = self.builder.create_block();
        self.builder.append_block_param(hdr, cl::I64);
        self.jump(hdr, &[zero_i]);
        self.enter(hdr);
        let i      = self.builder.block_params(hdr)[0];
        let cont   = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, i, cap);
        self.brif(cont, body, exit);
        self.enter(body);
        let off    = self.builder.ins().imul(i, eb);
        let x      = self.tensor_load_elem(inp, off, ScalarKind::F32);
        let x2     = self.builder.ins().fmul(x, x);
        let x3     = self.builder.ins().fmul(x2, x);
        let kx3    = self.builder.ins().fmul(k_val, x3);
        let xpkx3  = self.builder.ins().fadd(x, kx3);
        let u      = self.builder.ins().fmul(c_val, xpkx3);
        let t      = self.call_f32_math("__dmc_tanh_f32", u);
        let t2     = self.builder.ins().fmul(t, t);
        let sech2  = self.builder.ins().fsub(f1, t2);       // 1 - t²
        let f3kx2  = self.builder.ins().fmul(f3k, x2);      // 3*k*x²
        let one_3kx2 = self.builder.ins().fadd(f1, f3kx2);  // 1 + 3*k*x²
        let tx     = self.builder.ins().fmul(t, x);
        let c_one_3kx2 = self.builder.ins().fmul(c_val, one_3kx2); // c*(1+3*k*x²)
        let txck   = self.builder.ins().fmul(tx, c_one_3kx2);      // t*x*c*(1+3*k*x²)
        let inner  = self.builder.ins().fsub(f1, txck);             // 1 - t*x*c*(1+3*k*x²)
        let term1  = self.builder.ins().fmul(one_3kx2, inner);      // (1+3*k*x²)*inner
        let bracket = self.builder.ins().fadd(term1, f3kx2);        // term1 + 3*k*x²
        let c_sech2 = self.builder.ins().fmul(c_val, sech2);        // c*(1-t²)
        let gelu_dd = self.builder.ins().fmul(c_sech2, bracket);
        self.tensor_store_elem(out, off, gelu_dd);
        let inext  = self.builder.ins().iadd(i, one_i);
        self.jump(hdr, &[inext]);
        self.builder.seal_block(body);
        self.builder.seal_block(hdr);
        self.enter(exit);
        self.builder.seal_block(exit);
        out
    }

    /// Cast `v` from `from` to `to`. Only scalar conversions are legal. A
    /// tensor-to-tensor coercion is identity if the types match exactly,
    /// error otherwise.
    /// #324: upconvert a Bf16Tensor value (i64 ptr to 2-byte bf16 weights) to a
    /// fresh f32 `Tensor` for non-matmul consumers (embed source, rms_norm
    /// weight, transposed lm-head). Bit-identical to the old load-time widen.
    fn bf16_upconvert(&mut self, v: Value, bt: &Bf16TensorTy) -> (Value, TyKind) {
        let n = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, bt.nelems());
        let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_bf16_upconvert")
            .expect("__dmc_bf16_upconvert not registered").clone();
        let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
        let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[v, n]);
        let ptr = self.builder.inst_results(call)[0];
        (ptr, TyKind::Tensor(TensorTy { elem: ScalarKind::F32, shape: bt.shape.clone() }))
    }

    fn coerce_to(
        &mut self,
        v: Value,
        from: &TyKind,
        to: &TyKind,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<Value, JitError> {
        if from == to { return Ok(v); }
        // A maybe-nil `map_get` result coerced to anything concrete: decode it
        // (trapping on nil) then coerce the i64 payload onward. map_get is
        // dynamically typed (Unknown), so it flows into i64, fn-pointer, and
        // tensor-pointer positions — all i64-backed (#300.4).
        if matches!(from, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::OptI64))
            && !matches!(to, TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::OptI64)) {
            let i = self.opt_unwrap_or_trap(v);
            return self.coerce_to(i, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), to, span);
        }
        match (from, to) {
            (TyKind::Scalar(f), TyKind::Scalar(t)) => self.coerce_scalar(v, *f, *t, span),
            // Tensor values in JIT IR are I64 data pointers — passing a tensor
            // where *T is expected (extern fn boundary) is a zero-cost bitcast.
            (TyKind::Tensor(_), TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)) => Ok(v),
            // Passing an I64 opaque pointer where a Tensor field is expected —
            // allows `field: 0` or raw-pointer initialisation in model literals
            // (backwards compatible with pre-#179 code that typed exotic fields as I64).
            (TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), TyKind::Tensor(_)) => Ok(v),
            // #324: Bf16Tensor is likewise an i64 data pointer. A bf16 weight
            // field whose shape is symbolic at layout time resolves to opaque i64
            // (see lower_ty_for_model), so the constructor store (Bf16Tensor→i64)
            // and the access-time re-resolution (i64→Bf16Tensor) are pointer
            // no-ops, exactly like the Tensor arms above.
            (TyKind::Bf16Tensor(_), TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)) => Ok(v),
            (TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), TyKind::Bf16Tensor(_)) => Ok(v),
            // Two Bf16Tensor types with the same shape (or one symbolic) — pointer pass.
            (TyKind::Bf16Tensor(f), TyKind::Bf16Tensor(t))
                if f.shape == t.shape || f.shape.is_empty() || t.shape.is_empty() => Ok(v),
            // #324: an f32 tensor initializing a bf16 weight field — down-convert
            // to 2-byte bf16 storage (the general `Tensor[bf16]`-field case; Qwen
            // weights instead arrive pre-bf16 from load_npz).
            (TyKind::Tensor(ft), TyKind::Bf16Tensor(tt)) if ft.elem == ScalarKind::F32 => {
                let n = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, tt.nelems());
                let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_f32_to_bf16")
                    .expect("__dmc_f32_to_bf16 not registered").clone();
                let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[v, n]);
                Ok(self.builder.inst_results(call)[0])
            }
            // KV → KV: identical except for the compile-time-known capacity,
            // which is purely a runtime header field. Passing a constructed KV
            // (cap known) into a `KV` parameter (cap unknown) is a no-op on the
            // header pointer, provided element type, dims, and stream axis match.
            (TyKind::KV(f), TyKind::KV(t))
                if f.elem == t.elem && f.dims == t.dims && f.stream_axis == t.stream_axis => Ok(v),
            // KvArray → KvArray: same structural check (cap may differ between
            // a constructed literal and the callee's parameter annotation).
            (TyKind::KvArray(fkv, fn_), TyKind::KvArray(tkv, tn_))
                if fn_ == tn_
                && fkv.elem == tkv.elem
                && fkv.dims == tkv.dims
                && fkv.stream_axis == tkv.stream_axis => Ok(v),
            // ModelArray -> ModelArray: name and count must match exactly.
            (TyKind::ModelArray(fname, fn_, _), TyKind::ModelArray(tname, tn_, _))
                if fname == tname && fn_ == tn_ => Ok(v),
            // #350: enums are i64 ordinals. `l as i64` reads the ordinal (a
            // no-op on the value), and an i64 flows into an enum-typed slot
            // (e.g. an explicit `n as Light`) unchanged. Same-enum is the
            // `from == to` identity handled above; distinct enums never unify.
            // #350 Part 2b: a payload enum value is a pointer — `as i64` reads
            // the tag from slot 0. A tag-only enum value already *is* its ordinal.
            (TyKind::Enum(name), TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)) => {
                if self.enum_payload_layouts.contains_key(name) {
                    Ok(self.load_enum_tag(v))
                } else {
                    Ok(v)
                }
            }
            (TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), TyKind::Enum(_)) => Ok(v),
            // Model -> Model: model instances are i64 pointers whose layout is
            // keyed by name (see model_layouts). A param-shaped model field
            // (`inner: Inner[N]`) may resolve with unresolved/empty dims while
            // the value (e.g. a model-array element read) carries concrete dims;
            // both denote the same model with the same pointer layout, so a name
            // match is a no-op pointer pass. (Mirrors ModelArray above — #273.)
            (TyKind::Model(fname, _), TyKind::Model(tname, _))
                if fname == tname => Ok(v),
            // Fn → Fn: function pointers are opaque i64; allow structural match
            // (same param count/kinds and return kind).
            (TyKind::Fn(fp, fr), TyKind::Fn(tp, tr)) if fp.len() == tp.len() => {
                // Parameters and return type are pointer-sized (all i64 in practice).
                let _ = (fp, fr, tp, tr);  // structural check above is sufficient
                Ok(v)
            }
            // Fn → i64: a function pointer is already an i64 code address; allow
            // passing a fn-typed value where i64 is expected (e.g., map_set).
            (TyKind::Fn(_, _), TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64)) => Ok(v),
            // i64 → Fn: treat an opaque i64 (e.g., from map_get) as a function
            // pointer when the target type is explicitly annotated as fn(...).
            (TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), TyKind::Fn(_, _)) => Ok(v),
            // `b as str` — a bool renders as "true"/"false" (matching the
            // interpreter's Display for Value::Bool), NOT the "1"/"0" that
            // __dmc_str_from_int would give. Widen the cl::I8 bool to the i64 the
            // builtin takes (via coerce_scalar, like the int path) and select the
            // literal text. Must precede the generic int arm below.
            (TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::Bool), TyKind::Str) => {
                let b64 = self.coerce_scalar(v, ScalarKind::Bool, ScalarKind::I64, span)?;
                let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_str_from_bool")
                    .expect("__dmc_str_from_bool not registered").clone();
                let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[b64]);
                Ok(self.builder.inst_results(call)[0])
            }
            // `x as str` for a float — render the fractional value, NOT the
            // integer truncation the generic int arm below would produce by
            // coercing through `__dmc_str_from_int`. An f32 is widened to f64
            // first and formatted at 64-bit width, matching the interpreter,
            // which stores every scalar as f64 and renders via `format!("{}", x)`
            // — so a narrowed f32 shows the same f64 expansion in both backends
            // (e.g. `(0.1 as f32) as str` → "0.10000000149011612" in both).
            (TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F32), TyKind::Str) => {
                let widened = self.builder.ins().fpromote(cl::F64, v);
                let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_str_from_f64")
                    .expect("__dmc_str_from_f64 not registered").clone();
                let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[widened]);
                Ok(self.builder.inst_results(call)[0])
            }
            (TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::F64), TyKind::Str) => {
                let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_str_from_f64")
                    .expect("__dmc_str_from_f64 not registered").clone();
                let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[v]);
                Ok(self.builder.inst_results(call)[0])
            }
            // `n as str` — convert any integer scalar to a forge string.
            (TyKind::Scalar(sk), TyKind::Str) => {
                let i64_v = if *sk == ScalarKind::I64 {
                    v
                } else {
                    self.coerce_scalar(v, *sk, ScalarKind::I64, span)?
                };
                let entry = self.fns.get("__dmc_str_from_int")
                    .expect("__dmc_str_from_int not registered").clone();
                let func_ref = self.module.declare_func_in_func(entry.id, self.builder.func);
                let call = self.builder.ins().call(func_ref, &[i64_v]);
                Ok(self.builder.inst_results(call)[0])
            }
            _ => err(span, format!(
                "cannot convert `{}` to `{}`", from.render(), to.render(),
            )),
        }
    }

    /// Cast a scalar to a narrow / unsigned integer type the JIT doesn't model
    /// as a `ScalarKind`, returning an i64-backed value that matches the
    /// interpreter's `apply_cast` (#298-adjacent). For an integer source this is
    /// a two's-complement reduce-then-(sign|zero)-extend; for a float source it
    /// saturates directly into the target width (so `300.0 as i8 == 127`, like
    /// Rust's `as`), then extends. `u64`/`int4`/`int8` carry no narrowing — the
    /// value is just the i64 bits.
    fn lower_narrow_int_cast(
        &mut self,
        v: Value,
        k: &TyKind,
        s: &ScalarType,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<Value, JitError> {
        // (target bit width, signed?) — None width means "no narrowing".
        let (bits, signed): (Option<u32>, bool) = match s {
            ScalarType::I8  => (Some(8),  true),
            ScalarType::I16 => (Some(16), true),
            ScalarType::U8  => (Some(8),  false),
            ScalarType::U16 => (Some(16), false),
            ScalarType::U32 => (Some(32), false),
            // u64 / int4 / int8: no narrowing, value is the i64 as-is.
            _ => (None, false),
        };
        let Some(bits) = bits else {
            // No narrowing (u64 / int4 / int8 / i64). For u64 from a float we
            // need *unsigned* saturation to the full u64 range (`-5.0 as u64`
            // == 0, `1e30 as u64` == u64::MAX); a signed convert would give -5
            // / i64::MAX. Everything else is the plain (signed) coercion.
            if matches!(s, ScalarType::U64) && matches!(k, TyKind::Scalar(sk) if sk.is_float()) {
                return Ok(self.builder.ins().fcvt_to_uint_sat(cl::I64, v));
            }
            return self.coerce_to(v, k, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span);
        };
        let src_is_float = matches!(k, TyKind::Scalar(sk) if sk.is_float());
        if src_is_float {
            // Cranelift's x64 backend can only saturate-convert a float to i32/
            // i64, not i8/i16. Every narrow target here maxes out below
            // i64::MAX, so saturate (signed) to i64 — even for unsigned targets,
            // since fcvt_to_uint_sat to i64 would wrap a huge float to -1 bits —
            // then clamp to the target's [lo, hi] (Rust `f as T` saturates too).
            let sat = self.builder.ins().fcvt_to_sint_sat(cl::I64, v);
            let (lo, hi) = if signed {
                (-(1i64 << (bits - 1)), (1i64 << (bits - 1)) - 1)
            } else {
                (0i64, (1i64 << bits) - 1)
            };
            let lo_c = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, lo);
            let hi_c = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, hi);
            let below = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedLessThan, sat, lo_c);
            let v1 = self.builder.ins().select(below, lo_c, sat);
            let above = self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::SignedGreaterThan, v1, hi_c);
            Ok(self.builder.ins().select(above, hi_c, v1))
        } else {
            // integer source: down to i64, then two's-complement reduce/re-widen.
            let wt = match bits { 8 => cl::I8, 16 => cl::I16, _ => cl::I32 };
            let i64v = self.coerce_to(v, k, &TyKind::Scalar(ScalarKind::I64), span)?;
            let narrowed = self.builder.ins().ireduce(wt, i64v);
            if signed {
                Ok(self.builder.ins().sextend(cl::I64, narrowed))
            } else {
                Ok(self.builder.ins().uextend(cl::I64, narrowed))
            }
        }
    }

    fn coerce_scalar(
        &mut self,
        v: Value,
        from: ScalarKind,
        to: ScalarKind,
        span: &Span,
    ) -> Result<Value, JitError> {
        if from == to { return Ok(v); }
        // OptI64 — a maybe-nil `map_get` result (#300.4). Using it as a concrete
        // value decodes the payload, trapping cleanly on nil (matches the interp's
        // nil-in-arithmetic error); the reverse packs an i64/nil into the I128.
        if from == ScalarKind::OptI64 {
            let i = self.opt_unwrap_or_trap(v);
            return self.coerce_scalar(i, ScalarKind::I64, to, span);
        }
        if to == ScalarKind::OptI64 {
            return match from {
                ScalarKind::I64 => { let one = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 1); Ok(self.pack_opt(one, v)) }
                ScalarKind::Nil => Ok(self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I128, 0)),
                _ => err(span, format!("cannot convert `{}` to a maybe-nil value", from.name())),
            };
        }
        // Allow only the explicit-cast set; SPEC.md §3.1 forbids implicit
        // numeric conversion, but `let x: i64 = 0` and `let x: f64 = 0`
        // would otherwise reject a literal default. Cast happens here only
        // when an annotation or callee signature demands it.
        let v = match (from, to) {
            // int widen / narrow
            (ScalarKind::I32, ScalarKind::I64) => self.builder.ins().sextend(cl::I64, v),
            (ScalarKind::I64, ScalarKind::I32) => self.builder.ins().ireduce(cl::I32, v),
            // int <-> float
            (k, ScalarKind::F32) if k.is_int() => self.builder.ins().fcvt_from_sint(cl::F32, v),
            (k, ScalarKind::F64) if k.is_int() => self.builder.ins().fcvt_from_sint(cl::F64, v),
            (ScalarKind::F32, ScalarKind::F64) => self.builder.ins().fpromote(cl::F64, v),
            (ScalarKind::F64, ScalarKind::F32) => self.builder.ins().fdemote(cl::F32, v),
            // #250: use the saturating variant so NaN→0, +inf→i64::MAX,
            // -inf→i64::MIN, out-of-range→clamp — matching Rust `as` semantics
            // used by the interpreter.  The plain `fcvt_to_sint` traps on
            // NaN/out-of-range (Cranelift UB), producing a bare SIGILL.
            (k, kk) if k.is_float() && kk.is_int() => {
                self.builder.ins().fcvt_to_sint_sat(kk.cl(), v)
            }
            // bool <-> int
            (ScalarKind::Bool, ScalarKind::I32) => self.builder.ins().uextend(cl::I32, v),
            (ScalarKind::Bool, ScalarKind::I64) => self.builder.ins().uextend(cl::I64, v),
            (ScalarKind::I32, ScalarKind::Bool) => {
                let z = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I32, 0);
                self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::NotEqual, v, z)
            }
            (ScalarKind::I64, ScalarKind::Bool) => {
                let z = self.builder.ins().iconst(cl::I64, 0);
                self.builder.ins().icmp(IntCC::NotEqual, v, z)
            }
            // nil is unit; coerce to/from anything is an error.
            _ => return err(span, format!(
                "cannot convert `{}` to `{}` (slice 1 cast set)", from.name(), to.name(),
            )),
        };
        Ok(v)
    }
}

fn int_cc(op: &BinOp) -> IntCC {
    match op {
        BinOp::Eq    => IntCC::Equal,
        BinOp::NotEq => IntCC::NotEqual,
        BinOp::Lt    => IntCC::SignedLessThan,
        BinOp::Gt    => IntCC::SignedGreaterThan,
        BinOp::LtEq  => IntCC::SignedLessThanOrEqual,
        BinOp::GtEq  => IntCC::SignedGreaterThanOrEqual,
        _ => unreachable!(),
    }
}

fn float_cc(op: &BinOp) -> FloatCC {
    match op {
        BinOp::Eq    => FloatCC::Equal,
        BinOp::NotEq => FloatCC::NotEqual,
        BinOp::Lt    => FloatCC::LessThan,
        BinOp::Gt    => FloatCC::GreaterThan,
        BinOp::LtEq  => FloatCC::LessThanOrEqual,
        BinOp::GtEq  => FloatCC::GreaterThanOrEqual,
        _ => unreachable!(),
    }
}

// ─── Builtins exposed as runtime symbols ─────────────────────────────────────

/// #259: Called by JIT-compiled code when a tensor index is out of bounds.
/// Prints a clean diagnostic matching the interpreter's message, then exits(1).
/// Declared `extern "C"` so Cranelift can call it as a C ABI function.
extern "C" fn dmc_oob_trap(idx: i64, dim: i64) -> ! {
    eprintln!("runtime error: index {} out of bounds for axis 0 of size {}", idx, dim);
    std::process::exit(1);
}

// #399: a `<-` stream append that would exceed the KV reservation. Prints a
// clean message + exit(1), matching the interpreter, instead of the bare
// Cranelift trap (silent SIGILL) the capacity guard used to raise.
extern "C" fn dmc_kv_cap_trap(len: i64, l_frames: i64, cap: i64) -> ! {
    eprintln!("runtime error: stream `<-` append exceeded declared capacity {} \
               ({} frame(s) written, appending {} more)", cap, len, l_frames);
    std::process::exit(1);
}

/// #265: called by JIT-compiled code when a *runtime* shift count is outside
/// `0..=63`. Prints the same message the interpreter raises (#215/#256) then
/// exits(1), so the JIT no longer silently wraps the count mod 64. `op_is_shl`
/// selects the `<<`/`>>` spelling to match the interpreter's diagnostic.
extern "C" fn dmc_shift_trap(count: i64, op_is_shl: i64) -> ! {
    let op = if op_is_shl != 0 { "<<" } else { ">>" };
    eprintln!("runtime error: {} shift amount {} out of range (expected 0..=63)", op, count);
    std::process::exit(1);
}

/// #297: called by JIT-compiled code on `INT_MIN / -1` (or `% -1`), the one
/// signed division that overflows i64 and would otherwise raise SIGFPE. Prints
/// the same overflow error the interpreter raises (#296), then exits(1).
extern "C" fn dmc_div_overflow_trap(l: i64, r: i64, op_is_div: i64) -> ! {
    let op = if op_is_div != 0 { "/" } else { "%" };
    eprintln!("runtime error: integer overflow: {} {} {} exceeds the i64 range", l, op, r);
    std::process::exit(1);
}

extern "C" fn builtin_print_i64(x: i64) { println!("{}", x); }
extern "C" fn builtin_print_f64(x: f64) { println!("{}", x); }
extern "C" fn builtin_print_bool(x: u8) { println!("{}", x != 0); }
extern "C" fn builtin_print_nil()       { println!("nil"); }

// Scalar math primitives wired as runtime symbols. Cranelift has no
// portable `exp` / `sqrt` instructions on every ISA, so we route through
// Rust's f32 intrinsics. The JIT exposes these as `exp(x)` and `sqrt(x)`
// on the demoniC source surface.
extern "C" fn builtin_exp_f32(x: f32) -> f32 { x.exp() }
extern "C" fn builtin_sqrt_f32(x: f32) -> f32 { x.sqrt() }
extern "C" fn builtin_log_f32(x: f32) -> f32 { x.ln() }   // natural log (matches interpreter `log`)
extern "C" fn builtin_sin_f32(x: f32) -> f32 { x.sin() }
extern "C" fn builtin_cos_f32(x: f32) -> f32 { x.cos() }
// #209: f64 scalar-math variants. Scalar `exp`/`sqrt`/`log`/`sin`/`cos` compute
// in f64 to match the interpreter; the f32 versions above stay for tensor
// kernels (softmax/rms_norm/…) that operate on f32 elements.
extern "C" fn builtin_exp_f64(x: f64) -> f64 { x.exp() }
extern "C" fn builtin_sqrt_f64(x: f64) -> f64 { x.sqrt() }
extern "C" fn builtin_log_f64(x: f64) -> f64 { x.ln() }
extern "C" fn builtin_sin_f64(x: f64) -> f64 { x.sin() }
extern "C" fn builtin_cos_f64(x: f64) -> f64 { x.cos() }
extern "C" fn builtin_tanh_f32(x: f32) -> f32 { x.tanh() }
extern "C" fn builtin_gelu_f32(x: f32) -> f32 {
    let c = 0.7978845608_f32; // sqrt(2/pi)
    0.5 * x * (1.0 + (c * (x + 0.044715 * x * x * x)).tanh())
}
extern "C" fn builtin_sigmoid_f32(x: f32) -> f32 { 1.0 / (1.0 + (-x).exp()) }
// silu(x) = x * sigmoid(x) = x / (1 + exp(-x))
extern "C" fn builtin_silu_f32(x: f32) -> f32 { x / (1.0 + (-x).exp()) }
// elu(x) (α=1) = x for x>0, e^x - 1 for x≤0.
extern "C" fn builtin_elu_f32(x: f32) -> f32 { if x > 0.0 { x } else { x.exp() - 1.0 } }
// mish(x) = x * tanh(softplus(x)); softplus stable = max(x,0) + ln(1 + e^-|x|).
// Matches interp's activation_f64/softplus_f64 so run/jit agree at f32.
extern "C" fn builtin_mish_f32(x: f32) -> f32 {
    let sp = x.max(0.0) + (-(x.abs())).exp().ln_1p();
    x * sp.tanh()
}
// First derivatives used by the JIT reverse-mode VJP for these activations
// (#377 follow-up). Each mirrors interp's activation_deriv_f64 so run/jit
// gradients agree at f32.
extern "C" fn builtin_silu_deriv_f32(x: f32) -> f32 {
    let s = 1.0 / (1.0 + (-x).exp());
    s * (1.0 + x * (1.0 - s))
}
extern "C" fn builtin_elu_deriv_f32(x: f32) -> f32 { if x > 0.0 { 1.0 } else { x.exp() } }
extern "C" fn builtin_mish_deriv_f32(x: f32) -> f32 {
    let sp = x.max(0.0) + (-(x.abs())).exp().ln_1p();
    let t = sp.tanh();
    let s = 1.0 / (1.0 + (-x).exp());
    t + x * (1.0 - t * t) * s
}
extern "C" fn builtin_powf_f32(b: f32, e: f32) -> f32 { b.powf(e) }
extern "C" fn builtin_powf_f64(b: f64, e: f64) -> f64 { b.powf(e) }
// #289: scalar float `%` — Rust `%` on floats is truncated fmod, matching
// the interpreter's apply_binop.
extern "C" fn builtin_fmod_f64(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { a % b }

// ─── Test-only C-ABI helpers for extern fn JIT tests ─────────────────────────
//
// These are #[no_mangle] so that the JIT module's dlsym-based import
// resolution can find them when the test binary is the host process.

#[cfg(test)]
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn dmc_test_add_f32(a: f32, b: f32) -> f32 { a + b }

#[cfg(test)]
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn dmc_test_scale_ptr(ptr: *const f32, n: i64, scale: f32) -> f32 {
    // Sum ptr[0..n] * scale — exercises pointer passing from a tensor.
    let mut acc = 0.0f32;
    for i in 0..(n as usize) {
        acc += unsafe { *ptr.add(i) } * scale;
    }
    acc
}

// ─── @grad runtime: capture the gradient of a `!W` param ──────────────────
//
// fwd_bwd returns only the f32 loss. Grad pointers are published via
// capture_grad into GRAD_SLOTS and retrieved in-JIT by take_grad_at_idx.
// The Rust test harness drains the slot via take_grads() after each call.

thread_local! {
    // HashMap: each capture_grad call overwrites the previous entry for that
    // param index, so repeated fwd_bwd calls in a loop always see fresh grads.
    // Value is (data_ptr, nbytes); nbytes drives the epilogue compaction and
    // is 0 for non-tensor gradients (nothing to relocate).
    static GRAD_SLOTS: std::cell::RefCell<std::collections::HashMap<usize, (i64, i64)>> =
        std::cell::RefCell::new(std::collections::HashMap::new());
}

extern "C" fn capture_grad(param_idx: i64, ptr: i64, nbytes: i64) {
    GRAD_SLOTS.with(|s| { s.borrow_mut().insert(param_idx as usize, (ptr, nbytes)); });
}

/// Read the captured gradient pointer for `param_idx` (latest value, no drain).
/// Called from within JIT code by `lower_fwd_bwd_destructure`.
extern "C" fn take_grad_at_idx(param_idx: i64) -> i64 {
    GRAD_SLOTS.with(|s| {
        s.borrow().get(&(param_idx as usize)).map(|&(p, _)| p).unwrap_or(0)
    })
}

/// AUTODIFF.md §3 activation lifetime, entry half: called first thing inside a
/// compiled `f$fwd_bwd` / `f$fwd_bwd_bwd`. Clears any stale grad slots (a prior
/// grad call's entries must not leak into this call's epilogue) and returns the
/// forge watermark the epilogue will restore to.
extern "C" fn grad_call_prologue() -> i64 {
    GRAD_SLOTS.with(|s| s.borrow_mut().clear());
    forge_snapshot()
}

/// AUTODIFF.md §3 activation lifetime, exit half: called just before a compiled
/// grad fn returns. Every activation the call allocated is reclaimed in one
/// cursor rewind; the published gradients are the sole survivors, compacted
/// down to the entry watermark so they stay VALID (never dangling) until the
/// caller's own restore/rewind discards them.
///
/// The bounce through Rust-heap temporaries is deliberate: grads and
/// activations interleave in the arena, and forge_alloc zeroes on allocation,
/// so an in-arena move could clobber a source buffer before it is copied.
extern "C" fn grad_call_epilogue(mark: i64) {
    // Deterministic order: relocate in ascending param index.
    let mut entries: Vec<(usize, i64, i64)> = GRAD_SLOTS.with(|s| {
        s.borrow().iter().map(|(&k, &(p, n))| (k, p, n)).collect()
    });
    entries.sort_by_key(|&(k, _, _)| k);

    let saved: Vec<(usize, Vec<u8>)> = entries.iter()
        .filter(|&&(_, p, n)| n > 0 && p != 0)
        .map(|&(k, p, n)| {
            let bytes = unsafe {
                std::slice::from_raw_parts(p as *const u8, n as usize).to_vec()
            };
            (k, bytes)
        })
        .collect();

    forge_restore(mark);

    for (k, bytes) in saved {
        let new_ptr = forge_alloc(bytes.len() as i64);
        unsafe {
            std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(
                bytes.as_ptr(), new_ptr as *mut u8, bytes.len());
        }
        GRAD_SLOTS.with(|s| {
            if let Some(slot) = s.borrow_mut().get_mut(&k) { slot.0 = new_ptr; }
        });
    }
}

/// Drain and return all gradient pointers captured by the most recent
/// `fwd_bwd` invocation. Each entry is `(mut_param_index, data_ptr)`.
/// Test-harness helper (the CLI reads grads through the compiled program).
#[cfg(test)]
pub fn take_grads() -> Vec<(usize, i64)> {
    GRAD_SLOTS.with(|s| {
        let mut map = s.borrow_mut();
        let mut result: Vec<(usize, i64)> = map.iter().map(|(&k, &(p, _))| (k, p)).collect();
        result.sort_by_key(|(k, _)| *k);
        map.clear();
        result
    })
}

// ─── Forge arena ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Slice 2 keeps the arena lifecycle deliberately simple: a single global
// bump allocator, never reset. Memory leaks at program end. Per-function
// or per-block lifetime tracking is a slice-3 concern; the spec wants
// Forge to reset on each "step" (MEMORY.md §1), and a proper
// implementation needs JIT-side mark/restore around every function frame.
// That'll land when tensors start escaping fn boundaries in non-trivial
// ways. For now, single-shot `dmc jit` runs don't care.

struct ForgeArena {
    /// Chain of backing buffers. We hand out pointers into these and never
    /// move a buffer once allocated, so handed-out pointers stay valid for
    /// the program's lifetime. When the active chunk can't satisfy a
    /// request we advance to (or push) the next chunk rather than growing
    /// the current `Vec` in place (which would reallocate and invalidate
    /// every outstanding pointer). #292.
    chunks: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
    /// Index of the active chunk in `chunks`.
    cur: usize,
    /// Bump offset within the active chunk.
    cursor: usize,
    /// Default size for freshly pushed chunks. A single allocation larger
    /// than this gets its own right-sized chunk instead.
    chunk_size: usize,
}

impl ForgeArena {
    const ALIGN: usize = 64; // matches MEMORY.md §1.2 max-SIMD alignment
    // 512 MiB per chunk. Sized so whole-frame workloads that allocate fresh
    // tensors every iteration of a march/step loop (e.g. the SDF raymarcher)
    // stay within a single chunk; larger workloads (e.g. a 36-layer
    // transformer forward, #292) transparently chain more chunks. Each chunk
    // is committed lazily by the OS on first touch.
    const DEFAULT_CHUNK: usize = 512 * 1024 * 1024;

    fn new() -> Self {
        Self::with_chunk_size(Self::DEFAULT_CHUNK)
    }

    /// Construct an arena whose default chunk size is `chunk_size`. The first
    /// chunk is allocated lazily on the first `alloc`, so an unused arena
    /// costs nothing. (Small `chunk_size` values are used by the unit tests
    /// to exercise chunk chaining cheaply.)
    fn with_chunk_size(chunk_size: usize) -> Self {
        ForgeArena { chunks: Vec::new(), cur: 0, cursor: 0, chunk_size }
    }

    #[inline]
    fn align_up(n: usize) -> usize {
        (n + Self::ALIGN - 1) & !(Self::ALIGN - 1)
    }

    /// Allocate a zeroed chunk of `sz` bytes. A normal-sized chunk takes the
    /// fast `vec![0u8; _]` path (lazily zero-committed by the OS). An oversized
    /// single allocation — a huge tensor whose bytes exceed `chunk_size` — is
    /// reserved fallibly so the process exits with a clean message instead of
    /// aborting or OOM-killing with no output (#368 follow-up). (On a
    /// memory-overcommit OS a request that exceeds RAM may still be reaped by
    /// the OOM-killer on first touch — that is an OS policy we can't intercept.)
    fn alloc_zeroed_chunk(sz: usize, chunk_size: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
        if sz <= chunk_size {
            return vec![0u8; sz];
        }
        let mut v: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
        if v.try_reserve_exact(sz).is_err() {
            eprintln!(
                "runtime error: forge could not allocate {:.1} GiB — tensor shape too large for available memory",
                sz as f64 / (1024.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0));
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
        v.resize(sz, 0u8);
        v
    }

    fn alloc(&mut self, nbytes: usize) -> *mut u8 {
        // `vec![0u8; N]` lowers to `alloc_zeroed`; on Linux that hands back
        // lazily-committed zero pages, so a chunk costs only the pages
        // actually touched.
        if self.chunks.is_empty() {
            let sz = self.chunk_size.max(Self::align_up(nbytes));
            self.chunks.push(Self::alloc_zeroed_chunk(sz, self.chunk_size));
        }
        loop {
            let aligned = Self::align_up(self.cursor);
            if aligned + nbytes <= self.chunks[self.cur].len() {
                let ptr = unsafe { self.chunks[self.cur].as_mut_ptr().add(aligned) };
                // Zero the region (MEMORY.md: zeros are normative for
                // `forge.zeros`). This also re-zeroes memory reused after a
                // `restore`, so `restore` itself need not scrub.
                unsafe { std::ptr::write_bytes(ptr, 0, nbytes); }
                self.cursor = aligned + nbytes;
                return ptr;
            }
            // Doesn't fit in the active chunk — advance to the next one,
            // pushing or right-sizing it as needed. The tail of the current
            // chunk is left unused; for the small-alloc steady state that
            // waste is at most one allocation's worth.
            self.cur += 1;
            self.cursor = 0;
            let need = Self::align_up(nbytes);
            if self.cur == self.chunks.len() {
                let sz = self.chunk_size.max(need);
                self.chunks.push(Self::alloc_zeroed_chunk(sz, self.chunk_size));
            } else if self.chunks[self.cur].len() < need {
                // A reused (above-cursor, hence free) chunk that is too small
                // for this allocation. Nothing points into it, so replacing
                // it is safe.
                let sz = self.chunk_size.max(need);
                self.chunks[self.cur] = Self::alloc_zeroed_chunk(sz, self.chunk_size);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Pack the current `(chunk, offset)` watermark into an opaque i64 mark.
    /// Use with `restore` to free all tensors allocated since the snapshot —
    /// the renderer's per-frame reset pattern. The offset occupies the low
    /// 48 bits (a chunk never exceeds that) and the chunk index the next 15.
    fn snapshot(&self) -> usize {
        (self.cur << 48) | self.cursor
    }

    /// Free all allocations made after `mark` was taken by resetting the
    /// bump watermark. Chunks beyond the mark keep their capacity (so a
    /// per-frame loop doesn't re-allocate the backing store every frame);
    /// their bytes are re-zeroed lazily on the next `alloc`.
    fn restore(&mut self, mark: usize) {
        let ci = mark >> 48;
        let off = mark & ((1usize << 48) - 1);
        assert!(
            ci < self.chunks.len() || (ci == 0 && off == 0),
            "forge restore: chunk {} out of range (have {} chunks) — \
             snapshot from a different arena?",
            ci, self.chunks.len(),
        );
        assert!(
            ci < self.cur || (ci == self.cur && off <= self.cursor),
            "forge restore: mark ({}, {}) is ahead of cursor ({}, {})",
            ci, off, self.cur, self.cursor,
        );
        self.cur = ci;
        self.cursor = off;
    }
}

// JIT-emitted code runs single-threaded on the thread that calls
// `run_main` / `fwd_bwd`, so the arena lives in thread-local storage with
// no lock on the hot path — one `RefCell` borrow + a bump. This removes a
// mutex acquire from every tensor allocation.
thread_local! {
    static FORGE: std::cell::RefCell<Option<ForgeArena>> =
        const { std::cell::RefCell::new(None) };
}

extern "C" fn forge_alloc(bytes: i64) -> i64 {
    // #292 diagnostic: set DMC_FORGE_TRACE=1 to log every allocation, or
    // DMC_FORGE_TRACE=<N> to log only allocations of at least N bytes. Helps
    // pin down oversize/mis-broadcast buffers in a real-model forward.
    if let Ok(v) = std::env::var("DMC_FORGE_TRACE") {
        let threshold: i64 = v.parse().unwrap_or(1).max(1);
        if bytes >= threshold {
            FORGE_ALLOC_SEQ.with(|s| {
                let n = s.get() + 1;
                s.set(n);
                eprintln!("[forge #{n}] alloc {bytes} bytes ({:.1} MiB)", bytes as f64 / (1024.0 * 1024.0));
            });
        }
    }
    FORGE.with(|cell| {
        let mut g = cell.borrow_mut();
        if g.is_none() { *g = Some(ForgeArena::new()); }
        g.as_mut().unwrap().alloc(bytes as usize) as i64
    })
}

thread_local! {
    static FORGE_ALLOC_SEQ: std::cell::Cell<u64> = const { std::cell::Cell::new(0) };
}

/// Returns the current forge cursor as an opaque mark (i64). JIT source
/// calls this as `forge.snapshot()` to capture the pre-frame watermark.
extern "C" fn forge_snapshot() -> i64 {
    FORGE.with(|cell| {
        let mut g = cell.borrow_mut();
        if g.is_none() { *g = Some(ForgeArena::new()); }
        g.as_mut().unwrap().snapshot() as i64
    })
}

/// Reset the forge cursor to `mark`, freeing all tensors allocated after
/// that point. JIT source calls this as `forge.restore(mark)`.
extern "C" fn forge_restore(mark: i64) {
    if mark < 0 {
        panic!("forge.restore: mark {} is negative (snapshot returned from a different arena?)", mark);
    }
    FORGE.with(|cell| {
        let mut g = cell.borrow_mut();
        if g.is_none() { *g = Some(ForgeArena::new()); }
        g.as_mut().unwrap().restore(mark as usize);
    })
}

// ─── Tensor printers (special-cased, not generic builtins) ───────────────────
//
// These are not exposed as named symbols; the JIT lowers
// `print_tensor(t)` to a direct call to one of these by selecting on rank
// and shape at compile time.

// #223: tensor print matches the interpreter (the canonical source of truth).
// The interp formats a tensor as `Tensor{:?} {}` — the shape debug plus
// ndarray's Display of the f64 data (interp.rs, `Value::Tensor`). These runtime
// fns are Rust, so they rebuild an `ArrayD<f64>` from the raw f32 buffer and use
// the identical formatting, giving byte-for-byte parity with `dmc run`.
extern "C" fn print_tensor_1d_f32(ptr: i64, n: i64) {
    let s = unsafe {
        std::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr as *const f32, n as usize)
    };
    let data: Vec<f64> = s.iter().map(|&x| x as f64).collect();
    let arr = ndarray::ArrayD::from_shape_vec(ndarray::IxDyn(&[n as usize]), data)
        .expect("print_tensor_1d: shape");
    println!("Tensor{:?} {}", arr.shape(), arr);
}

extern "C" fn print_tensor_2d_f32(ptr: i64, rows: i64, cols: i64) {
    let s = unsafe {
        std::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr as *const f32, (rows * cols) as usize)
    };
    let data: Vec<f64> = s.iter().map(|&x| x as f64).collect();
    let arr = ndarray::ArrayD::from_shape_vec(
        ndarray::IxDyn(&[rows as usize, cols as usize]), data)
        .expect("print_tensor_2d: shape");
    println!("Tensor{:?} {}", arr.shape(), arr);
}

// ─── String runtime ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// These functions are called by JIT-emitted code to create and manipulate
// string values. Strings are represented as i64 forge pointers to a block
// with layout: [len: i64][data: u8 * len].
//
// Literal byte data is kept alive for the process lifetime in LEAKED_STRING_DATA.

use std::sync::Mutex;
static LEAKED_STRING_DATA: Mutex<Vec<Vec<u8>>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());

/// Create a new forge-allocated string from a raw pointer + length.
/// `data_ptr` points to the UTF-8 bytes of the literal (kept alive by
/// `LEAKED_STRING_DATA`). Returns an i64 forge pointer.
extern "C" fn dmc_str_new_from_raw(data_ptr: i64, len: i64) -> i64 {
    let buf = forge_alloc(len + 8);
    unsafe { *(buf as *mut i64) = len; }
    if len > 0 {
        unsafe {
            std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(
                data_ptr as *const u8,
                (buf + 8) as *mut u8,
                len as usize,
            );
        }
    }
    buf
}

/// Return the length (number of bytes) of a forge string.
extern "C" fn dmc_str_len(s: i64) -> i64 {
    unsafe { *(s as *const i64) }
}

/// Return the byte at index `i` of the forge string, or -1 if out of bounds.
extern "C" fn dmc_str_get_char(s: i64, i: i64) -> i64 {
    let len = unsafe { *(s as *const i64) };
    // Resolve negative indices from the end and trap on genuine OOB, matching
    // the interpreter (#297): previously this returned a -1 sentinel for both
    // negative and out-of-range indices, so `s[-1]` and `s[100]` diverged.
    let resolved = if i < 0 { len + i } else { i };
    if resolved < 0 || resolved >= len {
        eprintln!("runtime error: string index {} out of range (len {})", i, len);
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    unsafe { *((s + 8 + resolved) as *const u8) as i64 }
}

/// Return 1 if the two forge strings are byte-equal, 0 otherwise.
extern "C" fn dmc_str_eq(s1: i64, s2: i64) -> i64 {
    let len1 = unsafe { *(s1 as *const i64) };
    let len2 = unsafe { *(s2 as *const i64) };
    if len1 != len2 { return 0; }
    let d1 = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts((s1 + 8) as *const u8, len1 as usize) };
    let d2 = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts((s2 + 8) as *const u8, len2 as usize) };
    if d1 == d2 { 1 } else { 0 }
}

/// Concatenate two forge strings and return a new forge string.
extern "C" fn dmc_str_concat(s1: i64, s2: i64) -> i64 {
    let len1 = unsafe { *(s1 as *const i64) };
    let len2 = unsafe { *(s2 as *const i64) };
    let total = len1 + len2;
    let buf = forge_alloc(total + 8);
    unsafe { *(buf as *mut i64) = total; }
    if len1 > 0 {
        unsafe {
            std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(
                (s1 + 8) as *const u8, (buf + 8) as *mut u8, len1 as usize,
            );
        }
    }
    if len2 > 0 {
        unsafe {
            std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(
                (s2 + 8) as *const u8, (buf + 8 + len1) as *mut u8, len2 as usize,
            );
        }
    }
    buf
}

/// `n as str` — convert an i64 to a forge string (decimal representation).
/// String layout: [len: i64][bytes: u8*] (same as dmc_str_new_from_raw output).
extern "C" fn dmc_str_from_int(n: i64) -> i64 {
    let s = n.to_string();
    let bytes = s.as_bytes();
    let len = bytes.len() as i64;
    let buf = forge_alloc(len + 8);
    unsafe { *(buf as *mut i64) = len; }
    if len > 0 {
        unsafe {
            std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(
                bytes.as_ptr(),
                (buf + 8) as *mut u8,
                len as usize,
            );
        }
    }
    buf
}

/// Pack a Rust string into a fresh forge string [len: i64][bytes: u8*] —
/// the shared tail of every `*_from_*` string constructor.
fn forge_str_from_rust(s: &str) -> i64 {
    let bytes = s.as_bytes();
    let len = bytes.len() as i64;
    let buf = forge_alloc(len + 8);
    unsafe { *(buf as *mut i64) = len; }
    if len > 0 {
        unsafe {
            std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(bytes.as_ptr(), (buf + 8) as *mut u8, len as usize);
        }
    }
    buf
}

/// `x as str` for an f64 — render with Rust's `{}` (shortest round-tripping
/// decimal), matching the interpreter's Display for `Value::Float` (#368
/// follow-up: the JIT previously truncated floats to their integer part by
/// routing through `dmc_str_from_int`).
extern "C" fn dmc_str_from_f64(x: f64) -> i64 {
    forge_str_from_rust(&format!("{}", x))
}
